problems.prompt: A solid melts at {{Tm}} K with Δh_fus = {{dh}} kJ/mol. At what temperature does its ideal solubility reach x = {{xs}}? (R = 8.314)

parts.label: v
parts.explain: ln x = −(Δh_fus/R)(1/T − 1/T_m): ideal solubility depends only on the solute

problems.prompt: A mixture is {{y}} mole fraction gas 1 ($a = {{a1}}$) and the rest gas 2 ($a = {{a2}}$), in the same units. Find $a_{mix}$ with $a_{12} = \sqrt{a_1a_2}$.

parts.label: v
parts.explain: $a$ is quadratic in composition (pair interactions); the geometric-mean cross term is the classical combining rule

problems.prompt: Two gases have vdW b₁ = {{b1}} and b₂ = {{b2}} L/mol. What is b_mix for y₁ = {{y}}?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: b mixes linearly (the arithmetic cross term reduces the quadratic rule to Σ y_ib_i); a uses the geometric mean

problems.prompt: A gas has $B = {{B}}$ cm³/mol at {{T}} K. What is its fugacity coefficient at {{P}} bar?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: Integrate $(Z - 1)/P$ with $Z = 1 + BP/RT$. Negative $B$ (attraction) gives $\phi < 1$

problems.prompt: A gas has B = {{B}} cm³/mol at {{T}} K. At what pressure, in bar, does the truncated virial give φ = {{phi}}?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: ln φ = BP/RT: φ falls below 1 linearly in P where attraction dominates

problems.prompt: With van Laar parameters $A_{12} = {{a}}$, $A_{21} = {{b}}$, find $\ln\gamma_1$ at $x_1 = {{x1}}$.

parts.label: v
parts.explain: $\ln\gamma_1$ is the partial molar derivative of $nG^E/RT = n A_{12}A_{21}x_1x_2/(A_{12}x_1 + A_{21}x_2)$; at infinite dilution it tends to $A_{12}$

expect.v: diff((Symbol('n1') + Symbol('n2'))*nsimplify(a)*nsimplify(b)*(Symbol('n1')/(Symbol('n1') + Symbol('n2')))*(Symbol('n2')/(Symbol('n1') + Symbol('n2')))/(nsimplify(a)*Symbol('n1')/(Symbol('n1') + Symbol('n2')) + nsimplify(b)*Symbol('n2')/(Symbol('n1') + Symbol('n2'))), Symbol('n1')).subs({Symbol('n1'): nsimplify(x1), Symbol('n2'): 1 - nsimplify(x1)})

problems.prompt: A van Laar model has A₁₂ = {{a}} and A₂₁ = {{b}}. What is γ₂ at infinite dilution in component 1?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: ln γ₂ = A₂₁[A₁₂x₁/(A₁₂x₁ + A₂₁x₂)]² → A₂₁ as x₂ → 0

problems.prompt: A solute ($V_1 = {{V}}$ cm³/mol, $\delta_1 = {{d1}}$ (J/cm³)$^{1/2}$) in a solvent with $\delta_2 = {{d2}}$ has solvent volume fraction $\Phi_2 = {{F}}$ at {{T}} K. Find $\ln\gamma_1$.

problems.prompt: For {{sp}} the ground level has degeneracy ${{g0}}$ and the first excited level, ${{eps}}$ cm⁻¹ higher, has degeneracy ${{g1}}$. What is the electronic partition function at ${{T}}$ K? ($hc/k_B = 1.4388$ cm·K.)

parts.label: r
parts.explain: $q_{el} = g_0 + g_1e^{-\varepsilon/k_BT}$ with $\varepsilon/k_BT = 1.4388\,\tilde\nu/T$. Most molecules have their first excited electronic state far above $k_BT$ and $q_{el} = g_0$; these species are the exceptions because the gap is a spin–orbit splitting

cases.q: N₂ at 300 K or N₂ at 600 K
He at 300 K or Ar at 300 K
H₂ at 300 K or O₂ at 1200 K
CO₂ at 500 K or N₂ at 300 K
Xe at 900 K or Ne at 300 K

problems.prompt: Which gas has the faster, broader Maxwell speed distribution: {{q}}?

parts.label: a
parts.explain: Every characteristic speed goes as $\sqrt{T/M}$, and the width of the distribution scales the same way. Compare $T/M$: ${{T1}}/{{M1}}$ against ${{T2}}/{{M2}}$

problems.prompt: A molecule of diameter ${{d}}$ pm moves at a mean speed of ${{v}}$ m/s through a gas with $2.46 \times 10^{25}$ molecules per m³ (1 atm, 298 K). How many collisions does it make per second? Answer in units of $10^9$ s⁻¹.

parts.label: r
parts.explain: $z = \sqrt2\,\sigma\bar v\,(N/V)$ with collision cross-section $\sigma = \pi d^2$. The $\sqrt2$ is there because the targets move too: what matters is the mean relative speed. A few billion collisions a second is normal at 1 atm

problems.prompt: A solute with $D = {{D}} \times 10^{-9}$ m²/s has a concentration that falls by ${{dC}}$ mol/m³ across ${{dx}}$ mm. What is the magnitude of the diffusive flux, in µmol/(m²·s)?

parts.label: r
parts.explain: Fick's first law: $J = -D\,\dfrac{dC}{dx}$. The minus sign says the flux runs from high concentration to low. Same form as Fourier's law for heat and Newton's law for momentum

problems.prompt: A fluid of viscosity ${{eta}}$ mPa·s fills a ${{gap}}$ mm gap between two plates. One plate moves at ${{du}}$ m/s relative to the other. What is the shear stress, in Pa?

parts.label: r
parts.explain: $\tau = \eta\,\dfrac{du}{dz}$: momentum diffuses down the velocity gradient. The mPa and the mm cancel, leaving $\eta\,\Delta u/\text{gap}$ in Pa. For a gas $\eta = \tfrac13\rho\bar v\lambda$, which rises with temperature, the opposite of a liquid

problems.prompt: For {{rx}} the measured pre-exponential factor is ${{Ae}} \times {{u}}$ L/(mol·s) and collision theory predicts ${{At}} \times {{v}}$ L/(mol·s). What is the steric factor $p$?

parts.label: r
parts.explain: $k = pZ_{AB}e^{-E_a/RT}$, so $p = A_{exp}/A_{theory}$. A small $p$ means most collisions with enough energy still have the wrong orientation. $p > 1$, as for K + Br₂, means the reaction reaches further than the hard-sphere diameter: the electron jumps first (the harpoon mechanism)

problems.prompt: A ⇌ B with $k_1 = {{k1}}$ s⁻¹ forward and $k_{-1} = {{km}}$ s⁻¹ back, starting from pure A at 1 mol/L. What is [A] after ${{t}}$ s, in mol/L?

parts.label: r
parts.explain: The equilibrium value is $[A]_{eq} = \dfrac{k_{-1}}{k_1 + k_{-1}} = {{km/(k1 + km)}}$, and the distance from it decays with the sum of the two rate constants: $[A] = [A]_{eq} + ([A]_0 - [A]_{eq})e^{-(k_1 + k_{-1})t}$. A reversible reaction relaxes faster than either step alone

problems.prompt: In A → B → C with $k_1 = {{k1}}$ s⁻¹ and $k_2 = {{k2}}$ s⁻¹, at what time does the intermediate B reach its maximum, in s?

parts.label: r
parts.explain: [B] $\propto e^{-k_1t} - e^{-k_2t}$. Set its derivative to zero: $k_1e^{-k_1t} = k_2e^{-k_2t}$, so $t_{max} = \dfrac{\ln(k_1/k_2)}{k_1 - k_2}$. The faster B is consumed relative to how fast it forms, the earlier and lower the peak

problems.prompt: A ⇌ I → P with $k_1 = {{k1}}$ s⁻¹, $k_{-1} = {{km}}$ s⁻¹ and $k_2 = {{k2}}$ s⁻¹. Use the steady-state approximation for I to find the rate of formation of P when [A] = ${{A}}$ mol/L, in mol/(L·s).

parts.label: r
parts.explain: Set $d[I]/dt = k_1[A] - (k_{-1} + k_2)[I] = 0$, so $[I] = \dfrac{k_1[A]}{k_{-1} + k_2}$ and the rate is $k_2[I]$. If $k_2 \gg k_{-1}$ this is just $k_1[A]$: the first step is rate-determining

problems.prompt: A + B ⇌ I is fast with equilibrium constant $K = {{K}}$ L/mol, then I → P slowly with $k_2 = {{k2}}$ s⁻¹. What is the rate when [A] = ${{A}}$ and [B] = ${{B}}$ mol/L, in mol/(L·s)?

parts.label: r
parts.explain: The fast step stays at equilibrium, $[I] = K[A][B]$, and the slow step sets the rate: $v = k_2K[A][B]$. The observed rate constant is the product $k_2K$, which is why its apparent activation energy can even be negative

problems.prompt: In the Lindemann mechanism A + M ⇌ A* + M ($k_a = {{ka}}$, $k_{-a} = {{kma}}$ L/(mol·s)), A* → P ($k_b = {{kb}}$ s⁻¹). What is the effective first-order rate constant at [M] = ${{M}}$ mol/L, in s⁻¹?

parts.label: r
parts.explain: $k_{uni} = \dfrac{k_ak_b[M]}{k_{-a}[M] + k_b}$. At high pressure deactivation wins and it levels off at $k_ak_b/k_{-a} = {{ka*kb/kma}}$ s⁻¹, true first order. At low pressure it falls to $k_a[M]$: activation by collision becomes the slow step and the reaction turns second order

problems.prompt: A radical chain is initiated at ${{a}} \times 10^{-8}$ mol/(L·s), terminates by radical–radical combination with $k_t = 1 \times 10^{8}$ L/(mol·s), and propagates with $k_p = {{kp}}$ L/(mol·s) at monomer concentration ${{M}}$ mol/L. What is the kinetic chain length?

parts.label: r
parts.explain: Steady state: initiation equals termination, so $[R\cdot] = \sqrt{R_i/k_t} = {{sqrt(a)}} \times 10^{-8}$ mol/L. The chain length is propagation over initiation, $\dfrac{k_p[R\cdot][M]}{R_i}$: how many monomers each radical adds before it dies. More initiator means more radicals but shorter chains

problems.prompt: Expand $f(x) = 1$ on $0 \le x \le 1$ in the particle-in-a-box functions $\psi_n = \sqrt2\sin n\pi x$. What is the coefficient $c_{ {{n}} }$?

parts.label: r
parts.explain: $c_n = \displaystyle\int_0^1 \psi_n f\,dx = \sqrt2\,\dfrac{1 - \cos n\pi}{n\pi}$, which is $\dfrac{2\sqrt2}{n\pi}$ for odd $n$ and zero for even $n$: an even-$n$ function is antisymmetric about the middle of the box and $f$ is symmetric. The squares of the coefficients add to 1

problems.prompt: Are ${{ft}}$ and ${{gt}}$ orthogonal on ${{a}} \le x \le {{b}}$?

parts.label: a2
choice: Yes: the integral of their product is zero
No: the integral of their product is not zero
parts.explain: Integrate the product over the interval. Symmetry does most of the work: an odd integrand over a symmetric interval vanishes, and so does a product that is antisymmetric about the middle of the interval. Two eigenfunctions of the same Hermitian operator with different eigenvalues are always orthogonal

problems.prompt: The spherical harmonic $Y_{ {{l}} }^{ {{m}} }$ is an eigenfunction of $\hat L^2$. What is its eigenvalue, in units of $\hbar^2$?

parts.label: r
parts.explain: $\hat L^2Y_l^m = l(l + 1)\hbar^2Y_l^m$ and $\hat L_zY_l^m = m\hbar Y_l^m$: here ${{l*(l + 1)}}\hbar^2$ and ${{m}}\hbar$. The first depends only on $l$, so all $2l + 1$ values of $m$ share it

problems.prompt: An excited state has the same vibrational frequency as the ground state but a displaced minimum, with Huang–Rhys factor $S = {{Sv}}$. The band from $v = 0$ to $v'$ has intensity proportional to $\dfrac{S^{v'}e^{-S}}{v'!}$. Which $v'$ gives the strongest band?

parts.label: r
parts.explain: Each step up multiplies the intensity by $S/v'$, so the bands grow while $v' < S$ and shrink after: the peak is at the whole number just below $S$. A vertical transition lands where the ground-state wavefunction overlaps the upper state best; a bigger change in bond length means a longer progression peaking further out

problems.prompt: Use Walsh's rules to predict the shape of {{mol}}, which has ${{ve}}$ valence electrons.

parts.label: a
parts.explain: In an AH₂ molecule the first two valence orbitals prefer the linear shape. The next one is a pure p orbital when linear and drops sharply in energy on bending, because it can mix with s. So four electrons or fewer give a linear molecule; as soon as that third orbital is occupied the molecule bends

problems.prompt: Four electrons fill two spatial orbitals. In hartree: $h_1 = {{h1}}$, $h_2 = {{h2}}$, $J_{11} = {{J11}}$, $J_{22} = {{J22}}$, $J_{12} = {{J12}}$, $K_{12} = {{K12}}$. What is the Hartree–Fock electronic energy?

parts.label: r
parts.explain: $E = 2\sum h_i + \sum_{ij}(2J_{ij} - K_{ij})$ over the occupied orbitals. Every pair of electrons repels through $J$; only pairs with the same spin get the exchange lowering $K$. Between the two orbitals there are four pairs, two of them with parallel spins: $4J_{12} - 2K_{12}$

problems.prompt: Treat the ${{N}}$ π electrons of {{mol}} as particles in a box of length ${{L}}$ nm. At what wavelength does the lowest transition absorb, in nm? ($h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}$ J·s, $m_e = 9.109 \times 10^{-31}$ kg, $c = 2.998 \times 10^8$ m/s.)

parts.label: r
parts.explain: Two electrons per level fill $n = 1$ to $N/2 = {{N/2}}$. The transition is from $n = {{N/2}}$ to ${{N/2 + 1}}$: $\Delta E = (2n + 1)\dfrac{h^2}{8m_eL^2}$ with $2n + 1 = {{N + 1}}$, and $\lambda = hc/\Delta E$. Longer chains absorb at longer wavelength, which is why carotene is orange

problems.prompt: Light has wavelength $\lambda = {{lam}}\,\mathrm{nm}$. Use $h = 6.626\times10^{-34}\,\mathrm{J\,s}$ and $c = 2.998\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m/s}$.

parts.label: Eph
parts.explain: $E = \frac{hc}{\lambda} = \frac{(6.626\times10^{-34})(2.998\times10^{8})}{ {{lam*1e-9}} } = {{h*c/(lam*1e-9)}}\,\mathrm{J}$, with $\lambda$ in metres

parts.ask: Energy of a mole of these photons
parts.label: Emol
parts.explain: Times $N_A$: ${{h*c/(lam*1e-9)*NA/1000}}\,\mathrm{kJ/mol}$. A C–C bond is about 350 kJ/mol, which is why UV breaks bonds and red light does not

problems.prompt: Light of wavelength $\lambda = {{lam}}\,\mathrm{nm}$ strikes a metal with work function $\Phi = {{Phi}}\,\mathrm{eV}$. Use $1\,\mathrm{eV} = 1.602\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{J}$.

parts.label: Eph
parts.explain: $h\nu = \frac{hc}{\lambda} = {{h*c/(lam*1e-9)}}\,\mathrm{J} = {{Ev}}\,\mathrm{eV}$. Shortcut: $1240/\lambda(\mathrm{nm})$

parts.ask: Maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons
parts.label: KE
parts.explain: $KE = h\nu - \Phi = {{Ev}} - {{Phi}} = {{Ev - Phi}}\,\mathrm{eV}$

parts.label: nu0
parts.explain: $\nu_0 = \frac{\Phi}{h} = \frac{({{Phi}})(1.602\times10^{-19})}{6.626\times10^{-34}} = {{Phi*eV/h}}\,\mathrm{Hz}$. Below it, no electrons at any intensity

problems.prompt: An electron ($m_e = 9.109\times10^{-31}\,\mathrm{kg}$) moves at $v = {{v}}\,\mathrm{m/s}$.

parts.label: lam
parts.explain: $\lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{6.626\times10^{-34}}{ {{me*v}} } = {{h/(me*v)}}\,\mathrm{m} = {{h/(me*v)*1e12}}\,\mathrm{pm}$. Bond lengths are 100–200 pm, so electrons at these speeds diffract from crystals

problems.prompt: A hydrogen atom drops from $n = {{n2}}$ to $n = {{n1}}$. Use $E_n = -13.606\,\mathrm{eV}/n^2$.

parts.label: lam
parts.explain: $\lambda = \frac{hc}{\Delta E} = {{h*c/(Ry*(1/n1^2 - 1/n2^2)*eV)*1e9}}\,\mathrm{nm}$. Lyman ($n_1 = 1$) is UV, Balmer ($n_1 = 2$) visible, Paschen ($n_1 = 3$) infrared

problems.prompt: An electron is confined to a region $\Delta x = {{dx}}\,\mathrm{pm}$ wide. Use $\hbar = 1.0546\times10^{-34}\,\mathrm{J\,s}$.

parts.label: dp
parts.explain: $\Delta p \ge \frac{\hbar}{2\Delta x} = \frac{1.0546\times10^{-34}}{2({{dx*1e-12}})} = {{hbar/(2*dx*1e-12)}}\,\mathrm{kg\,m/s}$

parts.ask: The corresponding uncertainty in speed, $\Delta v$
parts.label: dv
parts.explain: $\Delta v = \frac{\Delta p}{m_e} = {{hbar/(2*dx*1e-12)/me}}\,\mathrm{m/s}$. Squeeze the box and the electron must move faster: this is why atoms do not collapse

problems.prompt: An electron is in a one-dimensional box of length $L = {{L}}\,\mathrm{nm}$.

parts.label: lam
parts.explain: $\lambda = \frac{hc}{\Delta E} = {{h*c/((2*n + 1)*h^2/(8*me*(L*1e-9)^2))*1e9}}\,\mathrm{nm}$. A longer box absorbs at longer wavelength, which is why longer conjugated dyes are more deeply coloured

problems.prompt: A diatomic molecule has force constant $k = {{k}}\,\mathrm{N/m}$ and reduced mass $\mu = {{mu}}\,\mathrm{u}$ ($1\,\mathrm{u} = 1.6605\times10^{-27}\,\mathrm{kg}$). Treat it as a harmonic oscillator.

parts.label: nu
parts.explain: $\nu = \frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{k}{\mu}} = \frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{ {{k}} }{ {{mu*amu}} }} = {{sqrt(k/(mu*amu))/(2*pi)}}\,\mathrm{Hz}$, with $\mu$ in kg

parts.label: wn
parts.explain: $\tilde\nu = \frac{\nu}{c}$ with $c$ in cm/s: ${{sqrt(k/(mu*amu))/(2*pi)/(c*100)}}\,\mathrm{cm^{-1}}$

parts.label: zpe
parts.explain: $E_0 = \tfrac12 h\nu$ per molecule, times $N_A$: ${{0.5*h*sqrt(k/(mu*amu))/(2*pi)*NA/1000}}\,\mathrm{kJ/mol}$. It never goes away, even at $0\,\mathrm{K}$

problems.prompt: A diatomic molecule has reduced mass $\mu = {{mu}}\,\mathrm{u}$ and bond length $r = {{r}}\,\mathrm{pm}$. Treat it as a rigid rotor.

parts.label: B
parts.explain: $\tilde B = \frac{h}{8\pi^2 c I}$ with $c$ in cm/s: ${{h/(8*pi^2*c*100*mu*amu*(r*1e-12)^2)}}\,\mathrm{cm^{-1}}$

parts.ask: Spacing between adjacent lines in the pure rotational spectrum
parts.label: sp
parts.explain: Lines sit at $2\tilde B(J + 1)$, so they are $2\tilde B = {{2*h/(8*pi^2*c*100*mu*amu*(r*1e-12)^2)}}\,\mathrm{cm^{-1}}$ apart. Measure the spacing and you have the bond length

problems.prompt: A solution of concentration ${{cuM}}\,\mathrm{\mu mol/L}$ has molar absorption coefficient $\varepsilon = {{eps}}\,\mathrm{L/mol\cdot cm}$ and is measured in a ${{l}}\,\mathrm{cm}$ cell.

parts.label: A
parts.explain: $A = \varepsilon c l = ({{eps}})({{cuM*1e-6}})({{l}}) = {{Av}}$, with $c$ in mol/L

problems.prompt: A proton ($\gamma = 2.6752\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}\,T^{-1}}$) sits in a magnetic field $B_0 = {{B0}}\,\mathrm{T}$.

parts.label: nu
parts.explain: $\nu_0 = \frac{\gamma B_0}{2\pi} = \frac{(2.6752\times10^{8})({{B0}})}{2\pi} = {{gyro*B0/(2*pi)/1e6}}\,\mathrm{MHz}$. That number is how the spectrometer is named

problems.prompt: On a ${{sf}}\,\mathrm{MHz}$ spectrometer a proton signal appears at $\delta = {{d}}\,\mathrm{ppm}$.

parts.ask: Its offset from the reference in hertz
parts.label: dnu
parts.explain:
$\delta =  rac{\Delta
u}{
u_\mathrm{ref}}	imes10^6$, so $\Delta
u = \delta	imes
u_\mathrm{ref}(\mathrm{MHz}) = ({{d}})({{sf}}) = {{d*sf}}\,\mathrm{Hz}$

parts.ask: The offset of the same signal on a ${{sf2}}\,\mathrm{MHz}$ instrument
parts.label: dnu2
parts.explain: The shift in ppm is the same on every instrument; the hertz scale with the field: $({{d}})({{sf2}}) = {{d*sf2}}\,\mathrm{Hz}$

problems.prompt: A gas of molar mass $M = {{Mg}}\,\mathrm{g/mol}$ is at $T = {{T}}\,\mathrm{K}$.

parts.label: vmp
parts.explain: $v_\mathrm{mp} = \sqrt{\frac{2RT}{M}} = \sqrt{\frac{2(8.314)({{T}})}{ {{Mg/1000}} }} = {{sqrt(2*R*T/(Mg/1000))}}\,\mathrm{m/s}$, with $M$ in kg/mol

parts.label: vav
parts.explain: $\bar v = \sqrt{\frac{8RT}{\pi M}} = {{sqrt(8*R*T/(pi*Mg/1000))}}\,\mathrm{m/s}$

parts.label: vrms
parts.explain: $v_\mathrm{rms} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}} = {{sqrt(3*R*T/(Mg/1000))}}\,\mathrm{m/s}$. Always $v_\mathrm{mp} < \bar v < v_\mathrm{rms}$, in the ratio $1 : 1.128 : 1.225$

problems.prompt: Gas 1 ($M_1 = {{M1}}\,\mathrm{g/mol}$) and gas 2 ($M_2 = {{M2}}\,\mathrm{g/mol}$) effuse through the same pinhole at the same temperature and pressure.

parts.label: ratio
parts.explain: $\frac{r_1}{r_2} = \sqrt{\frac{M_2}{M_1}} = \sqrt{\frac{ {{M2}} }{ {{M1}} }} = {{sqrt(M2/M1)}}$. The lighter gas is faster, by the square root of the mass ratio

problems.prompt: A gas of molecules with collision diameter $d = {{d}}\,\mathrm{pm}$ is at $T = {{T}}\,\mathrm{K}$ and $P = {{P}}\,\mathrm{Pa}$. Use $k_B = 1.381\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J/K}$.

parts.label: lam
parts.explain: $\lambda = \frac{k_BT}{\sqrt2\,\sigma P} = \frac{(1.381\times10^{-23})({{T}})}{\sqrt2({{pi*(d*1e-12)^2}})({{P}})} = {{kB*T/(sqrt(2)*pi*(d*1e-12)^2*P)}}\,\mathrm{m}$. About 70 nm in air at 1 bar; metres under high vacuum

problems.prompt: A species has diffusion coefficient $D = {{D}}\,\mathrm{m^2/s}$. Consider diffusion along one dimension for $t = {{t}}\,\mathrm{s}$.

parts.label: x
parts.explain: $x_\mathrm{rms} = \sqrt{2Dt} = \sqrt{2({{D}})({{t}})} = {{sqrt(2*D*t)}}\,\mathrm{m} = {{sqrt(2*D*t)*1e6}}\,\mathrm{\mu m}$. Distance grows as $\sqrt t$: four times the time, only twice as far

problems.prompt: Initial rates for $\mathrm{A} + \mathrm{B} \rightarrow$ products: run 1, $[\mathrm{A}] = {{A1}}$, $[\mathrm{B}] = {{B1}}\,\mathrm{M}$, rate $= {{r1}}\,\mathrm{M/s}$; run 2, $[\mathrm{A}] = {{2*A1}}$, $[\mathrm{B}] = {{B1}}\,\mathrm{M}$, rate $= {{r1*2^m}}\,\mathrm{M/s}$; run 3, $[\mathrm{A}] = {{A1}}$, $[\mathrm{B}] = {{3*B1}}\,\mathrm{M}$, rate $= {{r1*3^n}}\,\mathrm{M/s}$.

parts.label: oA
parts.explain: Runs 1 and 2 double [A] at fixed [B]; the rate goes up by ${{2^m}} = 2^{ {{m}} }$

parts.label: oB
parts.explain: Runs 1 and 3 triple [B] at fixed [A]; the rate goes up by ${{3^n}} = 3^{ {{n}} }$

parts.ask: Rate constant, $k$ (in units of M and s)
parts.label: k

problems.prompt: A first-order reaction has $k = {{k}}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ and starts at $[\mathrm{A}]_0 = {{A0}}\,\mathrm{M}$.

parts.label: th
parts.explain: $t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{k} = \frac{0.6931}{ {{k}} } = {{log(2)/k}}\,\mathrm{s}$, whatever the starting concentration

problems.prompt: A reaction that is second order in A has $k = {{k}}\,\mathrm{M^{-1}s^{-1}}$ and starts at $[\mathrm{A}]_0 = {{A0}}\,\mathrm{M}$.

parts.label: th
parts.explain: $t_{1/2} = \frac{1}{k[\mathrm{A}]_0} = \frac{1}{({{k}})({{A0}})} = {{1/(k*A0)}}\,\mathrm{s}$. Unlike first order, each half-life is twice the one before

problems.prompt: A reacts by two parallel first-order paths, $\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{B}$ with $k_1 = {{k1}}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ and $\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}$ with $k_2 = {{k2}}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. $[\mathrm{A}]_0 = {{A0}}\,\mathrm{M}$, no B or C at the start.

parts.label: At
parts.explain: A disappears by both paths at once: $[\mathrm{A}] = [\mathrm{A}]_0e^{-(k_1 + k_2)t} = ({{A0}})e^{-({{k1 + k2}})({{t}})} = {{A0*exp(-(k1 + k2)*t)}}\,\mathrm{M}$

parts.ask: Fraction of the reacted A that becomes B
parts.label: yB
parts.explain: $\frac{k_1}{k_1 + k_2} = \frac{ {{k1}} }{ {{k1 + k2}} } = {{k1/(k1 + k2)}}$, the same at every time

problems.prompt: An enzyme has $V_\mathrm{max} = {{Vmax}}\,\mathrm{\mu M/s}$ and $K_M = {{Km}}\,\mathrm{\mu M}$.

parts.label: v
parts.explain: $v = \frac{V_\mathrm{max}[\mathrm{S}]}{K_M + [\mathrm{S}]} = \frac{({{Vmax}})({{S}})}{ {{Km}} + {{S}} } = {{Vmax*S/(Km + S)}}\,\mathrm{\mu M/s}$

parts.ask: Substrate concentration needed to reach 90% of $V_\mathrm{max}$
parts.label: S90
parts.explain: Set $\frac{[\mathrm{S}]}{K_M + [\mathrm{S}]} = 0.9$: $[\mathrm{S}] = 9K_M = {{9*Km}}\,\mathrm{\mu M}$. Half of $V_\mathrm{max}$ takes only $K_M$; the last stretch is expensive

problems.prompt: A central atom has {{kb}} bonded atoms and {{kl}} lone pair(s), all in equivalent hybrids. What percent p character do the hybrids have?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: n domains mix one s orbital with n − 1 p orbitals, so each hybrid is 1/n s: 50% p for sp, 66.7% for sp², 75% for sp³

problems.prompt: By Walsh's rules, the AH₂ species {{q}} is:

parts.label: v
parts.explain: With four valence electrons only the two bonding orbitals are filled and they favour 180°. From the fifth electron on, the orbital that drops sharply on bending is occupied

problems.prompt: Two electrons occupy different orbitals with Coulomb integral J = {{kj}} eV and exchange integral K = {{kk}} eV. How far does the open-shell singlet lie above the triplet, in eV?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: E = h₁ + h₂ + J ± K: plus for the singlet, minus for the triplet, so the gap is 2K and the triplet is lower (Hund)

cases.q: symmetric stretch of CO₂
antisymmetric stretch of CO₂
bend of CO₂
symmetric stretch of H₂O
stretch of N₂
stretch of HCl

problems.prompt: The {{q}} is:

parts.label: v
parts.explain: IR needs a changing dipole, Raman a changing polarisability. In a molecule with a centre of symmetry no mode is both (mutual exclusion)

problems.prompt: On a {{km}} MHz spectrometer a proton resonates {{kh}} Hz downfield of TMS. What is its chemical shift in ppm?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: δ = (ν − ν_ref)/ν₀ × 10⁶, which is why the ppm scale does not depend on the magnet

a gauche arrangement (60°)
two axial hydrogens on adjacent carbons of a chair
an axial and an equatorial hydrogen on adjacent carbons
two equatorial hydrogens on adjacent carbons

problems.prompt: By the Karplus relation, the three-bond H–H coupling for {{q}} is:

parts.label: v
parts.explain: J is largest near 0° and 180° and passes through a minimum near 90°. Axial–axial is 180°; the other chair pairs are about 60°

problems.prompt: What is the density, in g/L, of {{g}} (M = {{M}} g/mol) at {{P}} kPa and {{T}} K, treated as ideal? (R = 8.314 J/mol·K)

parts.label: v
parts.explain: ρ = PM/RT: denser gases are heavier or colder, which is how a gas density gives a molar mass

problems.prompt: A gas starting at {{V1}} L expands against a constant external pressure of {{P}} kPa and does {{w}} J of work. What is its final volume, in L?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: w = −P_ext ΔV, with 1 kPa·L = 1 J

problems.prompt: For {{rx}}, ΔH = {{dH}} kJ/mol at 298 K. What is ΔU, in kJ/mol? (R = 8.314 J/mol·K)

parts.label: v
parts.explain: ΔH = ΔU + Δn_gas RT: only gas moles count, and RT is 2.48 kJ/mol at room temperature

problems.prompt: Burning {{m}} g of a compound (M = {{M}} g/mol) in a bomb calorimeter with heat capacity {{Cc}} kJ/K raises the temperature by {{dT}} K. What is ΔU of combustion, in kJ/mol?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: The heat the reaction releases at constant volume warms the calorimeter: q_V = ΔU

problems.prompt: Given C(s) + O₂ → CO₂, ΔH = {{h1}} kJ/mol, and CO + ½O₂ → CO₂, ΔH = {{h2}} kJ/mol, what is ΔH for C(s) + ½O₂ → CO, in kJ/mol?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: Run the second reaction backwards and add: enthalpy is a state function, so the path does not matter

problems.prompt: A reaction has ΔH = {{h1}} kJ/mol at {{T1}} K and {{h2}} kJ/mol at {{T2}} K. Assuming constant ΔC_p, what is ΔC_p, in J/(mol·K)?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: Kirchhoff's law run backwards: the slope of ΔH against T is ΔC_p

expect.v: solve(Eq(nsimplify(h1)*1000 + integrate(x, (Symbol('TT'), T1, T2)), nsimplify(h2)*1000), x)[0]

parts.label: v

parts.explain: E°_cell = E°_cathode − E°_anode: zinc (−0.76 V) gives the Daniell cell's 1.10 V

parts.label: v

parts.label: v
parts.explain: E° = (RT/nF) ln K: K = 10³⁷ (the Daniell cell) corresponds to 1.1 V

problems.prompt: A {{P}} mW laser emits at {{l}} nm. How many photons does it emit per second, in units of 10¹⁵? (h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, c = 2.998 × 10⁸ m/s, m_e = 9.109 × 10⁻³¹ kg, e = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, N_A = 6.022 × 10²³)

parts.label: v
parts.explain: A milliwatt of visible light is a few × 10¹⁵ photons per second

problems.prompt: A metal has a work function of {{phi}} eV. What is the longest wavelength, in nm, that ejects electrons? (hc = 1239.84 eV·nm)

problems.prompt: Through what potential difference, in V, must an electron be accelerated from rest to have a de Broglie wavelength of {{l}} pm? (h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, c = 2.998 × 10⁸ m/s, m_e = 9.109 × 10⁻³¹ kg, e = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, N_A = 6.022 × 10²³)

parts.label: v
parts.explain: λ = h/√(2meV): about 150 V gives 100 pm, the size of atoms, which is why electron diffraction sees crystals

problems.prompt: What is the shortest wavelength, in nm, of the hydrogen series that ends on n = {{nl}}? (R_H = 109 677 cm⁻¹)

parts.label: v
parts.explain: The series limit is the transition from the ionisation threshold: 91 nm (Lyman), 365 nm (Balmer)

problems.prompt: f(x) = {{fn}}(kx) with k = {{k}} nm⁻¹. What is its eigenvalue under d²/dx², in nm⁻²?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: Sines and cosines are eigenfunctions of d²/dx² (and so of the free-particle Hamiltonian) but not of d/dx

parts.explain: Tends to 1/3, the classical uniform value, at large n: the correspondence principle

problems.prompt: An electron in a {{L}} nm box is in an equal superposition of n = 1 and n = 2. With what period, in fs, does its probability density oscillate? (h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, c = 2.998 × 10⁸ m/s, m_e = 9.109 × 10⁻³¹ kg, e = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, N_A = 6.022 × 10²³)

parts.label: v
parts.explain: Only energy differences show up in |Ψ|²: the cross term oscillates at (E₂ − E₁)/h

parts.explain: ΔxΔp ≥ ħ/2: confining an electron to an atom implies speeds of order 10⁶ m/s

problems.prompt: An electron in a box absorbs at {{l}} nm on the n = {{n1}} → {{n2}} transition. How long is the box, in nm? (h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, c = 2.998 × 10⁸ m/s, m_e = 9.109 × 10⁻³¹ kg, e = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, N_A = 6.022 × 10²³)

parts.label: v
parts.explain: Longer boxes absorb at longer wavelength: the basis of colour in conjugated dyes

parts.label: v
parts.explain: Stretching one side lowers the levels along it and breaks the cube's degeneracies

problems.prompt: A linear conjugated chain with {{N}} π electrons absorbs at {{l}} nm. Treated as a free electron in a box, how long is the chain, in nm? (h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, c = 2.998 × 10⁸ m/s, m_e = 9.109 × 10⁻³¹ kg, e = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, N_A = 6.022 × 10²³)

parts.label: v

problems.prompt: An electron meets a barrier {{dV}} eV above its energy. Over what distance, in pm, does its wavefunction fall by a factor e (1/κ)? (h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, c = 2.998 × 10⁸ m/s, m_e = 9.109 × 10⁻³¹ kg, e = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, N_A = 6.022 × 10²³)

parts.label: v

problems.prompt: Two peaks are {{dHz}} Hz apart on a {{f1}} MHz spectrometer. How far apart are they, in Hz, at {{f2}} MHz?

parts.explain: Chemical shift in ppm is field-independent; frequency differences scale with field, while J couplings do not

parts.label: v

problems.prompt: At what temperature, in K, does {{g1}} (M = {{M1}}) have the same rms speed as {{g2}} (M = {{M2}}) at {{T}} K?

problems.prompt: A molecule makes {{z}} × 10⁹ collisions per second at {{P1}} bar and {{T1}} K. How many does it make at {{P2}} bar and {{T2}} K (×10⁹ per s)?

problems.prompt: At what pressure, in Pa, does N₂ (σ = 0.43 nm²) at {{T}} K have a mean free path of {{lam}}? (k = 1.381 × 10⁻²³ J/K)

parts.label: v
parts.explain: λ = kT/(√2σP): ultra-high vacuum (below 10⁻⁷ Pa) gives free paths of kilometres

problems.prompt: A solute with D = {{D}} × 10⁻⁹ m²/s must cross a membrane at {{J}} μmol/(m²·s). What concentration gradient, in mol/m⁴, is needed?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: Fick's first law, J = −D dc/dx

problems.prompt: How long, in s, does a molecule with D = {{D}} take to diffuse an rms distance of {{x}} in 3-D?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: ⟨r²⟩ = 6Dt: diffusion crosses a cell in milliseconds but a millimetre in minutes

problems.prompt: A heat flux of {{q}} W/m² crosses a {{d}} cm slab with a {{dT}} K temperature drop. What is the thermal conductivity, in W/(m·K)?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: Fourier's law q = −κ dT/dx, the heat analogue of Fick's

problems.prompt: A fluid with viscosity {{eta}} mPa·s carries a shear stress of {{tau}} Pa. What velocity gradient, in s⁻¹?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: Newton's law of viscosity: momentum flows down the velocity gradient

problems.prompt: A reaction is order {{a}} in A and order {{b}} in B. If [A] is multiplied by {{fa}} and [B] by {{fb}}, by what factor does the rate change?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: The rate law, not the stoichiometry, sets the response

problems.prompt: What fraction of collisions at {{T}} K has enough energy to clear a barrier of {{Ea}} kJ/mol (e^{−Ea/RT})? Give it in units of 10⁻⁶. (R = 8.314)

parts.label: v
parts.explain: The Boltzmann factor, not the collision rate, controls how rates change with temperature

problems.prompt: For A ⇌ B with k_f = {{kf}} s⁻¹ and k_r = {{kr}} s⁻¹, how long until A has gone halfway to its equilibrium value, in s?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: The approach to equilibrium runs at k_f + k_r, faster than either step alone: the principle of relaxation methods

problems.prompt: A decays by two parallel first-order paths with k₁ = {{k1}} and k₂ = {{k2}} s⁻¹. How long until {{f}}% of A remains, in s?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: Parallel paths add their rate constants; the product ratio k₁/k₂ stays fixed throughout

problems.prompt: For A → B → C with k₁ = {{k1}} and k₂ = {{k2}} s⁻¹, when does [B] peak, in s?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: Set d[B]/dt = 0: the time depends only on the rate constants, not on [A]₀

problems.prompt: A ⇌ I (k₁ = {{k1}}, k₋₁ = {{km}} s⁻¹), I → P (k₂ = {{k2}} s⁻¹). With the steady-state approximation for I, what is the effective first-order rate constant, in s⁻¹?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: If k₂ ≫ k₋₁ the first step limits; if k₋₁ ≫ k₂ it becomes pre-equilibrium

problems.prompt: A pre-equilibrium has ΔH° = {{dH}} kJ/mol for the fast step and E_a = {{E2}} kJ/mol for the slow step. What is the apparent activation energy, in kJ/mol?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: k_obs = K k₂, so ln k_obs = ln K + ln k₂: a negative ΔH can make a rate fall as temperature rises

problems.prompt: In the Lindemann mechanism, k_a = {{ka}} M⁻¹s⁻¹, k₋a = {{km}} M⁻¹s⁻¹ and k_b = {{kb}} s⁻¹. At what bath-gas concentration, in M, does the rate constant reach half its high-pressure limit?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: Fall-off happens where deactivation and reaction of the energised molecule are equally fast

problems.prompt: An enzyme has K_M = {{K}} mM. What substrate concentration, in mM, gives {{f}}% of V_max?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: Going from 10% to 90% needs an 81-fold rise in [S]: Michaelis–Menten enzymes respond gradually

problems.prompt: A chain reaction converts monomer at {{Rp}} × 10⁻⁴ M/s with kinetic chain length {{nu}}. What is the rate of initiation, in 10⁻⁷ M/s?

parts.label: v
parts.explain: ν = R_p/R_i: each initiation event carries many propagation steps

problems.prompt: $n = {{n}}\,\mathrm{mol}$ of an ideal gas occupies $V = {{VL}}\,\mathrm{L}$ at $T = {{T}}\,\mathrm{K}$.

parts.label: Ppa
parts.explain: $P = \frac{nRT}{V}$ with $V$ in m³ ($1\,\mathrm{L} = 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^3}$): $\frac{ {{n}}\times 8.314\times {{T}} }{ {{VL/1000}} } = {{n*R*T/(VL/1000)}}\,\mathrm{Pa}$

parts.label: Pbar
parts.explain: $1\,\mathrm{bar} = 10^5\,\mathrm{Pa}$, so $P = {{Ppa/1e5}}\,\mathrm{bar}$

problems.prompt: A gas goes from $V_1 = {{V1}}\,\mathrm{L}$ to $V_2 = {{V2}}\,\mathrm{L}$ against a constant external pressure $P_\mathrm{ext} = {{Pext}}\,\mathrm{bar}$.

parts.ask: Is work done on the gas or by the gas?
parts.label: who
parts.explain: Expansion pushes the surroundings back, so the gas does work and $w < 0$. Compression is the reverse

parts.label: w
parts.explain: $w = -P_\mathrm{ext}\Delta V = -({{Pext*1e5}}\,\mathrm{Pa})({{(V2 - V1)/1000}}\,\mathrm{m^3}) = {{-Pext*1e5*(V2 - V1)/1000}}\,\mathrm{J}$. Bar times litre is 100 J

problems.prompt: A reaction run at constant volume has $\Delta U = {{dU}}\,\mathrm{kJ/mol}$ at $T = {{T}}\,\mathrm{K}$. The balanced equation changes the moles of gas by $\Delta n_\mathrm{gas} = {{dn}}$.

parts.label: corr
parts.explain: $({{dn}})(8.314)({{T}}) = {{dn*R*T}}\,\mathrm{J/mol} = {{dn*R*T/1000}}\,\mathrm{kJ/mol}$. Only gases count

parts.label: dH
parts.explain: $\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_\mathrm{gas}RT = {{dU}} + ({{dn*R*T/1000}}) = {{dU + dn*R*T/1000}}\,\mathrm{kJ/mol}$. Keep both terms in kJ

problems.prompt: For the reaction ${{a}}\,\mathrm{A} + {{b}}\,\mathrm{B} \rightarrow {{c}}\,\mathrm{C}$, the standard enthalpies of formation are $\Delta H_f^\circ(\mathrm{A}) = {{HA}}$, $\Delta H_f^\circ(\mathrm{B}) = {{HB}}$ and $\Delta H_f^\circ(\mathrm{C}) = {{HC}}\,\mathrm{kJ/mol}$.

parts.label: dHr
parts.explain: Products minus reactants, each times its coefficient: ${{c}}({{HC}}) - [{{a}}({{HA}}) + {{b}}({{HB}})] = {{dH}}\,\mathrm{kJ/mol}$

parts.ask: Is the reaction exothermic or endothermic?
parts.label: sign
parts.explain: Negative $\Delta H$ releases heat

problems.prompt: A reaction has $\Delta H^\circ = {{dH1}}\,\mathrm{kJ/mol}$ at $298\,\mathrm{K}$ and $\Delta C_P = {{dCp}}\,\mathrm{J/mol\cdot K}$, constant over the range. Find $\Delta H^\circ$ at $T_2 = {{T2}}\,\mathrm{K}$.

parts.label: dH2
parts.explain: $\Delta H(T_2) = \Delta H(T_1) + \Delta C_P\,\Delta T = {{dH1}} + ({{dCp*(T2 - 298)/1000}}) = {{dH1 + dCp*(T2 - 298)/1000}}\,\mathrm{kJ/mol}$

problems.prompt: A Carnot engine runs between $T_H = {{TH}}\,\mathrm{K}$ and $T_C = {{TC}}\,\mathrm{K}$ and takes in $q_H = {{qH}}\,\mathrm{J}$ per cycle.

parts.label: eta
parts.explain: $\eta = 1 - \frac{T_C}{T_H} = 1 - \frac{ {{TC}} }{ {{TH}} } = {{1 - TC/TH}}$, in kelvin

parts.label: w
parts.explain: $|w| = \eta\,q_H = {{(1 - TC/TH)*qH}}\,\mathrm{J}$

parts.ask: Heat rejected to the cold reservoir, $|q_C|$
parts.label: qC
parts.explain: Energy balance over a cycle: $|q_C| = q_H - |w| = {{qH - (1 - TC/TH)*qH}}\,\mathrm{J}$. Check: $q_H/T_H = |q_C|/T_C$, no net entropy made

problems.prompt: $n = {{n}}\,\mathrm{mol}$ of an ideal gas expands isothermally from ${{V1}}\,\mathrm{L}$ to ${{V1*k}}\,\mathrm{L}$.

parts.ask: Entropy change of the gas, $\Delta S$
parts.label: dS
parts.explain: $\Delta S = nR\ln\frac{V_2}{V_1} = ({{n}})(8.314)\ln {{k}} = {{n*R*log(k)}}\,\mathrm{J/K}$. Same answer whether the expansion is reversible or free: $S$ is a state function

problems.prompt: $n = {{n}}\,\mathrm{mol}$ of a substance with $C_P = {{Cp}}\,\mathrm{J/mol\cdot K}$ (constant) is heated at constant pressure from ${{T1}}\,\mathrm{K}$ to ${{T2}}\,\mathrm{K}$.

parts.label: dS
parts.explain: $\Delta S = \int\frac{nC_P\,dT}{T} = nC_P\ln\frac{T_2}{T_1} = ({{n}})({{Cp}})\ln\frac{ {{T2}} }{ {{T1}} } = {{n*Cp*log(T2/T1)}}\,\mathrm{J/K}$

problems.prompt: $n = {{n}}\,\mathrm{mol}$ of a substance goes through a phase transition at $T_\mathrm{tr} = {{Ttr}}\,\mathrm{K}$ with $\Delta H_\mathrm{tr} = {{dH}}\,\mathrm{kJ/mol}$.

parts.ask: Entropy change of the substance, $\Delta S$
parts.label: dS
parts.explain: At the transition temperature the heat flows reversibly, so $\Delta S = \frac{n\Delta H_\mathrm{tr}}{T_\mathrm{tr}} = \frac{({{n}})({{dH*1000}})}{ {{Ttr}} } = {{n*dH*1000/Ttr}}\,\mathrm{J/K}$. Convert kJ to J first

problems.prompt: In a crystal at $T \to 0$ each molecule is frozen into one of ${{W}}$ equally likely orientations.

parts.label: S0
parts.explain: $S_0 = k_B\ln W_0^{N_A} = R\ln W_0 = 8.314\ln {{W}} = {{R*log(W)}}\,\mathrm{J/mol\cdot K}$. CO, with two orientations, gives $R\ln 2 = 5.76$

problems.prompt: A reaction has $\Delta H = {{dH}}\,\mathrm{kJ/mol}$ and $\Delta S = {{dS}}\,\mathrm{J/mol\cdot K}$, both taken as constant. Consider it at $T = {{T}}\,\mathrm{K}$.

parts.label: dG
parts.explain: $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S = {{dH}} - ({{T}})({{dS/1000}}) = {{dGv}}\,\mathrm{kJ/mol}$. Put $\Delta S$ in kJ first

parts.ask: Is the reaction spontaneous at this temperature?
parts.label: spont
parts.explain: At constant $T$ and $P$, spontaneous means $\Delta G < 0$

parts.ask: Temperature at which $\Delta G$ changes sign
parts.label: Tx
parts.explain: $\Delta G = 0$ when $T = \frac{\Delta H}{\Delta S} = \frac{ {{dH*1000}} }{ {{dS}} } = {{dH*1000/dS}}\,\mathrm{K}$

problems.prompt: $n = {{n}}\,\mathrm{mol}$ of an ideal gas is taken isothermally at $T = {{T}}\,\mathrm{K}$ from ${{P1}}\,\mathrm{bar}$ to ${{P2}}\,\mathrm{bar}$.

parts.label: dG
parts.explain: $\Delta G = nRT\ln\frac{P_2}{P_1} = ({{n}})(8.314)({{T}})\ln\frac{ {{P2}} }{ {{P1}} } = {{n*R*T*log(P2/P1)}}\,\mathrm{J}$. Compressing a gas raises $G$

problems.prompt: At $T = {{T}}\,\mathrm{K}$ and $P = {{P}}\,\mathrm{bar}$ a gas has a measured molar volume $V_m = {{Vm}}\,\mathrm{L/mol}$.

parts.ask: Which interaction dominates at this state?
parts.label: which
parts.explain: Attractions pull the molar volume below the ideal value; repulsions push it above

problems.prompt: A gas has van der Waals constants $a = {{a}}\,\mathrm{bar\,L^2/mol^2}$ and $b = {{b}}\,\mathrm{L/mol}$. Its molar volume is $V_m = {{Vm}}\,\mathrm{L/mol}$ at $T = {{T}}\,\mathrm{K}$. Use $R = 0.08314\,\mathrm{L\,bar/mol\cdot K}$.

parts.label: Pv
parts.explain: $P = \frac{RT}{V_m - b} - \frac{a}{V_m^2} = \frac{(0.08314)({{T}})}{ {{Vm}} - {{b}} } - \frac{ {{a}} }{ {{Vm}}^2 } = {{Rg*T/(Vm - b) - a/Vm^2}}\,\mathrm{bar}$. $b$ raises the pressure, $a$ lowers it

problems.prompt: A system at equilibrium has ${{C}}$ component(s) and ${{P}}$ phase(s). No reactions, no other constraints.

parts.label: F
parts.explain: $F = C - P + 2 = {{C}} - {{P}} + 2 = {{C - P + 2}}$: the number of intensive variables you can change without losing a phase

problems.prompt: A spherical droplet of a liquid with surface tension $\gamma = {{gam}}\,\mathrm{N/m}$ has radius $r = {{rum}}\,\mathrm{\mu m}$.

parts.ask: Excess pressure inside the droplet, $\Delta P$
parts.label: dP
parts.explain: $\Delta P = \frac{2\gamma}{r} = \frac{2({{gam}})}{ {{rum*1e-6}} } = {{2*gam/(rum*1e-6)}}\,\mathrm{Pa}$. Halve the radius and the pressure doubles

problems.prompt: ${{ms}}\,\mathrm{g}$ of a nonvolatile, non-dissociating solute ($M = {{M}}\,\mathrm{g/mol}$) is dissolved in ${{kg}}\,\mathrm{kg}$ of a solvent with $K_f = {{Kf}}\,\mathrm{K\,kg/mol}$.

parts.label: molal
parts.explain: $m = \frac{\text{mol solute}}{\text{kg solvent}} = \frac{ {{ms}}/{{M}} }{ {{kg}} } = {{ms/M/kg}}\,\mathrm{mol/kg}$

parts.label: dT
parts.explain: $\Delta T_f = K_f\,m = ({{Kf}})({{ms/M/kg}}) = {{Kf*ms/M/kg}}\,\mathrm{K}$ below the pure solvent

problems.prompt: A solution contains ${{cmM}}\,\mathrm{mmol/L}$ of a non-dissociating solute at $T = {{T}}\,\mathrm{K}$.

parts.label: Pi
parts.explain: $\Pi = cRT$ with $c$ in mol/m³ ($1\,\mathrm{mmol/L} = 1\,\mathrm{mol/m^3}$): $({{cmM}})(8.314)({{T}}) = {{cmM*R*T}}\,\mathrm{Pa} = {{cmM*R*T/1e5}}\,\mathrm{bar}$

problems.prompt: A fully dissociated salt gives ${{zm}}$ cation(s) of charge $+{{zp}}$ and ${{zp}}$ anion(s) of charge $-{{zm}}$ per formula unit. Its molality is $m = {{m}}\,\mathrm{mol/kg}$.

parts.label: Is
parts.explain: $I = \tfrac12\sum m_i z_i^2 = \tfrac12\left[({{zm*m}})({{zp}})^2 + ({{zp*m}})({{zm}})^2\right] = {{0.5*(zm*m*zp^2 + zp*m*zm^2)}}\,\mathrm{mol/kg}$. Each ion's molality is its count times $m$

problems.prompt: An electrolyte with ion charges $+{{zp}}$ and $-{{zm}}$ is in water at $298\,\mathrm{K}$ at ionic strength $I = {{Is}}\,\mathrm{mol/kg}$. Use $A = 0.509$.

parts.label: g
parts.explain: $\gamma_\pm = 10^{ {{-0.509*zp*zm*sqrt(Is)}} } = {{10^(-0.509*zp*zm*sqrt(Is))}}$. Always below 1 in this limit, and lower for higher charges

problems.prompt: A galvanic cell has a cathode half-reaction with $E^\circ = {{Ec}}\,\mathrm{V}$ and an anode half-reaction with $E^\circ = {{Ea}}\,\mathrm{V}$ (both written as reductions). The cell reaction transfers $n = {{n}}$ electrons.

parts.label: Ecell
parts.explain: $E^\circ_\mathrm{cell} = E^\circ_\mathrm{cathode} - E^\circ_\mathrm{anode} = {{Ec}} - ({{Ea}}) = {{Ec - Ea}}\,\mathrm{V}$. Never multiply a potential by a stoichiometric coefficient

parts.label: dG
parts.explain: $\Delta G^\circ = -nFE^\circ = -({{n}})(96\,485)({{Ec - Ea}}) = {{-n*F*(Ec - Ea)}}\,\mathrm{J/mol}$. Positive $E^\circ$, negative $\Delta G^\circ$: spontaneous

problems.prompt: A cell has $E^\circ = {{E0}}\,\mathrm{V}$ and transfers $n = {{n}}$ electrons. At $298.15\,\mathrm{K}$ the reaction quotient is $Q = {{Q}}$.

parts.label: Ecell
parts.explain: $E = E^\circ - \frac{RT}{nF}\ln Q = {{E0}} - \frac{0.02569}{ {{n}} }\ln({{Q}}) = {{E0 - R*T/(n*F)*log(Q)}}\,\mathrm{V}$. $Q < 1$ (reactant-rich) pushes $E$ above $E^\circ$

problems.prompt: A project costs {{I}} dollars now and returns {{A}} dollars a year for {{n}} years, plus a {{S}} dollar salvage value at the end. At {{pi}}% interest, what is its net present value (dollars)?

parts.label: y
parts.explain: NPV = −I + A·(P/A, i, n) + S(1 + i)⁻ⁿ, with the annuity factor (P/A) = [1 − (1 + i)⁻ⁿ]/i. Accept projects with NPV > 0 at the company's minimum rate

problems.prompt: An investment of {{I}} dollars returns {{ft}} dollars in successive years. What is the simple payback period (years)?

parts.label: y
parts.explain: Add the yearly cash flows until they cover the investment, interpolating within the final year. Payback ignores the time value of money and everything after the payback year

problems.prompt: Equipment of capacity {{S1}} cost {{C1}} dollars when the cost index was {{I1}}. Estimate a {{S2}}-capacity unit now (index {{I2}}) with a scaling exponent of {{n}}.

parts.label: y
parts.explain: Capacity: C₂ = C₁(S₂/S₁)ⁿ with n ≈ 0.6 (the six-tenths rule), reflecting economies of scale. Time: multiply by the ratio of cost indices (CEPCI) between the two dates

expect.y: scaled_cost(C1, S1, S2, n, I1, I2)

problems.prompt: Equipment costs {{P}} dollars, has a {{n}}-year life and a salvage value of {{S}} dollars. What is its book value after {{k}} years of {{kw}} depreciation (dollars)?

parts.label: y
parts.explain: Straight line takes (P − S)/n each year. Double-declining balance takes 2/n of the current book value each year (salvage ignored until the book value reaches it): faster write-off, earlier tax savings

problems.prompt: A loan charges a nominal {{pr}}% a year compounded {{m}} times a year. What is the effective annual rate (as a fraction)?

parts.label: y
parts.explain: $i_{eff} = (1 + r/m)^m - 1$; continuous compounding gives e^r − 1. Compare loans by effective rates, never nominal ones

problems.prompt: A fuel gas is {{mix}} (fuel basis). Lower flammable limits in air: {{lt}}. What is the mixture's LFL (vol % fuel in air)?

parts.label: y
parts.explain: Le Chatelier: $LFL_{mix} = 1/\sum (y_i/LFL_i)$, with yᵢ fractions of the fuel only. Keep a vessel below about 25% of the LFL (or inert it) to stay safe

cases.names: acetone 100 (TLV 500), MEK 150 (TLV 400)... with ethyl acetate 50 ppm (TLV 200)
chemical A 2 ppm (TLV 5), chemical B 0.5 ppm (TLV 1)

problems.prompt: Workers breathe {{names}}, all acting on the same organ. Is the combined exposure within the limit?

parts.label: y
parts.explain: For additive effects, sum Cᵢ/TLVᵢ: the mixture exceeds its limit if the sum is above 1, even when each component alone is below its own TLV
