los.do: Use the gradient to find the direction and rate of steepest ascent and the tangent plane to a level surface.
los.ek: Max rate |∇f| in direction ∇f; ∇F ⊥ the level surface F = k, so it is the plane's normal.

los.do: Find and classify the critical points of f(x, y) with the second derivatives test.
los.ek: ∇f = 0; D = f_xx f_yy − f_xy²: D > 0, f_xx > 0 min; D > 0, f_xx < 0 max; D < 0 saddle; D = 0 inconclusive.

los.do: Find absolute extrema of f on a closed bounded region by checking interior critical points and the boundary.
los.ek: Parametrise each boundary piece and reduce to one-variable problems; compare all candidates (EVT in 2-D).

los.do: Optimise f subject to a constraint g = k with Lagrange multipliers, and interpret λ.
los.ek: ∇f = λ∇g and g = k; λ = rate of change of the optimum with respect to k.

los.do: Evaluate a double integral over a rectangle as an iterated integral, in either order.
los.ek: Fubini: ∬_R f dA = ∫_a^b∫_c^d f dy dx = ∫_c^d∫_a^b f dx dy for continuous f; a double Riemann-sum limit.

los.do: Set up a double integral over a region bounded by curves as type I or type II, and evaluate it.
los.ek: Type I: x from a to b, y from g₁(x) to g₂(x). Inner limits may depend on the outer variable, never the reverse.

los.do: Reverse the order of integration by redrawing the region.
los.ek: Sketch the region, then read the new limits from the other direction; used when the inner integral has no elementary antiderivative.

los.do: Convert a double integral over a disc, annulus or polar region to polar coordinates and evaluate it.
los.ek: dA = r dr dθ — don't drop the r.

los.do: Compute the mass, centre of mass and moments of inertia of a lamina, and the average value of f over a region.
los.ek: m = ∬ρ dA; x̄ = ∬xρ dA/m; I_x = ∬y²ρ dA; f_avg = ∬f dA/area.

los.do: Set up and evaluate a triple integral over a solid bounded by surfaces, and use it for volume or mass.
los.ek: Project the solid onto a coordinate plane for the outer two limits; the inner limits are the bottom and top surfaces.

los.do: Evaluate a triple integral in cylindrical coordinates for solids with an axis of symmetry.
los.ek: x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ, z = z; dV = r dz dr dθ.

los.do: Evaluate a triple integral in spherical coordinates for balls, cones and shells.
los.ek: x = ρ sin φ cos θ, y = ρ sin φ sin θ, z = ρ cos φ; dV = ρ² sin φ dρ dφ dθ.

topics.title: Change of variables and the Jacobian

los.do: Change variables in a double or triple integral with the Jacobian determinant.
los.ek: dx dy = |∂(x, y)/∂(u, v)| du dv; polar, cylindrical and spherical factors are special cases.

los.do: Sketch or read a 2-D vector field and recognise a gradient field.
los.ek: F(x, y) = ⟨P, Q⟩ assigns an arrow to each point; F = ∇f is a gradient (conservative) field with potential f.

los.do: Evaluate a scalar line integral ∫_C f ds along a parametrised curve.
los.ek: ds = |r′(t)|dt; independent of orientation.

los.do: Evaluate the work or circulation ∫_C F·dr along a curve.
los.ek: ∫F(r(t))·r′(t)dt = ∫P dx + Q dy + R dz; reversing the orientation flips the sign.

topics.title: The fundamental theorem for line integrals

los.do: Test whether a 2-D field P i + Q j (or a differential P dx + Q dy) is conservative.
los.ek: On a simply connected region, conservative ⇔ ∂P/∂y = ∂Q/∂x — the same test as an exact differential.

los.do: Find a potential function and evaluate a line integral of a conservative field from endpoint values.
los.ek: f_x = P: integrate in x, differentiate in y, match Q; ∫_C ∇f·dr = f(end) − f(start), path-independent, 0 around a closed loop.

los.do: Convert a line integral around a closed plane curve into a double integral with Green's theorem, or the reverse (including areas).
los.ek: ∮_C P dx + Q dy = ∬_D (Q_x − P_y)dA, C positively oriented (region on the left); area = ½∮x dy − y dx.

los.do: Compute the divergence, curl and Laplacian of a vector or scalar field.
los.ek: div F = ∇·F; curl F = ∇ × F; ∇²f = ∇·∇f; curl ∇f = 0 and div curl F = 0.

los.do: Interpret divergence as net outflow per volume and curl as local rotation, and use curl F = 0 to test a 3-D field for being conservative.
los.ek: div > 0 is a source; curl F = 0 on a simply connected domain ⇒ F = ∇f.

los.do: Parametrise a surface (graph, cylinder, sphere, cone) and compute its area.
los.ek: r(u, v); dS = |r_u × r_v| du dv; for z = g(x, y), dS = √(1 + g_x² + g_y²)dA.

los.do: Evaluate a surface integral ∬_S f dS of a scalar function.
los.ek: ∬f(r(u, v))|r_u × r_v| du dv.

los.do: Compute the flux ∬_S F·n dS of a vector field through an oriented surface.
los.ek: ∬F·(r_u × r_v) du dv, with r_u × r_v pointing the chosen way (outward for closed surfaces).

los.do: Use Stokes' theorem to trade a circulation around a closed curve for the flux of the curl through a surface it bounds, or the reverse.
los.ek: ∮_C F·dr = ∬_S (∇ × F)·n dS; orientation of C and n by the right-hand rule; any surface with the same boundary gives the same answer.

los.do: Use the divergence theorem to compute the outward flux through a closed surface as a volume integral, or the reverse.
los.ek: ∯_S F·n dS = ∭_E ∇·F dV, n outward.

los.do: Turn an integral balance on an arbitrary control volume into a differential conservation law with the divergence theorem.
los.ek: d/dt∭c dV = −∯N·n dS + ∭R dV for every volume ⇒ ∂c/∂t + ∇·N = R.

los.do: Recognise sinh, cosh and tanh from their exponential definitions and evaluate them at ln a.
los.ek: cosh x = ½(eˣ + e⁻ˣ), sinh x = ½(eˣ − e⁻ˣ); eˣ = cosh x + sinh x.

los.do: Use cosh² − sinh² = 1 and the double-argument identities, and tell a true hyperbolic identity from a false one.
los.ek: Osborn's rule: flip the sign of any product of two sines.

los.do: Describe the graphs: parity, range and behaviour for small and large x.
los.ek: cosh ≥ 1 and even; sinh odd and unbounded; tanh odd and between −1 and 1.

los.do: Differentiate and integrate hyperbolic functions.
los.ek: sinh′ = cosh, cosh′ = sinh, tanh′ = sech²; no sign changes.

los.do: Solve y″ = k²y with cosh and sinh, connect them to the circular functions, and say where each turns up.
los.ek: cos(ix) = cosh x; catenary, fins and slabs use cosh; saturating ratios use tanh.

los.do: Write an inverse hyperbolic function as a logarithm.
los.ek: sinh⁻¹ s = ln(s + √(s² + 1)).

units.title: Calculus in business, the sciences and probability

los.do: Find a marginal cost or revenue as a derivative.
los.ek: Marginal cost C′(q) approximates the cost of one more unit.

los.do: Maximise profit from revenue and cost functions.
los.ek: Profit is maximal where marginal revenue equals marginal cost.

los.do: Optimise a model from the natural sciences.
los.ek: Set the derivative to zero and check that the critical point is a maximum.

los.do: Compute a price elasticity of demand.
los.ek: E = −(dq/dp)(p/q); |E| > 1 is elastic.

los.do: Find a consumer surplus.
los.ek: CS = ∫₀^q₀ (demand price − market price) dq.

los.do: Find cardiac output from a dye-dilution curve.
los.ek: F = amount injected / ∫ c dt.

los.do: Use a probability density function.
los.ek: A density integrates to 1; probabilities are areas under it.

los.do: Integrate a product of powers of sine and cosine.
los.ek: With an odd power, save one factor and convert the rest; with even powers, use half-angle identities.

los.do: Evaluate an integral by trigonometric substitution.
los.ek: √(a² − x²): x = a sin θ; √(a² + x²): x = a tan θ; √(x² − a²): x = a sec θ.

los.do: Use an integral from a table.
los.ek: Match the integrand to the table form, identify the constants, then substitute.

los.do: Use and check a computer algebra system's antiderivative.
los.ek: Differentiate the CAS answer to check it, then apply the fundamental theorem.

los.do: Find a volume by cylindrical shells.
los.ek: V = ∫ 2π (radius)(height) dx.

los.do: Find the same volume by two methods.
los.ek: Discs or washers in one variable and shells in the other must agree.

los.do: Find the area of a surface of revolution.
los.ek: S = ∫ 2π y √(1 + y′²) dx.

los.do: Find the hydrostatic force on a submerged plate by integration.
los.ek: F = ∫ ρ g (depth) (width at that depth) d(depth).

units.title: Sequences, series strategy, parametric and polar curves

los.do: Find the limit of a sequence.
los.ek: Divide by the highest power of n.

los.do: Apply the root test.

Convert a frequency to a period.
los.ek: A peak at frequency index k in N samples has period N/k samples.

los.do: Choose a method of proof and state what it assumes and what it must reach.
los.ek: Direct: assume p, reach q. Contrapositive: assume not q, reach not p. Contradiction: assume p and not q, reach an impossibility. Induction: base case plus the step from k to k + 1.

los.do: Evaluate a compound proposition and count the cases in which it is true.
los.ek: A proposition in n variables has 2^n rows. p → q is false only when p is true and q is false; it is equivalent to (not p) or q.

los.do: Negate a quantified statement and say what a counterexample must be.
los.ek: Negation swaps 'for all' and 'there exists' and negates the inside. A universal claim falls to one counterexample; an existential claim needs one witness.

los.do: Apply a definition exactly as written to decide whether an object qualifies.
los.ek: A definition is a test. n is even if n = 2k for some integer k; a divides b if b = ak for some integer k; a number is rational if it is a quotient of integers with non-zero denominator. Edge cases (0, 1, negatives) are settled by the wording, not by intuition.

los.do: Carry out the algebra a direct proof turns on.
los.ek: A direct proof unpacks the hypothesis with the definition, computes, and repacks the result in the form the conclusion's definition demands: to show a product is odd, exhibit it as 2(something) + 1.

los.do: State the contrapositive of a claim and recognise the contradiction a proof reaches.
los.ek: The contrapositive of 'if P then Q' is 'if not Q then not P' and is equivalent to it. A proof by contradiction assumes P and not Q together and derives something impossible.

los.do: Split a claim into cases and check them all.
los.ek: A proof by cases must cover every possibility. Working modulo m reduces a claim about all integers to m cases: squares are 0 or 1 modulo 4, and 0, 1 or 4 modulo 8.

los.do: Prove existence with a witness and say what uniqueness requires.
los.ek: An existence claim needs one example. Uniqueness needs an argument that any two objects with the property are equal. 'There is exactly one' needs both.

los.do: Lay out an induction: base cases, hypothesis and step, including strong induction.
los.ek: Ordinary induction proves P(1) and that P(k) implies P(k + 1). Strong induction may use every earlier case, and needs as many base cases as the step reaches back.

los.do: Use a closed form established by induction and identify the inductive step.
los.ek: 1 + 2 + … + n = n(n + 1)/2; the first n odd numbers sum to n²; 1² + … + n² = n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6. The step adds the (k + 1)th term to the assumed formula for k.

los.do: Iterate a linear recurrence and solve it from its characteristic roots.
los.ek: f(n) = a f(n−1) + b f(n−2) has solutions rⁿ for the roots of r² = ar + b; distinct roots give f(n) = A r₁ⁿ + B r₂ⁿ with A and B fixed by the first two values.

los.do: Count unions, power sets and Cartesian products of finite sets.
los.ek: |A ∪ B| = |A| + |B| − |A ∩ B|; a set with n elements has 2^n subsets; |A × B| = |A||B|.

los.do: Count functions, injections and surjections between finite sets.
los.ek: From an n-set to a k-set there are k^n functions, k(k−1)…(k−n+1) injections, and the surjections are counted by inclusion-exclusion: Σ (−1)^j C(k, j)(k − j)^n.

los.do: Decide whether a set is countable and say what Cantor's diagonal argument shows.
los.ek: A set is countable if it can be listed. The integers, the rationals and any countable union of countable sets are countable; the reals and the power set of the naturals are not, and no set maps onto its own power set.

los.do: Test a relation for reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity, and count equivalence relations.
los.ek: An equivalence relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive and is the same thing as a partition into classes; a 3-set has 5 and a 4-set has 15.

los.do: Count arrangements with repeated letters and selections under a constraint.
los.ek: n objects with repeats of sizes a, b, … have n!/(a! b! …) arrangements. 'At least one' is counted through the complement.

los.do: Count distributions of identical objects by stars and bars.
los.ek: x₁ + … + x_k = n has C(n + k − 1, k − 1) solutions in non-negative integers and C(n − 1, k − 1) in positive integers.

los.do: Use the binomial theorem to read off a coefficient or a sum.
los.ek: (a + b)^n = Σ C(n, k) a^k b^(n−k). Setting a = b = 1 gives Σ C(n, k) = 2^n; a = −1 gives the alternating sum 0.

los.do: Count with inclusion-exclusion, including derangements.
los.ek: |A ∪ B ∪ C| = Σ|A| − Σ|A ∩ B| + |A ∩ B ∩ C|. Derangements: n! Σ (−1)^k / k!, close to n!/e.

los.do: Apply the pigeonhole principle to find a guaranteed minimum.
los.ek: If more than kn objects go into n boxes, some box holds more than k. To force k + 1 in one box you need kn + 1 objects.

los.do: Extract a coefficient from a product of geometric series.
los.ek: 1/(1 − x)^k = Σ C(n + k − 1, k − 1) x^n: the coefficient of x^n counts selections of n objects from k types with repetition.

los.do: Model a selection problem with a generating function and read off the count.
los.ek: A coin of value c contributes the factor 1/(1 − x^c); the number of ways to make n is the coefficient of x^n in the product.

los.do: Use the handshake lemma on a degree sequence.
los.ek: The degrees sum to twice the number of edges, so the number of odd-degree vertices is even.

los.do: Count the edges of a tree or forest and the spanning trees of a small graph.
los.ek: A tree on n vertices has n − 1 edges; a forest with c components has n − c. A cycle C_n has n spanning trees and the complete graph K_n has n^(n−2).

los.do: Decide whether a graph has an Euler circuit or trail from its degrees.
los.ek: A connected graph has an Euler circuit exactly when every degree is even, and an Euler trail exactly when two vertices have odd degree.

los.do: Recognise Hamilton cycles, matchings and the first Ramsey number.
los.ek: A Hamilton cycle visits every vertex once; Dirac: minimum degree at least n/2 guarantees one. Hall: a bipartite graph has a matching covering X exactly when every set S in X has at least |S| neighbours. R(3, 3) = 6.

los.do: Find a chromatic number and count proper colourings.
los.ek: χ(G) is the fewest colours with adjacent vertices different. A tree on n vertices has k(k − 1)^(n−1) colourings; the cycle C_n has (k − 1)^n + (−1)^n (k − 1); an odd cycle needs 3 colours.

los.do: Apply Euler's formula and the edge bound for planar graphs.
los.ek: A connected plane graph has V − E + F = 2. A simple planar graph with V ≥ 3 has E ≤ 3V − 6, and E ≤ 2V − 4 if it has no triangles; so K₅ and K₃,₃ are not planar.

los.do: Decide independence by counting: rank, the number of vectors and the dimension of the space.
los.ek: More than n vectors in Rⁿ are always dependent; n vectors in Rⁿ are independent exactly when the matrix they form has nonzero determinant (rank n).

los.do: Solve a linear system by row reduction.
los.ek: Pivots give the basic variables; a row 0 = c means no solution.

los.do: Decide whether a set of vectors is linearly independent.
los.ek: Independent exactly when the only solution of Ax = 0 is zero.

los.do: Read the number of solutions off an echelon form.
los.ek: A pivot in every variable column: one; a free variable: infinitely many; a row 0 = c: none.

los.do: Count the free variables of a consistent system.
los.ek: Free variables are the non-pivot columns.

los.do: Describe a span geometrically and find its dimension.
los.ek: The span of vectors in R³ is a point, a line, a plane or all of R³, as its dimension (the rank) is 0, 1, 2 or 3.

los.do: Decide whether a vector is in the span of others.
los.ek: b is in the span exactly when [v1 … vk | b] has no pivot in the last column.
los.std: cupm-2015-la:1, lay-5e:1, webwork-opl:LA1.5, webwork-opl:LA4.2, webwork-opl:LA4.3, cupm-2023-la:E3

los.do: Describe the solution set of Ax = b as a shifted null space.
los.ek: Every solution is a particular solution plus a solution of Ax = 0.

los.do: Find the inverse of a 2 × 2 matrix.
los.ek: Swap the diagonal, negate the off-diagonal, divide by the determinant.

los.do: Solve Ax = b with a known inverse.
los.ek: x = A⁻¹b; row i of A⁻¹ dotted with b gives x_i.

los.do: Use the invertible matrix theorem.
los.ek: For a square matrix, invertible, n pivots, independent columns, det ≠ 0 and 0 not an eigenvalue stand or fall together.

los.do: Compute one entry of a product without computing the rest.
los.ek: (AB)_ij is row i of A dotted with column j of B.

los.do: Track sizes through products and transposes.
los.ek: (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ; an m × n times an n × p is m × p.

los.do: Factor a matrix as LU.
los.ek: The multipliers of row reduction go below the diagonal of L; U is the echelon form.

los.do: Solve with LU by forward and back substitution.
los.ek: Ly = b, then Ux = y.

los.do: Compute a 3 × 3 determinant.
los.ek: Expand along the row or column with the most zeros.

los.do: Use det(AB) = det A det B, det Aᵀ = det A and det(kA) = kⁿ det A.
los.ek: A scalar multiplies every row, so it comes out to the nth power.

los.do: Track the determinant through row operations.
los.ek: Swap: sign flips; scale a row: scales; add a multiple of a row: no change.

los.do: Read |det A| as the factor by which A scales area or volume.
los.ek: Area of the image = |det A| × area.

los.do: Find the rank of a matrix and use the rank theorem.
los.ek: rank + dim Nul = number of columns.

los.do: Decide whether a set is a subspace.
los.ek: Contains 0, closed under addition and scaling.

los.do: Find the dimension of a span.
los.ek: Dimension = the number of independent vectors = rank.

los.do: Find the coordinates of a vector in a basis.
los.ek: Solve P_B [x]_B = x.

los.do: Convert coordinates back to the standard basis.
los.ek: x = P_B [x]_B, with the basis vectors as columns.

los.do: Find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a 2 × 2 matrix.
los.ek: Sum of eigenvalues = trace, product = determinant.

los.do: Decide whether a matrix is diagonalisable and use the diagonal form.
los.ek: n independent eigenvectors; powers act on the eigenvalues.
los.std: lacsg-2:F3, lay-5e:5, webwork-opl:LA3.1, webwork-opl:LA7.2, cupm-2023-la:E8, cupm-2023-la:E9

los.do: Compute Aᵏx by expanding x in eigenvectors.
los.ek: Each eigenvector component is multiplied by λᵏ.

los.do: Find the steady state of a Markov chain.
los.ek: The eigenvector for λ = 1, scaled to sum to 1.

los.do: Read a complex eigenvalue as a rotation and a scaling.
los.ek: [[a, −b], [b, a]] rotates by arg λ and scales by |λ| = √(a² + b²).

los.do: Fit a least-squares line with the normal equations and read its residuals.
los.ek: Solve AᵀA c = Aᵀy for c = (b, m); the residual vector is orthogonal to every column of A, so its entries sum to zero when an intercept is fitted.

los.do: Test orthogonality, project one vector on another and take a Gram–Schmidt step.
los.ek: proj = (u·v / v·v) v.
los.std: lay-5e:6, webwork-opl:LA8.1, webwork-opl:LA8.3, webwork-opl:LA8.4, webwork-opl:LA8.5, cupm-2023-la:E10, cupm-2023-la:O2

los.do: Set up and solve a least-squares problem.
los.ek: AᵀAx = Aᵀb.

los.do: Find lengths and distances.
Find vectors in an orthogonal complement.
los.ek: W⊥ is everything orthogonal to a spanning set of W.

los.do: Find an entry of the QR factorisation.
los.ek: r_ii = length after removing earlier directions; r_ij = q_i · a_j.

los.do: Find a singular value of a small matrix.
los.ek: Singular values are the square roots of the eigenvalues of AᵀA.

los.do: Use orthogonality of a symmetric matrix's eigenvectors.
los.ek: Different eigenvalues, orthogonal eigenvectors.

los.do: Classify a quadratic form.
los.ek: The signs of the eigenvalues of its symmetric matrix decide.

los.do: Find the extreme values of a quadratic form on the unit sphere.
los.ek: The largest and smallest eigenvalues, at their eigenvectors.

los.do: Find the error of the best low-rank approximation from the singular values.
los.ek: Eckart–Young: the best rank-k approximation drops σ_(k+1), …; its 2-norm error is σ_(k+1), its Frobenius error √(σ_(k+1)² + …).

los.do: Use the pseudo-inverse to get the least-squares solution of a full-column-rank system.
los.ek: A⁺ = (AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀ when the columns are independent; x = A⁺b solves the normal equations; A⁺ inverts each nonzero singular value.

los.do: Find the condition number from the singular values.
los.ek: κ = σ_max / σ_min.

topics.title: The matrix of a linear map

los.do: Build a map from the images of the basis vectors.
los.ek: The columns of the standard matrix are T(e1), …, T(en).
los.std: lacsg-2:F1, cupm-2015-la:4, lay-5e:1, webwork-opl:LA9.1, webwork-opl:LA9.2, cupm-2023-la:E6

los.do: Compose linear maps as matrix products.
los.ek: S ∘ T has matrix ST: the first map stands on the right.
los.std: lacsg-2:F2, lacsg-2:F1, cupm-2015-la:4, lay-5e:2, webwork-opl:LA9.3, cupm-2023-la:E6, cupm-2023-la:E4

los.do: Decide whether a map is one-to-one or onto from its rank.
los.ek: One-to-one: rank = number of columns; onto: rank = number of rows.

los.do: Find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a linear operator on a function space.
los.ek: Apply the operator to a basis (monomials, exponentials): T(p) = λp makes p an eigenvector; the matrix of D on polynomials is nilpotent, so its only eigenvalue is 0.

los.do: Find the dimensions of the kernel and range of a map on a function space.
los.ek: Rank–nullity holds for any linear map on a finite-dimensional space.
los.std: cupm-2015-la:4, lay-5e:4, webwork-opl:LA6.6, webwork-opl:LA9.5, cupm-2023-la:E6, cupm-2023-la:E7

los.do: Write the matrix of a map relative to a basis.
los.ek: Columns are the coordinates of T(b1), …, T(bn).
los.std: lacsg-2:F1, cupm-2015-la:4, lay-5e:4, webwork-opl:LA6.7, webwork-opl:LA9.3, cupm-2023-la:E6, cupm-2023-la:E9

units.title: Abstract vector spaces and special matrices

los.do: Decide whether a set with its operations is a vector space.
los.ek: Check the zero vector, closure under addition and under scaling; the rest of the axioms usually come free.

los.do: Write a polynomial as a combination of other polynomials.
los.ek: Match coefficients of each power and solve the linear system.

los.do: Decide whether a polynomial lies in the span of others.
los.ek: In the span exactly when the coefficient system is consistent.

los.do: Decide when polynomials are linearly dependent.
los.ek: Dependent exactly when the matrix of their coefficient vectors is singular.

los.do: Find the dimension of a standard space of matrices or polynomials.
los.ek: Count the free entries: symmetric n(n+1)/2, skew n(n−1)/2, trace zero n² − 1, P_n has n + 1.

los.do: Compute an inner product of functions.
los.ek: ⟨f, g⟩ = ∫ f g dx is an inner product on continuous functions.

los.do: Balance a chemical equation from the null space of its composition matrix.
los.ek: Each element gives one equation; the coefficients span the null space.

los.do: Invert an elementary matrix.
los.ek: The inverse undoes the row operation: add −k instead of k, divide instead of multiply, swap back.

los.do: Compute with complex matrix entries.
los.ek: Arithmetic is ordinary arithmetic with i² = −1; conjugates pair up into real numbers.

los.do: Compute a power of a Jordan block.
Use the properties of an orthogonal matrix.
los.ek: Qᵀ Q = I, so Q⁻¹ = Qᵀ and lengths and angles are preserved.

los.do: Invert a linear transformation.
los.ek: T is invertible exactly when its matrix is; T⁻¹ has the inverse matrix.

los.do: Evaluate an integral by u-substitution, choosing u so its derivative appears in the integrand.
los.ek: ∫f(g(x))g′(x)dx = ∫f(u)du; a missing constant factor is fine, a missing x is not.

los.do: Evaluate an integral by parts, including tabular and cyclic (e^ax·trig) cases.
los.ek: ∫u dv = uv − ∫v du; LIATE picks u; cyclic integrals return to themselves and are solved algebraically.

los.do: Decompose a rational function into partial fractions (distinct, repeated, irreducible quadratic, improper) and integrate it.
los.ek: Divide first if improper; repeated factor (x−a)^k needs k terms; irreducible quadratic gets (Ax+B).

los.do: Convert complex numbers between rectangular, polar and exponential form.
los.ek: e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ; z = re^(iθ), r = |z|, θ = arg z.
los.std: webwork-opl:CX1.1, webwork-opl:CX1.2, webwork-opl:CX1.3, webwork-opl:CX1.4, webwork-opl:CX1.5, webwork-opl:CX1.6, webwork-opl:CX1.7, webwork-opl:CX1.8

los.do: Compute powers and roots of a complex number with De Moivre's formula.
los.ek: (re^(iθ))^n = r^n e^(inθ); n distinct n-th roots spaced 2π/n apart.

los.do: Find the complex roots α ± βi of a real quadratic.
los.ek: Complex roots of real polynomials come in conjugate pairs; α = −b/2a, β = √(4ac − b²)/2a.

los.do: Shift a summation index so two power series start at the same index and carry the same power of x.
los.ek: Replace m by m ± k and adjust the limits; the sum is unchanged.

los.do: Compute first and mixed partial derivatives of a function of two variables.
los.ek: Hold the other variable constant; for smooth functions u_xy = u_yx.

los.do: Find dy/dx for a curve defined implicitly by F(x, y) = c.
los.ek: dy/dx = −F_x / F_y.

los.do: Test whether M dx + N dy is an exact differential.
los.ek: Exact on a simply connected domain ⇔ ∂M/∂y = ∂N/∂x.

topics.title: Basic concepts, direction fields and Euler's method

los.do: Classify an ODE by order and linearity, and verify that a given function solves it.
los.ek: Order = highest derivative; linear ⇔ y and its derivatives appear to first power with coefficients in x only.

los.do: Sketch a direction field and solution curves from isoclines of y′ = f(x, y).
los.ek: Isocline f(x, y) = k has slope k everywhere; solution curves are tangent to the field.

los.do: Approximate an IVP solution with a few steps of Euler's method and estimate the error trend.
los.ek: y_(n+1) = y_n + h f(x_n, y_n); global error is O(h).

los.do: Solve a separable ODE explicitly where possible, including the IVP constant.
los.ek: g(y)dy = f(x)dx, integrate both sides; check for lost equilibrium solutions when dividing by g.

los.do: Reduce an ODE to separable form with u = y/x or u = ax + by + c, and solve it.
los.ek: y′ = f(y/x): y = ux ⇒ u + xu′ = f(u); y′ = f(ax + by + c): u′ = a + bf(u).

los.do: Solve an exact ODE by finding the potential u(x, y) = c, and fit an IVP.
los.ek: u_x = M, u_y = N; integrate one, differentiate, match the other.

los.do: Decide whether an integrating factor depending only on x or only on y exists.
los.ek: R = (M_y − N_x)/N a function of x alone ⇒ F(x) = exp∫R dx; R* = (N_x − M_y)/M of y alone ⇒ F(y).

los.do: Find the integrating factor and solve the resulting exact equation.
los.ek: Multiply by F, re-check exactness, then solve as exact.

los.do: Solve a first-order linear ODE whose forcing switches on or off at a given time.
los.ek: Solve on each interval and carry y across the switch: the solution is continuous even where the forcing jumps.

los.do: Solve a linear first-order ODE with an integrating factor, including IVPs and forcing that matches e^(−∫p).
los.ek: y′ + py = r ⇒ y = e^(−h)[∫e^h r dx + c], h = ∫p dx.

los.do: Solve a linear ODE whose integrating-factor integral needs integration by parts.
los.ek: ∫e^h r dx often pairs a polynomial or trig with an exponential.

los.do: Reduce a Bernoulli equation to a linear one with u = y^(1−a) and solve it.
los.ek: y′ + py = g y^a ⇒ u′ + (1−a)p u = (1−a)g.

los.do: Identify which first-order method (separable, substitution, linear, Bernoulli, exact) solves a given ODE.
los.ek: Check in order: separable? linear in y? y^a term? exact? homogeneous in y/x?

los.do: Model a mixing tank whose volume changes because inflow and outflow differ.
los.ek: V(t) = V₀ + (q_in − q_out)t; x′ = c_in q_in − q_out x/V(t) is linear with a variable coefficient.

los.do: Set up and solve a mixing-tank balance for concentration or mass of solute.
los.ek: dm/dt = (rate in) − (rate out), rate out = (m/V)·Q_out.

los.do: Model Newton's cooling and first-order decay, and extract a time constant, half-life or time to reach a value.
los.ek: dT/dt = −k(T − T_a); y = y_0 e^(−kt), t_1/2 = ln 2/k.

los.do: Solve the logistic equation and find its equilibria and carrying capacity.
los.ek: y′ = ky(1 − y/K) is separable and Bernoulli; y → K for y_0 > 0.

los.do: Find and classify the equilibria of an autonomous ODE y′ = f(y) from a phase line.
los.ek: f(y*) = 0; stable if f′(y*) < 0.

los.do: Decide whether an IVP has a unique solution near the initial point from the continuity of f and ∂f/∂y.
los.ek: f and f_y continuous on a rectangle around (x_0, y_0) ⇒ unique solution on some |x − x_0| < α.

topics.title: Homogeneous theory, reduction of order and the Wronskian

los.do: Use superposition to build a general solution from a basis and fit it to an IVP.
los.ek: For a linear homogeneous ODE, any combination c_1y_1 + c_2y_2 of solutions is a solution; two independent ones form a basis.

los.do: Find a second solution from a known one by reduction of order.
los.ek: y_2 = u y_1, u′ = U = e^(−∫p dx)/y_1² (standard form y″ + py′ + qy = 0).

los.do: Compute the Wronskian of two or three functions and use it to decide linear independence.
los.ek: W = det of the functions and their derivatives; W ≠ 0 somewhere ⇒ independent; for ODE solutions W ≡ 0 or never 0 (Abel).

los.do: Solve a second-order boundary-value problem and decide whether it has none, one or infinitely many solutions.
los.ek: Fit the general solution to the two boundary values; the system is singular exactly when the boundary points sit at zeros of the homogeneous solution.

los.do: Write the general solution of ay″ + by′ + cy = 0 for each of the three root cases of the characteristic equation.
los.ek: Distinct real: e^(λ₁x), e^(λ₂x); double: e^(λx), xe^(λx); complex α ± iβ: e^(αx)cos βx, e^(αx)sin βx.

los.do: Solve a constant-coefficient IVP.
los.ek: Two conditions y(x_0), y′(x_0) fix c_1, c_2.

los.do: Find the roots of the auxiliary equation of an Euler–Cauchy ODE.
los.ek: x²y″ + axy′ + by = 0 with y = x^m ⇒ m² + (a − 1)m + b = 0.

los.do: Write the general solution of an Euler–Cauchy ODE for each root case and fit an IVP.
los.ek: Distinct: x^(m₁), x^(m₂); double: x^m, x^m ln x; complex: x^μ cos(ν ln x), x^μ sin(ν ln x).

los.do: Find the natural frequency, period, amplitude and phase of an undamped mass–spring system.
los.ek: my″ + ky = 0 ⇒ ω₀ = √(k/m); A cos ω₀t + B sin ω₀t = C cos(ω₀t − δ), C = √(A² + B²).

los.do: Solve an undamped oscillator IVP.
los.ek: y(0) and y′(0) give A and B/ω₀.

los.do: Classify a damped oscillator as over-, critically or underdamped from c² − 4mk.
los.ek: c² > 4mk overdamped, = critical, < under; underdamped frequency ω* = √(4mk − c²)/2m.

los.do: Solve a damped oscillator IVP in each damping regime.
los.ek: Same three root cases as 3.2.A, with α = −c/2m < 0 so every solution decays.

los.do: Find a particular solution by undetermined coefficients, including the modification rule.
los.ek: Guess the form of r(x) (poly, e^(γx), cos/sin); multiply by x (or x²) when the guess solves the homogeneous ODE.

los.do: Assemble y = y_h + y_p and fit an IVP for a nonhomogeneous ODE.
los.ek: Apply initial conditions to the full solution, never to y_h alone.

los.do: Find a particular solution by variation of parameters when r(x) is not of undetermined-coefficient form or coefficients vary.
los.ek: y_p = −y₁∫y₂r/W dx + y₂∫y₁r/W dx, ODE in standard form.

los.do: Find the steady-state response of a damped oscillator to sinusoidal forcing and its amplitude.
los.ek: y_p = a cos ωt + b sin ωt; amplitude C*(ω) = F₀/√((k − mω²)² + c²ω²); the transient dies out.

los.do: Recognise undamped resonance and beats and write the resulting solution.
los.ek: ω = ω₀, c = 0 ⇒ t sin ω₀t growth; ω near ω₀ ⇒ beats with envelope frequency |ω − ω₀|/2.

los.do: Find the practical-resonance frequency of a damped forced oscillator.
los.ek: ω_max² = k/m − c²/2m², exists only if c² < 2mk.

los.do: Model an RLC circuit as a second-order ODE and map it onto the mass–spring analogy.
los.ek: LI″ + RI′ + I/C = E′(t): L ↔ m, R ↔ c, 1/C ↔ k.

los.do: Find the roots of the auxiliary equation of a third-order Euler–Cauchy ODE.
los.ek: Try y = x^m: x^m factors out of every term, leaving m(m − 1)(m − 2) + a m(m − 1) + b m + c = 0.

los.do: Test n functions for linear independence with the n×n Wronskian.
los.ek: Rows are f, f′, …, f^(n−1); expand by cofactors.

los.do: Find the roots of an n-th order characteristic polynomial.
los.ek: Rational root test, then synthetic division to a quadratic.

los.do: Write the general solution of an n-th order constant-coefficient ODE with distinct, repeated and complex roots, and fit an IVP.
los.ek: A root of multiplicity k gives e^(λx), xe^(λx), …, x^(k−1)e^(λx).

los.do: Write the form of a particular solution of a higher-order ODE, multiplying by x as often as the root repeats.
los.ek: A forcing term whose exponent matches a characteristic root of multiplicity k needs x^k times the usual trial.

los.do: Find a particular solution of an n-th order ODE by undetermined coefficients or variation of parameters.
los.ek: Same modification rule; variation of parameters uses Cramer's rule with W_k/W.

units.title: Systems of ODEs, phase plane and stability

los.do: Convert an n-th order ODE into a first-order system.
los.ek: y₁ = y, y₂ = y′, …; the companion matrix's eigenvalues are the characteristic roots.

los.do: Write the rate matrix for series first-order kinetics A → B → C.
los.ek: d[A]/dt = −k₁[A], d[B]/dt = k₁[A] − k₂[B]; C follows from mass conservation.

los.do: Find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors that give the basis solutions of y′ = Ay.
los.ek: y = x e^(λt) with (A − λI)x = 0.

los.do: Write the general solution of a 2×2 system with real distinct eigenvalues and fit an IVP.
los.ek: y = c₁x⁽¹⁾e^(λ₁t) + c₂x⁽²⁾e^(λ₂t).

los.do: Write real solutions of a 2×2 system with complex eigenvalues and fit an IVP.
los.ek: Take real and imaginary parts of x e^((α+iβ)t).

los.do: Solve a 2×2 system with a repeated eigenvalue using a generalised eigenvector.
los.ek: Second solution x t e^(λt) + u e^(λt), (A − λI)u = x.

los.do: Solve series kinetics A → B → C and find the time of maximum intermediate.
los.ek: Eigenvalues −k₁, −k₂; [B] = k₁A₀(e^(−k₁t) − e^(−k₂t))/(k₂ − k₁); t_max = ln(k₁/k₂)/(k₁ − k₂), = 1/k when k₁ = k₂.

los.do: Sketch a phase portrait with eigenvector directions and trajectory orientation.
los.ek: Trajectories leave along the fast-growing eigenvector and approach along the slow-decaying one.

los.do: Classify the critical point of a linear 2×2 system (node, saddle, centre, spiral) from its eigenvalues or from trace and determinant.
los.ek: p = tr A, q = det A, Δ = p² − 4q: q < 0 saddle; q > 0, Δ ≥ 0 node; Δ < 0 spiral (p ≠ 0) or centre (p = 0).

los.do: Decide whether a critical point is stable, asymptotically stable or unstable.
los.ek: Asymptotically stable ⇔ p < 0, q > 0; centre is stable, not asymptotically.

los.do: Find the critical points of a nonlinear autonomous system and linearise at each with the Jacobian.
los.ek: Set f = g = 0; J = [[f_x, f_y], [g_x, g_y]] at the point.

los.do: Classify each critical point of a nonlinear system from its linearisation, noting when linearisation is inconclusive.
los.ek: Hyperbolic points keep their type; a linear centre may be a spiral in the nonlinear system.

los.do: Find a particular solution of y′ = Ay + g by undetermined coefficients, diagonalisation or variation of parameters.
los.ek: Fundamental matrix Y: y_p = Y∫Y⁻¹g dt.

los.do: Classify a point as ordinary, regular singular or irregular singular.
los.ek: Standard form y″ + py′ + qy = 0: ordinary if p, q analytic; regular singular if (x − x₀)p and (x − x₀)²q are analytic.

los.do: Give the guaranteed radius of convergence of a power-series solution about an ordinary point.
los.ek: At least the distance to the nearest singular point in the complex plane.

los.do: Derive the recurrence relation for the coefficients of a power-series solution.
los.ek: Substitute Σa_m x^m, shift indices to a common power, set each coefficient to zero.

los.do: Generate the first terms of the series solution from the recurrence and initial values.
los.ek: a₀ = y(0), a₁ = y′(0); even and odd coefficients often split into two basis series.

los.do: Find the indicial equation and its roots at a regular singular point.
los.ek: r(r − 1) + b₀r + c₀ = 0, b₀ = lim xp, c₀ = lim x²q.

los.do: Decide which Frobenius case applies and what form the second solution takes.
los.ek: Roots not differing by an integer: two x^r series; double root: second has ln x; differ by an integer: second may have ln x.

los.do: Construct the first Frobenius series solution from the larger indicial root.
los.ek: y = x^r Σa_m x^m; same index-shifting as the power series method.

los.do: Recognise Legendre's, Bessel's and Euler–Cauchy equations in a given ODE and read off the order or degree.
los.ek: (1 − x²)y″ − 2xy′ + n(n+1)y = 0; x²y″ + xy′ + (x² − ν²)y = 0.

los.do: Solve a scaled Bessel equation x²y″ + xy′ + (λ²x² − ν²)y = 0 with J_ν(λx), Y_ν(λx).
los.ek: Substitute z = λx.

los.do: Write the general solution of Bessel's equation, choosing J₋ν or Y_ν as the second solution.
los.ek: J_ν, J₋ν independent unless ν is an integer, where J₋ₙ = (−1)ⁿJₙ; then use Y_ν.

los.do: Use Legendre polynomials' explicit form, Rodrigues' formula or orthogonality to evaluate P_n or an integral.
los.ek: P_n(x) = (1/2ⁿn!) dⁿ/dxⁿ (x² − 1)ⁿ; ∫P_mP_n = 0 on [−1, 1] for m ≠ n.

los.do: Find the Laplace transform of a combination of elementary functions from the table, using identities where needed.
los.ek: L{tⁿ} = n!/s^(n+1); L{e^(at)} = 1/(s − a); L{cos ωt} = s/(s² + ω²); sin² = (1 − cos 2t)/2.

los.do: Apply the first shifting theorem forwards and in reverse.
los.ek: L{e^(at)f(t)} = F(s − a); complete the square to expose s − a.

los.do: Invert a rational F(s) by partial fractions with distinct, repeated or complex poles.
los.ek: Repeated pole ⇒ tⁿe^(at)/n!; complex pole pair ⇒ e^(at)(cos, sin).

los.do: Find f(0⁺) and f(∞) from F(s) with the initial- and final-value theorems, and say when the final-value theorem fails.
los.ek: f(0⁺) = lim s→∞ sF(s); f(∞) = lim s→0 sF(s), valid only if every pole of sF(s) lies in the open left half-plane.

los.do: Solve a constant-coefficient IVP by transforming, solving the subsidiary equation and inverting.
los.ek: L{y′} = sY − y(0); L{y″} = s²Y − sy(0) − y′(0); initial conditions enter automatically.

los.do: Identify the transfer function of a linear system and relate its poles to stability and damping.
los.ek: Q(s) = Y/R with zero ICs = 1/(as² + bs + c); poles in the left half-plane ⇔ decay.

los.do: Transform a periodic function with the one-period formula.
los.ek: L{f} = ∫₀ᵀ e^(−st) f(t) dt ÷ (1 − e^(−sT)).

los.do: Write a piecewise function with unit step functions and transform it.
los.ek: f = f₁ + (f₂ − f₁)u(t − a) + …; L{f(t − a)u(t − a)} = e^(−as)F(s).

los.do: Invert a transform containing e^(−as).
los.ek: e^(−as)F(s) ↦ f(t − a)u(t − a).

los.do: Solve an IVP with switched or piecewise forcing.
los.ek: Transform the step-written forcing; the solution is piecewise with continuous y and y′.

los.do: Model a sudden impulse with δ(t − a) and solve the resulting IVP, including the impulse response.
los.ek: L{δ(t − a)} = e^(−as); impulse response = L⁻¹{transfer function}.

los.do: Compute a convolution integral directly.
los.ek: (f * g)(t) = ∫₀ᵗ f(τ)g(t − τ)dτ.

los.do: Invert a product of transforms or transform an integral using the convolution theorem.
los.ek: L{f * g} = FG; L{∫₀ᵗ f dτ} = F/s.

los.do: Solve a Volterra integral equation of convolution type.
los.ek: Transform, solve for Y algebraically, invert.

los.do: Use L{tf(t)} = −F′(s) to transform or invert functions and solve ODEs with linear coefficients.
los.ek: Differentiation in s ↔ multiplication by −t; integration in s ↔ division by t.

los.do: Solve a linear system of ODEs by Laplace transform.
los.ek: Transform each equation, solve the algebraic system (Cramer), invert each component.

los.do: Solve a linear system by row reduction and state whether it has none, one or infinitely many solutions.
los.ek: Echelon form; rank A vs rank [A|b] decides existence; free variables give a family.

los.do: Decide whether a set of vectors is linearly independent.
los.ek: Independent ⇔ only the trivial combination is zero ⇔ rank = number of vectors; for n vectors in ℝⁿ, det ≠ 0.

los.do: Evaluate a 3×3 determinant by cofactor expansion.
los.ek: Expand along the row or column with most zeros; sign pattern (−1)^(i+j).

los.do: Find the inverse of a 2×2 matrix, or show it does not exist.
los.ek: A⁻¹ = (1/det A)[[d, −b], [−c, a]]; singular ⇔ det A = 0.

los.do: Find the eigenvalues of a 2×2 matrix from its characteristic polynomial.
los.ek: λ² − (tr A)λ + det A = 0.

los.do: Find an eigenvector for each eigenvalue of a 2×2 matrix.
los.ek: Solve (A − λI)x = 0; one row suffices in 2×2.

los.do: Diagonalise a matrix with a full set of eigenvectors and use it to decouple a linear system.
los.ek: D = X⁻¹AX; symmetric A has real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenvectors.

los.do: Find the rank of a matrix and the dimension of its null space.
los.ek: Rank + nullity = number of columns.

los.do: Project one vector onto another, test orthogonality, and take one Gram–Schmidt step.
los.ek: proj_u y = (y·u / u·u) u; subtracting it leaves the part orthogonal to u.

los.do: Set up and solve a least-squares problem with the normal equations, and say what the solution means geometrically.
los.ek: AᵀA x̂ = Aᵀb; Ax̂ is the projection of b onto Col A.

los.do: Use eigenvalues to find powers and traces, know when a matrix is diagonalisable, and read a singular value.
los.ek: A^k has eigenvalues λ^k; symmetric matrices are always diagonalisable; σ = √(eigenvalue of AᵀA).

units.title: Fourier series and Sturm–Liouville boundary-value problems

los.do: Find what a Fourier series converges to at a jump, and sum a series of coefficients with Parseval's identity.
los.ek: At a jump the series gives the average of the one-sided limits; Parseval: a₀²/2 + Σ(aₙ² + bₙ²) = (1/π)∫f² over a period (period 2π, a₀ the full constant).

los.do: Compute the Fourier coefficients of a 2π-periodic function given on one period.
los.ek: a₀ = (1/2π)∫f, a_n = (1/π)∫f cos nx, b_n = (1/π)∫f sin nx over (−π, π).

los.do: Compute the Fourier series of a function of period 2L, using even/odd symmetry to skip coefficients.
los.ek: Replace nx by nπx/L and 1/π by 1/L; even ⇒ cosine series, odd ⇒ sine series.

los.do: Write the half-range sine or cosine expansion of a function on (0, L).
los.ek: Odd extension ⇒ sine series; even extension ⇒ cosine series; b_n = (2/L)∫₀ᴸ f sin(nπx/L).

los.do: Find the periodic steady-state response of an oscillator to a periodic non-sinusoidal force by Fourier series.
los.ek: Solve term by term; the term with nω nearest ω₀ dominates.

los.do: Find the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of y″ + λy = 0 with periodic boundary conditions.
los.ek: y(−L) = y(L), y′(−L) = y′(L): λ₀ = 0 with a constant, then λₙ = (nπ/L)² each with two eigenfunctions cos and sin.

los.do: Rewrite a second-order eigenvalue ODE in Sturm–Liouville form and identify p, q and r.
los.ek: (py′)′ + (q + λr)y = 0; multiply by the integrating factor e^(∫a₁/a₂)/a₂ when needed.

los.do: Classify a Sturm–Liouville problem as regular, periodic or singular.
los.ek: Regular: p > 0, r > 0 on [a, b] with separated BCs; periodic: y(a) = y(b), y′(a) = y′(b); singular: p vanishes at an end.

los.do: Find the eigenvalues of y″ + λy = 0 under Dirichlet, Neumann or mixed boundary conditions.
los.ek: Check λ < 0, = 0, > 0 separately; Dirichlet on [0, L]: λ = (nπ/L)², n ≥ 1.

los.do: Find the eigenfunction belonging to each eigenvalue.
los.ek: Determined up to a constant multiple; sin(nπx/L), cos(nπx/L) or sin((2n−1)πx/2L).

los.do: Find the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a shifted problem y″ + (λ + c)y = 0 and count its negative eigenvalues.
los.ek: Set μ = λ + c, solve as 9.2.C, then λ = μ − c.

los.do: Verify orthogonality of eigenfunctions with respect to the weight r(x).
los.ek: ∫ₐᵇ r y_m y_n dx = 0 for m ≠ n in a regular or periodic S–L problem.

los.do: Expand a function in a generalised Fourier series of S–L eigenfunctions (e.g. Legendre or Fourier–Bessel).
los.ek: a_n = ∫ r f y_n dx / ∫ r y_n² dx.

los.do: Build the Green's function of y″ = f with y(0) = y(L) = 0 and use it to solve for a given f.
los.ek: G(x, s) = x(s − L)/L for x < s and s(x − L)/L for x > s: continuous at x = s, slope jumps by 1, zero at both ends; y = ∫G f ds.

los.do: Build the Green's function of y″ + k²y = f with fixed ends from the homogeneous solutions and the jump condition.
los.ek: G = −sin(kx_<) sin(k(L − x_>))/(k sin kL); it fails to exist exactly when kL = nπ, an eigenvalue of the homogeneous problem.

los.do: Solve a forced initial-value problem by convolving the forcing with the impulse response.
los.ek: For y″ + ω²y = f, g(t) = sin(ωt)/ω; for τy′ + y = f, g(t) = e^(−t/τ)/τ; y = ∫₀ᵗ g(t − u) f(u) du from rest.

los.do: Substitute u = X(x)T(t) (or X(x)Y(y)), split into two ODEs with a separation constant, and decide the constant's sign from the boundary conditions.
los.ek: Only the sign that gives sines and cosines can meet two zero boundary conditions nontrivially.

los.do: Classify a second-order linear PDE as elliptic, parabolic or hyperbolic and verify a solution.
los.ek: Au_xx + 2Bu_xy + Cu_yy: AC − B² > 0 elliptic, = 0 parabolic, < 0 hyperbolic.

topics.title: Heat equation by separation of variables

los.do: Find the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions for Dirichlet, Neumann, mixed and convective (Robin) ends.
los.ek: Dirichlet sin(nπx/L); Neumann cos(nπx/L) with n = 0; mixed sin((2n−1)πx/2L); Robin: a transcendental condition such as λ tan λL = h.

los.do: Compute the Fourier sine or cosine coefficients of the initial condition.
los.ek: b_n = (2/L)∫ f sin(nπx/L) dx; a constant start has odd modes only, 4U/nπ.

los.do: Separate u = F(x)G(t) in the heat equation and find each mode's decay rate.
los.ek: F″ + kF = 0 (an S–L problem), G′ + c²kG = 0 ⇒ G = e^(−c²λ_n t).

los.do: Solve the heat equation on a finite rod with Dirichlet or insulated ends by Fourier series.
los.ek: Dirichlet ⇒ sine series; insulated ⇒ cosine series with a constant term (the mean).

los.do: Solve the heat equation with nonzero fixed ends by subtracting the steady state.
los.ek: u = u_s(x) + v; u_s linear; v satisfies zero BCs with v(x, 0) = f − u_s.

los.do: Find the steady state with a flux or insulated end, and handle a flux boundary in the transient problem.
los.ek: −k u'(L) = q″ fixes the slope; with insulated ends the steady state is the initial mean.

los.do: Shift a boundary value that changes in time (w = x g(t)/L) and identify the source term it leaves in the equation.
los.ek: v = u − w has zero ends and v_t = k v_xx − w_t + k w_xx.

los.do: Solve the heat equation with a source: steady state from k u_s″ = −Q, transient by expanding the source in the eigenfunctions.
los.ek: Both ends zero: u_s = Qx(L − x)/2k; each mode obeys T_n′ + λ_n T_n = q_n.

los.do: Solve the vibrating string by separation of variables and Fourier series.
los.ek: u = Σ(B_n cos λ_n t + B_n* sin λ_n t) sin(nπx/L), λ_n = cnπ/L.

los.do: Write d'Alembert's solution for an infinite string from initial displacement and velocity.
los.ek: u = ½[f(x + ct) + f(x − ct)] + (1/2c)∫ g.

los.do: Solve the steady 2-D Dirichlet problem on a rectangle by separation, one nonzero side at a time.
los.ek: The direction with two zero sides oscillates (sines); the other carries sinh or cosh; superpose one problem per nonzero side.

los.do: Separate a PDE in polar, cylindrical or spherical coordinates and identify the Bessel or Legendre equation that appears.
los.ek: Radial part in cylinders ⇒ Bessel; polar angle in spheres ⇒ Legendre in cos θ.

los.do: Solve transient conduction in a cylinder with Fourier–Bessel series, including a nonzero wall temperature by shifting.
los.ek: u = ΣA_nJ₀(α_nr/a)e^(−k(α_n/a)²t); weight r; uniform start A_n = 2U/(α_nJ₁(α_n)).

los.do: Solve transient conduction in a sphere with v = r·u, which turns it into a rod.
los.ek: v_t = kv_rr, v(0) = v(a) = 0; u = Σ B_n sin(nπr/a)e^(−k(nπ/a)²t)/r.

los.do: Write the heat kernel as the Green's function of the diffusion equation and use images for a fixed or insulated end.
los.ek: G = e^(−(x−x₀)²/4κt)/√(4πκt) on the line; on x > 0 subtract the mirror image for u(0) = 0, add it for an insulated end.

los.do: Solve a PDE on a semi-infinite or infinite domain by Laplace or Fourier transform.
los.ek: Transform out t (Laplace) or x (Fourier) to get an ODE in the other variable; bounded at infinity keeps e^(−√s x).

los.do: Solve a finite rod by Laplace transform and invert by residues: the poles are the eigenvalues.
los.ek: Residue at s = 0 is the steady state; s_n = −(nπ/L)² rebuild the Fourier series.

los.do: Choose the method for a PDE problem: separation, shift, transform or numerics.
los.ek: Finite domain with homogeneous BCs: separate. Nonzero BCs: shift first. Semi-infinite: transform. Messy geometry or data: finite differences.

los.do: Write central-difference approximations and state their truncation order.
los.ek: u_xx ≈ (u_{i+1} − 2u_i + u_{i−1})/h², O(h²); forward difference is O(h).

los.do: Take an explicit time step and check stability.
los.ek: u_i^{n+1} = u_i + r(u_{i+1} − 2u_i + u_{i−1}), stable for r = kΔt/h² ≤ ½.

los.do: Handle a flux or insulated boundary with a ghost node.
los.ek: u_{−1} = u_1 − 2h g from the central difference of u_x(0) = g.

los.do: Take an implicit or Crank–Nicolson step by solving the tridiagonal system.
los.ek: θ = 1 backward Euler, θ = ½ Crank–Nicolson; unconditionally stable; Thomas algorithm.

los.do: Represent a non-periodic function by its Fourier integral, or its cosine or sine transform.
los.ek: Limit L → ∞ of the Fourier series; even ⇒ cosine transform, odd ⇒ sine.

los.do: Compute a Fourier transform and use its derivative property to turn an ODE into algebra.
los.ek: F{f′} = iwF{f}; F{e^(−ax²)} is Gaussian.

los.do: Compute Fourier transforms of the Gaussian and the rectangular pulse.
los.ek: With f̂(w) = (1/√2π)∫f e^(−iwx)dx: e^(−ax²) → e^(−w²/4a)/√(2a); a pulse of height 1 on |x| < b → √(2/π) sin(bw)/w.

los.do: Use the shift, scaling and convolution properties of the Fourier transform.
los.ek: f(x − c) → e^(−iwc)f̂; f(bx) → f̂(w/b)/|b|; f∗g → √(2π) f̂ ĝ.

los.do: Solve the heat equation on an infinite line by Fourier transform and read the spreading Gaussian.
los.ek: A point release Q spreads as u = Q e^(−x²/4κt)/√(4πκt): the peak falls as t^(−1/2) and the variance grows as 2κt.

los.do: Convolve functions directly and through the Fourier transform: Gaussians, pulses, and an initial profile spreading by diffusion.
los.ek: Gaussian widths add in quadrature (σ² = σ₁² + σ₂²); two pulses give a triangle; u(x, t) = u₀ ∗ heat kernel, so σ² grows by 2κt.

topics.title: Random walks and the diffusion limit

los.do: Compute end-point probabilities and moments of a 1-D random walk, with or without bias.
los.ek: N steps of ±a: P(m) = C(N, (N + m)/2)/2^N; ⟨x⟩ = Na(2p − 1), Var x = 4Np(1 − p)a², so ⟨x²⟩ = Na² when unbiased.

los.do: Take the diffusion limit of a random walk: D from step length and time, and the time to diffuse a distance.
los.ek: D = a²/(2Δt) in 1-D; ⟨x²⟩ = 2Dt, and ⟨r²⟩ = 2dDt in d dimensions; t ~ L²/(2D).

los.do: Use the Gaussian limit of the walk to find the fraction of walkers past a distance, and add the variances of successive stages.
los.ek: P(x, t) = e^(−x²/4Dt)/√(4πDt); fraction beyond |x| > ℓ is erfc(ℓ/√(4Dt)); independent stages convolve, so variances add.

topics.title: Grad, div, curl and the integral theorems

los.do: Derive a differential conservation equation from an integral balance with the divergence theorem.
los.ek: ∭∇·F dV = ∯F·n dA ⇒ ∂c/∂t + ∇·N = R.

los.do: Compute the Laplacian of a radial function in cylindrical and spherical coordinates.
los.ek: Cylindrical: (1/r)(r f′)′; spherical: (1/r²)(r² f′)′; for f = rⁿ these are n² r^(n−2) and n(n + 1) r^(n−2).

los.do: Solve steady radial conduction or diffusion in a cylindrical or spherical shell.
los.ek: Cylinder: T = A ln r + B; sphere: T = A/r + B; fit the inner and outer values.

los.do: Compute the divergence of a radial field in cylindrical and spherical coordinates.
los.ek: ∇·(F(r) e_r) = (1/r)(rF)′ in a cylinder and (1/r²)(r²F)′ in a sphere.

los.do: Compute the gradient, divergence, curl and Laplacian of a field in Cartesian coordinates.

units.title: More on ODEs: circuits, bifurcations, operators, existence

los.do: Solve an RC circuit.
los.ek: R q′ + q/C = E: the charge rises with time constant RC and the current decays.

los.do: Locate a saddle-node bifurcation.
los.ek: Equilibria appear or vanish where f(y) = 0 and f′(y) = 0 together.

los.do: Apply a differential operator.
los.ek: L[e^{kx}] = p(k)e^{kx} for L = p(D) with constant coefficients.

los.do: Find the interval on which a linear IVP is guaranteed a unique solution.
los.ek: The largest open interval around x₀ on which all coefficients are continuous.

los.do: Verify that a vector function solves a linear system.
los.ek: x = e^{λt}v solves x′ = Ax exactly when Av = λv.

los.do: Solve a linear equation in z.
los.ek: Divide by multiplying top and bottom by the conjugate.

los.do: Solve a nonlinear equation in z.
los.ek: Write the right side in polar form; z² = w has two roots ±√w.

los.do: Decide whether a point lies in a region of the plane.
los.ek: |z − z₀| < r is the open disc of radius r about z₀.

los.do: Find the image of a point under a complex map.
los.ek: w = z² squares the modulus and doubles the argument.

los.do: Evaluate a limit of a complex function.
los.ek: A complex limit must agree from every direction; algebra works as for real limits.

los.do: Use the Cauchy–Riemann equations.
los.ek: f = u + iv is analytic where uₓ = v_y and u_y = −vₓ.

los.do: Test whether a function is harmonic.
los.ek: u is harmonic when u_xx + u_yy = 0; real parts of analytic functions are.

los.do: Recognise entire functions.
los.ek: Entire = analytic at every point of the plane.

los.do: Find a harmonic conjugate.
los.ek: Integrate v_y = uₓ in y, then fix the function of x with vₓ = −u_y.

los.do: Use Cauchy's integral formula.
los.ek: ∮ f(z)/(z − z₀) dz = 2πi f(z₀) for z₀ inside the contour and f analytic.

los.do: Decide whether a complex sequence converges.
los.ek: zⁿ → 0 when |z| < 1 and diverges when |z| > 1.

los.do: Find a Taylor coefficient of an analytic function.
los.ek: e^{az} = Σ aᵏ zᵏ / k!; 1/(1 − az) = Σ aᵏ zᵏ for |az| < 1.

los.do: Find a Laurent coefficient (a residue).
los.ek: The coefficient of 1/(z − z₀) is the residue.

los.do: Find the order of a zero.
los.ek: The order is the power of the first nonzero term of the Taylor series.

units.title: Complex analysis: mappings, contours and residues

los.do: Find how an analytic map stretches and turns at a point, and where it fails to be conformal.
los.ek: An analytic f is conformal wherever f′ ≠ 0: it magnifies by |f′(z₀)| and rotates by arg f′(z₀). Angles are lost exactly at the zeros of f′.

los.do: Work with a Möbius map: its pole and the image of a point or a line.
los.ek: w = (az + b)/(cz + d) sends z = −d/c to infinity and circles and lines to circles and lines; the Cayley map (z − i)/(z + i) sends the real axis to the unit circle.

los.do: Evaluate the principal logarithm and principal powers and say where the branch cut lies.
los.ek: Log z = ln|z| + i Arg z with −π < Arg z ≤ π, cut along the negative real axis; z^c = exp(c Log z), so i^i is real.

los.do: Evaluate a contour integral by parametrising the path.
los.ek: ∫ f(z) dz = ∫ f(z(t)) z′(t) dt. For a function that is not analytic, such as the conjugate, the answer depends on the path and a closed loop need not give zero.

los.do: Use Cauchy's theorem and deformation of contours to evaluate a closed integral.
los.ek: A closed integral of an analytic function is zero; around a simple pole it is 2πi times the coefficient, and only the singularities inside the contour count.

los.do: Use Cauchy's integral formula for a function and for its derivatives.
los.ek: f⁽ⁿ⁾(a) = (n!/2πi) ∮ f(z)/(z − a)ⁿ⁺¹ dz: values and all derivatives inside are fixed by the values on the contour.

los.do: Bound a contour integral by the ML inequality and say when an arc's contribution vanishes.
los.ek: |∫ f dz| ≤ M·L with M the largest |f| on the path and L its length; on a large semicircle the arc dies if |f| falls faster than 1/R.

los.do: Apply the maximum modulus principle and Liouville's theorem.
los.ek: A non-constant analytic function takes its maximum modulus on the boundary; a bounded entire function is constant, which is how the fundamental theorem of algebra is proved.

los.do: Find Laurent coefficients of the same function in different annuli.
los.ek: A function has a different Laurent series in each annulus between its singularities; only the series in the punctured disc around a point gives that point's residue.

los.do: Classify an isolated singularity as removable, a pole of given order, or essential.
los.ek: Look at the principal part: none is removable, finitely many terms is a pole whose order is the highest negative power, infinitely many is essential.

los.do: Compute a residue at a simple pole and at a pole of higher order.
los.ek: Simple pole: lim (z − a)f(z), or p(a)/q′(a). Order m: the (m − 1)th derivative of (z − a)ᵐf(z) at a, over (m − 1)!.

los.do: Find a Taylor series' radius of convergence from the singularities.
los.ek: The series converges out to the nearest singularity in the complex plane, even when that singularity is not on the real line.

topics.title: The residue theorem and real integrals

los.do: Evaluate a closed integral with the residue theorem.
los.ek: ∮ f dz = 2πi × (sum of the residues inside). Enlarging the contour past a pole adds that pole's residue.

los.do: Evaluate an integral over the whole real line by closing the contour in the upper half-plane.
los.ek: For a rational function decaying faster than 1/x, the semicircle contributes nothing and the integral is 2πi times the residues in the upper half-plane.

los.do: Evaluate a trigonometric integral over a full period on the unit circle.
los.ek: With z = e^{iθ}, cos θ = (z + 1/z)/2 and dθ = dz/(iz): the integral becomes a closed contour integral around |z| = 1.

los.do: Evaluate a Fourier-type integral with Jordan's lemma.
los.ek: For e^{ikz} with k > 0 close in the upper half-plane: the exponential decays there, so the arc vanishes even when f only falls like 1/R.

los.do: Count zeros with the argument principle and Rouché's theorem.
los.ek: (1/2πi)∮ f′/f dz = zeros − poles inside, counted with multiplicity. If |g| < |f| on the contour, f and f + g have the same number of zeros inside.

los.do: Run Euclid's algorithm and say how long it takes.
los.ek: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b); the last non-zero remainder is the gcd. Consecutive Fibonacci numbers are the slowest inputs.

los.do: Solve a linear congruence or a linear Diophantine equation with Bezout's identity.
los.ek: ax + by = c has integer solutions exactly when gcd(a, b) divides c; running Euclid backwards finds one, and the rest differ by multiples of (b/g, −a/g).

los.do: Count and sum the divisors of an integer from its prime factorisation.
los.ek: If n = Π p^a then n has Π (a + 1) divisors and σ(n) = Π (p^(a+1) − 1)/(p − 1); both functions are multiplicative.

los.do: Apply the division algorithm, including to negative numbers.
los.ek: For any integer a and positive n there is exactly one pair q, r with a = qn + r and 0 ≤ r < n. The remainder is never negative: −7 = (−2)·5 + 3.

los.do: Find how often a prime divides a factorial.
los.ek: The exponent of p in n! is ⌊n/p⌋ + ⌊n/p²⌋ + ⌊n/p³⌋ + … (Legendre). The number of trailing zeros of n! is the exponent of 5.

los.do: Read the gcd and lcm off prime factorisations.
los.ek: Take the smaller exponent of each prime for the gcd and the larger for the lcm, so gcd(a, b) · lcm(a, b) = ab.

los.do: Find a modular inverse and reduce a large power with Fermat's little theorem.
los.ek: a has an inverse modulo n exactly when gcd(a, n) = 1. For a prime p not dividing a, a^(p−1) ≡ 1 (mod p), so exponents reduce modulo p − 1.

los.do: Compute Euler's function and use Euler's theorem.
los.ek: φ(n) = n Π (1 − 1/p) over the primes dividing n, and a^φ(n) ≡ 1 (mod n) whenever gcd(a, n) = 1.

los.do: Solve simultaneous congruences and use Wilson's theorem.
los.ek: If m and n are coprime, x ≡ a (mod m), x ≡ b (mod n) has exactly one solution modulo mn. Wilson: (p − 1)! ≡ −1 (mod p) exactly when p is prime.

los.do: Find an RSA decryption exponent and encrypt a small message.
los.ek: With n = pq and φ = (p − 1)(q − 1), the public exponent e and private exponent d satisfy ed ≡ 1 (mod φ); encryption is m^e mod n and decryption c^d mod n.

los.do: Add, multiply and take powers of residues.
los.ek: Congruence respects addition and multiplication, so any integer may be replaced by its remainder at any stage. Powers of a residue repeat in a cycle.

los.do: Explain and use the digit tests for 9 and 11.
los.ek: Since 10 ≡ 1 (mod 9), a number is congruent to its digit sum modulo 9; since 10 ≡ −1 (mod 11), it is congruent to its alternating digit sum modulo 11.

los.do: Solve a linear congruence and count its solutions.
los.ek: ax ≡ b (mod n) has a solution exactly when d = gcd(a, n) divides b, and then it has exactly d solutions modulo n.

los.do: Reduce an exponent with Euler's theorem and invert with Fermat's.
los.ek: If gcd(a, n) = 1 then exponents may be reduced modulo φ(n). Modulo a prime p, the inverse of a is a^(p−2).

los.do: Find the order of an element modulo a prime and count primitive roots.
los.ek: The order of a modulo p divides p − 1. A primitive root has order p − 1; every prime has φ(p − 1) of them.

los.do: Evaluate a Legendre symbol with Euler's criterion and the reciprocity laws.
los.ek: (a/p) ≡ a^((p−1)/2) (mod p). (−1/p) = 1 exactly when p ≡ 1 (mod 4); (2/p) = 1 exactly when p ≡ ±1 (mod 8); for odd primes (p/q)(q/p) = −1 only when both are 3 mod 4.

los.do: Evaluate a Jacobi symbol by reciprocity and say what it does and does not tell you.
los.ek: The Jacobi symbol (a/n) for odd n multiplies the Legendre symbols over the prime factors of n and obeys the same reciprocity rules, so it is computed without factorising. (a/n) = −1 means a is not a square modulo n; (a/n) = 1 does not mean it is.

los.do: List the squares modulo a prime and count the solutions of x² ≡ a.
los.ek: Modulo an odd prime p the non-zero squares are the (p − 1)/2 values of 1², 2², …, ((p − 1)/2)². x² ≡ a has two solutions if a is a non-zero square, one if a ≡ 0, none otherwise.

los.do: Apply Euler's criterion by direct computation.
los.ek: a^((p−1)/2) is congruent to 1 if a is a non-zero square modulo p and to −1 (that is, p − 1) if it is not.

los.do: Decide whether an integer is a sum of two squares.
los.ek: An odd prime is a sum of two squares exactly when it is 1 mod 4. In general n is one exactly when every prime that is 3 mod 4 divides n to an even power.

los.do: Expand a rational as a continued fraction and solve a Pell equation.
los.ek: The continued fraction of p/q is Euclid's algorithm written down. The convergents of √d give the solutions of x² − dy² = 1, and every solution is a power of the smallest.

los.do: Estimate how many primes lie below a bound and apply the Fermat primality test.
los.ek: π(x) is about x/ln x. If a^(n−1) is not 1 modulo n then n is composite; composites that pass for base a are pseudoprimes, and Carmichael numbers such as 561 pass for every coprime base.

los.do: Factorise an integer by writing it as a difference of squares.
los.ek: If n = a² − b² then n = (a − b)(a + b). Fermat's method tries a = ⌈√n⌉, ⌈√n⌉ + 1, … until a² − n is a square. More generally x² ≡ y² (mod n) with x ≢ ±y gives the factor gcd(x − y, n).

los.do: Count primes in a range with the sieve of Eratosthenes.
los.ek: To find the primes up to N, cross out multiples of each prime up to √N; what survives is prime. A number below N with no prime factor up to √N is prime.

los.do: Connect Mersenne primes to even perfect numbers.
los.ek: If 2ᵖ − 1 is prime then 2ᵖ⁻¹(2ᵖ − 1) is perfect, and every even perfect number has this form (Euclid, Euler). 2ᵖ − 1 can only be prime when p is prime, but need not be: 2¹¹ − 1 = 23 · 89.

los.do: Generate Pythagorean triples.
los.ek: For m > n > 0, (m² − n², 2mn, m² + n²) is a Pythagorean triple; it is primitive exactly when m and n are coprime and of opposite parity, and every primitive triple arises this way.

los.do: Decide whether a set with an operation is a group and name the axiom that fails.
los.ek: A group needs closure, associativity, an identity and an inverse for every element. Commutativity is not required.

los.do: Find the order of an element of a cyclic group and count elements of a given order.
los.ek: In Z_n the element a has order n/gcd(a, n). A cyclic group of order n has φ(d) elements of order d for each divisor d, and none of any other order.

los.do: Use Lagrange's theorem to limit subgroup orders and count cosets.
los.ek: The order of a subgroup divides the order of the group, and the index |G|/|H| is the number of cosets. A group of prime order is cyclic.

los.do: Find the order of the group of units modulo n and decide whether it is cyclic.
los.ek: The units modulo n form a group of order φ(n). It is cyclic exactly for n = 1, 2, 4, p^k and 2p^k with p an odd prime.

los.do: Compute in the group of units modulo n: products and inverses.
los.ek: The units modulo n are the residues coprime to n, multiplied modulo n. The identity is 1 and each unit has exactly one inverse, which is again a unit.

los.do: Find the order of an element of a multiplicative group by taking powers.
los.ek: The order of a is the least k ≥ 1 with a^k equal to the identity. The powers of a cycle with that period, so a^m is the identity exactly when the order divides m.

los.do: Find the subgroup an element generates and list the subgroups of a cyclic group.
los.ek: In Z_n the element a generates the multiples of gcd(a, n), a subgroup of order n/gcd(a, n). Z_n has exactly one subgroup for each divisor of n.

los.do: Split a cyclic group into the cosets of a subgroup.
los.ek: The cosets of ⟨d⟩ in Z_n (d dividing n) are the residue classes modulo d: there are d of them, each of size n/d, and they partition the group.

los.do: Compute in a dihedral group with the relation between rotations and reflections.
los.ek: The symmetry group of a regular n-gon has n rotations and n reflections. With r a rotation by one step and s a reflection, s r s = r⁻¹, so s rᵏ s = r⁻ᵏ and every reflection has order 2.

los.do: Decide whether two small groups are isomorphic by comparing invariants.
los.ek: Isomorphic groups have the same order, the same number of elements of each order, and are both abelian or both not. One mismatch is enough to tell two groups apart.

los.do: Compose permutations in cycle notation and find the order of a permutation.
los.ek: Disjoint cycles commute and the order of a permutation is the least common multiple of its cycle lengths. Products are applied right to left.

los.do: Find the sign of a permutation and work with the alternating group.
los.ek: A cycle of length k is a product of k − 1 transpositions, so it is even when k is odd. The even permutations form A_n, of order n!/2.

los.do: Count conjugacy classes in a symmetric group and the size of a class.
los.ek: Two permutations are conjugate in S_n exactly when they have the same cycle type, so the classes are the partitions of n. A class with m_k cycles of length k has n!/Π(k^m_k · m_k!) elements.

los.do: Turn a permutation written as a list of images into cycles.
los.ek: Start at 1, follow where each point is sent until you return, and repeat from the smallest point not yet reached. Fixed points are cycles of length 1.

los.do: Find powers and the inverse of a permutation.
los.ek: σᵏ moves each point k steps along its cycle, and σ⁻¹ runs each cycle backwards. A cycle of length m satisfies σᵐ = identity.

los.do: Write a permutation as a product of transpositions and count how many are needed.
los.ek: A cycle of length m is a product of m − 1 transpositions, so a permutation of n points with c cycles (fixed points included) needs n − c, and no fewer.

los.do: Conjugate a permutation by relabelling its cycles.
los.ek: τστ⁻¹ has the same cycle shape as σ, with every entry a replaced by τ(a). This is why conjugacy classes in S_n are cycle types.

los.do: Use the orbit-stabiliser theorem to find the order of a symmetry group.
los.ek: |G| = |orbit| × |stabiliser|. The rotations of a cube move a face to any of 6 faces and 4 rotations fix a face, so there are 24.

los.do: Count orbits with Burnside's lemma.
los.ek: The number of orbits is the average number of fixed points: (1/|G|) Σ |Fix(g)|. A rotation by r places of an n-bead ring fixes k^gcd(n, r) colourings.

los.do: Use centralisers, the class equation and Cauchy's theorem.
los.ek: The size of a conjugacy class is |G| divided by the size of the centraliser. The class equation forces a non-trivial centre in a p-group, and Cauchy: if a prime p divides |G| there is an element of order p.

los.do: Find the orbits of a small group acting on a set.
los.ek: The orbit of a point is everything the group can move it to; orbits partition the set. For the group generated by one permutation the orbits are its cycles.

los.do: Count the colourings a symmetry fixes and apply Burnside to a polygon.
los.ek: A symmetry fixes a colouring exactly when each cycle of the symmetry is one colour, so it fixes k^(number of cycles) colourings. Averaging over rotations and reflections counts patterns up to turning over.

los.do: Find the centre and the conjugacy classes of a dihedral group.
los.ek: In the symmetry group of a regular n-gon the centre is trivial for odd n and contains the half-turn for even n. There are (n + 3)/2 conjugacy classes for odd n and (n + 6)/2 for even n.

los.do: Apply the first isomorphism theorem and count homomorphisms between cyclic groups.
los.ek: The image of a homomorphism is isomorphic to G/ker, so |image| = |G|/|kernel|. A homomorphism from Z_m to Z_n is fixed by where 1 goes, and there are gcd(m, n) of them.

los.do: Classify finite abelian groups of a given order and decide when a product is cyclic.
los.ek: Every finite abelian group is a product of cyclic groups of prime-power order. For n = Π p^a the number of abelian groups is Π (number of partitions of a). Z_m × Z_n is cyclic exactly when gcd(m, n) = 1.

los.do: Use the Sylow theorems to limit the number of Sylow subgroups.
los.ek: If |G| = p^a m with p not dividing m, the number of Sylow p-subgroups divides m and is 1 mod p. When that leaves only 1, the subgroup is normal and the group is not simple.

topics.title: Quotients and products of small groups

los.do: Decide whether a subgroup is normal.
los.ek: N is normal when gNg⁻¹ = N for every g, equivalently when left and right cosets agree. Every subgroup of an abelian group is normal, and so is every subgroup of index 2.

los.do: Compute in a quotient of a cyclic group.
los.ek: Z_n/⟨d⟩ is cyclic of order d. The coset of a has order d/gcd(a, d): the least k for which ka lands back in the subgroup.

los.do: Find the kernel and image of a concrete homomorphism.
los.ek: For x ↦ kx on Z_n the kernel has gcd(k, n) elements and the image n/gcd(k, n). The sign map on S_n has kernel A_n; the determinant on invertible matrices has kernel the matrices of determinant 1.

los.do: Find orders of elements in a direct product.
los.ek: The order of (a, b) is the least common multiple of the orders of a and b. Counting elements of each order is the quickest way to tell products such as Z₂ × Z₄ and Z₈ apart.

los.do: Count units, zero divisors and idempotents in Z_n.
los.ek: In Z_n a non-zero residue is a unit if it is coprime to n and a zero divisor otherwise. Z_n has 2^k idempotents, where k is the number of distinct primes dividing n.

los.do: Decide whether a quotient ring is a field and count roots of a polynomial over Z_p.
los.ek: Z_n is a field exactly when n is prime, and F[x]/(f) is a field exactly when f is irreducible. Over a field a polynomial of degree d has at most d roots; over Z_n with n composite it can have more.

los.do: Work with norms in the Gaussian integers and recognise failures of unique factorisation.
los.ek: N(a + bi) = a² + b² is multiplicative, so an element of prime norm is irreducible. Z[i] has unique factorisation; Z[√−5] does not, since 6 = 2 · 3 = (1 + √−5)(1 − √−5).

los.do: Do arithmetic with polynomials whose coefficients are taken modulo a prime.
los.ek: Coefficients add and multiply modulo p. Because p divides the middle binomial coefficients, (x + 1)ᵖ = xᵖ + 1 in Z_p[x]: the 'freshman's dream' is true in characteristic p.

los.do: Combine ideals of the integers and count the ideals of Z_n.
los.ek: Every ideal of Z is (m) for some m. (a) + (b) = (gcd), (a) ∩ (b) = (lcm), and (a) contains (b) exactly when a divides b. The ideals of Z_n correspond to the divisors of n.

los.do: Use the remainder and factor theorems over Z_p.
los.ek: Dividing f(x) by x − a leaves the remainder f(a); so a is a root exactly when x − a is a factor. A quadratic or cubic over a field is irreducible exactly when it has no root.

topics.title: Extensions, finite fields and the Galois correspondence

los.do: Find the degree of a field extension and use the tower law.
los.ek: [K(α) : K] is the degree of the minimal polynomial of α over K, and degrees multiply up a tower: [M : K] = [M : L][L : K].

los.do: Count the elements, subfields and irreducible polynomials of a finite field.
los.ek: There is exactly one field of each prime-power order pⁿ. Its non-zero elements form a cyclic group, its subfields are the fields of order p^d for d dividing n, and xᵖⁿ − x is the product of every monic irreducible over F_p whose degree divides n.

los.do: Find the order of a Galois group and read the Galois correspondence.
los.ek: For a Galois extension the group has order equal to the degree, and subgroups correspond to intermediate fields with inclusions reversed; a subfield is normal over the base exactly when its subgroup is normal. Q(ζ_n) has group the units modulo n, of order φ(n).

los.do: Decide what can be constructed by ruler and compass or solved by radicals.
los.ek: A length is constructible only if its degree over Q is a power of 2, so a regular n-gon is constructible exactly when φ(n) is a power of 2. A polynomial is soluble by radicals exactly when its Galois group is soluble; S₅ is not.

topics.title: Lines and triangles on the sphere

los.do: Find great-circle distances and the areas of lunes.
los.ek: Spherical lines are great circles. The distance between two points is R times the angle they subtend at the centre, and a lune between two great circles meeting at angle θ has area 2θR².

los.do: Use the angle excess of a spherical triangle or polygon.
los.ek: A spherical triangle with angles α, β, γ on a sphere of radius R has area (α + β + γ − π)R². An n-gon has area (angle sum − (n − 2)π)R².

los.do: Describe the isometries of the sphere and its finite rotation groups.
los.ek: The isometries of the sphere are the orthogonal maps: rotations about an axis and their compositions with reflections. The finite groups of rotations are cyclic, dihedral, or the rotation groups of the tetrahedron (order 12), cube (24) and icosahedron (60).

los.do: Find the central angle between two points given by latitude and longitude.
los.ek: Write each point as a unit vector (cos φ cos λ, cos φ sin λ, sin φ); the central angle is the angle between the vectors, so cos c = sin φ₁ sin φ₂ + cos φ₁ cos φ₂ cos Δλ. On one meridian the angle is just the difference in latitude.

los.do: Compare a circle of latitude with a great circle.
los.ek: The circle at latitude φ has radius R cos φ, so its length is 2πR cos φ. Only the equator is a great circle; travelling along any other parallel is longer than the great-circle route between the same points.

los.do: Find the area of a spherical cap or zone.
los.ek: The cap within angular radius θ of a pole has area 2πR²(1 − cos θ), which is 2πR times its height (Archimedes). A cap is the spherical disc, and it has less area than the flat disc of the same radius.

los.do: Measure length in the upper half-plane and identify its geodesics.
los.ek: The half-plane metric is (dx² + dy²)/y². Geodesics are vertical lines and semicircles centred on the real axis; the distance from ai to bi is |ln(b/a)|.

los.do: Use the angle defect of a hyperbolic triangle and compare parallels in the three geometries.
los.ek: A hyperbolic triangle with angles α, β, γ has area π − (α + β + γ), so no triangle has area above π; an ideal triangle has area exactly π. Through a point off a line there are infinitely many lines that never meet it.

los.do: Compare circumferences of circles in the three geometries.
los.ek: A circle of geodesic radius r has circumference 2π sin r on the unit sphere, 2πr in the plane and 2π sinh r in the hyperbolic plane: less room than flat on the sphere, more in the hyperbolic plane.

los.do: Compute the length of a horizontal or vertical segment in the half-plane.
los.ek: With metric (dx² + dy²)/y², a horizontal segment of Euclidean length L at height y has length L/y, and a vertical segment from height a to b has length ln(b/a). Lengths grow without bound near the boundary y = 0.

los.do: Find the geodesic through two points of the half-plane.
los.ek: If the points share an x-coordinate the geodesic is the vertical line. Otherwise it is the semicircle centred on the real axis at the point equidistant from both: solve (x₁ − c)² + y₁² = (x₂ − c)² + y₂².

los.do: Compute hyperbolic areas by integrating and by the angle defect.
los.ek: The area element is dx dy / y². The region above height h over a base of width w has finite area w/h although it extends to infinity. A geodesic n-gon has area (n − 2)π minus its angle sum.

los.do: State the Gaussian curvature of the model spaces and how it scales.
los.ek: A sphere of radius R has curvature 1/R², the plane 0, and the hyperbolic plane −1. Scaling lengths by a factor c divides curvature by c².

los.do: Use the Gauss-Bonnet relation between curvature, area and angle sum.
los.ek: For a geodesic triangle, α + β + γ − π = ∫ K dA. For a closed surface, ∫ K dA = 2πχ: 4π for any sphere, 0 for a torus, 4π(1 − g) for genus g.

los.do: Estimate curvature from a measured geodesic triangle.
los.ek: For a small geodesic triangle, K ≈ (α + β + γ − π)/area. On a sphere this is exact and gives the radius: R = √(area/excess).

los.do: Estimate curvature from the circumference of a small circle.
los.ek: A geodesic circle of radius r has circumference 2πr(1 − Kr²/6 + …). Positive curvature shortens it, negative curvature lengthens it; K ≈ 3(2πr − C)/(πr³).

los.do: Find the supremum and infimum of a set and say whether they are attained.
los.ek: The supremum is the least upper bound. Every non-empty set of reals that is bounded above has one, which need not belong to the set; the rationals lack this property.
