los.ek: AgCl + 2NH₃ ⇌ Ag(NH₃)₂⁺ + Cl⁻ with K = K_sp K_f; s ≈ √K [NH₃].

los.do: Write and use K for a heterogeneous equilibrium.
los.ek: Pure solids and liquids are left out of K.

los.do: Find the pH at points of a diprotic titration.
los.ek: First half-equivalence: pH = pKa₁; first equivalence: (pKa₁ + pKa₂)/2; second half-equivalence: pKa₂.

los.do: Find an average oxidation state.
los.ek: Charge balance with the usual values for the other atoms.

los.do: Combine half-reaction potentials.
los.ek: Potentials do not add; ΔG = −nFE does: E₃ = (n₁E₁ + n₂E₂)/(n₁ + n₂).

los.do: Use the Nernst equation.
los.ek: E = E° − (RT/nF) ln Q.

los.do: Find K from a standard cell potential.
los.ek: ln K = nFE°/RT.

los.do: Count electrons in a redox half-reaction.
los.ek: Change in oxidation state × atoms changed.

units.title: USNCO band 8: atomic structure and periodicity

los.do: Identify a group from successive ionisation energies.
los.ek: The big jump comes after the last valence electron.

los.do: Count electrons with given quantum numbers.
los.ek: Each orbital holds 2; there are 2l + 1 orbitals per subshell and n² per shell.

los.do: Explain anomalies in periodic trends.
los.ek: Half-filled and filled subshells resist adding or removing electrons.

los.do: Find the wavelength of a hydrogen transition.
Count unpaired electrons in a transition-metal ion.
los.ek: Remove s electrons first, then put the d electrons into five orbitals by Hund's rule (free ion).

los.do: Predict a radioactive decay mode.
los.ek: Neutron-rich nuclides β⁻ decay; proton-rich ones β⁺ or capture electrons; very heavy ones α decay.

units.title: USNCO band 9: bonding and molecular structure

los.do: Predict a VSEPR shape including lone pairs.
los.ek: Count electron domains, then name the shape from the atoms only.

los.do: Count the stereoisomers of an octahedral complex.
los.ek: Enumerate arrangements up to rotation; mirror images count separately.

los.do: Find a bond order from a molecular-orbital diagram.
los.ek: Bond order = (bonding − antibonding)/2.

los.do: Choose the most stable resonance arrangement or isomer by formal charge.
los.ek: Prefer formal charges near zero, with negative charge on the more electronegative atom.

los.do: Find a fractional bond order from resonance.
los.ek: Spread the π bonds over the equivalent positions: bond order = total bonds / positions.

units.title: USNCO band 10: organic chemistry, biochemistry and spectroscopy

los.do: Count structural isomers.
los.ek: Enumerate chains, then branches; include rings when the formula allows.

los.do: Find the degree of unsaturation.
los.ek: DoU = (2C + 2 + N − H − X)/2: rings plus π bonds.

los.do: Assign an infrared band.
los.ek: O–H broad 3200–3550; C=O sharp near 1700; C≡N near 2250; C–H just below 3000 (sp³) or above (sp²).

los.do: Count ¹H NMR environments.
los.ek: Equivalent hydrogens (by symmetry) give one signal.

los.do: Identify the monomer of a polymer.
los.ek: Addition polymers repeat the alkene's carbons; condensation polymers lose a small molecule at each link.

los.do: Find an amino acid's isoelectric point.
los.ek: pI is the average of the two pKa values on either side of the neutral form.

los.do: Find a molar solubility with a common ion, then compare it with pure water.
los.ek: Ksp = s(s + c) ≈ s c when c ≫ s.

los.do: Get ΔS° of a cell reaction from the temperature dependence of E°.
los.ek: ΔS° = nF(dE°/dT); ΔH° = ΔG° + TΔS°.

los.do: Find ΔS° from ΔG° and calorimetric ΔH°.
los.ek: ΔG° = −RT ln K; ΔS° = (ΔH° − ΔG°)/T.

los.do: Find a hydrate's water count from an iodometric titration.
los.ek: Cu²⁺ + I⁻ → CuI + ½I₂; I₂ + 2 S₂O₃²⁻: one thiosulfate per Cu.

los.do: Find a density and an oxidation state from a perovskite unit cell.
los.ek: ABO₃: A at the corners (1), B at the centre (1), O at the face centres (3).

los.do: Find a photon energy per mole for bond breaking.
los.ek: E = N_A hc/λ.

los.do: Read the number of electrons transferred from an electrode's slope per decade.
los.ek: At 25 °C a Nernstian electrode moves 59.16/n mV for each tenfold change in concentration, so the slope gives n before any chemistry is assumed.

los.do: Find an acid's K_a from the shift in an ion-selective electrode's potential with pH.
los.ek: The electrode sees only the free anion; the shift from its strong-base reading gives the free fraction α = 10^(−ΔE/59.16), and K_a = [H⁺]α/(1 − α).

los.do: Find the solubility of two sparingly soluble salts of weak acids sharing a cation.
los.ek: The cation balances both anions in all their forms: [M⁺]² = K_spA(1 + [H⁺]/K_A) + K_spB(1 + [H⁺]/K_B).

los.do: Find two anions from the successive end points of one silver titration.
los.ek: Cyanide first takes silver as Ag(CN)₂⁻ (one Ag⁺ per two CN⁻), then precipitates as AgCN, and only then does chloride precipitate, so the volumes between end points count each anion.

los.do: Find the cell emf at the equivalence point of a precipitation titration.
los.ek: At the equivalence point of a 1:1 salt [Ag⁺] = √K_sp, and the silver electrode reads E° + 0.05916 log[Ag⁺] against the reference.

los.do: Find the vacancy fraction of a nonstoichiometric oxide from the share of cations oxidised.
los.ek: With the anion lattice intact, charge balance fixes the cation count: for Cu₂₋ₓO with a fraction f of copper as Cu²⁺, (2 − x)(1 + f) = 2.

los.do: Find the temperature at which two solid phases exchange stability from formation data.
los.ek: Build ΔH° and ΔS° of the interconversion from the formation values, then T = ΔH°/ΔS°; with three phases, each pair has its own boundary.

los.do: Find a rate constant from the time a limiting reagent takes to vanish at constant rate.
los.ek: A straight concentration–time line means zero order in the limiting reagent: the rate is its initial concentration over the reaction time, and the other species give the rate law.

los.do: Find the overall activation energy of a chain reaction from its composite rate constant.
los.ek: Activation energies combine the way the rate constants do: a product adds them, a quotient subtracts them, and a square root halves them.

los.do: Identify the metal of a chloride hydrate from a silver titration.
los.ek: Silver counts chloride; mass per mole of chloride times the chlorides per formula is the formula mass, and what is left after chloride and water is the metal.

los.do: Count valence electrons of carbonyl and nitrosyl complexes and spot the 17-electron ones.
los.ek: Neutral counting: the metal's group number, two per CO, three per linear NO, minus the charge. Seventeen-electron fragments either dimerise through a metal–metal bond or are easily reduced.

los.do: Find the metal–metal bonds a carbonyl cluster needs and say what light does to them.
los.ek: Metal–metal bonds = (18 × metals − total electrons)/2. The M–M σ bond is the weakest in the molecule, and UV light promotes σ → σ*, breaking it into two 17-electron radicals.

los.do: Predict the chemistry of nitrogen fluorides: where they form, what stabilises NF₄⁺ and how it hydrolyses.
los.ek: Fluorination is an oxidation, so NF₃ forms at the anode; NF₄⁺ needs a strong fluoride acceptor to hold the counter-ion, and with water it gives back NF₃ and oxidises water to O₂.

los.do: Write the products of reactions that are not simple exchange: disproportionation, hydrolysis and redox in base.
los.ek: Copper(I) disproportionates in non-complexing acid, acyl chlorides hydrolyse to HCl and the acid (oxalyl chloride falls apart to CO and CO₂), and permanganate in strong base stops at green manganate.

los.do: Rank substituents by the CIP rules and assign R or S.
los.ek: Rank by atomic number at the first point of difference, counting multiple bonds as duplicated atoms; with the lowest group pointing away, 1 → 2 → 3 clockwise is R.

los.do: Read a Fischer projection: its geometry, what moves are allowed, and D or L.

units.title: Inorganic principles across the ACS content map

los.do: Estimate the effective nuclear charge on a valence electron with Slater's rules.
los.ek: S = 0.35 per other electron in the same (ns, np) group, 0.85 per electron in shell n − 1, 1.00 per electron deeper; for an ns electron of a d-block atom the (n − 1)d electrons count 0.85.

los.do: Decide from a molecule's point group whether it can be polar and whether it can be chiral.
los.ek: Polar only in C₁, Cₛ, Cₙ and Cₙᵥ; chiral only when there is no improper axis (C₁, Cₙ, Dₙ).

los.do: Find an organometallic fragment's isolobal organic partner from its electron count.
los.ek: A fragment one electron short of 18 (Mn(CO)₅, CpFe(CO)₂) is isolobal with CH₃ (one short of 8); two short with CH₂; three short with CH.

los.do: Compare ligands by steric bulk (cone angle) and by donor or acceptor strength.
los.ek: Tolman cone angle grows PMe₃ < PPh₃ < PCy₃ < P(t-Bu)₃; stronger π-acceptors (CO, PF₃, phosphites) raise the ν(CO) of the other carbonyls.

los.do: Identify constitutional isomers of complexes and use precipitation or conductivity to tell them apart.
los.ek: Ionisation, hydrate, linkage and coordination isomers; only ions outside the coordination sphere precipitate with Ag⁺ or Ba²⁺ (Werner's evidence).

los.do: Name a coordination compound and write the formula from a name.
los.ek: Ligands alphabetically before the metal; anionic ligands end in -o; the metal takes -ate in an anionic complex, with its oxidation state in Roman numerals.

los.do: Find a lattice enthalpy or an enthalpy of formation from a Born–Haber cycle.
los.ek: ΔH_f = ΔH_sub + IE + ½D + ΔH_eg + ΔH_lattice (lattice formation from gaseous ions, negative).

los.do: Relate point defects and nonstoichiometry to composition and oxidation state.
los.ek: Schottky: cation–anion vacancy pairs; Frenkel: an ion moved to an interstitial site; in Fe₁₋ₓO each missing Fe²⁺ is balanced by two Fe³⁺.

los.do: Classify doped semiconductors and predict how conductivity changes with temperature.
los.ek: Group 15 dopants in Si give n-type, group 13 p-type; intrinsic carriers grow as e^(−E_g/2kT), so semiconductors conduct better when hot while metals conduct worse.

los.do: Recall superconductors, perovskites, polymorphs, layered solids and crystal systems.
los.ek: Below T_c resistance vanishes and fields are expelled (Meissner); Cooper pairs (BCS) in conventional ones; YBa₂Cu₃O₇ is a layered perovskite; 7 crystal systems, 14 Bravais lattices, 230 space groups.

los.do: Describe framework, self-assembled and nanoscale materials and how synthesis sets their properties.
los.ek: MOFs join metal nodes with organic linkers into porous crystals; thiols on gold self-assemble into monolayers; quantum dots' band gaps widen as they shrink.

los.do: Assign a substitution mechanism (A, D, Iₐ, I_d) and compute a rate through an outer-sphere pre-equilibrium.
los.ek: Eigen–Wilkins: k_obs = K_os k_i [L]; a negative volume of activation and dependence on the entering ligand point to association; square-planar d⁸ is associative.

los.do: Tell inner- from outer-sphere electron transfer and estimate a cross rate with the Marcus relation.
los.ek: Inner sphere needs a bridging ligand that is transferred (Taube: Cl from Co to Cr); outer sphere keeps both coordination shells; k₁₂ ≈ √(k₁₁k₂₂K₁₂).

los.do: Use the trans effect to plan the synthesis of a square-planar isomer.
los.ek: Trans effect order roughly CO, CN⁻ > PR₃ > I⁻ > Br⁻ > Cl⁻ > NH₃ > H₂O; [PtCl₄]²⁻ + 2 NH₃ gives cis-platin, [Pt(NH₃)₄]²⁺ + 2 Cl⁻ gives the trans isomer.

los.do: Quantify the chelate effect and explain its entropic and kinetic origins.
los.ek: Chelates release more free ligands (entropy gain) and, once one end binds, the other is held near the metal; ΔΔG = −RT ln 10 · Δlog β.

los.do: Compute the barrier of a fluxional process from NMR coalescence.
los.ek: At coalescence k = πΔν/√2; ΔG‡ = RT ln(k_B T/(h k)); Berry pseudorotation exchanges axial and equatorial sites of a trigonal bipyramid.

los.do: Combine stepwise formation constants and find the fraction of each complex at a given ligand concentration.
los.ek: β_n = K₁K₂…K_n; α_ML = β₁[L]/(1 + β₁[L] + β₂[L]² + …); Irving–Williams: Mn < Fe < Co < Ni < Cu > Zn.

los.do: Predict acid–base behaviour in nonaqueous solvents, levelling and superacids.
los.ek: The strongest acid that can exist in a solvent is its lyonium ion; acids stronger than that are levelled; differentiating solvents (acetic acid) separate them; superacids have H₀ below −12.

los.do: Relate a chiral catalyst's selectivity to the free-energy difference of the competing transition states.
los.ek: er = e^(ΔΔG‡/RT), ee = (er − 1)/(er + 1); about 11 kJ/mol at 25 °C gives 98% ee.

los.do: Use LFSE to explain the double hump in hydration enthalpies of first-row M²⁺ ions.
los.ek: High-spin octahedral LFSE (in Δ_o): 0, −0.4, −0.8, −1.2, −0.6, 0, −0.4, −0.8, −1.2, −0.6, 0 for d⁰–d¹⁰; d⁰, d⁵ and d¹⁰ lie on the baseline.

los.do: Find Δ_o from a d–d absorption and apply the selection rules and Tanabe–Sugano reading of d–d spectra.
los.ek: For d¹, Δ_o = hc/λ_max (ν̃ = 10⁷/λ in cm⁻¹); Laporte-forbidden d–d bands are weak, spin-forbidden ones weaker; Tanabe–Sugano diagrams map band energies to Δ_o/B.

los.do: Compute an effective magnetic moment from a measured susceptibility and infer the number of unpaired electrons.
los.ek: μ_eff = 2.828 √(χ_M T) (cgs) ≈ √(8χ_M T); spin-only μ = √(n(n + 2)).

los.do: Predict multiplets in multinuclear NMR from spin I and the number of equivalent coupled nuclei.
los.ek: Lines = 2nI + 1: three ¹⁹F split ³¹P into a 1:3:3:1 quartet; deuterium (I = 1) splits ¹³C of CDCl₃ into a 1:1:1 triplet.

los.do: Use an ion-selective electrode's Nernstian response, and choose a microscopy or luminescence technique.
los.ek: ΔE = (RT ln 10/zF)·Δlog a, 59.16/z mV per decade at 25 °C; fluorescence is spin-allowed and fast (ns), phosphorescence spin-forbidden and slow; STM and AFM reach atoms.

topics.title: AI, machine learning, deep learning, generative AI

los.do: Place a system in the nested fields AI ⊃ machine learning ⊃ deep learning ⊃ generative AI.
los.ek: ML learns from data; deep learning uses many-layer networks; generative AI produces new content.

los.do: Say how images, text, audio and categories are encoded, and count the numbers in an image.
los.ek: Pixels × 3 channels; tokens → embeddings; one-hot for categories.

los.do: Compute a dot product and a cosine similarity between vectors.
los.ek: Cosine = dot ÷ (lengths); 1 same direction, 0 unrelated.

los.do: Name the parts of a network and say why activations must be nonlinear.
los.ek: Parameters, forward pass, backpropagation; stacked linear layers collapse to one.

los.do: Compute a neuron's output with ReLU or sigmoid.
los.ek: Weighted sum plus bias, then the activation.

los.do: Count the parameters of a fully connected layer or small network.
los.ek: Each neuron: one weight per input plus a bias.

los.do: Define token, context window, embedding, inference, attention, temperature and hallucination, and order the steps of generating text.
los.ek: Generation is repeated next-token prediction.

los.do: Estimate token counts and how much text fits in a context window.
los.ek: About 0.75 English words per token.

los.do: Compute next-token probabilities with softmax, with and without temperature.
los.ek: Low temperature sharpens, high flattens.

los.do: Convert a parameter count and precision to the memory the weights need.
los.ek: 16-bit = 2 bytes per parameter; a billion bytes ≈ 1 GB.

los.do: Classify a task as supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement or self-supervised learning, and name the stages of building a chat assistant.
los.ek: Pretraining, fine-tuning, feedback-based RL, then inference.

los.do: Take a gradient-descent step, compute a mean squared error and count training updates.
los.ek: w ← w − learning rate × gradient.

los.do: Diagnose overfitting and underfitting, name the data splits, and compute precision and recall.
los.ek: Judge on unseen data; precision is of what was flagged, recall of what was there.

los.do: Explain hallucination, say what a model can know, and decide what to verify.
los.ek: Training data up to a cutoff, plus the context window; nothing else.

los.do: Choose the prompt change that fixes a given problem with an answer.
los.ek: Context, format, examples, steps.

los.do: Name the parts of an agent and the steps of its loop and of retrieval-augmented generation.
los.ek: Model + tools + memory + loop; embed, retrieve, answer from context.

los.do: Choose a kind of model for a job and work out what an API job costs.
los.ek: Input and output tokens are priced separately.

los.do: Respond safely to a voice-clone, deepfake or phishing attempt, check where media came from, and decide what not to share with a chatbot.
los.ek: Verify through a channel you already trust; provenance beats detectors.

los.do: Define scaling laws, alignment, AGI and foundation models, and estimate training compute and compute-optimal data.
los.ek: Compute ≈ 6 × parameters × tokens; about 20 tokens per parameter.

los.do: Classify a statement as DML, DDL, DCL or transaction control.
los.ek: TRUNCATE, RENAME and COMMENT are DDL; MERGE is DML.

los.do: Identify primary keys, foreign keys and self-references in a schema.
los.ek: A foreign key may be null and may point into its own table.

los.do: Evaluate an arithmetic expression in the select list, including one with NULL.
los.ek: Usual precedence; anything combined with NULL is NULL.

los.do: Count the rows DISTINCT returns over one or more columns.
los.ek: DISTINCT covers the whole select list; all NULLs are one value.

los.do: Use aliases, concatenation and the q-quote correctly, including Oracle's treatment of empty strings.
los.ek: Aliases exist only from SELECT onward; '' is NULL; || ignores NULL.

los.do: Count the rows a WHERE clause keeps, with AND/OR precedence, BETWEEN, IN, LIKE and IS NULL.
los.ek: AND before OR; a comparison with NULL is never true.

los.do: Predict the order of rows from ORDER BY, including where Oracle puts NULLs, and which rows FETCH and OFFSET keep.
los.ek: NULLs sort high: last ascending, first descending.

los.do: Say how &, &&, DEFINE and VERIFY behave.
los.ek: && prompts once and defines the variable for the session.

los.do: Evaluate character functions: SUBSTR, INSTR, LENGTH, LPAD, RPAD, TRIM, REPLACE, INITCAP.
los.ek: Positions count from 1; a negative SUBSTR start counts from the end.

los.do: Evaluate ROUND, TRUNC and MOD, including negative places and negative numbers.
los.ek: ROUND halves away from zero; MOD takes the dividend's sign.

los.do: Do date arithmetic and evaluate MONTHS_BETWEEN, ADD_MONTHS, LAST_DAY and NEXT_DAY.
los.ek: DATE − DATE is days; month-ends stay month-ends.

los.do: Evaluate NVL, NVL2, NULLIF and COALESCE.
los.ek: COALESCE returns its first non-null argument.

los.do: Evaluate CASE and DECODE.
los.ek: DECODE matches NULL to NULL; CASE with no ELSE gives NULL.

los.do: Read TO_CHAR and TO_NUMBER format models and say when Oracle converts implicitly.
los.ek: Too-narrow models print #; strings compared with dates use NLS_DATE_FORMAT.

los.ek: COUNT(*) counts rows; everything else skips NULLs.

los.do: Count the groups a GROUP BY … HAVING query returns and evaluate a nested group function.

los.do: Spot the grouping error in a query and state the logical order of the clauses.

los.do: Count the rows of an inner, outer, cross, natural or USING join, and choose the join that keeps the rows asked for.

los.do: Evaluate a self-join and a non-equijoin.
los.ek: Two aliases of one table; a range condition instead of =.

los.do: Translate Oracle's (+) outer-join notation to ANSI syntax.
los.ek: (+) marks the side that may be missing.

los.do: Count the rows of a query with a single-row, multiple-row (IN, ANY, ALL), correlated or EXISTS subquery.
los.ek: > ALL is above the maximum; a correlated subquery reruns per row.

los.do: Say whether a subquery comparison runs, returns nothing or fails.
los.ek: = with a multi-row subquery raises ORA-01427.

los.do: Predict the result of a correlated UPDATE or DELETE.
los.ek: The subquery sees the table as the statement began.

los.do: Count the rows of UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT and MINUS.
los.ek: Only UNION ALL keeps duplicates.

los.do: State the rules for compound queries: matching columns, names, ORDER BY and precedence.
los.ek: Names from the first query; ORDER BY once at the end; equal precedence.

los.do: Predict a table after INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE.
los.ek: No WHERE means every row; omitted columns get their default.

los.do: Predict the result of MERGE and of a multitable INSERT ALL or INSERT FIRST.
los.ek: INSERT FIRST stops at the first true WHEN.

los.do: Trace COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT and implicit commits through a session.
los.ek: ROLLBACK TO keeps the transaction open; DDL commits.

los.do: Compute the values a sequence hands out, with and without CYCLE.
los.ek: First NEXTVAL is START WITH; CURRVAL repeats the session's last.

los.do: Say whether an index can serve a condition, and how indexes and synonyms relate to their tables.
los.ek: Functions and leading wildcards defeat a plain index; synonyms grant nothing.

los.do: Find the INSERT that violates a PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, CHECK or FOREIGN KEY constraint, and name constraint types by their dictionary code.
los.ek: UNIQUE allows many NULLs; a CHECK passes on NULL.

los.do: Choose between DELETE, TRUNCATE and DROP, and state the rules for data types, temporary and external tables and unused columns.
los.ek: TRUNCATE is DDL; NUMBER(p,s) rounds extra decimals.

los.do: Say whether DML works through a view and what OR REPLACE, FORCE and dropping do.
los.ek: GROUP BY, DISTINCT and READ ONLY block DML; CHECK OPTION keeps rows visible.

los.do: Classify privileges as system or object and predict what REVOKE takes from others.
los.ek: Object grants cascade on revoke; ADMIN OPTION grants do not.

los.do: Name the dictionary view that answers a question and the scope of its prefix.
los.ek: USER_ ⊂ ALL_ ⊂ DBA_.

los.do: Say what CURRENT_DATE, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, LOCALTIMESTAMP, SYSDATE and the TIMESTAMP types hold.
los.ek: CURRENT_ follow the session; SYS follow the server.

los.do: Convert and add INTERVAL YEAR TO MONTH and DAY TO SECOND values.
los.ek: Adding a month interval to the 31st can fail.

los.do: Evaluate ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, LAG and running or partitioned aggregates.
los.ek: PARTITION BY restarts; RANK leaves gaps after ties.

los.do: Predict the rows of a top-n-per-group or paging query built on a window function.
los.ek: Number in an inline view, filter outside it.

los.do: Evaluate an aggregation over a star schema: fact joined to dimensions, filtered and grouped.
los.ek: Compute the measure per fact row, then sum.

los.do: Write an everyday procedure as ordered, unambiguous steps and trace it on an input.
los.ek: An algorithm is a finite sequence of precise steps; sequence, selection and iteration are enough to express any algorithm.

los.do: Put the steps of writing, compiling and running a Java program in order and say which step catches which problem.
los.ek: javac turns .java source into .class bytecode; the JVM runs the bytecode; the compiler checks syntax and types before anything runs.

los.do: Choose test inputs, including boundary cases, and state the output each should produce.
los.ek: Test typical, boundary (0, 1, empty, the limits) and invalid inputs; a test is useful only with a predicted answer.

los.do: Classify an error as syntax (compile-time), run-time (exception) or logic, given the code and its symptom.
los.ek: Syntax errors stop compilation; run-time errors throw during execution (int division by 0 throws ArithmeticException); logic errors run and give a wrong answer.

los.do: Convert a non-negative integer between decimal and binary.
los.ek: Place values are powers of 2: 1011₂ = 8 + 2 + 1 = 11.

los.do: Count the distinct values n bits can represent, and the bits needed for N values.
los.ek: n bits give 2ⁿ patterns; N values need ⌈log₂ N⌉ bits.

los.do: Choose a primitive type (int, double, boolean) or a reference type (String, an object) for a described quantity.
los.ek: A primitive variable holds the value itself; a reference variable holds the address of an object.

los.do: Declare and initialise variables of type int, double and boolean.
los.ek: type name = value; a variable is declared before use and keeps one type for its lifetime.

los.do: Evaluate an arithmetic expression with int and double operands, including integer division and %.
los.ek: int / int truncates toward zero (7 / 2 = 3, −7 / 2 = −3); % keeps the sign of the dividend (−7 % 2 = −1); one double operand makes the result double; * / % bind tighter than + −.

los.do: Predict exactly what print and println statements display, including string concatenation with numbers.
los.ek: + runs left to right: "1" + 2 + 3 is "123" but 1 + 2 + "3" is "33"; println ends the line, print does not.

los.do: Trace a sequence of assignment statements and give each variable's final value.
los.ek: = evaluates the right side first, then overwrites the variable on the left; the old value is gone, so a swap needs a temporary.

los.do: Predict the value stored after compound assignment and ++ / −− operators.
los.ek: x += 3 means x = x + 3; x++ adds 1; for int x, x /= 2 truncates.

los.do: Predict the result of casting between int and double, including rounding a positive double to the nearest int.
los.ek: (int) truncates toward zero; (int)(x + 0.5) rounds a non-negative x; the cast binds tighter than arithmetic: (double) 7 / 2 = 3.5 but (double)(7 / 2) = 3.0.

los.do: Predict when int arithmetic overflows and the value that results.
los.ek: int is 32-bit two's complement, −2³¹ to 2³¹ − 1 (Integer.MIN_VALUE to Integer.MAX_VALUE); MAX_VALUE + 1 wraps to MIN_VALUE.

los.do: Explain why a double calculation is approximate, and compare doubles with a tolerance instead of ==.
los.ek: A double stores a binary fraction in 64 bits, so 0.1 is inexact and 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 is false; test Math.abs(a − b) < tol.

topics.title: APIs, method signatures and the Math class

los.do: Read API documentation to find what a class provides and which method to call.
los.ek: Documentation gives each method's signature (name, parameter types in order) and return type; a caller needs nothing more.

los.do: Write a call to a void or non-void method with arguments that match its signature, and pick which overload runs.
los.ek: Arguments match parameters by number, order and type; overloads share a name but differ in parameter list; a non-void result must be stored or used or it is lost.

los.do: Call a static (class) method as ClassName.method(...) and give the value it returns.
los.ek: Static methods belong to the class, not to an object; inside the same class the class name can be left off.

los.do: Write a comment stating what a method does, its preconditions and its postconditions.
los.ek: A precondition must be true before the call (the caller's job); a postcondition is what the method guarantees afterwards.

los.do: Evaluate expressions with Math.abs, Math.pow, Math.sqrt and Math.random, including mapping Math.random to an integer range.
los.ek: Math.random() is a double in [0.0, 1.0); (int)(Math.random() * n) + a is an int from a to a + n − 1; pow and sqrt return double.

los.do: Explain how a class relates to its objects, and declare a reference variable that holds an object or null.
los.ek: A class is the blueprint; each object is an instance with its own state; a reference variable holds null or the address of an object.

los.do: Create an object with new, choosing the constructor from its parameter list.
los.ek: new ClassName(args) allocates the object and runs the constructor whose parameters match the arguments.

los.do: Call instance methods on an object, trace how its state changes, and predict a NullPointerException.
los.ek: obj.method() acts on that object's fields; calling a method through a null reference throws NullPointerException.

los.do: Predict the effect of aliasing — two references to one object — after a change through either reference.
los.ek: b = a copies the reference, not the object; a change made through b is seen through a.

los.do: Create and concatenate String objects and predict the result.
los.ek: Strings are immutable: concatenation and every String method build a new String, leaving the original unchanged.

los.do: Evaluate length, substring, indexOf, equals and compareTo calls on strings.
los.ek: Indices run 0 to length() − 1; substring(a, b) is characters a to b − 1 (length b − a); indexOf returns −1 when absent; compareTo is negative, zero or positive in dictionary order.

los.do: Distinguish == from equals when comparing strings and other objects.
los.ek: == asks whether two references point to the same object; equals compares contents.

los.do: Evaluate relational expressions (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=) to true or false.
los.ek: Relational operators compare two values and produce a boolean; they bind looser than arithmetic, so a + 1 < b compares the sum.

los.do: Trace if, if–else and else-if chains and say which branch runs and what is printed.
los.ek: Exactly one branch of an if / else if / else chain runs — the first whose condition is true; a lone if may run zero times.

los.do: Trace nested if statements, matching each else to its if.
los.ek: Without braces an else attaches to the nearest unmatched if, whatever the indentation suggests.

los.do: Write a selection algorithm from a stated rule, such as grade bands or the leap-year rule.
los.ek: Order else-if conditions so no earlier condition shadows a later one; leap year: divisible by 4 and (not by 100, or by 400).

los.do: Evaluate expressions with &&, || and !, including short-circuit evaluation.
los.ek: ! binds tightest, then &&, then ||; && skips its right side when the left is false, || when the left is true — so x != 0 && y / x > 1 never divides by zero.

los.do: Rewrite a negated compound condition with De Morgan's laws.
Decide whether two boolean expressions are equivalent with a truth table or one counterexample.
los.ek: n boolean inputs give 2ⁿ rows; one row where they differ proves they are not equivalent.

los.do: Trace a while loop and give the number of iterations and the final value of each variable.
los.ek: The condition is checked before every pass, so the body may run zero times; something in the body must move the condition toward false.

los.do: Identify a loop that never runs or never stops, and fix its initialisation, condition or update.
los.ek: Check three things: the start value, the stopping condition, and that the update moves toward it.

los.do: Write a condition-controlled loop for an unknown number of repetitions, such as peeling the digits off an int or halving until below a threshold.
los.ek: n % 10 is the last digit and n / 10 drops it; the loop ends when n reaches 0.

los.do: Count the iterations of a for loop from its header, for any start, bound and step.
los.ek: for (int i = a; i < b; i++) runs b − a times; with i <= b, b − a + 1 times; with i += k, ⌈(b − a)/k⌉ times (zero if a ≥ b).

los.do: Trace a for loop and give its output or the final value of an accumulator.
los.ek: Order of one pass: test the condition, run the body, then the update; the loop variable is out of scope after the loop.

los.do: Find and fix an off-by-one error in a loop's start value or bound.
los.ek: Check the first and last pass by hand: indices 0 to n − 1 need i = 0 and i < n.

los.do: Implement and trace the accumulator patterns: sum, average, product and count of matches.
los.ek: Initialise before the loop (0 for sums and counts, 1 for products), update inside it, use the result after it; divide by a count as a double.

los.do: Implement and trace a running minimum or maximum.
los.ek: Initialise to the first value, not 0, so all-negative data still works.

los.do: Implement digit and divisibility algorithms: digit sum, factor list, primality test, gcd.
los.ek: Trial division up to √n settles primality; Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) until b = 0.

los.do: Traverse a string with substring or charAt to count or locate characters or substrings.
los.ek: s.substring(i, i + 1) for i from 0 to s.length() − 1; a window of length k needs i <= s.length() − k.

los.do: Build a new string in a loop: reverse it, remove a character, or test for a palindrome.
los.ek: Start from an empty string and concatenate; reversing prepends each character, or appends while counting down from the end.

los.do: Count how many times an inner-loop statement runs in nested loops, including triangular bounds.
los.ek: Independent bounds multiply (n·m); an inner j from i + 1 to n − 1 over i = 0 … n − 1 gives n(n − 1)/2.

los.do: Trace nested loops that print a pattern and give the exact output.
los.ek: The inner loop runs to completion for each pass of the outer loop; println placement decides the line breaks.

los.do: Compare algorithms by counting statement executions as a function of input size n.
los.ek: One loop over n ~ n; nested ~ n²; halving each pass ~ log₂ n; polynomial counts run in reasonable time, exponential ones do not.

topics.title: Abstraction, design and anatomy of a class

los.do: Decompose a described task into classes and methods, naming each class's attributes and behaviours.
los.ek: Abstraction hides how something works behind what it does; nouns in the description suggest classes and fields, verbs suggest methods.

los.do: Write a class with private instance variables and public methods, and say what code outside the class can use.
los.ek: Encapsulation: fields private, interface public; outside code reaches state only through public methods.

los.do: Write a constructor that sets every instance variable from its parameters.
los.ek: A constructor has the class name and no return type; it runs once, when new creates the object.

los.do: Predict the default values of instance variables a constructor leaves unset.
los.ek: Unset fields are 0 (int), 0.0 (double), false (boolean) and null (references); a class with no constructor written gets a no-argument default.

los.do: Write accessor and mutator methods with the correct return types.
los.ek: An accessor returns a value without changing state; a mutator, usually void, changes it; a non-void method must return on every path.

los.do: Predict whether a method call changes the caller's variable, for primitive and for reference arguments.
los.ek: Java passes copies of values: reassigning a parameter never affects the caller, but changing the object a reference parameter points to does.

los.do: Trace a sequence of calls on objects of a user-written class and give every object's final state.
los.ek: Each object has its own copy of the instance variables; track them in a table, one column per object.

los.do: Identify who a program's design affects and the legal or ethical constraints on it, such as licences on reused code and privacy of stored data.
los.ek: Code taken from elsewhere must be credited and used under its licence; a design decides what data is kept, and for how long.

los.do: Predict the value of a static variable shared by all instances, such as an instance counter.
los.ek: A static variable has one copy per class, shared by every object; static methods cannot use instance variables or this.

los.do: Decide which variable a name refers to when a parameter or local shadows a field, and resolve it with this.
los.ek: A local exists only inside its block; the innermost declaration wins; this.x always names the field.

los.do: Identify what a data set and its metadata can tell you, and what cleaning it needs (missing, invalid or inconsistent entries).
los.ek: Metadata (units, source, date) describes the data; correlation in data does not show causation; invalid entries must be removed or fixed before analysis.

los.do: Identify privacy, bias and consent risks in collecting a data set, including personally identifiable information.
los.ek: Data that under-represents a group biases every result built on it; combined fields (ZIP + birth date + sex) can identify a person.

los.do: Create an array, give its length and default element values, and access an element by index.
los.ek: new int[n] has indices 0 to n − 1, filled with 0 (0.0, false, null for other types); arr.length is a field, no parentheses; an initialiser list {…} fixes the length.

los.do: Predict an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException from an index expression.
los.ek: Valid indices satisfy 0 ≤ i < arr.length; arr[arr.length] is always out of bounds.

los.do: Traverse an array with an indexed for loop and with an enhanced for loop, and say which one can change the array.
los.ek: for (int x : arr) hands out copies of the elements, so assigning x leaves arr unchanged; modifying needs an index.

los.do: Trace a traversal that steps by 2, skips elements or runs backwards, and list the indices it visits.
los.ek: Backwards: for (int i = arr.length − 1; i >= 0; i−−); the first and last index visited settle off-by-one questions.

los.do: Implement sum, mean, minimum, maximum and count-matching over an array.
los.ek: The Unit 2 accumulator patterns, with arr[i] as the value at each pass.

los.do: Implement algorithms over adjacent pairs: detect a repeat, check that the array is sorted, count increases.
los.ek: Comparing arr[i] with arr[i + 1] needs i < arr.length − 1.

los.do: Reverse, shift or rotate an array in place and give its contents afterwards.
los.ek: Reverse by swapping i with length − 1 − i for i < length / 2; a rotation must save the element it is about to overwrite.

los.do: Read a text file line by line with Scanner and File, splitting each line into fields.
los.ek: while (sc.hasNextLine()) reads to the end; line.split(",") turns a CSV line into a String[]; opening a missing file throws FileNotFoundException, which must be declared or caught.

los.do: Predict autoboxing and unboxing between int and Integer, and parse numbers from strings.
los.ek: Integer.parseInt("42") gives 42; an int is boxed to Integer automatically when stored in a collection; unboxing a null Integer throws NullPointerException.

los.do: Predict the contents and size of an ArrayList after add, add(i, x), set, remove and get.
los.ek: add(i, x) shifts later elements right; remove(i) shifts them left and returns the removed element; size(), not length.

los.do: Find and fix the skipped-element bug when removing from an ArrayList inside a forward indexed loop.
los.ek: After remove(i) the next element slides into index i: don't increment that pass, or loop backwards; removing inside an enhanced for throws ConcurrentModificationException.

los.do: Create a 2D array and give its number of rows, number of columns and the element at [r][c].
los.ek: int[][] g = new int[R][C]; g.length = R; g[0].length = C; g[r][c] is row r, column c (row-major).

los.do: Trace row-major and column-major nested traversals and give the visiting order or output.
los.ek: Row-major: outer loop over rows, inner over columns; swap the loops for column-major.

los.do: Implement 2D algorithms: row sums, column sums, the main diagonal and in-bounds neighbours.
los.ek: The main diagonal is g[i][i]; neighbour (r + dr, c + dc) exists only if 0 ≤ r + dr < R and 0 ≤ c + dc < C.

los.do: Trace a linear search and count its comparisons in the best and worst case.
los.ek: Best case 1 comparison (first element), worst case n (last or absent).

los.do: Trace an iterative binary search on a sorted array: list the midpoints examined and count the iterations.
los.ek: mid = (low + high) / 2, then discard the half that cannot hold the target; needs sorted data; at most ⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1 iterations.

los.do: Trace selection sort and give the array after k passes.
los.ek: Pass k swaps the smallest remaining element into index k; always n(n − 1)/2 comparisons, whatever the input.

los.do: Trace insertion sort, give the array after k passes, and count comparisons in the best and worst case.
los.ek: Pass k inserts element k into the sorted prefix; already sorted: n − 1 comparisons; reverse sorted: n(n − 1)/2.

topics.title: Recursion, recursive search and merge sort

los.do: Trace a recursive method and give its return value (factorial, digit sum, power).
los.ek: Each call gets its own parameters; the base case stops the descent; results combine as the calls return, last called first finished.

los.do: Find and fix a missing or unreachable base case that causes a StackOverflowError.
los.ek: Every recursive call must move the argument toward a base case that is actually tested.

los.do: Count the calls a recursive method makes, including two-branch recursion such as naive Fibonacci.
los.ek: One recursive call per level: n + 1 calls; naive fib(n) with base cases 0 and 1 makes 2·fib(n + 1) − 1 calls — exponential.

los.do: Trace recursive binary search and merge sort, giving the subarrays at each level of recursion.
los.ek: Merge sort halves down to single elements, then merges sorted halves: about n log₂ n comparisons, recursion depth ⌈log₂ n⌉.

los.do: Resolve an absolute or relative path (with ., .. and ~) from a given working directory to the directory or file it names.
los.ek: / is the root; a path not starting with / is relative to pwd; .. is the parent, . the current directory, ~ your home.

los.do: Predict the output of a sequence of cd, pwd and ls (-a, -l, -F) commands.
los.ek: cd with no argument returns home; ls -a shows hidden dot-files; -F marks directories with /.

los.do: Predict the file tree after mkdir, touch, cp, mv and rm commands.
los.ek: mv moves or renames and silently overwrites; cp copies; rm deletes for good (no trash); cp and rm need -r for directories.

los.do: Expand a wildcard pattern (*, ?) against a directory listing.
los.ek: The shell expands *.pdb before the command runs; * matches any run of characters, ? exactly one.

los.do: Predict the output of wc, sort (-n, -r), head, tail, cut and uniq on given text.
los.ek: sort is alphabetical unless -n (so 10 sorts before 2); uniq removes only adjacent duplicates, so sort first; wc -l counts lines.

los.do: Build a pipeline with |, > and >> that answers a question about files, and predict its output.
los.ek: > overwrites a file, >> appends; | sends one command's standard output to the next command's input.

los.do: Trace a shell for loop over files and list the commands it runs, including variable expansion and quoting.
los.ek: for f in *.dat; do ...; done expands $f once per file; write "$f" so a name with spaces stays one argument.

los.do: Write a script that uses $1, $@ and $#, and predict what it does for given arguments.
los.ek: $1 is the first argument, $@ all of them, $# how many; run it with bash script.sh args.

los.do: Make a script executable and run it, and diagnose 'command not found' and 'permission denied'.
los.ek: chmod +x script.sh, then ./script.sh — the current directory is not on PATH, so a bare script.sh is not found.

los.do: Predict which lines grep matches with -i, -v, -w, -n, -c and -r.
los.ek: -i ignores case, -v inverts, -w matches whole words, -n numbers lines, -c counts, -r searches directories.

los.do: Predict which files find selects with -name, -type and -maxdepth, and feed its result to another command with $(...).
los.ek: Quote the pattern (find . -name '*.txt') so the shell does not expand it first; $(command) is replaced by that command's output.

los.do: Explain what a commit records and why it beats keeping copies like thesis_final_v2.
los.ek: A commit is a snapshot of the staged files with author, time, message and a link to its parent; history is the chain of commits.

los.do: Predict git status (untracked, modified, staged) after edits, git add and git commit.
los.ek: Working tree → git add → staging area → git commit → repository; only staged changes go into a commit.

los.do: Read git log and git diff output, and name a commit with HEAD, HEAD~n or a hash prefix.
los.ek: HEAD is the current commit, HEAD~1 its parent; git diff shows unstaged changes, git diff --staged staged ones; + lines added, − lines removed.

los.do: Choose the command that undoes a change: discard a file's edits, unstage it, or revert a commit.
los.ek: git restore file discards working-tree edits; git restore --staged file unstages; git revert makes a new commit that undoes an old one without rewriting history.

topics.title: Ignoring files and what not to commit

los.do: Predict which files a .gitignore excludes, including directory patterns and ! negation.
los.ek: *.dat ignores every .dat file; results/ ignores a directory; !keep.dat re-includes one; files already tracked are not affected.

los.do: Decide what stays out of a repository (secrets, large raw data, generated output) and add a licence and citation file to shared code.
los.ek: A secret pushed once stays in history; with no licence, others may not legally reuse the code; CITATION.cff tells people how to cite it.

los.do: Predict the state of the local and remote repositories after clone, push and pull.
los.ek: clone copies the whole history and names the source origin; push sends local commits; pull is fetch + merge; a push is rejected if the remote has commits you lack.

los.do: Create and switch branches, and predict which commits each branch contains after new commits and a merge.
los.ek: A branch is a movable pointer to a commit; git switch -c name creates one; a fast-forward merge only moves the pointer, otherwise merge makes a two-parent commit.

los.do: Read conflict markers and resolve a merge conflict to a stated intended result.
los.ek: <<<<<<< HEAD marks your side, ======= separates, >>>>>>> branch ends theirs; edit to the final text, delete the markers, then add and commit.

los.do: Translate a short Java method into Python: indentation for blocks, no type declarations, print().
los.ek: A colon plus indentation marks a block; names are bound by assignment and carry no declared type; # starts a comment.

los.do: Evaluate Python arithmetic with /, //, %, ** and mixed int/float, and say where it differs from Java.
los.ek: 7 / 2 = 3.5 always; 7 // 2 = 3 but −7 // 2 = −4 (floor, where Java truncates to −3); −7 % 2 = 1; ints never overflow; 2 ** 10 = 1024.

los.do: Predict the truthiness of values and the result of and, or, not and chained comparisons.
los.ek: 0, 0.0, '', [], {} and None are falsy; and / or return one of their operands, not just True or False; 1 < x < 5 chains.

los.do: List the values range(start, stop, step) produces and count them, including negative steps.
los.ek: range stops before stop: range(2, 10, 3) → 2, 5, 8; len(range(a, b)) = b − a; range(5, 0, −1) → 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.

los.do: Trace for loops over lists, strings, enumerate and zip, and while loops with break and continue.
los.ek: for x in seq yields elements, not indices; enumerate yields (i, x); zip stops at the shorter sequence; break leaves the loop, continue skips to the next pass.

los.do: Evaluate indexing and slicing with negative indices and steps on lists and strings.
los.ek: s[−1] is the last element; s[a:b] runs a to b − 1; s[::−1] reverses; a slice out of range is empty, never an IndexError.

los.do: Predict a list after append, extend, insert, pop and remove, and tell sort() from sorted().
los.ek: List methods change the list in place and return None (so a = a.sort() loses it); sorted() returns a new list.

los.do: Predict the effect of aliasing versus copying lists, including lists of lists.
los.ek: b = a aliases; a[:] or list(a) is a shallow copy; [[0] * 3] * 2 repeats one inner list, so changing one row changes both.

los.do: Write and evaluate a list comprehension with a condition.
los.ek: [f(x) for x in seq if test(x)] filters, then maps, in one expression.

los.do: Predict a dictionary after insertions, updates and deletions, and count items with one.
los.ek: Keys are unique; d[k] raises KeyError when k is missing, d.get(k, 0) does not; d[k] = d.get(k, 0) + 1 counts occurrences.

los.do: Evaluate string methods (split, strip, join, replace) and f-string formatting with a set precision.
los.ek: f'{x:.3f}' prints 3 decimals, f'{x:.2e}' scientific notation; split() with no argument splits on any run of whitespace.

los.do: Trace a function with default and keyword arguments and give its return value, including an implicit None.
los.ek: A function that reaches its end without return gives None; a default value is evaluated once, when the function is defined.

los.do: Import names from a module and guard script code with if __name__ == '__main__'.
los.ek: import numpy as np binds a module name; code under the guard runs when the file is executed, not when it is imported.

los.do: Read a traceback to find the failing line and the exception type, and handle an expected error with try / except.
los.ek: Read a traceback bottom up: the last line names the exception, the frame just above it the line that raised it; catch only the exception you expect.

los.do: Read a text file line by line in a with-block, skip a header, split fields and convert them to numbers.
los.ek: with open(path) as f closes the file automatically; each line keeps its newline until strip(); float('1.5e-3') parses scientific notation.

los.do: Create arrays with np.array, zeros, ones, arange and linspace, and give their shape, dtype and length.
los.ek: np.arange(0, 1, 0.25) excludes the end (4 values); np.linspace(0, 1, 5) includes it (5 values, spacing 0.25); all-integer input gives an int dtype.

los.do: Index and slice 1-D and 2-D arrays, including x[:, 0], x[1:, ::2] and boolean masks.
los.ek: x[i, j] is row i, column j; x[:, j] is column j; a slice is a view (writing to it changes x), x[mask] is a copy.

los.do: Reduce an array along an axis (sum, mean, max) and give the shape of the result.
los.ek: For shape (R, C), axis=0 collapses the rows and leaves C values (one per column); axis=1 leaves R; no axis gives a single number.

los.do: Replace an explicit loop with an element-wise array expression that gives the same result.
los.ek: x**2 + 3*x acts element by element in compiled code — typically 10–100× faster than the same Python loop.

los.do: Decide whether two shapes broadcast and give the result's shape.
los.ek: Align shapes from the right; each pair of dimensions must be equal or 1: (3, 1) with (4,) gives (3, 4); (3,) with (4,) fails.

los.do: Tell element-wise * from the matrix product @ and give the shape of each result.
los.ek: (n, k) @ (k, m) → (n, m); * needs broadcastable shapes and multiplies matching entries.

los.do: Compute all pairwise distances among N particles by broadcasting, giving each intermediate shape.
los.ek: r[:, None, :] − r[None, :, :] has shape (N, N, 3); the norm over the last axis gives the (N, N) distance matrix, zero on the diagonal.

los.do: Load a numeric text file with np.loadtxt or np.genfromtxt using delimiter, skiprows and usecols, and give the shape of the result.
los.ek: Lines starting with # are skipped by default; a CSV needs delimiter=','; unpack=True returns the columns as separate arrays.

los.do: Compute summary statistics of a column (mean, std, min, argmax) and select the rows that meet a condition.
los.ek: np.argmax returns the index, not the value; np.std divides by N unless ddof=1 (sample standard deviation).

los.do: Save an array to a text or .npy file and reload it unchanged.
los.ek: np.save / np.load keep dtype and full precision; np.savetxt writes text, set fmt and header for readable columns.

los.do: Plot y against x with matplotlib, label the axes with units, add a legend and save the figure.
los.ek: plt.plot(x, y, label='…'); plt.xlabel('t (ps)'); plt.legend(); call plt.savefig('fig.png', dpi=300) before plt.show().

los.do: Choose linear, semilog or log-log axes from the expected relationship, and read an exponent or rate from the straight line.
los.ek: y = a·e^(−kt) is straight on semilog-y with slope −k (natural log); y = a·xⁿ is straight on log-log with slope n.

los.do: Write a forward-Euler loop for dy/dt = f(y, t), compute the number of steps, and give y after a few steps.
los.ek: y_(n+1) = y_n + Δt·f(y_n, t_n); steps = T/Δt; global error shrinks in proportion to Δt.

los.do: Integrate a 1-D harmonic oscillator with velocity Verlet and trace the first steps.
los.ek: v += (Δt/2)·a; x += Δt·v; a = F(x)/m; v += (Δt/2)·a — one force evaluation per step.

los.do: Track total energy along a trajectory and diagnose a timestep that is too large.
los.ek: Velocity Verlet keeps the energy bounded, oscillating about its start; Euler's energy grows steadily; Δt should be a small fraction (≲ 1/20) of the fastest period.

los.do: Compute the Lennard-Jones energy and force for a pair of particles, then vectorise it over all pairs.
los.ek: U = 4ε[(σ/r)¹² − (σ/r)⁶]; F(r) = (24ε/r)[2(σ/r)¹² − (σ/r)⁶]; minimum at r = 2^(1/6)σ with U = −ε.

los.do: Seed a random number generator so a run reproduces exactly, and draw initial velocities from a normal distribution.
los.ek: rng = np.random.default_rng(seed); rng.normal(0, σ, size=(N, 3)); the same seed gives the same stream.

los.do: Test a numerical function against a case with a known answer, using a tolerance.
los.ek: np.isclose / np.allclose with rtol and atol; e.g. a harmonic oscillator must return to its start after one period 2π√(m/k).

los.do: Organise an analysis as a script with functions and command-line arguments that writes its outputs to files, run from the shell and tracked in Git.
los.ek: Inputs from sys.argv or argparse, results to files, no hand edits between steps — so one command reruns everything.

los.do: Describe how data crosses the internet in packets, and what IP, TCP, HTTP and DNS each do.
los.ek: Data is split into packets that may take different routes and arrive out of order; IP addresses and routes, TCP reassembles and resends, DNS maps names to addresses, HTTP carries web requests.

los.do: Compute the run time and speedup of a workload split across processors.
los.ek: Parallel time = sequential part + the longest parallel branch; speedup = sequential time / parallel time, capped by the part that cannot be split.

los.do: Choose lossless or lossy compression for a kind of data, and run-length encode a short string.
los.ek: Lossless restores every bit (text, code, trajectories); lossy discards detail people won't notice (photos, audio); AAAABB → 4A2B.

los.do: Identify beneficial and harmful effects of a computing innovation, including the digital divide and bias built into its data.
los.ek: One innovation can help some groups and harm others; unequal access and unrepresentative training data both shift who benefits.

los.do: Decide whether two propositional formulas are equivalent, by truth table or by algebraic laws.
los.ek: Equivalent ⇔ same truth value on every assignment; p → q ≡ ¬p ∨ q; De Morgan swaps ∧ and ∨ under negation.

los.do: Prove a claim about a recursive definition or a loop by induction, naming base case, hypothesis and step.
los.ek: Weak induction assumes P(k) to show P(k+1); strong induction assumes all P(j ≤ k); structural induction follows the recursive definition.

los.do: Count arrangements or selections with the product rule, permutations, combinations and inclusion–exclusion, giving a number.
los.ek: Order matters ⇒ P(n,k) = n!/(n−k)!; order ignored ⇒ C(n,k); |A ∪ B| = |A| + |B| − |A ∩ B|.

los.do: Evaluate a summation or simple linear recurrence in closed form (e.g. T(n) = T(n−1) + n).
los.ek: Σ i = n(n+1)/2; Σ 2^i = 2^(n+1) − 1; geometric series with ratio < 1 is bounded by its first term.

los.do: Compute degrees, connectivity, and whether a small graph is bipartite, acyclic or a tree.
los.ek: Σ deg = 2|E|; a tree on n vertices has n − 1 edges; bipartite ⇔ no odd cycle.

los.do: Compute the mean, standard deviation and a confidence interval from repeated benchmark runs, and decide whether two configurations differ.
los.ek: CI ≈ x̄ ± t·s/√n; overlapping intervals do not prove no difference; report variance, not one run.

los.do: Compute an expected count (collisions, comparisons, hits) using linearity of expectation over indicator variables.
los.ek: E[ΣX_i] = ΣE[X_i] even when the X_i are dependent; E[indicator] = P(event).

los.do: Apply Bayes' rule to a detector or classifier scenario and find the probability an alert is real.
los.ek: P(A|B) = P(B|A)P(A)/P(B); a low base rate makes most positives false even for an accurate test.

los.do: Rank a set of functions by growth rate (constant, log, polylog, polynomial, exponential, factorial).
los.ek: log n ≪ n^ε ≪ n^k ≪ c^n ≪ n!; bases of logs differ by a constant factor.

los.do: Compute the Big-O of described or shown code — nested loops, dependent bounds, index doubling or halving — as an auto-checked answer.
los.ek: Nested independent loops multiply; i *= 2 runs log n times; Σ_{i=1..n} i = Θ(n²); sequential blocks add, the largest wins.

los.do: Write the running-time recurrence of a recursive function from its code.
los.ek: T(n) = a·T(n/b) + f(n): a recursive calls on size n/b plus non-recursive work f(n).

los.do: Solve a divide-and-conquer recurrence with the master theorem or a recursion tree, naming the case that applies.
los.ek: Compare f(n) with n^(log_b a): smaller ⇒ Θ(n^(log_b a)); equal ⇒ ×log n; larger (regular) ⇒ Θ(f(n)).

los.do: Identify the best-, worst- and average-case inputs of an algorithm and their costs (e.g. quicksort on sorted input).
los.ek: Worst case is a guarantee over all inputs of size n; average case needs an input distribution.

los.do: Compute the amortized cost per operation of a sequence (dynamic-array doubling, binary counter) by the aggregate or accounting method.
los.ek: Doubling capacity costs n total copies over n appends ⇒ O(1) amortized; growing by a constant is O(n) amortized.

los.do: State a loop invariant for an iterative algorithm and use initialization, maintenance and termination to prove it correct.
los.ek: An invariant holds before each iteration; at exit, invariant + negated loop condition ⇒ postcondition.

los.do: Find the boundary input on which a given binary-search or loop variant fails (off-by-one, infinite loop, overflow in mid).
los.ek: Check empty, one-element and target-at-ends inputs; lo + (hi − lo)/2 avoids overflow; the interval must shrink every step.

los.do: State the cost of access, insert-at-front, append and delete for arrays, dynamic arrays, singly and doubly linked lists and deques.
los.ek: Arrays: O(1) index, O(n) front insert; linked lists: O(1) splice given the node, O(n) index; contiguous memory is cache-friendly.

los.do: Trace insertions into a hash table under chaining, linear probing or double hashing for a given hash function, giving the final table.
los.ek: Linear probing tries h, h+1, h+2 … mod m; deletion under open addressing needs tombstones.

los.do: Compute the load factor and expected probes for a hash table and decide when it must resize.
los.ek: α = n/m; chaining: expected chain length α; linear probing degrades sharply above α ≈ 0.7.

los.do: Trace BST insertion and deletion and produce the in-, pre- and post-order traversals of the result.
los.ek: In-order of a BST is sorted; deleting a two-child node swaps in its successor; height ranges from log n to n.

los.do: Trace the rotations an AVL or red-black tree performs after an insertion.
los.ek: AVL keeps |balance| ≤ 1 via single or double rotations; both guarantee O(log n) height.

los.do: Compute the height of a B-tree or B+-tree of order m holding n keys and explain why databases use it.
los.ek: Height ≈ log_m n; high fanout makes each level one disk page, so a lookup costs a few I/Os.

los.do: Trace a binary heap's array after insert, extract-min and bottom-up heapify.
los.ek: Children of i at 2i+1, 2i+2; sift-up/down are O(log n); bottom-up build is O(n).

los.do: Choose an adjacency list or matrix for a graph's density and operations and give its space and edge-query cost.
los.ek: List: Θ(V + E) space, O(deg) edge test; matrix: Θ(V²) space, O(1) edge test; sparse graphs favour lists.

los.do: Trace union-find with union by rank and path compression and give the resulting parent array.
los.ek: Both heuristics together give O(α(n)) amortized per operation — effectively constant.

los.do: Pick the data structure for a described access pattern (LRU cache, top-k of a stream, prefix search, range queries, membership with false positives allowed) — auto-checked choice.
los.ek: LRU = hash map + doubly linked list; top-k = size-k min-heap; prefixes = trie; ranges = balanced BST/B-tree; approximate membership = Bloom filter.

los.do: Pick a sort for a scenario by worst-case time, stability, extra space and adaptivity, and explain when counting or radix sort beats Ω(n log n).
los.ek: Comparison sorts need Ω(n log n) comparisons; merge sort is stable, heapsort in-place, quicksort fast on average; radix sort is O(d(n + k)).

los.do: Trace the array after k passes of insertion, selection or bubble sort, a quicksort partition, or a merge step.
los.ek: Insertion sort keeps a sorted prefix; selection places the k-th smallest at pass k; Lomuto/Hoare partitions differ in pivot placement.

los.do: Apply a greedy rule (interval scheduling by earliest finish, Huffman coding) and give its output; for coin change with non-canonical coins, produce the counterexample.
los.ek: Greedy is correct only with the greedy-choice property and optimal substructure, shown by an exchange argument.

los.do: Build a Huffman code for given symbol frequencies and compute the encoded length in bits.
los.ek: Repeatedly merge the two least-frequent nodes; total bits = Σ freq × depth.

los.do: Write the state, recurrence and base cases for a described optimisation problem and give its time and space.
los.ek: Time ≈ (# states) × (work per state); overlapping subproblems + optimal substructure ⇒ DP.

los.do: Fill a DP table (LCS, edit distance, 0/1 knapsack, coin-change count) and read off the optimum and one optimal solution.
los.ek: Each cell is a subproblem combined from already-filled cells; traceback through choices recovers the solution.

los.do: Trace BFS or DFS from a source (neighbours in given order) and give the visit order, BFS distances or DFS discovery/finish times.
los.ek: BFS finds fewest-edge paths using a queue; DFS uses a stack/recursion; both are O(V + E).

los.do: Produce a topological order of a DAG, or report the cycle that prevents one.
los.ek: Kahn: repeatedly remove in-degree-0 vertices; DFS: reverse finish order; a back edge means a cycle.

los.do: Run Bellman–Ford to find distances or detect a negative cycle, and explain why Dijkstra fails with negative edges.
los.ek: V − 1 rounds of relaxing every edge; an improvement in round V means a negative cycle.

los.do: Trace Dijkstra's distance array and settled set after k extractions.
los.ek: Greedily settle the closest unsettled vertex and relax its edges; O((V + E) log V) with a binary heap.

los.do: Compute an MST's weight with Kruskal or Prim and give the order in which edges are chosen.
los.ek: Cut property: the lightest edge crossing any cut is safe; Kruskal uses union-find.

units.title: Models of computation and complexity classes

los.do: Write a regular expression or DFA for a described language, or argue it is not regular.
los.ek: Regular languages cannot count unboundedly (e.g. aⁿbⁿ); pumping lemma gives the contradiction.

los.do: Derive a string from a context-free grammar and show the grammar is ambiguous by giving two parse trees.
los.ek: CFGs capture nesting (balanced brackets) that regular expressions cannot; ambiguity = two leftmost derivations.

los.do: Trace a DFA or NFA on an input string and decide whether it accepts.
los.ek: A DFA has exactly one transition per symbol; an NFA accepts if any path does; every NFA has an equivalent DFA.

los.do: Show a described problem is undecidable by reducing the halting problem to it.
los.ek: If a decider for X would yield a decider for HALT, X is undecidable; Rice's theorem covers non-trivial semantic properties.

los.do: Classify a described problem as in P, NP-complete, or undecidable, and verify a given certificate in polynomial time.
los.ek: NP = polynomially verifiable; NP-complete = in NP and every NP problem reduces to it; P = NP is open.

los.do: State the direction of a polynomial reduction needed to prove a new problem NP-hard, and carry out a small one (3-SAT → independent set, vertex cover ↔ independent set).
los.ek: Reduce a known NP-hard problem TO the new one; S is a vertex cover ⇔ V∖S is an independent set.

los.do: Rewrite a vague requirement as a testable functional or non-functional requirement with an acceptance criterion.
los.ek: Testable = measurable outcome and condition ('p95 latency < 200 ms at 500 rps'); NFRs cover performance, security, usability, reliability.

los.do: Identify which SOLID principle a code snippet violates and the refactoring that fixes it.
los.ek: SRP one reason to change; OCP extend without editing; LSP subtypes substitutable; ISP small interfaces; DIP depend on abstractions.

los.do: Name the design pattern a snippet implements or needs (strategy, observer, factory, adapter, decorator, singleton, repository).
los.ek: Patterns are named solutions to recurring forces: vary an algorithm ⇒ strategy; notify dependents ⇒ observer; wrap an incompatible API ⇒ adapter.

los.do: Predict the commit graph after a git merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert or reset on a described history.
los.ek: Merge adds a two-parent commit; rebase replays commits with new hashes; revert adds an inverse commit; reset moves the branch pointer.

los.do: Design test inputs for a specification by equivalence partitioning and boundary-value analysis.
los.ek: One input per partition plus each boundary and its neighbours; invalid partitions need tests too.

los.do: Compute statement and branch coverage of a test suite on a given snippet, and add the test that raises it.
los.ek: Branch coverage counts each decision outcome; 100% statement coverage can miss a false branch.

los.do: Write pre- and postconditions for a function and decide whether a given Hoare triple holds.
los.ek: {P} S {Q}: if P holds before S and S terminates, Q holds after; assignment rule substitutes backward.

los.do: Compute availability from MTBF and MTTR, and for components in series or redundant parallel; convert nines to downtime per year.
los.ek: A = MTBF/(MTBF + MTTR); series multiply A; parallel 1 − Π(1 − A_i); 99.9% ≈ 8.8 h/yr down.

los.do: Build an ER model with cardinalities for a scenario and map it to relational tables with primary and foreign keys.
los.ek: 1:N ⇒ FK on the N side; M:N ⇒ junction table with composite key; weak entities borrow the owner's key.

los.do: Evaluate a relational-algebra expression (σ, π, ⋈, ∪, −, ρ) on small tables and give the result.
los.ek: Selection filters rows, projection columns (removing duplicates); natural join matches equal-named attributes.

los.do: Write a SQL query with joins, GROUP BY and HAVING for a described question — auto-checked by comparing result sets.
los.ek: WHERE filters rows before grouping, HAVING filters groups after; every non-aggregated SELECT column must be grouped.

los.do: Write a query using a correlated subquery, CTE or window function (rank, running total, top-n per group).
los.ek: Window functions compute over a PARTITION BY … ORDER BY frame without collapsing rows.

los.do: Predict the result of an outer join, a comparison with NULL, or an aggregate over a column containing NULLs.
los.ek: NULL = NULL is unknown, not true; COUNT(*) counts rows, COUNT(col) skips NULLs; LEFT JOIN keeps unmatched left rows with NULLs.

los.do: Compute an attribute closure from a set of FDs and find all candidate keys.
los.ek: X⁺ = everything X determines by repeatedly applying FDs; X is a superkey iff X⁺ = all attributes.

los.do: Determine the highest normal form (1NF–BCNF) a relation satisfies under given FDs.
los.ek: 2NF: no partial dependency on a key; 3NF: every non-trivial FD has a superkey LHS or prime RHS; BCNF: superkey LHS always.

los.do: Decompose a relation into BCNF or 3NF and check the decomposition is lossless and dependency-preserving.
los.ek: Binary split R1, R2 is lossless iff R1 ∩ R2 → R1 or → R2; 3NF synthesis always preserves dependencies, BCNF may not.

los.do: Decide whether a schedule is conflict-serializable by drawing its precedence graph, and give an equivalent serial order.
los.ek: Conflicts: two ops on the same item, different transactions, at least one write; acyclic precedence graph ⇔ conflict-serializable.

los.do: Name the anomaly (dirty read, non-repeatable read, phantom, lost update, write skew) in a described interleaving and the weakest isolation level that prevents it.
los.ek: READ COMMITTED stops dirty reads; REPEATABLE READ stops non-repeatable reads; SERIALIZABLE stops phantoms and write skew.

los.do: Estimate the page I/Os of a lookup or range query with no index, a B+-tree index and a hash index, and pick the index for a workload.
los.ek: Scan = all pages; B+-tree = height + matching leaf pages (+ row fetches if unclustered); hash = ~1–2 I/Os for equality only.

los.do: Choose a data model (relational, document, key-value, wide-column, graph) for a described access pattern and consistency need.
los.ek: Model data around queries in NoSQL; joins and multi-row transactions favour relational; deep traversals favour graph.

los.do: Apply CAP and PACELC to say what a described system gives up during a network partition and in normal operation.
los.ek: During a partition choose consistency or availability; else trade latency against consistency.

los.do: Convert integers between binary, hex and decimal, including n-bit two's complement, and detect overflow.
los.ek: Two's complement range −2^(n−1) … 2^(n−1) − 1; negate = invert + 1; overflow iff same-sign operands give opposite-sign result.

los.do: Decode an IEEE 754 single-precision bit pattern and explain why 0.1 + 0.2 ≠ 0.3 in binary floating point.
los.ek: (−1)^s × 1.f × 2^(e−127); most decimal fractions have no finite binary expansion, so they round.

los.do: Trace register and memory contents through a short RISC-V or x86 instruction sequence.
los.ek: Loads/stores move data between memory and registers; branches compare and set the PC; the stack grows downward.

los.do: Split an address into tag, index and offset bits for a given cache size, block size and associativity.
los.ek: offset = log₂(block bytes); sets = size/(block × ways); index = log₂(sets); tag = rest.

los.do: Simulate a direct-mapped or set-associative LRU cache on an address trace and compute the hit rate — auto-checked.
los.ek: Compulsory, capacity and conflict misses; higher associativity removes conflict misses only.

los.do: Compute average memory access time for a multi-level hierarchy.
los.ek: AMAT = hit time + miss rate × miss penalty, applied recursively per level.

los.do: Compute CPU time from instruction count, CPI and clock rate, and compare two designs.
los.ek: CPU time = IC × CPI / f; the 'iron law' — no single factor alone measures speed.

los.do: Apply Amdahl's law to compute overall speedup, or the fraction that must be sped up to hit a target.
los.ek: S = 1 / ((1 − p) + p/s); the serial fraction caps speedup at 1/(1 − p).

los.do: Apply Little's law and utilisation to relate throughput, latency and queue length in a service.
los.ek: L = λW; utilisation ρ = λ/μ; queueing delay explodes as ρ → 1.

los.do: Predict the output and number of processes created by code that calls fork(), exec() and wait().
los.ek: fork returns 0 in the child and the child PID in the parent; n sequential forks make 2ⁿ processes; exec replaces the image.

los.do: Compute the schedule (Gantt order), average waiting and turnaround time under FCFS, SJF, SRTF, round-robin with quantum q, or priority — auto-checked.
los.ek: Turnaround = completion − arrival; waiting = turnaround − burst; SJF minimises average waiting time; RR trades it for response time.

los.do: Identify the race condition in a shared-memory snippet and give an interleaving that produces a wrong result.
los.ek: count++ is load–add–store; two threads interleaving those steps lose an update.

los.do: Fix a race with a mutex, semaphore or condition variable and trace the semaphore values through a schedule.
los.ek: wait/P decrements and blocks below zero; signal/V increments and wakes one; check condition variables in a while loop.

los.do: Detect deadlock in a resource-allocation or wait-for graph, and run the banker's algorithm to decide whether a state is safe.
los.ek: Deadlock needs mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption and circular wait; safe ⇔ some order lets every process finish.

los.do: Translate a virtual address to a physical one by walking a one- or two-level page table, counting memory accesses — auto-checked.
los.ek: VPN = high bits, offset = low log₂(page size) bits; each level indexes one table; PA = frame × page size + offset.

los.do: Compute page-table size and effective access time with a TLB of given hit rate.
los.ek: Entries = 2^(VA bits − offset bits); EAT = h·(t_TLB + t_mem) + (1 − h)·(t_TLB + (levels + 1)·t_mem).

los.do: Simulate FIFO, LRU and optimal page replacement on a reference string and count page faults.
los.ek: OPT evicts the page used farthest in future; LRU approximates it; FIFO can suffer Belady's anomaly.

los.do: Decide whether a user can read, write or execute a file from its Unix permission bits, owner and group (e.g. chmod 754).
los.ek: Three octal digits for owner/group/other; r = 4, w = 2, x = 1; the first matching class applies.

los.do: Compute the maximum file size for an inode with given direct, single-, double- and triple-indirect pointers.
los.ek: Pointers per block = block size / pointer size; max = (direct + p + p² + p³) × block size.

los.do: Compare a VM and a container for a described deployment by isolation boundary, startup cost and overhead.
los.ek: VMs virtualise hardware with a guest kernel; containers share the host kernel, isolated by namespaces and limited by cgroups.

los.do: Compute transmission, propagation and total delay of a transfer, and the bandwidth–delay product of a link.
los.ek: d_trans = L/R; d_prop = distance/speed; BDP = R × RTT is the data in flight needed to fill the pipe.

los.do: Trace a DNS resolution and an HTTP request, and predict the status code and caching behaviour from given headers.
los.ek: Recursive resolver walks root → TLD → authoritative, caching by TTL; Cache-Control/ETag decide 200 vs 304.

los.do: Trace sequence and acknowledgement numbers through a TCP handshake and data exchange.
los.ek: SYN and FIN each consume one sequence number; ACK = next byte expected.

los.do: Compute link utilisation and throughput for stop-and-wait and sliding-window protocols.
los.ek: U = (W · L/R) / (RTT + L/R), capped at 1; window ≥ BDP keeps the link busy.

los.do: Trace TCP's congestion window across RTTs through slow start, congestion avoidance, a timeout and a triple duplicate ACK.
los.ek: Slow start doubles cwnd per RTT until ssthresh; AIMD adds 1 MSS per RTT; loss halves ssthresh (Reno fast recovery) or resets cwnd (timeout).

los.do: Compute a router's table after one round of distance-vector updates, or by link-state Dijkstra.
los.ek: DV: D_x(y) = min_v (c(x,v) + D_v(y)); link-state floods topology then runs Dijkstra locally.

los.do: Compute the network address, broadcast address, usable host range and host count for an IPv4 CIDR block, or subnet it into k pieces — auto-checked.
los.ek: Mask = prefix ones; network = IP AND mask; hosts = 2^(32 − prefix) − 2; borrowing b bits makes 2^b subnets.

los.do: Forward a packet by longest-prefix match against a routing table.
los.ek: Among matching prefixes, the longest (most specific) wins; 0.0.0.0/0 is the default route.

los.do: Evaluate an ordered firewall rule set against a list of packets and say which are allowed.
los.ek: First match wins; end with default deny; stateful firewalls allow return traffic of established connections.

los.do: Classify a described incident by the CIA property violated and separate threat, vulnerability and risk.
los.ek: Confidentiality, integrity, availability; risk = likelihood × impact of a threat exploiting a vulnerability.

los.do: Apply STRIDE to a data-flow diagram and list one threat and one mitigation per crossed trust boundary.
los.ek: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege; threats concentrate at trust boundaries.

los.do: Identify the vulnerability class in a code snippet — SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, buffer overflow, path traversal, IDOR, TOCTOU race, insecure deserialization — and its CWE — auto-checked.
los.ek: Most classes are untrusted input reaching an interpreter or memory without validation; IDOR is a missing authorization check, not an input bug.

los.do: Give the specific fix for an identified vulnerability (parameterised query, context-aware output encoding, CSRF token/SameSite, bounds check, server-side authorization).
los.ek: Fix the sink, not the symptom: blocklists fail; parameterisation separates code from data.

los.do: Pick the primitive for a goal — confidentiality, integrity, authentication, non-repudiation — among symmetric cipher, hash, MAC, signature and key exchange.
los.ek: Hashes give integrity only against accidents; MACs need a shared key; signatures give non-repudiation; use AEAD for confidentiality + integrity.

los.do: Encrypt and decrypt with toy RSA (small primes): compute n, φ(n), d and c = m^e mod n.
los.ek: d = e⁻¹ mod φ(n); modular exponentiation by repeated squaring; security rests on factoring n.

los.do: Compute password entropy and brute-force time at a given guess rate, and state how passwords must be stored.
los.ek: Entropy = L·log₂(alphabet); time = 2^H / rate; store with a unique salt and a slow hash (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2).

los.do: Trace an OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow with PKCE and identify the token mishandling in a described implementation.
los.ek: Authentication says who; authorization says what; access tokens are bearer credentials; the ID token (OIDC) identifies the user.

los.do: Compute annualised loss expectancy for a risk and decide whether a control is worth its cost.
los.ek: SLE = asset value × exposure factor; ALE = SLE × ARO; a control is justified if ΔALE > its annual cost.

los.do: Predict the output of a snippet that mixes overriding, overloading and dynamic dispatch.
los.ek: Overloads resolve at compile time on static types; overrides dispatch at run time on the object's dynamic type.

los.do: Rewrite a loop with map, filter and reduce, and evaluate an expression built from higher-order functions and closures.
los.ek: A closure captures its defining environment; reduce folds with an accumulator from an initial value.

los.do: Decide whether an expression type-checks and infer the type of a polymorphic function.
los.ek: Hindley–Milner unifies constraints to the most general type, e.g. map : (a → b) → [a] → [b].

los.do: Identify the variance error in a generic subtyping snippet (arrays, List<T>, function parameters).
los.ek: Producers are covariant, consumers contravariant; mutable containers must be invariant; functions are contravariant in arguments.

los.do: Predict a program's output under lexical versus dynamic scope, and under pass-by-value, -reference and -sharing.
los.ek: Lexical scope resolves names where code is written; pass-by-sharing copies the reference, so mutation is visible but rebinding is not.

los.do: Predict the output order of async JavaScript mixing synchronous code, promises, await and setTimeout.
los.ek: Run the call stack to empty, then all microtasks (promise callbacks), then one macrotask (timers, I/O).

los.do: Parse an expression under a grammar's precedence and associativity into an AST and evaluate it.
