los.ek: Lower-precedence operators sit nearer the root; left-associative ⇒ left-leaning tree.

los.do: Trace uniform-cost or A* search — frontier and expansion order — and check whether a heuristic is admissible and consistent.
los.ek: A* expands lowest f = g + h; admissible h never overestimates ⇒ optimal tree search; consistent ⇒ optimal graph search.

los.do: Diagnose under- or overfitting from training and validation curves and choose a remedy.
los.ek: High train and val error ⇒ bias; low train, high val ⇒ variance; regularise, add data or simplify for variance.

los.do: Classify a point by k-NN, or compute the information gain or Gini decrease of a decision-tree split.
los.ek: Entropy H = −Σ p log₂ p; gain = H(parent) − weighted H(children); Gini = 1 − Σ p².

los.do: Compute accuracy, precision, recall and F1 from a confusion matrix and pick the metric a scenario needs.
los.ek: Precision = TP/(TP + FP); recall = TP/(TP + FN); imbalanced classes make accuracy misleading.

los.do: Compute one gradient-descent update for linear or logistic regression on a tiny dataset.
los.ek: w ← w − η∇L; for MSE ∇_w = (2/n)Xᵀ(Xw − y); too large η diverges.

los.do: Compute cosine similarity between embedding vectors and the softmax attention weights for a tiny query–key set.
los.ek: cos = a·b/(|a||b|); attention = softmax(QKᵀ/√d)V; cost grows as n² in sequence length.

los.do: Compute demographic parity and equal-opportunity gaps for a classifier from per-group counts, and name the harm.
los.ek: Parity compares positive rates; equal opportunity compares true-positive rates; the two generally cannot both hold when base rates differ.

los.do: Compute strong- and weak-scaling efficiency from timings and explain the gap with Amdahl and Gustafson.
los.ek: Efficiency = S/p; Gustafson: scaled speedup = p − α(p − 1) when the problem grows with p.

los.do: Compute work, span and parallelism of a task DAG and bound the runtime on p processors.
los.ek: T₁ = work, T∞ = span; parallelism = T₁/T∞; greedy scheduling gives T_p ≤ T₁/p + T∞.

los.do: Assign Lamport timestamps or vector clocks to events in a message diagram and decide whether two events are causally ordered or concurrent.
los.ek: Lamport: L = max(local, received) + 1, consistent with but not implying causality; vector clocks capture happened-before exactly.

los.do: Decide whether quorum settings R, W, N guarantee read-your-latest-write, and place keys on a consistent-hash ring.
los.ek: R + W > N ⇒ read and write quorums overlap; consistent hashing moves ~1/n of keys when a node joins.

los.do: Identify which of Nielsen's usability heuristics a described interface violates.
los.ek: Visibility of status, match with the real world, user control, consistency, error prevention, recognition over recall, …

los.do: Use Fitts's law to compare the movement time for two target layouts.
los.ek: MT = a + b·log₂(1 + D/W); bigger, closer targets are faster; screen edges act as infinitely deep targets.

los.do: Choose an evaluation method (usability test, heuristic review, A/B test, survey) for a question, and decide whether an A/B result is significant.
los.ek: Formative tests find problems with ~5 users; A/B tests measure effects and need a pre-set sample size and two-proportion z-test.

los.do: Compute a colour-contrast ratio and identify the WCAG 2.x failure in a markup snippet (alt text, labels, focus, contrast).
los.ek: Ratio = (L₁ + 0.05)/(L₂ + 0.05); AA needs ≥ 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text; every control needs an accessible name.

los.do: Identify the ACM Code of Ethics principle at stake in a scenario and the action it requires.
los.ek: Avoid harm (1.2) and the public good outrank employer instructions; honesty and competence obligations follow.

los.do: State the obligations a reuse scenario triggers under MIT, Apache-2.0, GPL-3.0 or AGPL-3.0.
los.ek: Permissive: keep notice; Apache adds a patent grant; GPL: distribute derived source; AGPL: network use counts as distribution.

los.do: Check whether a released table is k-anonymous for given quasi-identifiers and name the re-identification risk.
los.ek: Each quasi-identifier combination must appear ≥ k times; k-anonymity does not stop attribute disclosure (l-diversity).

los.do: Estimate the energy and carbon of a compute job from hardware power, utilisation, PUE and grid intensity.
los.ek: kWh = W × h × PUE / 1000; CO₂e = kWh × grid intensity (g/kWh); location and time shift matter.

los.do: Compute a maximum flow and minimum cut with Ford–Fulkerson/Edmonds–Karp, tracing augmenting paths in the residual graph.
los.ek: Max-flow value = min-cut capacity; Edmonds–Karp's BFS paths give O(VE²).

los.do: Model a bipartite matching or assignment problem as a flow network and read the matching from the flow.
los.ek: Unit capacities source → left → right → sink; integral flow ⇒ a matching of the same size.

los.do: Compute the approximation ratio of a greedy algorithm (e.g. maximal-matching vertex cover) on an instance and argue its bound.
los.ek: Ratio = ALG/OPT; taking both endpoints of a maximal matching gives a 2-approximation.

los.do: Compute the KMP failure function for a pattern, or a Rabin–Karp rolling hash across a text window.
los.ek: Failure[i] = length of the longest proper prefix that is also a suffix of pattern[0..i]; rolling hash updates in O(1).

los.do: Trace Raft leader election and log replication through a described sequence of timeouts, votes and crashes.
los.ek: A candidate needs a majority in its term; an entry commits once replicated on a majority; n = 2f + 1 tolerates f crashes.

los.do: Identify where two-phase commit blocks when the coordinator fails, and what consensus-based commit changes.
los.ek: Participants that voted yes cannot decide alone; replicating the coordinator's decision with consensus removes the block.

los.do: Compute the monthly cost of a workload under on-demand, reserved and serverless pricing and pick the cheapest model for its load shape.
los.ek: Serverless bills per request × duration and wins at low or spiky load; reserved wins at steady high utilisation.

los.do: Compute the instances an autoscaler needs for a target load and utilisation, and the origin load left after a cache or CDN with a given hit rate.
los.ek: Instances = ⌈load / (per-instance capacity × target utilisation)⌉; origin load = (1 − hit rate) × requests.

los.do: Choose a shard key for a described dataset and query mix and predict hot-spotting.
los.ek: High-cardinality, evenly-accessed keys spread load; monotonic keys (timestamps) send all writes to one shard.

los.do: Compute a forward pass of a small MLP and the backpropagated gradient for one weight.
los.ek: Chain rule layer by layer: ∂L/∂w = δ_out · a_in; ReLU passes gradient only where its input > 0.

los.do: Count the parameters and output shape of a convolutional or fully-connected layer.
los.ek: Conv params = (k_h·k_w·C_in + 1)·C_out; output = ⌊(n + 2p − k)/s⌋ + 1.

los.do: Trace one k-means iteration (assign, recompute centroids), or compute variance explained by the top PCA components from eigenvalues.
los.ek: k-means minimises within-cluster squared distance and converges to a local optimum; variance explained = λ_i / Σλ.

los.do: Classify a described system by its strategic role (cost leadership, differentiation, focus) and the Porter value-chain activity it changes.
los.ek: IT advantage lasts only if hard to copy — complementary processes and data, not the technology itself.

los.do: Place each application of a portfolio in the McFarlan grid (support, factory, turnaround, strategic) from its current and future impact.
los.ek: Strategic = high current and future impact; factory = high current, low future; the quadrant sets how it should be governed and funded.

los.do: Compute NPV, ROI and payback period of an IT project from its cash flows and discount rate, and accept or reject it.
los.ek: NPV = Σ CF_t/(1 + r)^t − I₀; accept if NPV > 0; payback ignores the time value of money and later flows.

los.do: Compute total cost of ownership over a horizon for build, buy (licence) and SaaS options, including hidden costs.
los.ek: TCO = acquisition + implementation + operation + support + exit; licences are often < 30% of TCO.

los.do: Rank a set of proposed projects by a weighted scoring model under a budget constraint.
los.ek: Score = Σ weight × rating; pick in score-per-cost order until the budget binds, checking dependencies.

los.do: Assign decision rights for an IT decision domain (principles, architecture, infrastructure, applications, investment) to a governance archetype for a scenario.
los.ek: Weill & Ross archetypes: business monarchy, IT monarchy, federal, duopoly, feudal, anarchy; investment is usually business-led.

los.do: Match a governance need to the framework that addresses it — COBIT, ITIL, ISO/IEC 27001, NIST CSF, TOGAF.
los.ek: COBIT governs and audits IT overall; ITIL runs services; 27001 certifies an ISMS; NIST CSF organises cyber risk; TOGAF develops architecture.

los.do: Build a RACI matrix for a described process and find its defects (no A, several A's, no R).
los.ek: Exactly one Accountable per activity; at least one Responsible; Consulted is two-way, Informed one-way.

los.do: Assign an artefact or decision to its architecture domain (business, data, application, technology) and to the TOGAF ADM phase that produces it.
los.ek: ADM: Preliminary, A Vision, B Business, C Information Systems (data + application), D Technology, E Opportunities, F Migration, G Governance, H Change.

los.do: Build a capability map for a described organisation and mark the capabilities where heat-mapped investment should go.
los.ek: Capabilities say what the business does, independent of org chart and systems; they are stable while processes change.

los.do: Classify applications as Tolerate, Invest, Migrate or Eliminate from their business value and technical fit.
los.ek: Gartner TIME: high value + good fit ⇒ invest; high value + poor fit ⇒ migrate; low + good ⇒ tolerate; low + poor ⇒ eliminate.

los.do: Choose an integration style (file transfer, shared database, API/RPC, messaging, event streaming) for a described pair of systems and count point-to-point links avoided by a hub.
los.ek: n systems point-to-point need n(n − 1)/2 links; a bus or hub needs n; asynchronous messaging decouples availability.

los.do: Identify which migration strategy a cloud move uses (rehost, replatform, refactor, repurchase, retire, retain) from its description.
los.ek: Rehost = lift-and-shift; refactor rewrites for cloud-native; repurchase moves to SaaS.

los.do: Model a described business process in BPMN with pools, lanes, gateways and events, and spot the hand-off that causes delay.
los.ek: Exclusive gateway = one path; parallel = all paths; message flows cross pools, sequence flows stay inside one.

los.do: Write a use case (actor, preconditions, main flow, extensions) or user stories with acceptance criteria from an interview transcript.
los.ek: Story = as a <role> I want <goal> so that <benefit>; INVEST: independent, negotiable, valuable, estimable, small, testable.

los.do: Prioritise a requirement list with MoSCoW or Kano and justify which items fall out of a release.
los.ek: Must / Should / Could / Won't (this time); Kano: basic, performance and delighter features age into basics.

los.do: Find the critical path, project duration and each activity's slack from an activity-on-node network — auto-checked.
los.ek: Forward pass gives earliest start/finish, backward pass latest; slack = LS − ES; zero-slack activities form the critical path.

los.do: Compute earned-value metrics (PV, EV, AC, CV, SV, CPI, SPI, EAC) from a status report and say whether the project is over budget or late.
los.ek: CPI = EV/AC, SPI = EV/PV; < 1 means over cost or behind; EAC = BAC/CPI if the trend continues.

los.do: Choose a delivery approach (predictive, agile, hybrid) and a deployment strategy (big bang, phased, parallel, pilot, blue-green, canary) for a described rollout.
los.ek: Parallel running costs most and risks least; canary exposes a small share of users first; regulated or fixed-scope work leans predictive.

los.do: Capture a scenario's data requirements as a conceptual model and choose the data-management technology the domain needs.
los.ek: Conceptual (entities, relationships) → logical (tables, keys) → physical; the access pattern and consistency need pick the store.

los.do: Compute data-quality scores (completeness, validity, uniqueness, timeliness) for a sample table and name the root cause of the worst one.
los.ek: Completeness = non-null / total; uniqueness = distinct keys / rows; quality problems are fixed at the source process, not downstream.

los.do: Assign data owner, steward and custodian roles for a data domain and write the policy decision each makes.
los.ek: Owner is accountable (business); steward defines meaning and quality rules; custodian (IT) operates storage and access.

los.do: Design a star schema for a described analytic question: declare the grain, the fact table measures and the dimensions.
los.ek: State the grain first; facts are additive numeric measures at that grain; dimensions carry descriptive attributes, denormalised.

los.do: Choose the slowly-changing-dimension type (1, 2, 3) for an attribute whose history does or doesn't matter, and show the resulting rows.
los.ek: Type 1 overwrites; type 2 adds a new row with effective dates and a surrogate key; type 3 keeps a previous-value column.

los.do: Choose between ETL into a warehouse, ELT into a lakehouse and streaming ingestion for a described data volume, variety and latency need.
los.ek: ELT pushes transformation to scalable storage; streaming fits seconds-level latency; schema-on-read trades governance for flexibility.

los.do: Write the SQL aggregation that answers a business question over a star schema — auto-checked by result set.
los.ek: Join the fact to the needed dimensions, filter on dimension attributes, GROUP BY the reporting level.

los.do: Match a business question to descriptive, diagnostic, predictive or prescriptive analytics and to a method (dashboard, cohort, regression, classification, optimisation).
los.ek: Descriptive = what happened; diagnostic = why; predictive = what will; prescriptive = what to do.

los.do: Compute the expected profit of acting on a classifier's predictions from its confusion matrix and the cost of each error.
los.ek: Expected value = Σ count × payoff per cell; the best threshold depends on error costs, not accuracy.

los.do: Define a KPI for a described objective with formula, target, owner and data source, and flag a vanity metric.
los.ek: A KPI ties to a decision and has a target; vanity metrics (raw sign-ups, page views) move without changing outcomes.

los.do: Size the servers or cloud instances a described workload needs at peak with headroom, and the cost of each option.
los.ek: Capacity = peak demand / (per-unit capacity × target utilisation); size for peak, not average.

los.do: Choose IaaS, PaaS, SaaS or on-premises for a described system and state who manages each layer under the shared-responsibility model.
los.ek: The provider takes more layers as you move IaaS → PaaS → SaaS; data and identity stay the customer's responsibility in every model.

los.do: Recommend in-house, outsourced, offshored or cloud sourcing for a function using transaction-cost reasoning.
los.ek: Outsource commodity, well-specified work; keep asset-specific, strategic, hard-to-monitor work inside.

los.do: Classify a described event as an incident, problem, service request or change, and the change as standard, normal or emergency.
los.ek: Incident = restore service fast; problem = find the root cause; standard changes are pre-approved and low-risk.

los.do: Compute SLA attainment, MTTR and allowed downtime from an incident log and decide whether a credit is owed.
los.ek: Availability = (agreed time − downtime) / agreed time; MTTR = total repair time / incidents.

los.do: Prioritise an incident from its impact and urgency using a priority matrix.
los.ek: Priority = f(impact, urgency): high/high = P1; priority sets the response and resolution targets.

los.do: Choose a vendor by a weighted evaluation of a set of RFP responses and name the contract terms that protect exit.
los.ek: Weight criteria before scoring; protect exit with data-portability, termination-assistance and escrow clauses.

los.do: Score risks on a likelihood × impact matrix and choose a treatment (avoid, mitigate, transfer, accept) for each.
los.ek: Inherent risk before controls, residual after; accept only within the stated risk appetite.

los.do: Compute ALE before and after a proposed control and its return on security investment.
los.ek: ROSI = (ALE_before − ALE_after − control cost) / control cost.

los.do: Classify a control as preventive, detective or corrective and administrative, technical or physical.
los.ek: Defense in depth layers control types so one failure is caught by another.

los.do: Derive RTO and RPO for a business process from a business-impact analysis, and pick the recovery site and backup frequency that meet them.
los.ek: RPO = tolerable data loss ⇒ backup or replication interval; RTO = tolerable downtime ⇒ hot, warm or cold site.

los.do: Compute what a full, incremental or differential backup schedule must restore after a failure on a given day, and the worst-case data loss.
los.ek: Incremental restore = last full + every incremental since; differential = last full + latest differential; loss = time since last backup.

los.do: Map a described control to its NIST CSF 2.0 function (Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover).
los.ek: Govern was added in 2.0 for strategy and supply-chain risk; the functions run concurrently, not as a sequence.

los.do: Identify the segregation-of-duties conflict in a described set of user roles and propose the compensating control.
los.ek: No one person should both initiate and approve, or both hold assets and record them; where SoD can't be split, add review.

los.do: Predict adoption of a described system from TAM/UTAUT factors and name the intervention that raises it.
los.ek: Perceived usefulness and ease of use drive intention; UTAUT adds social influence and facilitating conditions.

los.do: Place a described organisation's change effort in a change model (Lewin, Kotter, ADKAR) and name the step it skipped.
los.ek: Kotter: urgency, coalition, vision, communicate, empower, short-term wins, consolidate, anchor; skipping urgency stalls most efforts.

los.do: Locate a technology's adopters on the diffusion curve and decide how to cross the chasm to the early majority.
los.ek: Innovators 2.5%, early adopters 13.5%, early majority 34%; the early majority buys whole-product solutions and references.

los.do: Fill a business model canvas for a described digital venture and identify its riskiest assumption.
los.ek: Nine blocks: segments, value proposition, channels, relationships, revenue, resources, activities, partners, costs; test the riskiest first.

los.do: Compute customer lifetime value and CAC payback for a subscription product and decide whether growth is profitable.
los.ek: LTV ≈ ARPU × gross margin / churn; healthy SaaS often wants LTV/CAC ≥ 3 and payback < 12 months.

los.do: Identify the network effects (direct, indirect/two-sided) in a platform and the side to subsidise.
los.ek: Subsidise the side whose participation most attracts the other and that is more price-sensitive.

los.do: Determine whether GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, HIPAA or FERPA applies to a described data flow and the lawful basis or consent it needs.
los.ek: GDPR follows EU data subjects; CCPA/CPRA covers qualifying businesses handling California residents' data; HIPAA covers health data of covered entities; FERPA covers education records.

los.do: Decide when a data-protection impact assessment is required and list the privacy-by-design measures for a described system.
los.ek: High-risk processing (large-scale sensitive data, profiling, monitoring) needs a DPIA; minimise, pseudonymise, limit retention, default to private.

los.do: Analyse a described IS decision with stakeholder, utilitarian and rights-based reasoning and recommend an action.
los.ek: Identify every affected stakeholder; consequences and duties can disagree — state which one governs and why.

los.do: Compare the lifetime carbon and cost of keeping versus refreshing a hardware fleet, including embodied emissions.
los.ek: Embodied carbon of manufacture often exceeds years of use-phase emissions for end-user devices; extending life is usually greener.

topics.title: The three modes and their rate equations

los.do: Identify which modes act in a described system and write the rate law for each.
los.ek: Conduction needs a medium; convection needs fluid motion; radiation needs neither.

los.do: Calculate a conduction flux or rate, or an unknown k, from Fourier's law across a plane layer.
los.ek: q'' = k ΔT / L; heat flows down the temperature gradient.

los.do: Calculate a convection rate from Newton's law of cooling and judge whether h is plausible.
los.ek: q = hA(T_s − T∞); h ~ 2–25 free gas, 25–250 forced gas, 50–20 000 forced liquid, 2 500–100 000 phase change (W/m²·K).

los.do: Calculate net radiation between a small surface and large surroundings, and linearise it to a radiation coefficient h_r.
los.ek: q'' = εσ(T_s⁴ − T_sur⁴) in kelvin; h_r = εσ(T_s + T_sur)(T_s² + T_sur²).

topics.title: Energy balances on control volumes and surfaces

los.do: Apply conservation of energy to a control volume: in − out + generated = stored.
los.ek: Generation is volumetric (I²R, reaction); storage is ρcV dT/dt; both vanish from a surface balance.

los.do: Apply a surface energy balance linking conduction, convection and radiation at a boundary.
los.ek: A surface has no volume: what conducts in, convects and radiates out.

los.do: Find the instantaneous rate of temperature change of a body from an unsteady energy balance.
los.ek: dT/dt = (Σq_in − Σq_out + Ė_g)/(ρcV) at that instant.

units.title: The heat equation and boundary conditions

los.do: Calculate heat flux (magnitude and direction) from a given temperature field.
los.ek: q'' = −k∇T; flux points from hot to cold, normal to isotherms.

los.do: Use k, ρc_p and α = k/ρc_p to compare how materials conduct, store and diffuse heat.
los.ek: High k moves heat; high ρc_p stores it; α sets how fast a disturbance spreads.

los.do: Write the heat equation in Cartesian, cylindrical or spherical coordinates and simplify it for a stated case (steady, 1-D, no generation, constant k).
los.ek: (1/r)d/dr(r dT/dr) and (1/r²)d/dr(r² dT/dr) are the radial Laplacians; each assumption strikes a term.

los.do: From a given T field, find the generation rate, the surface fluxes or the local rate of change ∂T/∂t.
los.ek: k∇²T + q̇ = ρc ∂T/∂t; read each term off the derivatives of T.

los.do: Decide whether a temperature field can be a steady, generation-free solution.
los.ek: Steady, no q̇, constant k ⇒ ∇²T = 0 (Laplace).

los.do: Translate a physical boundary into its mathematical condition: fixed temperature, fixed flux, insulated or symmetry plane, convection, radiation, perfect-contact interface.
los.ek: −k dT/dx|_s = q''_s; insulated or symmetric ⇒ dT/dx = 0; convection: −k dT/dx|_s = h(T_s − T∞); interface: T and k dT/dx continuous.

los.do: Write the complete formulation (equation + two BCs, or + IC) of a 1-D problem from a word description.
los.ek: A second-order ODE needs two independent conditions; a transient one also needs T(x, 0).

los.do: Sketch T(x) and read boundary conditions and k ratios from slopes.
los.ek: Insulated ⇒ zero slope; in series, slope ∝ 1/k; with generation the profile curves (concave down for q̇ > 0).

topics.title: The plane wall and thermal resistance

los.do: Find T(x) and q in a plane wall with fixed-temperature or convective boundaries.
los.ek: No generation ⇒ linear T(x); q is the same at every x.

los.do: Build a series–parallel resistance network for a composite wall and compute q, U and every interface temperature.
los.ek: R_cond = L/kA, R_conv = 1/hA; series add, parallel add as conductances; U = 1/(R_tot A).

los.do: Include thermal contact resistance and judge when it matters.
los.ek: R''_t,c in series at the interface; matters when it rivals L/k of the layers.

los.do: Reason qualitatively about a network: same q in series, largest ΔT across the largest R, which change helps most.
los.ek: ΔT_i / ΔT_tot = R_i / R_tot.

los.do: Find q and T(x) when the cross-section A(x) or k(T) varies, by integrating Fourier's law with q constant.
los.ek: Steady, no q̇ ⇒ q_x constant; q ∫dx/A(x) = −∫k(T)dT.

los.do: Calculate q′ and T(r) for a cylindrical wall or insulated pipe using its resistance.
los.ek: R′ = ln(r₂/r₁)/(2πk); T(r) is logarithmic.

los.do: Calculate q for a spherical shell using its resistance.
Find the critical insulation radius and decide whether adding insulation raises or lowers q.
los.ek: r_cr = k/h (cylinder), 2k/h (sphere); below r_cr insulation increases q.

los.do: State which quantities stay constant with radius in steady radial conduction.
los.ek: q (or q′) is constant; q″ falls as 1/r (cylinder) or 1/r² (sphere).

los.do: Find the surface temperature from an overall energy balance before solving for the profile.
los.ek: Everything generated leaves through the cooled surfaces: q̇V = hA(T_s − T∞).

los.do: Solve for the parabolic T(x) and T_max with symmetric fixed-temperature or convective boundaries.
los.ek: T_max − T_s = q̇L²/2k; the midplane (or insulated face) is adiabatic.

los.do: With unequal face temperatures, locate the maximum and find the flux through each face.
los.ek: x_max = k(T₂ − T₁)/(2q̇L); more heat leaves through the cooler face.

los.do: Analyse a generating layer bonded to non-generating layers, chaining flux, interface and maximum temperatures.
los.ek: Flux leaving the generating layer = q̇L_A and passes unchanged through the plain layers.

los.do: Find surface and centreline temperatures of a solid cylinder or wire with generation, including q̇ from Joule heating.
los.ek: T_s = T∞ + q̇r_o/2h; T₀ − T_s = q̇r_o²/4k; q̇ = I²ρ_e/A².

los.do: Find surface and centre temperatures of a sphere with generation.
los.ek: T_s = T∞ + q̇r_o/3h; T₀ − T_s = q̇r_o²/6k.

los.do: Solve a hollow cylinder with generation and one insulated or convective surface.
los.ek: General T = −q̇r²/4k + C₁ ln r + C₂; apply one BC per surface.

los.do: Find the largest allowable q̇, or the h or thickness needed, to keep T_max below a limit.
los.ek: T_max − T∞ = q̇L/h + q̇L²/2k: a film rise plus a conduction rise.

topics.title: The fin equation and its solutions

los.do: Derive the fin equation from an energy balance on a fin element and compute m for a given geometry.
los.ek: d²θ/dx² − m²θ = 0, m² = hP/kA_c; θ = T − T∞.

los.do: Choose the tip condition (infinite, adiabatic, convective via corrected length) and compute fin heat rate and tip or local temperature.
los.ek: q_f = M tanh mL (adiabatic); M = √(hPkA_c)θ_b; L_c = L + D/4 for a pin.

los.do: Explain why fin temperature decays exponentially rather than linearly, and how to change the decay.
los.ek: Side convection removes heat along the length; larger m (low k, high h, thin) ⇒ faster decay.

los.do: Calculate fin efficiency and effectiveness and decide whether a fin is worthwhile.
los.ek: η_f = q_f/(hA_fθ_b); ε_f = q_f/(hA_c,bθ_b); fins pay off when ε_f ≳ 2, i.e. high k, low h.

los.do: Calculate overall surface efficiency and heat rate of a fin array and its resistance.
los.ek: η_o = 1 − (NA_f/A_t)(1 − η_f); q_t = η_o h A_t θ_b; R_t,o = 1/(η_o h A_t).

los.do: Set up the separable solution for a rectangle with one non-homogeneous edge and evaluate its leading terms.
los.ek: θ = Σ C_n sin(nπx/L) sinh(nπy/L)/sinh(nπW/L); homogeneous BCs set the eigenfunctions.

los.do: Pick the matching shape-factor case and compute q = Sk ΔT.
los.ek: S has units of length; R = 1/Sk; check the geometric validity condition.

los.do: Combine shape-factor resistances with other resistances in a network.
los.ek: Two buried objects ⇒ two resistances in series across T₁ − T₂.

los.do: Write the finite-difference equation of an interior, surface or corner node by an energy balance on its cell, including Δx ≠ Δy, convection and radiation.
los.ek: Each face: conductance × (T_neighbour − T_m); boundary faces get h·ℓ or h_r·ℓ terms; half cells on edges.

los.do: Solve a small node system directly or by Gauss–Seidel iteration and check the energy balance.
los.ek: Iterate T_i = (Σa_jT_j + b)/a_i until changes are below tolerance.

los.do: Compute the Biot number with L_c = V/A_s and decide whether lumped capacitance applies.
los.ek: Bi = hL_c/k < 0.1 ⇒ internal gradients negligible; L_c = r/3 sphere, r/2 cylinder, half-thickness wall.

los.do: Find temperature at a time, or the time to reach a temperature, for a lumped body.
los.ek: θ/θ_i = exp(−t/τ), τ = ρVc/hA_s.

los.do: Find the energy transferred over an interval.
los.ek: Q = ρVcθ_i[1 − exp(−t/τ)].

los.do: Set up and solve a general lumped balance with radiation, surface flux or generation.
los.ek: ρVc dT/dt = q''_sA − hA(T − T∞) − εσA(T⁴ − T_sur⁴) + Ė_g; solve or integrate numerically.

los.do: Compute Bi and Fo and find the centre temperature of a wall, cylinder or sphere with the one-term approximation.
los.ek: θ₀* = C₁exp(−ζ₁²Fo), valid for Fo > 0.2; ζ₁, C₁ from Bi (wall uses half-thickness).

los.do: Find the temperature at another position, or the time to reach a temperature.
los.ek: θ* = θ₀* cos(ζ₁x*) (wall), θ₀* J₀(ζ₁r*) (cylinder), θ₀* sin(ζ₁r*)/(ζ₁r*) (sphere).

los.do: Find the fraction of the maximum energy transferred, Q/Q₀.
los.ek: Wall: Q/Q₀ = 1 − (sin ζ₁/ζ₁)θ₀*; cylinder and sphere have their own forms.

los.do: Find temperature at a depth and time, the depth reached, or the time needed, after a sudden surface temperature change.
los.ek: (T − T_s)/(T_i − T_s) = erf(x/2√(αt)); valid while the far side hasn't felt it.

los.do: Find the temperature in a semi-infinite solid with a constant surface heat flux or with convection at the surface.
los.ek: Flux: T − T_i = (2q″√(αt/π)/k)e^(−x²/4αt) − (q″x/k)erfc(x/2√αt). Convection: erfc η − exp(hx/k + h²αt/k²)erfc(η + h√αt/k); h → ∞ recovers the fixed surface.

los.do: Find the surface heat flux, and the contact temperature when two semi-infinite solids touch.
los.ek: q''_s = k(T_s − T_i)/√(παt); T_s = (√(kρc)_A T_A + √(kρc)_B T_B)/(√(kρc)_A + √(kρc)_B).

los.do: Build a 2-D or 3-D transient solution as a product of 1-D solutions.
los.ek: Short cylinder = infinite cylinder × plane wall, each in dimensionless θ*.

los.do: Write the explicit finite-difference equation for a transient node and check its stability limit.
los.ek: T_m^{p+1} = Fo(T_{m+1}^p + T_{m−1}^p) + (1 − 2Fo)T_m^p; stable if Fo ≤ 1/2 (interior, 1-D).

los.do: Compute Re, Pr and Nu and identify laminar, transitional or turbulent flow.
los.ek: Re_x = u∞x/ν (transition ≈ 5×10⁵ on a plate); Pr = ν/α; Nu = hL/k_f.

los.do: Relate local and average convection coefficients.
los.ek: h̄ = (1/L)∫h_x dx; laminar h_x ∝ x^(−1/2) ⇒ h̄ = 2h_x(L).

los.do: Estimate velocity and thermal boundary-layer thicknesses and how Pr relates them.
Use the Reynolds–Colburn analogy to get h from friction (or friction from h).

topics.title: The flat plate in parallel flow

los.do: Calculate average h and q for laminar flow over a flat plate, with properties at the film temperature.
Calculate average h for a mixed laminar–turbulent boundary layer.

topics.title: Cylinders and spheres in cross flow

los.do: Calculate h and q for a cylinder or sphere in cross flow with the appropriate correlation.
los.ek: Churchill–Bernstein (cylinder, Re Pr > 0.2); Whitaker (sphere, μ ratio).

los.do: Find the maximum velocity, average h and outlet temperature for flow across a tube bank.
los.ek: V_max from the minimum free area (aligned vs staggered); Žukauskas Nu̅ with row correction; log-mean ΔT across the bank.

los.do: Compute Re_D from ṁ and decide whether the flow is laminar and how long the entry regions are.
los.ek: Re_D = 4ṁ/(πDμ); laminar below ≈ 2300; x_fd,h ≈ 0.05 Re_D D; x_fd,t ≈ 0.05 Re_D Pr D.

los.do: Find outlet temperature or required length with uniform wall heat flux.
los.ek: q = ṁc_p(T_m,o − T_m,i) = q''_s πDL; T_m rises linearly.

los.do: Find outlet temperature or heat rate with uniform wall temperature, using the log-mean temperature difference.
los.ek: ΔT_o/ΔT_i = exp(−PL h̄/ṁc_p); q = h̄A_s ΔT_lm.

los.do: Find the outlet temperature when the tube exchanges heat with an external fluid through an overall coefficient U.
los.ek: (T∞ − T_m,o)/(T∞ − T_m,i) = exp(−UA_s/ṁc_p): the constant-T_s result with T∞ and U.

los.do: Use the fully developed laminar results for constant flux or constant wall temperature.
los.ek: Nu_D = 4.36 (uniform q''_s), 3.66 (uniform T_s).

los.do: Calculate h for turbulent flow with Dittus–Boelter (or Gnielinski), choosing the right exponent and property temperature.
los.ek: Nu_D = 0.023 Re^(4/5) Pr^n, n = 0.4 heating, 0.3 cooling; properties at mean T_m.

los.do: Use the hydraulic diameter and annulus results for noncircular passages.
los.ek: D_h = 4A_c/P; laminar Nu depends on shape; annulus uses D_o − D_i.

topics.title: Buoyancy-driven flow and when it matters

los.do: Compute Gr and Ra and identify laminar or turbulent free convection.
los.ek: Ra_L = gβΔT L³/(να); β = 1/T_f for an ideal gas; transition near Ra ≈ 10⁹ on a vertical plate.

los.do: Decide whether free, forced or mixed convection governs.
los.ek: Gr/Re² ≪ 1 forced, ≫ 1 free, ~1 mixed.

los.do: Calculate h for a vertical plate with the Churchill–Chu correlation.
Calculate h for horizontal plates (hot side up or down) and horizontal cylinders and spheres.
los.ek: L = A_s/P for horizontal plates; separate correlations for upper/lower surfaces.

los.do: Calculate heat transfer across a vertical or horizontal enclosure (e.g. double-pane window).
los.ek: Ra_L across the gap; Nu = 1 means pure conduction below the critical Ra.

los.do: Use Stefan–Boltzmann and Wien's law to relate emissive power, peak wavelength and temperature.
los.ek: E_b = σT⁴; λ_max T = 2898 μm·K.

los.do: Find the fraction of blackbody emission in a wavelength band.
los.ek: F(0→λ) from λT (Table 12.2); band = difference of two fractions.

los.do: Find total emissivity or absorptivity from spectral data and apply Kirchhoff's law and the gray-surface assumption.
los.ek: α = ∫α_λG_λdλ / G; ε = α only for a gray or diffuse-gray surface at the same T.

los.do: Solve a surface energy balance with irradiation, emission and convection for a steady surface temperature.
los.ek: αG = εσT⁴ (+ h(T − T∞)) at steady state.

los.do: Find view factors with reciprocity, summation and symmetry, including long ducts and cavities.
los.ek: A_iF_ij = A_jF_ji; Σ_j F_ij = 1; flat or convex surfaces have F_ii = 0.

los.do: Evaluate view factors for standard geometries from formulas or charts.
los.ek: Concentric cylinders/spheres: F₁₂ = 1; coaxial disks, aligned rectangles from Tables 13.1–13.2.

los.do: Calculate net exchange between black surfaces.
los.ek: q_ij = A_iF_ijσ(T_i⁴ − T_j⁴).

los.do: Calculate net exchange in a two-surface gray enclosure (parallel plates, concentric cylinders or spheres).
los.ek: q = σ(T₁⁴ − T₂⁴)/[(1−ε₁)/ε₁A₁ + 1/A₁F₁₂ + (1−ε₂)/ε₂A₂].

los.do: Quantify the effect of radiation shields.
los.ek: Each shield adds two surface resistances and one space resistance in series.

los.do: Solve a three-surface enclosure with a reradiating (adiabatic) surface by the radiosity network.
los.ek: Reradiating: J = E_b at that surface, net q = 0.

los.do: Combine radiation exchange with conduction and convection at a surface or in an enclosure.
los.ek: Radiation and convection from one surface act in parallel; h_r lets radiation join the resistance network.

units.title: Heat exchangers and system-level thermal analysis

los.do: Calculate U for a tube wall including both films, fouling and finned surfaces.
los.ek: 1/UA = 1/(η_o hA)_c + R''_f,c/(η_oA)_c + R_w + R''_f,h/(η_oA)_h + 1/(η_o hA)_h.

los.do: Size a parallel-flow or counterflow exchanger with q = UA ΔT_lm when all inlet and outlet temperatures are known.
los.ek: ΔT_lm = (ΔT₁ − ΔT₂)/ln(ΔT₁/ΔT₂), end differences defined by flow arrangement; counterflow needs less area.

los.do: Apply the LMTD correction factor for shell-and-tube and cross-flow exchangers.
los.ek: q = UAF ΔT_lm,CF with F from P and R charts.

los.do: Find effectiveness and heat rate from NTU and C_r.
los.ek: NTU = UA/C_min; C_r = C_min/C_max; ε from the arrangement's relation; q = εC_min(T_h,i − T_c,i).

los.do: Predict outlet temperatures of an existing exchanger when they are unknown.
los.ek: ε–NTU avoids iteration when outlets are unknown; then energy balances give each outlet.

los.do: Model a device (electronics package, building wall, pipe run) as a network of conduction, convection and radiation resistances and find its operating temperature.
los.ek: One energy balance per node; parallel paths from a surface (convection ∥ radiation); iterate when h_r depends on T.

los.do: Identify the controlling resistance and choose the design change that best meets a temperature limit.
los.ek: Reduce the largest R first; compare options by their effect on R_tot.

los.do: Identify the boiling regime from the excess temperature on the boiling curve.
los.ek: Free convection → nucleate → transition → film; CHF at the nucleate peak.

los.do: Calculate nucleate boiling flux (Rohsenow) and critical heat flux.
los.ek: q''_s ∝ ΔT_e³; q''_max = 0.149 h_fg ρ_v [σg(ρ_l − ρ_v)/ρ_v²]^(1/4).

los.do: Calculate film condensation on a vertical plate or horizontal tube.
los.ek: Nusselt analysis with h′_fg = h_fg(1 + 0.68 Ja); tube constant 0.729.

los.do: Calculate a diffusive flux in a stationary medium with Fick's law, including membranes and solubility.
los.ek: N_A = −D_AB dC_A/dx; at an interface C = S·p.

los.do: Solve transient diffusion into a semi-infinite solid (carburizing, doping) with the error-function solution.
los.ek: (C − C_s)/(C_i − C_s) = erf(x/2√(Dt)); depth scales with √(Dt).

los.do: Calculate evaporation through a stagnant gas column (Stefan flow).
Solve diffusion with a homogeneous reaction.
los.ek: D d²C/dx² − k₁C = 0 ⇒ cosh/sinh profile, like a fin.

topics.title: Convective mass transfer and the analogy

los.do: Use the heat–mass analogy to convert between h and h_m, and Nu and Sh correlations.
los.ek: h/h_m = ρc_p Le^(2/3); Sh = f(Re, Sc) mirrors Nu = f(Re, Pr).

los.do: Solve a coupled heat and mass balance at an evaporating surface (wet bulb).
los.ek: h(T∞ − T_s) = h_m h_fg(ρ_A,s − ρ_A,∞).

los.do: Count ordered selections of distinguishable objects (permutations).
los.ek: N!/(N − k)! ordered ways to fill k slots from N.

los.do: Count arrangements of indistinguishable particles on distinguishable sites.
los.ek: C(M, N) = M!/(N!(M − N)!) — the lattice-gas multiplicity.

los.do: Count distinct sequences of a multiset (multinomial coefficient).
los.ek: N!/(n_A! n_B! …); identical units are not reordered.

los.do: Apply Stirling's approximation to ln W for large N.
los.ek: ln N! ≈ N ln N − N; turns ln C(M, N) into −M Σ x ln x.

los.do: Calculate the probability of exactly k outcomes in N independent two-outcome trials.
Calculate an 'at least one' probability through the complement.
los.ek: P(≥ 1) = 1 − (1 − p)^N for independent events.

los.do: Calculate the mean and variance of a discrete distribution.
los.ek: ⟨x⟩ = Σ p_i x_i; σ² = ⟨x²⟩ − ⟨x⟩².

units.title: Entropy, equilibrium and the fundamental equation

topics.title: Multiplicity and S = k ln W

los.do: Calculate the multiplicity of a system of independent two-state units with a given number excited.
los.ek: W = N!/(n!(N − n)!); S = k_B ln W.

los.do: Calculate the multiplicity of an Einstein solid with N oscillators and q quanta.
Calculate ΔS from the change in multiplicity of a lattice or spin system.
los.ek: ΔS = k_B ln(W₂/W₁).

los.do: Derive the entropy of isothermal ideal-gas expansion by lattice counting.
los.ek: W ∝ M^N, M ∝ V ⇒ ΔS = nR ln(V₂/V₁).

los.do: Calculate the probability of each energy split between two solids in thermal contact and identify the most probable one.
los.ek: P(q_A) ∝ W_A(q_A) W_B(q − q_A); the peak sharpens as N grows.

los.do: Derive equality of T, P and μ by maximising total entropy over exchange of U, V and N.
los.ek: ∂S/∂U = 1/T, ∂S/∂V = P/T, ∂S/∂N = −μ/T must match across the wall.

los.do: Show that maximum entropy at fixed U is equivalent to minimum energy at fixed S.
los.ek: Internal constraints released ⇒ S rises (second law); the energy-minimum principle is its inverse.

topics.title: The fundamental equation and its integrated forms

los.do: Find T, P or μ as derivatives of a given S(U, V, N).
los.ek: dS = (1/T)dU + (P/T)dV − (μ/T)dN.

los.do: Find T, P or μ as derivatives of a given U(S, V, N).
los.ek: dU = T dS − P dV + μ dN.

los.do: Check that a proposed fundamental equation is extensive (first-order homogeneous).
los.ek: S(λU, λV, λN) = λS(U, V, N); exponents of extensive variables sum to 1.

los.do: Calculate U, or any one term, from the Euler relation.
los.ek: U = TS − PV + μN; equivalently G = μN for one component.

los.do: Apply the Gibbs–Duhem equation to relate changes in the intensive variables.
los.ek: S dT − V dP + N dμ = 0; at fixed T, dμ = v dP.

topics.title: Work and heat on reversible paths

los.do: Calculate q, w and ΔU for a reversible isothermal ideal-gas process.
los.ek: ΔU = 0; w = −nRT ln(V₂/V₁) = −q.

los.do: Calculate q, w and ΔU for a reversible isobaric ideal-gas process.
los.ek: w = −PΔV = −nRΔT; q = nC_pΔT.

los.do: Calculate q, w and ΔU for a constant-volume ideal-gas process.
los.ek: w = 0; q = ΔU = nC_vΔT.

los.do: Find the final state of a reversible adiabatic ideal-gas process.
los.ek: TV^(γ−1) constant; C_v = 3R/2 monatomic, 5R/2 diatomic (no vibration).

los.do: Calculate the total entropy change of system plus bath for an irreversible process and decide whether it can occur.
los.ek: ΔS_bath = −q/T_bath; ΔS_tot ≥ 0, equal only when reversible.

los.do: Calculate the maximum efficiency or coefficient of performance of a cycle between two reservoirs.
los.ek: η_max = 1 − T_C/T_H from ΔS_tot = 0.

los.do: Apply steady-flow energy and entropy balances to a turbine, compressor, nozzle or throttle.
los.ek: Δh = q + w_s per unit mass; throttling is isenthalpic; Δs ≥ q/T.
los.std: webwork-opl:TH1.13, webwork-opl:TH5.2, webwork-opl:TH5.4, webwork-opl:TH5.5, webwork-opl:TH5.6, webwork-opl:TH5.8, webwork-opl:TH7.15

los.do: Test whether a differential is exact (a state function) by equality of cross-derivatives.
los.ek: M dx + N dy exact ⇔ ∂M/∂y = ∂N/∂x; δq and δw are not exact.

los.do: Apply the triple-product and chain rules to rewrite a partial derivative.
Construct F, H or G from a given U(S, V, N) by Legendre transform.
los.ek: F = U − TS; eliminate S using T = ∂U/∂S. H = U + PV; G = U − TS + PV.

los.do: State the natural variables and differential of any potential, including the grand potential.
los.ek: dF = −S dT − P dV + μ dN; dG = −S dT + V dP + μ dN; dΩ = −S dT − P dV − N dμ.

los.do: Choose the potential minimised at equilibrium for given bath conditions.
los.ek: T, V, N → F; T, P, N → G; T, V, μ → Ω; S, P, N → H.

los.do: Derive P, S, μ or U from a given F(T, V, N) or G(T, P, N).
Use the Gibbs–Helmholtz relation to get S or H from G(T).
Identify the Maxwell relation that equals a given partial derivative.
los.ek: Cross-derivatives of the potential whose natural variables are the two held fixed: (∂S/∂V)_T = (∂P/∂T)_V from F.

los.do: Evaluate an entropy derivative from an equation of state through a Maxwell relation.
Express a thermodynamic derivative in terms of α, κ_T and c_p and evaluate it.
Estimate the pressure rise when a liquid is heated at constant volume.
los.ek: ΔP ≈ (α/κ_T) ΔT — large for liquids (tens of bar per K).

los.do: Derive and evaluate c_p − c_v from α and κ_T.
los.ek: c_p − c_v = Tvα²/κ_T; = R for an ideal gas.

los.do: Derive (∂U/∂V)_T or the Joule–Thomson coefficient for a real gas from its equation of state.
Decide whether a fundamental equation is stable from the concavity of S(U, V).
los.ek: ∂²S/∂U² ≤ 0, ∂²S/∂V² ≤ 0, and the Hessian determinant ≥ 0.

los.do: Derive C_V from a fundamental equation and check that it is positive.
los.ek: C_V = (∂U/∂T)_V = −(∂S/∂U)²/(∂²S/∂U²) > 0 for stability.

los.do: Test whether a homogeneous van der Waals state is mechanically stable.
los.ek: Stable ⇔ (∂P/∂V)_T < 0 ⇔ κ_T > 0.

los.do: Calculate κ_T of a fluid from its equation of state.
los.ek: κ_T = −1/[V(∂P/∂V)_T]; for vdW (∂P/∂V)_T = −RT/(V − b)² + 2a/V³.

los.do: Find the critical constants of a cubic equation of state.
los.ek: (∂P/∂V)_T = (∂²P/∂V²)_T = 0; vdW: T_c = 8a/27Rb, V_c = 3b, P_c = a/27b².

los.do: Locate the spinodal and classify a state as stable, metastable or unstable.
los.ek: Spinodal: (∂P/∂V)_T = 0; between binodal and spinodal the state is metastable.

los.do: Find coexisting states by a common tangent on G or F, or Maxwell's equal-area rule on a vdW isotherm.
los.ek: Equal μ and P in both phases ⇔ common tangent ⇔ ∫P dV over the loop = P_sat ΔV.

los.do: Write μ(T, P) for a pure ideal gas and for a component of an ideal-gas mixture and calculate Δμ.
los.ek: μ = μ°(T) + RT ln(P/P°); in a mixture replace P by p_i = y_iP.

los.do: Calculate Z and residual (departure) properties from a virial or cubic equation of state.
los.ek: Z = PV/RT = 1 + B/V + …; h − h^ig = ∫[T(∂P/∂T)_V − P]dV + RT(Z − 1).

los.do: Calculate a fugacity coefficient from a virial or cubic equation of state.
los.ek: ln φ = ∫₀^P (Z − 1) dP/P; truncated virial: ln φ = BP/RT.

los.do: Relate the second virial coefficient to the intermolecular pair potential.
los.ek: B(T) = −2πN_A ∫(e^(−βu(r)) − 1) r² dr; B < 0 when attraction dominates.

los.do: Estimate properties of a gas or gas mixture by corresponding states and mixing rules.
los.ek: Z = f(T_r, P_r, ω); a_mix = ΣΣ y_iy_j √(a_ia_j)(1 − k_ij), b_mix = Σ y_ib_i.

topics.title: Conditions for phase equilibrium and the phase rule

los.do: State the conditions for phase coexistence and apply the Gibbs phase rule to a phase diagram.
los.ek: T, P, μ_i equal in every phase; F = C − π + 2.

los.do: Calculate the slope of a coexistence curve from the Clapeyron equation.
los.ek: dP/dT = Δh/(TΔv).

los.do: Estimate a vapor pressure at a new temperature with the integrated Clausius–Clapeyron equation.
los.ek: ln(P₂/P₁) = −(Δh_vap/R)(1/T₂ − 1/T₁); ideal vapor, v_liq ≪ v_vap, constant Δh.

los.do: Find Δh_vap from vapor pressures at two temperatures.
los.ek: Slope of ln P vs 1/T is −Δh_vap/R.

los.do: Find the boiling temperature at a new pressure.
los.ek: 1/T₂ = 1/T₁ − (R/Δh_vap) ln(P₂/P₁).

topics.title: Order parameters and types of transition

los.do: Classify a transition as first- or second-order from which derivatives of G are discontinuous.
los.ek: First order: jumps in S, V (latent heat); continuous: jumps or divergences in C_p, κ_T; the order parameter vanishes at T_c.

los.do: Calculate the entropy of ideal mixing.
los.ek: ΔS_mix = −nR Σ x_i ln x_i (from lattice counting).

los.do: Calculate the Gibbs energy of ideal mixing.
los.ek: ΔG_mix = nRT Σ x_i ln x_i; ΔH_mix = ΔV_mix = 0.

topics.title: Partial molar quantities and Gibbs–Duhem in mixtures

los.do: Calculate partial molar properties from a total property, e.g. by the tangent-intercept method.
los.ek: v̄_i = (∂V/∂n_i)_{T,P,n_j}; V = Σ n_i v̄_i.

los.do: Use Gibbs–Duhem to get one activity coefficient from the other or to test data for consistency.
los.ek: Σ x_i d ln γ_i = 0 at fixed T, P.

los.do: Calculate total pressure and vapor composition of an ideal solution with Raoult's law.
los.ek: p_i = x_iP_i*; P = Σ x_iP_i*; y_i = p_i/P.

los.do: Calculate the solubility of a dilute solute from Henry's law.
los.ek: p_i = x_iK_H,i for x_i → 0; K_H grows with T for most gases in water.

los.do: Perform bubble-point, dew-point and isothermal flash calculations for a multicomponent mixture.
los.ek: K_i = y_i/x_i; flash: Σ z_i(K_i − 1)/[1 + β(K_i − 1)] = 0 (Rachford–Rice).

los.do: Calculate activity coefficients from an excess-Gibbs-energy model (regular solution, Margules).
los.ek: G^ex/n = W x_Ax_B ⇒ RT ln γ_A = W x_B².

los.do: Derive the regular-solution model from a lattice with nearest-neighbour interactions and predict when the mixture phase-separates.
los.ek: ΔG_mix/nRT = Σ x ln x + χ x_Ax_B; unstable for χ > 2 (upper critical point at χ = 2, x = ½).

los.do: Calculate VLE with modified Raoult's law and identify an azeotrope.
los.ek: y_iP = x_iγ_iP_i*; at an azeotrope x_i = y_i and γ_A P_A* = γ_B P_B*.

los.do: Calculate boiling-point elevation, freezing-point depression or osmotic pressure of a dilute solution.
los.ek: ΔT_b = RT_b²x_B/Δh_vap; ΔT_f = RT_f²x_B/Δh_fus; Π = c_BRT (van 't Hoff).

los.do: Relate a partition coefficient to the free energy of transferring a solute between phases.
los.ek: ΔG°_transfer = −RT ln K_partition; set by μ° differences in the two solvents.

los.do: Calculate K from ΔG°.
los.ek: K = exp(−ΔG°/RT); standard state fixes the units of each activity.

los.do: Calculate ΔG° from K.
los.ek: ΔG° = −RT ln K.

los.do: Predict the direction of reaction from Q versus K.
los.ek: ΔG = ΔG° + RT ln Q = RT ln(Q/K); Q < K ⇒ forward.

los.do: Solve for the equilibrium extent of reaction and composition from K and the feed.
los.ek: n_i = n_i0 + ν_iξ; K = Π(y_iP/P°)^ν_i for ideal gases.

los.do: Predict how pressure, inerts or a nonideal phase shift an equilibrium.
los.ek: K_y = K(P/P°)^(−Δν); raising P favours fewer gas moles; fugacity or activity replaces y_iP in real phases.

los.do: Find ΔH° from K at two temperatures, or K at a new temperature, with the van 't Hoff equation.
los.ek: d ln K/d(1/T) = −ΔH°/R.

topics.title: Reaction equilibrium from molecular partition functions

los.do: Calculate K for a gas-phase reaction from molecular partition functions.
los.ek: K = Π(q_i/V)^ν_i e^(−ΔE₀/k_BT) (per standard volume); dissociation energies set ΔE₀.

units.title: The Boltzmann distribution and the canonical ensemble

los.do: Calculate the population ratio of two levels at a given temperature.
los.ek: N₂/N₁ = (g₂/g₁) e^(−ΔE/k_BT); 1 cm⁻¹ ↔ 1.439 K.

los.do: Calculate the fraction of molecules in a given level of a multi-level system.
los.ek: p_j = g_j e^(−βE_j)/q.

los.do: Find the temperature at which a level reaches a given population ratio.
los.ek: T = ΔE/[k_B ln(g₂N₁/g₁N₂)].

topics.title: The partition function and thermodynamic properties

los.do: Calculate a molecular partition function from a list of levels and degeneracies.
los.ek: q = Σ g_j e^(−βE_j); q counts thermally accessible states.

los.do: Derive the average energy U from ln q for a two-level system or harmonic oscillator.
los.ek: U = −N ∂ln q/∂β; oscillator U/Nε = 1/(e^x − 1).

los.do: Derive the entropy from the partition function.
los.ek: S = U/T + Nk_B ln q (localized); S/Nk_B = ln q + βU/N.

los.do: Calculate the Helmholtz free energy from the partition function.
los.ek: F = −k_BT ln Q; localized independent molecules: Q = q^N.

los.do: Assemble the system partition function from molecular ones for distinguishable or indistinguishable particles.
los.ek: Q = q^N (localized) or q^N/N! (gas); independent modes multiply: q = q_t q_r q_v q_e.

units.title: Molecular models of gases and solids

topics.title: Translation and the classical ideal gas

los.do: Calculate the thermal de Broglie wavelength of a molecule.
los.ek: Λ = h/√(2πmk_BT); classical when Λ³ ≪ V/N.

los.do: Calculate the translational partition function of a molecule in a box.
los.ek: q_trans = V/Λ³.

los.do: Derive the ideal-gas law and the Sackur–Tetrode entropy from Q = q^N/N!.
los.ek: P = k_BT ∂ln Q/∂V = Nk_BT/V; S/Nk_B = ln(V/NΛ³) + 5/2.

los.do: Calculate the rotational temperature of a diatomic from masses and bond length.
los.ek: I = μr²; θ_rot = ħ²/(2Ik_B).

los.do: Calculate the high-temperature rotational partition function, including the symmetry number.
los.ek: q_rot = T/(σθ_rot); σ = 2 homonuclear, 1 heteronuclear.

los.do: Calculate the vibrational temperature and vibrational partition function.
los.ek: θ_vib = hcν̃/k_B; q_vib = 1/(1 − e^(−θ_vib/T)) from the ground state.

los.do: Calculate the classical heat capacity of a gas by equipartition.
los.ek: ½k_B per quadratic term: 3 translational, 2 or 3 rotational, 2 per vibration (3N − 5 or 3N − 6 modes).

los.do: Calculate C_V of a diatomic gas with classical translation and rotation and quantum vibration.
los.ek: C_V,m = 5R/2 + R x²eˣ/(eˣ − 1)², x = θ_vib/T.

los.do: Derive the heat capacity of a two-level (Schottky) system.
los.ek: C_V = (∂U/∂T)_V; peaks near k_BT ~ ε and vanishes at both limits.

los.do: Derive the heat capacity of a quantum harmonic oscillator.
los.ek: C_V/Nk_B = x²eˣ/(eˣ − 1)² → 1 classically.

los.do: Calculate the molar heat capacity of a crystal from the Einstein model.
los.ek: C_V,m = 3R x²eˣ/(eˣ − 1)², x = θ_E/T; Dulong–Petit 3R at high T.

los.do: Apply the Debye T³ law at low temperature and explain why Einstein fails there.
los.ek: C_V ∝ (T/θ_D)³ at T ≪ θ_D: low-frequency acoustic modes stay active.

los.do: Compute averages from the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distribution.
los.ek: f(v) ∝ v² e^(−mv²/2k_BT); v_mp = √(2k_BT/m), ⟨v⟩ = √(8k_BT/πm), v_rms = √(3k_BT/m).

los.do: Write the classical canonical partition function as a phase-space integral and reduce it to a configurational integral.
Calculate an absolute entropy from heat-capacity data, including residual entropy of a disordered crystal.
los.ek: S(T) = ∫₀^T C_p/T dT + Σ Δh_trans/T_trans; residual S = R ln W per mole (CO: R ln 2).

topics.title: Energy fluctuations in the canonical ensemble

los.do: Calculate the energy variance of a molecule with a few discrete levels.
los.ek: σ_E² = ⟨E²⟩ − ⟨E⟩² = ∂²ln q/∂β².

los.do: Derive the energy variance of a quantum harmonic oscillator.
los.ek: σ_E²/ε² = eˣ/(eˣ − 1)².

los.do: Calculate the rms energy fluctuation from the heat capacity.
los.ek: σ_E² = k_BT²C_V — positive C_V is the stability condition again.

los.do: Calculate the relative energy fluctuation of a macroscopic system and explain why ensembles agree.
los.ek: σ_E/⟨E⟩ ∝ N^(−1/2); monatomic ideal gas: √(2/3N).

los.do: Calculate the occupancy probabilities of a site exchanging molecules with a reservoir at fixed μ.
los.ek: Ξ_site = 1 + e^(β(μ + ε)); p_empty = 1/Ξ.

los.do: Calculate the average number of bound molecules on independent sites from the grand partition function.
los.ek: Ξ = (1 + λe^(βε))^M; ⟨N⟩ = λ ∂ln Ξ/∂λ.

los.do: Calculate the particle-number variance in the grand canonical ensemble.
Calculate the population ratio of two states that differ in energy and volume at fixed T and P.
los.ek: P_B/P_A = e^(−β(ΔE + PΔV)); G = −k_BT ln Δ.

topics.title: The Gibbs entropy and choosing an ensemble

los.do: Calculate entropy from microstate probabilities with the Gibbs formula and match each ensemble to its potential.
los.ek: S = −k_B Σ p_i ln p_i; NVE ↔ S, NVT ↔ F, NPT ↔ G, μVT ↔ Ω = −PV.

los.do: Calculate fractional occupancy of a single-site receptor from K_d.
los.ek: θ = c/(K_d + c).

los.do: Find the gas pressure that gives a target Langmuir coverage.
Calculate the standard binding free energy from K_d.
los.ek: ΔG°_bind = RT ln(K_d/c°), c° = 1 M.

los.do: Calculate the average number bound to a two-site molecule with a pair interaction from its binding polynomial.
los.ek: Ξ = 1 + 2y + wy²; ⟨N⟩ = (2y + 2wy²)/Ξ; w > 1 cooperative.

los.do: Calculate fractional saturation from the Hill equation.
Find the Hill coefficient from saturation at two concentrations.
los.ek: n_H = Δ ln[θ/(1 − θ)] / Δ ln c.

los.do: Solve the Zimm–Bragg helix–coil or 1-D Ising model with a transfer matrix, or a mean-field Ising model for T_c.
los.ek: Q = λ₁^N for large N; mean field: k_BT_c = zJ.

los.do: Find the activation energy from rate constants at two temperatures.
los.ek: ln(k₂/k₁) = −(E_a/R)(1/T₂ − 1/T₁).

los.do: Find a rate constant at a new temperature from E_a.
los.ek: k₂ = k₁ exp[−(E_a/R)(1/T₂ − 1/T₁)].

los.do: Calculate the factor by which a rate rises over a temperature interval.
los.ek: k₂/k₁ = exp[(E_a/R)(1/T₁ − 1/T₂)]; the 'doubles per 10 K' rule ↔ E_a ≈ 50 kJ/mol near 300 K.

los.do: Calculate a rate constant from ΔH‡ and ΔS‡ with the Eyring equation.
los.ek: k = (k_BT/h) e^(ΔS‡/R) e^(−ΔH‡/RT).

los.do: Find the activation free energy from a measured rate constant.
los.ek: ΔG‡ = −RT ln(kh/k_BT).

los.do: Relate forward and reverse rate constants to K by detailed balance and read rates off a free-energy profile along a reaction coordinate.
los.ek: k_f/k_r = K; barrier height on F(ξ) sets k; catalysts lower ΔG‡, not ΔG°.

los.do: Calculate an equilibrium potential with the Nernst equation and a mean ionic activity coefficient with Debye–Hückel.
los.ek: E = E° − (RT/zF) ln Q; ln γ± = −A|z₊z₋|√I (dilute limit).

los.do: Calculate the Flory–Huggins free energy of mixing and the critical χ for a polymer solution.
los.ek: ΔG_mix/k_BT = (φ/N) ln φ + (1 − φ) ln(1 − φ) + χφ(1 − φ); χ_c = ½(1 + 1/√N)².

los.do: Apply the Metropolis acceptance rule and compute an ensemble average from a sampled trajectory.
los.ek: acc = min(1, e^(−βΔE)); ⟨A⟩ = time average over equilibrated, decorrelated samples.

units.title: Properties of pure substances and simple processes

los.do: Compute spring and electrical work.
los.ek: Spring: W = ½k(x₂² − x₁²); electrical: W = VIt.

los.do: Read a compressed-liquid state.
los.ek: h ≈ h_f(T) + v_f (P − P_sat(T)); otherwise treat it as saturated liquid at T.

los.do: Use saturated-liquid and saturated-vapour properties.
los.ek: At saturation, h_g = h_f + h_fg; the mass in a tank is V/v_g.

los.do: Find the quality and enthalpy of a two-phase mixture.
los.ek: x = (h − h_f)/h_fg; h = h_f + x h_fg.

los.do: Interpolate in the superheated table.
los.ek: Linear interpolation between neighbouring entries.

los.do: Find the heat to melt or boil a substance.
los.ek: Q = m(c ΔT + latent heat).

los.do: Find the work of a polytropic process.
los.ek: PVⁿ = const; W = (P₂V₂ − P₁V₁)/(1 − n) for n ≠ 1.

los.do: Handle incompressible substances.
los.ek: Δu = cΔT; Δh = cΔT + vΔP; Δs = c ln(T₂/T₁).

los.do: Read entropy on a T–s diagram.
los.ek: Area under a reversible path is the heat; an isentropic process is a vertical line.

los.do: Find the entropy of a saturated or two-phase state.
los.ek: s = s_f + x s_fg; the entropy of vaporisation is h_fg/T_sat.

los.do: Find the entropy change of heating a solid.
los.ek: Δs = c ln(T₂/T₁) for a solid with constant c.

units.title: Control volumes, the second law and exergy

los.do: Compute flow work.
los.ek: Flow work per unit mass = Pv.

los.do: Analyse several devices together.
los.ek: Write the balance for each device and add the powers.

los.do: Account for isentropic efficiency.
los.ek: Turbine: η = (h₁ − h₂)/(h₁ − h₂ₛ); compressor: η = (h₂ₛ − h₁)/(h₂ − h₁).

los.do: Recognise the Kelvin–Planck and Clausius statements.
los.ek: No cycle turns heat from one reservoir entirely into work; none moves heat from cold to hot with no work.

los.do: Use the thermodynamic temperature scale.
los.ek: For a reversible engine Q_H/Q_L = T_H/T_L.

los.do: Find the exergy of a hot body.
los.ek: X = m c[(T − T₀) − T₀ ln(T/T₀)].

los.do: Find the exergy carried by heat.
los.ek: X_Q = Q(1 − T₀/T).

los.do: Find the exergy destroyed in a process.
los.ek: X_destroyed = T₀ S_gen.

los.do: Compute flow exergy.
los.ek: ψ = (h − h₀) − T₀(s − s₀) (ignoring kinetic and potential terms).

los.do: Compute a second-law efficiency.
los.ek: η_II = W_actual/W_reversible (or actual/maximum COP).

los.do: Put a price on exergy destruction.
los.ek: Cost rate = (exergy destroyed per second) × (price of energy).

los.do: Find the efficiency of a Rankine cycle.
los.ek: η = (w_turbine − w_pump)/q_in with q_in = h₁ − h₄.

los.do: Find the bleed fraction of an open feedwater heater.
los.ek: y h_bleed + (1 − y) h_in = h_out (saturated liquid).

los.do: Find the air-standard Otto efficiency.
Find the air-standard Diesel efficiency.
Find the air-standard dual-cycle efficiency.
los.ek: Heat is added partly at constant volume (pressure ratio r_p), partly at constant pressure (cutoff r_c).

los.do: Find the efficiency of a regenerated Stirling or Ericsson cycle.
los.ek: With perfect regeneration both reach the Carnot efficiency.

los.do: Find the Brayton cycle efficiency.
Find the efficiency of a Brayton cycle with ideal regeneration.
Choose the intercooling pressure for minimum compressor work.
los.ek: Two stages with intercooling to T₁: P_x = √(P₁P₂).

los.do: Combine the efficiencies of a gas–steam cycle.
los.ek: η = η_gas + η_steam − η_gas η_steam when the steam cycle runs on the gas cycle's rejected heat.

los.do: Find the thrust of a turbojet.
los.ek: F = ṁ(V_exit − V_inlet).

los.do: Find the COP of a vapour-compression refrigerator.
los.ek: COP_R = (h₁ − h₄)/(h₂ − h₁).

los.do: Find the COP of a gas (reversed Brayton) refrigeration cycle.
Find the humidity ratio from an adiabatic-saturation (wet-bulb) reading.
los.ek: ω₁ = [c_p(T₂ − T₁) + ω₂h_fg₂]/(h_g₁ − h_f₂).

los.do: Find a dew point.
los.ek: T_dp is the saturation temperature at the vapour's partial pressure.

los.do: Find the enthalpy of moist air.
los.ek: h = 1.005T + ω(2501 + 1.82T) kJ per kg dry air, T in °C.

los.do: Balance an air-conditioning process.
los.ek: Dry air is conserved; water and energy balances fix the heat and the condensate.

los.do: Heat moist air at constant composition.
los.ek: Simple heating: ω constant, Q = ṁ_a c_p,moist ΔT.

los.do: Humidify air.
los.ek: Water added = ṁ_a(ω₂ − ω₁).

los.do: Find the outlet temperature of an evaporative cooler.
los.ek: The process is nearly at constant enthalpy (constant wet-bulb).

los.do: Mix two moist air streams.
los.ek: ω₃ = (ṁ₁ω₁ + ṁ₂ω₂)/(ṁ₁ + ṁ₂); h₃ likewise.

units.title: Combustion, reacting systems and liquid-phase fugacity

los.do: Estimate an adiabatic flame temperature.
los.ek: Heat released heats the products: Σnᵢc_p,ᵢ(T − T₀) = LHV.

los.do: Find a mixture's lower flammability limit.
los.ek: Le Chatelier: LFL_mix = 1/Σ(yᵢ/LFLᵢ) with yᵢ the fuel-only fractions.

los.do: Find the temperature rise of an adiabatic batch reactor.
los.ek: ΔT_ad = (−ΔH_r) C₀ X / (ρ c_p).

los.do: Combine a reaction equilibrium with a phase equilibrium.
los.ek: Over pure liquid A, p_A = P_sat; then p_B = K p_A for A(g) ⇌ B(g).

los.do: Find the chemical exergy of a gas from its dilution.
los.ek: Per mole, RT₀ ln(1/y_env) for a gas present at mole fraction y_env in the environment.

topics.title: Liquids and solids at high pressure

los.do: Estimate a saturated-liquid volume with the Rackett equation.
Find the fugacity of a compressed liquid with the Poynting factor.
los.ek: f = φ_sat P_sat exp[V_L(P − P_sat)/RT].

los.do: Find the Poynting factor for a solid.
los.ek: Same integral with the solid's molar volume and the sublimation pressure.

los.do: Find the boiling pressure of two immiscible liquids.
los.ek: Each liquid exerts its own vapour pressure: P = P₁sat + P₂sat.

los.do: Find an ideal solid solubility.
los.ek: ln x = −(ΔH_fus/R)(1/T − 1/T_m).

los.do: Apply van der Waals mixing rules.
los.ek: a_mix = (Σyᵢ√aᵢ)², b_mix = Σyᵢbᵢ.

los.do: Find a fugacity coefficient from the virial equation.
los.ek: ln φ = BP/RT.

los.do: Use the van Laar model.
los.ek: ln γ₁ = A₁₂(A₂₁x₂/(A₁₂x₁ + A₂₁x₂))².

los.do: Use regular-solution (Scatchard–Hildebrand) theory.
los.ek: ln γ₁ = V₁Φ₂²(δ₁ − δ₂)²/RT.

los.do: Use Wilson's equation.
los.ek: ln γ₁ = −ln(x₁ + Λ₁₂x₂) + x₂[Λ₁₂/(x₁ + Λ₁₂x₂) − Λ₂₁/(x₂ + Λ₂₁x₁)].

los.do: Use the NRTL model at infinite dilution.
los.ek: ln γ₁^∞ = τ₂₁ + τ₁₂ exp(−ατ₁₂).

los.do: Know what group-contribution and other activity models need.
los.ek: UNIFAC: group volumes, areas and group interaction parameters; UNIQUAC: r and q plus binary energies; MOSCED: dispersion, polarity, induction and hydrogen-bond parameters.

los.do: Choose the ensemble (NVE, NVT, NPT, μVT) that matches a described experiment or simulation goal — choice rep.
los.ek: Bench conditions (fixed T and P) ⇒ NPT, whose free energy is G; NVT gives A; NVE conserves H and is used to test integrators and measure unperturbed dynamics.

los.do: State the ergodic hypothesis and identify features of a system that break it on simulation timescales.
los.ek: Time average = ensemble average only if the trajectory visits all relevant states; barriers of many k_BT (slow rotamers, buried waters, unfolding) make runs quasi-nonergodic.

los.do: Calculate the instantaneous temperature from kinetic energy and the count of degrees of freedom — numeric rep.
los.ek: ⟨K⟩ = (N_df/2) k_B T; N_df = 3N − N_constraints − 3 when centre-of-mass motion is removed.

los.do: Calculate the population ratio of two states from their energy difference at a given temperature — numeric rep.
los.ek: p_i/p_j = exp[−(E_i − E_j)/k_BT]; k_BT = 0.593 kcal/mol at 298.15 K, so 1.36 kcal/mol is a factor of 10.

los.do: Convert between a population (or probability) ratio and a free-energy difference — numeric rep.
los.ek: ΔG_A→B = −k_BT ln(P_B/P_A); a free energy counts every microstate of a state, so it includes entropy, not just the lowest energy.

los.do: Distinguish Helmholtz and Gibbs free energy and the potential of mean force along a coordinate, and state which one a given simulation yields.
los.ek: A = −k_BT ln Q (NVT), G = −k_BT ln Δ (NPT); W(ξ) = −k_BT ln P(ξ) + const. Absolute Q is intractable, but ratios of Q are ensemble averages.

los.do: Write the CHARMM potential energy function term by term and name each parameter and the pairs each term excludes.
los.ek: Bonds K_b(b − b₀)², angles K_θ(θ − θ₀)², Urey–Bradley, dihedrals K_φ[1 + cos(nφ − δ)], impropers, CMAP, LJ ε[(R_min/r)¹² − 2(R_min/r)⁶], Coulomb; 1-2 and 1-3 pairs excluded, 1-4 pairs use special LJ parameters.

los.do: Calculate a Lennard-Jones or Coulomb pair energy from CHARMM parameters using the combining rules — numeric rep.
los.ek: ε_ij = √(ε_i ε_j), R_min,ij = R_min,i/2 + R_min,j/2; Coulomb = 332.06 q_i q_j / r kcal/mol with r in Å and q in e.

los.do: Explain what RTF, PRM, PSF, CRD and toppar.str files each contain and which ones CHARMM reads in what order.
los.ek: RTF: atoms, types, charges, connectivity and patches per residue (which terms exist); PRM: the constants in those terms; PSF: the generated list of atoms, bonds, angles, dihedrals of this system; CRD: coordinates; toppar.str streams the RTF/PRM set.

los.do: Map a residue's chemical state to its CHARMM36 name or patch: ASPP, GLUP, HSD/HSE/HSP, LSN, NTER/CTER, ACE/CT3 — choice rep.
los.ek: ASP, GLU deprotonated and LYS protonated by default; HIS must always be specified; charged termini for a whole protein, neutral ACE/CT3 caps for a peptide cut from a chain.

los.do: Describe how CHARMM36/CGenFF charges, dihedrals and LJ parameters are fitted, and why water model, cutoffs, constraints and 1-4 treatment belong to the parameter set.
los.ek: Charges fit to QM interaction energies with TIP3P water; dihedrals to QM scans; LJ to liquid densities and heats of vaporization. Constraint and cutoff settings are part of the force field definition — match the parameterizing work.

los.do: Judge a CGenFF (ParamChem) parameter assignment from its penalty scores and decide whether to validate or reoptimize — choice rep.
los.ek: Penalty < 10 ≈ fine; 10–50 validate; > 50 reparameterize against QM.

los.do: Compare TIP3P (CHARMM variant), SPC/E and TIP4P-type models by geometry, rigidity and known property errors, and name the model CHARMM36 assumes.
los.ek: TIP3P: rigid 3-site; the CHARMM variant adds LJ on H; diffuses ~2× too fast but CHARMM36 is fitted with it. TIP4P models add a virtual M site carrying the negative charge.

los.do: Write one step of velocity Verlet and of leapfrog and explain why their time reversibility and symplecticity give bounded energy error.
los.ek: Leapfrog: v(t + ½Δt) = v(t − ½Δt) + a(t)Δt, x(t + Δt) = x(t) + v(t + ½Δt)Δt. Symplectic integrators conserve a shadow Hamiltonian, so NVE energy fluctuates without drift; drift signals a bad Δt or cutoff artifacts.

los.do: Advance positions and velocities through one or two integration steps for a given 1-D force — numeric rep.
los.ek: Velocity Verlet: x₁ = x₀ + v₀Δt + ½a₀Δt²; v₁ = v₀ + ½(a₀ + a₁)Δt.

los.do: Calculate the period of the fastest vibration from its wavenumber and pick the largest stable timestep with and without hydrogen-bond constraints — numeric rep.
los.ek: T = 1/(c ν̃); X–H stretches at 3000–3600 cm⁻¹ have T ≈ 9–11 fs; with Δt ≲ T/10 that is ~1 fs unconstrained, ~2 fs with X–H constrained (rigid water roughly doubles Δt).

los.do: Explain how SHAKE, RATTLE and SETTLE impose holonomic constraints and count the degrees of freedom they remove.
los.ek: Lagrange multipliers iteratively restore bond lengths each step; SETTLE solves rigid 3-site water analytically; each constraint removes one degree of freedom (enters N_df).

los.do: Decide when to use hydrogen mass repartitioning at 4 fs, or drop constraints and use 1 fs, including for bonds to alchemical atoms — choice rep.
los.ek: HMR moves mass from heavy atoms to their H, conserving total mass and thermodynamics but altering kinetics. Constraints on bonds that change length between alchemical states bias single-topology results; 1 fs without them is the general fix.

los.do: Diagnose an unstable timestep or bad starting structure from run symptoms (SHAKE failures, energy blow-up, temperature spikes).
los.ek: Early crashes usually mean unrelaxed contacts (minimize) or too large a Δt; steady NVE drift means Δt, constraint tolerance or cutoff treatment is too loose.

los.do: Choose a thermostat for a stated goal — fast equilibration, canonical production, or dynamical properties — and justify it — choice rep.
los.ek: Bussi: general purpose; Nosé–Hoover chains: canonical, better ergodicity in small systems; Langevin: canonical, robust, damps dynamics; Berendsen and simple velocity rescaling give the wrong ensemble (flying ice cube).

los.do: Write the Langevin equation and explain how the friction coefficient (CHARMM fbeta, ps⁻¹) trades temperature control against dynamical fidelity.
los.ek: m dv/dt = F − γmv + R(t), ⟨R(t)R(t′)⟩ = 2γm k_BT δ(t − t′). BLaDE uses a g-BAOAB Langevin integrator; the tutorial's fbeta 0.1 ps⁻¹ is weak coupling.

los.do: Choose a barostat for equilibration vs production and for isotropic vs anisotropic cells — choice rep.
los.ek: Berendsen only for early equilibration; Monte Carlo barostat, Langevin piston and Parrinello–Rahman sample NPT; anisotropic or semi-isotropic coupling for membranes and crystals.

los.do: Explain how a Monte Carlo barostat accepts a volume move and set its BLaDE parameters (prmc, iprs, pref, prdv).
los.ek: Accept with min{1, exp[−β(ΔU + PΔV) + N ln(V′/V)]}; BLaDE's N counts heavy atoms. iprs = steps between attempts (default 50), pref = pressure in atm (1), prdv = σ of ΔV in Å³ (100).

los.do: Calculate a system's density from its box dimensions and total mass and check it against the expected value — numeric rep.
los.ek: ρ = M/(N_A V); 1 g/cm³ = 0.6022 amu/Å³. Pure TIP3P at 298 K should sit near 0.98–1.0 g/cm³.

topics.title: Periodic boundary conditions and box choice

los.do: Apply the minimum-image convention to find the distance between two atoms in a periodic box — numeric rep.
los.ek: Δx ← Δx − L·round(Δx/L) per axis; valid only when the nonbonded cutoff is below L/2.

los.do: Size a solvent box from the solute's extent and edge distance and compare atom counts for cubic, truncated-octahedral and rhombic-dodecahedral cells — numeric rep.
los.ek: Cube side = d_max + 2 × edge (10 Å is standard; more for highly charged solutes like RNA). For the same image distance d: V_cube = d³, V_oct ≈ 0.770 d³ (23% fewer atoms), V_RD ≈ 0.707 d³ (29% fewer). Water ≈ 0.0334 molecules/Å³.

los.do: Explain why periodic artifacts are smaller than vacuum-interface artifacts and name the cases where they are not.
los.ek: A droplet's surface distorts the solute; images avoid it. Artifacts grow with net charge, small boxes, and solutes that expand (unfolded chains need a fixed, larger box, e.g. 40 Å for the pentapeptides).

los.do: Explain why truncating Coulomb interactions fails in condensed phases and how Ewald splitting into real- and reciprocal-space sums fixes it.
los.ek: 1/r decays slower than the number of neighbours grows (∝ r²). Ewald: erfc(κr)/r is short-ranged in real space; the smooth remainder is summed on a reciprocal grid (PME, O(N log N)); a uniform neutralizing background handles net charge.

los.do: Choose PME parameters (real-space cutoff, κ, grid spacing, interpolation order) consistent with a target accuracy — choice rep.
los.ek: Typical CHARMM36 setup: 12 Å cutoff, κ ≈ 0.34 Å⁻¹, grid spacing ≤ 1 Å, order 4–6 (BLaDE supports 4, 6, 8). Larger κ shifts work to reciprocal space.

los.do: Distinguish switched, shifted and force-switched LJ cutoffs and pick the CHARMM36 standard, including neighbour-list buffer.
los.ek: CHARMM36: vfswitch from 10 to 12 Å, pair list to 14–16 Å; BLaDE requires PME or VSWITCH for electrostatics and VFSWITCH or VSHIFT for LJ. Apply long-range dispersion corrections only if the force field was fitted with them.

los.do: Assign protonation states from propka pKa predictions at the experimental pH, using predicted pKa for the folded state and model pKa for an unfolded peptide — numeric rep.
los.ek: pH < pKa ⇒ protonated; fraction protonated = 1/(1 + 10^(pH − pKa)). Check ASP, GLU, HIS, LYS; ARG, TYR, CYS rarely titrate. Record the states — they go in the methods section.

los.do: Choose a histidine tautomer (HSD, HSE, HSP) from its pKa and hydrogen-bond environment — choice rep.
los.ek: Protonated ⇒ HSP; otherwise put H on the δ or ε N according to nearby donors/acceptors; HSE when exposed or unclear (marginally more stable in the unfolded state).

los.do: Calculate the number of counterions and salt ion pairs needed to neutralize a box and reach a target concentration — numeric rep.
los.ek: N_pairs ≈ c(M) × V(Å³) × 6.022 × 10⁻⁴; neutralize the net solute charge first. Mimic the experiment; otherwise ~150 mM (Na⁺ extracellular, K⁺ intracellular).

los.do: Build a solvated, ionized protein box in CHARMM-GUI Solution Builder at the experimental temperature, pH and salt, deciding which crystallographic components and termini to keep.
los.ek: Keep crystallographic waters for the folded protein (pockets refill slowly); drop BME/Cl⁻ additives unless relevant; set temperature to the experiment (often 298.15 K, not the 303.15 K default).

los.do: Order the preparation stages — minimize, assign velocities, restrained NVT, NPT, production — and justify each stage.
los.ek: Minimize to remove clashes; relax solvent at constant volume with solute restrained; then relax volume at constant pressure; NVT production at a set density needs NPT equilibration first.

los.do: Calculate the per-component velocity spread or RMS speed of an atom drawn from a Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution — numeric rep.
los.ek: σ_v = √(k_BT/m) per Cartesian component; v_rms = √(3k_BT/m).

los.do: Decide when equilibration is complete from time series of energy, temperature, pressure, density and RMSD, and discard the burn-in.
los.ek: No drift and fluctuation about a stable mean in several observables; if unsure, extend. Analyse only the production portion, applying the cut uniformly.

los.do: Compute a normalized autocorrelation function and integrated correlation time from a short time series — numeric rep.
los.ek: C_j = ⟨δx_k δx_{k+j}⟩ / s²; τ_int = Σ_j C_j, summed until it converges but before it integrates noise.

los.do: Calculate the statistical inefficiency and effective number of independent samples, and from them the standard error of a mean — numeric rep.
los.ek: g = 1 + 2Σ_{j≥1} C_j (in frames); N_ind = N/g; s(x̄) = s(x)/√N_ind. Saving frames more often than τ adds disk, not information.

los.do: Compute a standard error from block averages and identify the block size at which the estimate plateaus — numeric rep.
los.ek: Split N frames into M equal blocks of n; s(x̄) = s(block means)/√M; increase n until s(x̄) stops growing.

los.do: Compute a standard error and 95% confidence interval from n independent trials using the Student t factor — numeric rep.
los.ek: SE = s/√n with s over trial means; CI = x̄ ± t·SE, t(0.975, n − 1) = 2.78 for n = 5, 2.57 for n = 6. Starting structures must be independent for this to hold.

los.do: Propagate uncertainty through sums, differences and nonlinear functions, e.g. σ(ΔΔG) from two legs — numeric rep.
los.ek: Independent legs: σ²(a − b) = σ²_a + σ²_b; nonlinear F: σ²_F ≈ Σ(∂F/∂x_i)² σ²_i, valid when noise-to-signal is small.

los.do: Bootstrap a confidence interval for a derived quantity from correlated data, and report it with significant figures that match the uncertainty.
los.ek: Resample blocks or independent trials, not raw frames; 95% CI = 2.5th–97.5th percentile. Report the confidence level and only meaningful digits.

los.do: Distinguish statistical uncertainty from sampling error that no error bar reveals, and detect insufficient sampling from drift, rare transitions and disagreement between independent runs.
los.ek: Checks can rule out good sampling but never prove it. Independent runs from diverse starts that disagree beyond their error bars signal unvisited states ('dark uncertainty').

los.do: Define the vocabulary of alchemical free energies: end states, λ, decoupling versus annihilation, and phase-space overlap.
los.ek: Alchemical intermediates are unphysical states that bridge two physical end states; only free-energy differences are defined; neighbouring states must overlap in phase space.

los.do: State the accuracy and reproducibility to expect from alchemical calculations and convert an energy error into a fold error in K.
los.ek: Favourable cases reach about 1–2 kcal/mol RMS error; 1.36 kcal/mol is a tenfold change in K at 298 K; repeat 2–3 times, ideally from different starting coordinates.

los.do: Estimate the compute a free-energy campaign needs, and decide when a pilot study or an experiment is the better use of time.
los.ek: Typical calculations use 20–40 or more λ states per leg; GPU throughput is a few hundred ns/day; run a small pilot before committing.

los.do: Design a perturbation network: star maps, denser networks with cycles, and how many independent cycles a network has.
los.ek: A star map links each ligand to one hub (N − 1 edges); a connected network with E edges on N ligands has E − N + 1 independent cycles for closure checks.

los.do: Calculate ΔA from given ⟨exp(−βΔU)⟩ or a list of ΔU samples with the Zwanzig relation, forward and reverse — numeric rep.
los.ek: ΔA_0→1 = −k_BT ln⟨exp(−βΔU)⟩_0, ΔU = U₁ − U₀ evaluated on state-0 samples; exact in the limit, derived from Q₁/Q₀.

los.do: Estimate ΔA from the mean and variance of ΔU with the second-order cumulant expansion — numeric rep.
los.ek: ΔA ≈ ⟨ΔU⟩₀ − βσ²_ΔU/2; exact for Gaussian ΔU.

los.do: Judge whether an FEP estimate is reliable from the ΔU distribution width and forward–reverse hysteresis.
los.ek: The exponential average is biased and dominated by rare low-ΔU samples; reliable only when σ_ΔU ≲ 1–2 k_BT, i.e. neighbouring states overlap. Large forward–reverse disagreement means too few windows.

los.do: Calculate ΔA by integrating ⟨∂U/∂λ⟩ over λ windows with the trapezoid or Simpson rule — numeric rep.
los.ek: ΔA = ∫₀¹ ⟨∂U/∂λ⟩_λ dλ; trapezoid needs evenly or explicitly weighted windows; Simpson needs an odd number of evenly spaced points.

los.do: Derive ∂U/∂λ for a linear mixing potential and explain why curvature near the endpoints demands more windows or soft-core.
