los.do: Find a time from a first-order step response.
Find the overshoot of an underdamped second-order process.
los.ek: OS = exp(−πζ/√(1 − ζ²)), independent of τ.

los.do: Find the offset under proportional control.
los.ek: Final value theorem: setpoint offset = 1/(1 + K K_c) for a first-order process.

los.do: Find the ultimate gain of a third-order process.
los.ek: Substitute s = iω in 1 + K_cG = 0: the imaginary part fixes ω_u, the real part K_c,u.

los.do: Find the ultimate period, then a Ziegler–Nichols setting.
los.ek: ω_u = √(a₁/a₃); P_u = 2π/ω_u; ZN PI: K_c = 0.45K_cu, τ_I = P_u/1.2.

los.do: Find an amplitude ratio from the frequency response.
los.ek: First order: AR = K/√(1 + ω²τ²), phase −atan(ωτ).

los.do: Find the crossover frequency of a first-order-plus-dead-time process.
los.ek: Phase −atan(ωτ) − ωθ = −π; no closed form.

los.do: Find what remains in a Rayleigh batch distillation.
los.ek: ln(W₀/W) = ∫ dx/(y − x) from x to x₀; with constant α it has a closed form.

los.do: Find the minimum absorbent rate.
los.ek: (L/G)_min = (y_in − y_out)/(x*_out − x_in), x*_out = y_in/m for a dilute linear system.

los.do: Find where the feed line meets the rectifying line.
los.ek: q-line y = qx/(q − 1) − z/(q − 1); rectifying line y = Rx/(R + 1) + x_D/(R + 1).

los.do: Scale a convection-diffusion problem and say which term the limit drops.
los.ek: Pe = UL/D weighs convection against diffusion; at large Pe the diffusive term survives only in a thin layer, so dropping it everywhere is wrong at the boundary.

los.do: Find the length at which two transport mechanisms balance.
los.ek: Setting Pe = 1 gives the crossover length L = D/U: below it diffusion wins, above it convection does.

los.do: Get a boundary-layer thickness from the scaling alone.
los.ek: Balancing convection along the plate with diffusion across it gives δ/L ~ Re^(-1/2), without solving anything.

los.do: Find the first correction from a regular perturbation.
los.ek: For x² + εx − 1 = 0, writing x = x₀ + εx₁ + … gives x₀ = 1 and x₁ = −1/2, so x ≈ 1 − ε/2.

los.do: Size the inner layer of a singular perturbation.
los.ek: For εy″ + y′ + y = 0 the highest derivative is lost at ε = 0, so a layer of thickness O(ε) carries the dropped boundary condition.

los.do: Find a penetration depth from the similarity variable.
los.ek: Diffusion into a half-space depends on x and t only through η = x/√(4Dt), so the depth grows as √(4Dt).

los.do: Say when a semi-infinite solution stops being valid.
los.ek: The similarity solution assumes the far boundary is never felt; it fails once √(4Dt) reaches the slab's half-thickness, at t = h²/(4D).

los.do: Find the slowest decay mode in a non-Cartesian geometry.
los.ek: A sphere's eigenvalues are λ_n = nπ/R exactly, so the slowest mode decays as exp(−π²Dt/R²) — unlike a cylinder, whose eigenvalues are Bessel zeros.

los.do: Decide how many terms an expansion needs.
los.ek: Successive terms decay as exp(−n²π²Fo), so the second term is exp(−3π²Fo) of the first: past Fo ≈ 0.2 one term is enough.

topics.title: Numerical methods and the limits of the software

los.do: Find the step an explicit solver is held to by stiffness.
los.ek: Forward Euler is stable only for Δt < 2/|λ_max|, so a stiff system is limited by its fastest mode however slowly the answer evolves.

los.do: Say how many digits an ill-conditioned solve loses.
los.ek: A relative perturbation is amplified by the condition number, so about log₁₀ κ of the available digits are gone.

los.do: Balance truncation against round-off in a difference.
los.ek: A forward difference has error O(h) + O(ε/h), minimised near h ≈ √ε, so the best achievable accuracy is about √ε, not ε.

los.do: Identify scarcity and compute an opportunity cost.
los.ek: Resources are limited and wants are not, so every choice gives something up. Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative, including implicit costs such as forgone wages.

los.do: Read a production possibilities curve.
los.ek: Points on the curve are efficient, points inside are inefficient (unemployed or misallocated resources), points outside are unattainable now. A bowed-out curve shows increasing opportunity cost; growth shifts the curve outward.

los.do: Find comparative advantage and acceptable terms of trade.
los.ek: A producer has the comparative advantage in the good it makes at the lower opportunity cost. Both sides gain when each specialises that way and they trade at a price between their two opportunity costs.

los.do: Choose a quantity by marginal analysis and apply the utility-maximising rule.
los.ek: Do more of an activity while marginal benefit exceeds marginal cost; stop where they are equal. A consumer maximises utility by equalising marginal utility per dollar across goods, within the budget.

los.do: Tell a shift of a curve from a movement along it.
los.ek: A change in the good's own price moves along the curve (a change in quantity demanded or supplied). Demand shifts with income, tastes, prices of related goods, expectations and the number of buyers; supply shifts with input prices, technology, taxes and subsidies, expectations and the number of sellers.

los.do: Solve for a linear market equilibrium.
los.ek: Equilibrium is where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied. With Qd = a − bP and Qs = c + dP, set them equal and solve for P, then substitute for Q.

los.do: Predict how equilibrium price and quantity change when a curve shifts.
los.ek: Demand up: price and quantity both rise. Supply up: price falls, quantity rises. When both curves shift, one of price or quantity is determined and the other is ambiguous.

los.do: Compute price elasticity by the midpoint method and link it to revenue.
los.ek: Elasticity = percentage change in quantity ÷ percentage change in price, with each percentage taken on the midpoint. Above 1 in size is elastic, below 1 inelastic. When demand is elastic a price cut raises total revenue; when inelastic it lowers it.

los.do: Use income and cross-price elasticities to classify goods.
los.ek: Income elasticity is positive for normal goods and negative for inferior goods. Cross-price elasticity is positive for substitutes and negative for complements.

los.do: Measure consumer and producer surplus.
los.ek: Consumer surplus is the area under the demand curve above the price; producer surplus is the area above the supply curve below the price. With straight lines each is a triangle: half base times height.

los.do: Analyse price controls and a per-unit tax.
los.ek: A ceiling below equilibrium causes a shortage; a floor above it causes a surplus; a control on the wrong side of equilibrium is not binding. A per-unit tax drives a wedge between the buyers' and sellers' prices, lowers quantity and creates a deadweight loss of half the tax times the fall in quantity.

los.do: Find imports at a world price and the effect of a tariff.
los.ek: If the world price is below the domestic equilibrium the country imports the gap between quantity demanded and domestic quantity supplied. A tariff raises the domestic price, shrinks imports and raises revenue equal to the tariff times the imports that remain.

los.do: Compute marginal product and recognise diminishing returns.
los.ek: Marginal product is the extra output from one more unit of a variable input. With a fixed input it eventually falls (diminishing marginal returns); total product still rises while marginal product is positive.

los.do: Compute short-run cost measures.
los.ek: Total cost = fixed + variable. ATC = TC/Q = AFC + AVC. Marginal cost is the change in total cost per extra unit; it cuts AVC and ATC at their minimum points.

los.do: Separate economic from accounting profit and read the long-run average cost curve.
los.ek: Economic profit subtracts implicit (opportunity) costs as well as explicit ones; zero economic profit is a normal profit. Falling long-run average cost is economies of scale, rising is diseconomies, flat is constant returns to scale.

los.do: Find a competitive firm's profit and decide whether it produces, shuts down or exits.
los.ek: A firm maximises profit where MR = MC; for a price taker MR is the price. Profit = (P − ATC) × Q. In the short run it produces if P ≥ AVC and shuts down otherwise; in the long run it exits if P < ATC.

los.do: Describe long-run equilibrium in perfect competition.
los.ek: Entry and exit drive economic profit to zero: price settles at the minimum of average total cost, where P = MC = minimum ATC, which is both allocatively and productively efficient.

los.do: Solve a linear monopoly and its deadweight loss.
los.ek: With P = a − bQ, marginal revenue is MR = a − 2bQ. The monopolist sets MR = MC, then charges the price on the demand curve at that quantity. Output is below the competitive level, and the deadweight loss is the triangle between demand and marginal cost over the lost units.

los.do: Explain price discrimination and its effect on output and surplus.
los.ek: Price discrimination charges different prices for the same good for reasons other than cost; it needs market power, a way to sort buyers and no resale. Under perfect discrimination the firm sells the competitive quantity, takes all the consumer surplus and leaves no deadweight loss.

los.do: Describe monopolistic competition in the short and long run.
los.ek: Many firms sell differentiated products with free entry. Each faces a downward-sloping demand curve and sets MR = MC; entry shifts each firm's demand left until price equals average total cost and economic profit is zero, with price above marginal cost and excess capacity.

los.do: Find dominant strategies and the Nash equilibrium of a two-firm game.
los.ek: A dominant strategy is best whatever the rival does. A Nash equilibrium is a pair of strategies from which neither player gains by changing alone. In a prisoners' dilemma both have a dominant strategy and the equilibrium leaves both worse off than cooperation would.

los.do: Compute marginal revenue product and decide how many workers to hire.
los.ek: Demand for a factor is derived from demand for what it makes. For a price-taking firm, marginal revenue product = marginal product × output price; hire as long as MRP is at least the wage.

los.do: Predict shifts in factor demand and supply.
los.ek: Factor demand rises with the output price, with the factor's productivity, and with the price of a substitute input; factor supply shifts with population, preferences for work and alternative opportunities.

los.do: Apply the least-cost rule for combining inputs.
los.ek: Cost is minimised when the marginal product per dollar is equal across inputs: MP of labour ÷ wage = MP of capital ÷ rental rate. If labour's ratio is higher, use more labour and less capital.

los.do: Solve a monopsony and compare it with a competitive labour market.
los.ek: A monopsonist faces the upward-sloping market supply curve, so its marginal factor cost lies above the wage. It hires where MRP = MFC and pays the wage on the supply curve at that quantity: fewer workers at a lower wage than competition.

units.title: Market failure and the role of government

los.do: Find the socially optimal quantity and the corrective tax.
los.ek: The efficient quantity is where marginal social benefit equals marginal social cost. With a constant external cost per unit, marginal social cost = marginal private cost + the external cost, and a per-unit tax equal to the external cost moves the market to the efficient quantity.

los.do: Classify externalities and their remedies.
los.ek: A negative externality (pollution) makes the market produce too much; a positive one (vaccination, education) too little. Taxes and subsidies equal to the external effect, or tradable permits, bring private incentives into line.

los.do: Classify goods by rivalry and excludability.
los.ek: Private goods are rival and excludable; public goods are neither, so free riders make private provision too small; common resources are rival but not excludable and are overused; club (artificially scarce) goods are excludable but not rival.

los.do: Predict how taxes and regulation affect a monopolist.
los.ek: A lump-sum tax changes neither marginal cost nor marginal revenue, so output and price stay the same and only profit falls. A per-unit tax raises marginal cost and lowers output. Regulating price at marginal cost is efficient but may cause a loss for a natural monopoly; price at average total cost gives zero economic profit.

los.do: Measure inequality and classify taxes.
los.ek: The Lorenz curve plots cumulative income share against cumulative population share; the Gini coefficient is the area between it and the line of equality divided by the whole area under that line (0 is perfect equality, 1 perfect inequality). A tax is progressive if its average rate rises with income, regressive if it falls.

units.title: Economic indicators and the business cycle

los.do: Compute GDP by expenditure and decide what counts.
los.ek: GDP is the market value of final goods and services produced within a country in a period: C + I + G + (X − M). It leaves out intermediate goods, used goods, purely financial transactions, transfer payments and unpaid household work.

los.do: Compute the unemployment rate and classify unemployment.
los.ek: The labour force is the employed plus the unemployed (without work and looking). Unemployment rate = unemployed ÷ labour force. Frictional unemployment is between jobs, structural is a mismatch of skills or place, cyclical comes from recessions; the natural rate is frictional plus structural.

los.do: Compute a price index and the inflation rate.
los.ek: CPI = cost of the market basket this year ÷ cost in the base year × 100. The inflation rate is the percentage change in the index from one year to the next.

los.do: Convert nominal to real values and say who unexpected inflation helps.
los.ek: Real GDP = nominal GDP ÷ GDP deflator × 100. Real values strip out price changes. Unexpected inflation moves wealth from lenders and people on fixed incomes to borrowers, because debts are repaid in cheaper dollars.

los.do: Read the business cycle and the output gap.
los.ek: Output moves through expansion, peak, contraction and trough around potential output. The output gap is actual minus potential real GDP: negative (recessionary) when unemployment is above the natural rate, positive (inflationary) when it is below.

los.do: Explain the slope of aggregate demand and predict its shifts.
los.ek: AD slopes down through the real wealth, interest rate and exchange rate effects. It shifts with changes in consumption, investment, government purchases and net exports that are not caused by the price level.

los.do: Compute spending and tax multipliers.
los.ek: Spending multiplier = 1 ÷ (1 − MPC) = 1 ÷ MPS. Tax multiplier = −MPC ÷ (1 − MPC), smaller in size because part of a tax cut is saved. A balanced-budget change has a multiplier of 1.

los.do: Predict shifts of short-run and long-run aggregate supply.
los.ek: SRAS slopes up because wages and some prices are sticky; it shifts with input prices, expected inflation and productivity. LRAS is vertical at potential output and shifts only with resources, technology and institutions.

los.do: Predict short-run effects of demand and supply shocks.
los.ek: A rise in AD raises both the price level and real output; a fall lowers both. A leftward shift of SRAS raises the price level and lowers output (stagflation); a rightward shift does the opposite.

los.do: Describe long-run self-adjustment.
los.ek: In a recessionary gap unemployment pushes nominal wages down over time, SRAS shifts right and output returns to potential at a lower price level. In an inflationary gap wages rise, SRAS shifts left and output returns to potential at a higher price level.

los.do: Choose a fiscal policy and size it with the multiplier.
los.ek: Expansionary fiscal policy (more spending, lower taxes) closes a recessionary gap; contractionary policy closes an inflationary gap. The spending change needed is the gap divided by the multiplier. Automatic stabilisers (income taxes, unemployment benefits) act without new legislation.

los.do: Relate bond prices to interest rates and compare assets by liquidity.
los.ek: Bond prices and interest rates move in opposite directions: a bond paying a fixed coupon is worth less when new bonds pay more. Liquidity is how easily an asset becomes spendable without loss: cash, then deposits, then bonds and stocks.

los.do: Convert between nominal and real interest rates.
los.ek: Real interest rate ≈ nominal rate − inflation. Lenders set the nominal rate from the real return they want plus the inflation they expect (the Fisher relation), so the realised real rate depends on what inflation turns out to be.

los.do: Define money by its functions and its measures.
los.ek: Money is a medium of exchange, a unit of account and a store of value. M1 is currency in circulation plus liquid deposits; M2 adds less liquid near-monies such as small time deposits and retail money market funds. Credit cards and stocks are not money.

los.do: Compute bank reserves and the money multiplier.
los.ek: Required reserves = reserve ratio × deposits; excess reserves are what a bank may lend. With no leakages the banking system can expand deposits by the money multiplier, 1 ÷ reserve ratio, times the initial excess reserves.

los.do: Use the money market to find the direction of the nominal interest rate.
los.ek: The demand for money falls as the nominal interest rate rises; the supply is set by the central bank. An increase in the money supply lowers the nominal interest rate; an increase in money demand (higher price level or real income) raises it.

los.do: Classify monetary policy actions and trace their effects.
los.ek: Expansionary monetary policy lowers interest rates to raise investment, aggregate demand and output; contractionary policy does the opposite. Buying bonds, lowering the rates the central bank administers or lowering reserve requirements are expansionary; the reverse actions are contractionary.

los.do: Use the loanable funds market to find the direction of the real interest rate.
los.ek: Savers supply loanable funds and borrowers demand them; the price is the real interest rate. Government borrowing raises demand (or reduces supply) and raises the real rate; more saving lowers it.

los.do: Combine fiscal and monetary policy.
los.ek: Expansionary fiscal and expansionary monetary policy both raise output and the price level but push interest rates in opposite directions: fiscal expansion raises them, monetary expansion lowers them. So the mix decides the interest rate when both are used.

los.do: Read the Phillips curve.
los.ek: The short-run Phillips curve slopes down: lower unemployment comes with higher inflation. Demand shocks move the economy along it; supply shocks and changes in expected inflation shift it. The long-run curve is vertical at the natural rate of unemployment.

los.do: Apply the quantity theory of money.
los.ek: The equation of exchange is M × V = P × Y. With velocity and real output fixed, the price level moves in proportion to the money supply; in growth rates, inflation ≈ money growth + velocity growth − real output growth.

los.do: Compute deficits and debt ratios and explain crowding out.
los.ek: A deficit is one year's spending minus revenue; the debt is the accumulated total. The debt-to-GDP ratio measures the burden. Government borrowing raises the real interest rate and crowds out private investment, which slows capital accumulation and growth.

los.do: Measure growth and name its sources.
los.ek: Growth is the rise in real GDP per person, driven by physical capital, human capital and technology, and shown as an outward shift of the PPC and a rightward shift of LRAS. A quantity growing at g% a year doubles in about 70 ÷ g years.

los.do: Place transactions in the balance of payments.
los.ek: The current account records trade in goods and services, income from abroad and transfers. The capital and financial account records purchases and sales of assets. Apart from measurement error the two sum to zero: a current account deficit is matched by a financial account surplus.

los.do: Convert currencies and measure appreciation.
los.ek: An exchange rate is the price of one currency in terms of another. A currency appreciates when it buys more of the other currency, which makes that country's exports dearer abroad and its imports cheaper.

los.do: Predict movements in the foreign exchange market.
los.ek: The demand for a currency comes from foreigners buying that country's goods and assets; the supply from residents buying foreign goods and assets. Higher domestic real interest rates, lower domestic prices or stronger foreign demand for exports make the currency appreciate.

los.do: Link exchange rates and interest rates to net exports and capital flows.
los.ek: An appreciation makes exports dearer and imports cheaper, reducing net exports and aggregate demand; a depreciation raises them. A higher domestic real interest rate attracts a financial capital inflow, which appreciates the currency.

los.do: Place an item in the statement where it is reported.
los.ek: A short list of unrealized items goes to OCI; owner transactions to the statement of changes in equity.

los.do: Classify cash flows and compute operating cash flow by the indirect method and cash collected from customers.
los.ek: Interest paid and dividends received are operating under US GAAP.

los.do: Compute goodwill, the noncontrolling interest's share of income, and intercompany profit to eliminate in consolidation.
los.ek: Goodwill = consideration + NCI fair value − net identifiable assets.

los.do: Classify contributions and releases between net assets with and without donor restrictions.
los.ek: Only donors restrict; board designations do not.

los.do: Give the measurement focus and basis for each fund type and the government-wide statements, and pick the fund for an activity.
los.ek: Governmental funds: current financial resources, modified accrual.

topics.title: Public companies and special purpose frameworks

los.do: Name SEC filings and the segment reporting thresholds.
los.ek: 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K; 10% tests, 75% coverage.

los.do: Apply the cash, modified cash and tax bases.
los.ek: Describe the basis and its differences from GAAP.

los.do: Compute liquidity and activity ratios: current, quick, days in receivables and days in inventory.
los.ek: Turnover uses averages; days = 365 ÷ turnover.

los.do: Compute weighted-average shares and basic EPS.
los.ek: Subtract preferred dividends; weight shares by time outstanding.

los.do: Decide what counts as a cash equivalent and reconcile a bank balance.
los.ek: Original maturity of three months or less.

los.do: Estimate the allowance for credit losses and bad debt expense.
los.ek: The expense brings the allowance to its required balance.

los.do: Cost ending inventory by FIFO, LIFO and weighted average, apply lower of cost and NRV, and estimate it by the gross profit method.
los.ek: Rising prices: FIFO gives the highest ending inventory.

los.do: Compute straight-line, double-declining-balance and sum-of-the-years'-digits depreciation, a disposal gain or loss, and depreciation after a change in estimate.
los.ek: Estimates change prospectively.

los.do: Compute interest capitalized during construction.
los.ek: Avoidable interest, capped at actual.

los.do: Choose the measurement for a debt or equity investment and apply the equity method.
los.ek: Trading FV-NI, AFS FV-OCI, HTM amortized cost; 20–50% equity method.

los.do: Measure a goodwill impairment.
los.ek: Carrying amount over fair value, capped at goodwill.

los.do: Accrue interest on a note payable.
los.ek: Principal × rate × time.

los.do: Price a bond and amortize its discount or premium by the effective interest method.
los.ek: Expense at the market rate on carrying amount; cash at the coupon rate on face.

los.do: Record a stock dividend and roll retained earnings forward, including a prior-period adjustment.
los.ek: Small stock dividends at fair value; error corrections adjust opening retained earnings.

los.do: Tell a change in principle, a change in estimate and an error correction apart, and say how each is reported.
los.ek: Retrospective, prospective, restatement.

los.do: Decide whether to accrue, disclose or ignore a contingency.
los.ek: Probable and estimable → accrue; a range → best estimate or minimum.

los.do: Decide whether a subsequent event is recognized or only disclosed.
los.ek: Conditions existing at the balance-sheet date are recognized.

los.do: Order the five steps, allocate a price by standalone selling prices, estimate variable consideration, and recognize revenue over time.
los.ek: Cost-to-cost: cumulative revenue minus what earlier years recognized.

los.do: Classify temporary and permanent differences and measure a deferred tax liability at the enacted rate.
los.ek: Use the rate enacted for the reversal years.

los.do: Place a valuation input in the fair value hierarchy.
los.ek: Level 1 quoted identical, Level 2 observable, Level 3 unobservable.

los.do: Classify a lease as finance or operating and measure the lease liability.
los.ek: Five tests; liability = PV of remaining payments.

los.do: Classify a cost as product or period, direct or indirect, fixed or variable.
los.ek: Product costs (direct materials, direct labour, manufacturing overhead) attach to inventory and are expensed when the goods are sold; period costs (selling and administrative) are expensed as incurred. Variable costs change in total with volume; fixed costs do not within the relevant range.

los.do: Split a mixed cost with the high-low method.
los.ek: Variable cost per unit = change in cost ÷ change in activity between the highest and lowest activity levels; fixed cost = total cost at either point minus the variable part.

los.do: Compare income under absorption and variable costing.
los.ek: Absorption costing puts fixed manufacturing overhead into unit cost; variable costing expenses it in the period. When production exceeds sales, absorption income is higher by the fixed overhead per unit times the increase in inventory.

los.do: Allocate a joint cost.
los.ek: Joint costs up to the split-off point are allocated by relative sales value at split-off, by net realisable value (final sales value minus separable costs) or by physical units. The allocation is for inventory costing; it is irrelevant to the decision to process further.

los.do: Set a predetermined overhead rate and find over- or underapplied overhead.
los.ek: Predetermined rate = budgeted overhead ÷ budgeted activity. Applied overhead = rate × actual activity. If actual overhead exceeds applied, overhead is underapplied.

los.do: Cost a job and choose between job-order and process costing.
los.ek: Job cost = direct materials + direct labour + applied overhead. Job-order costing suits distinct, custom jobs; process costing suits a continuous flow of identical units.

los.do: Find equivalent units and cost per equivalent unit by the weighted-average method.
los.ek: Equivalent units = units completed and transferred out + ending work in process × its percentage of completion. Cost per equivalent unit = (beginning WIP cost + costs added) ÷ equivalent units.

los.do: Assign overhead with activity-based costing.
los.ek: Each activity pool has its own rate = pool cost ÷ total driver volume; a product is charged rate × the driver units it uses. ABC shifts overhead toward low-volume, complex products compared with a single volume-based rate.

los.do: Allocate service department costs.
los.ek: The direct method allocates each service department's cost only to production departments. The step-down method allocates in sequence and recognises some service-to-service use; the reciprocal method recognises all of it with simultaneous equations.

los.do: Find contribution margin and the breakeven point.
los.ek: Contribution margin per unit = price − variable cost per unit. Breakeven units = fixed costs ÷ unit contribution margin; breakeven sales = fixed costs ÷ contribution margin ratio.

los.do: Find the volume for a target profit and the margin of safety.
los.ek: Units for a target profit = (fixed costs + target profit) ÷ unit contribution margin. Margin of safety = actual or budgeted sales − breakeven sales.

los.do: Handle a sales mix and measure operating leverage.
los.ek: With several products, breakeven uses the weighted-average contribution margin at the given mix. Degree of operating leverage = contribution margin ÷ operating income; it multiplies a percentage change in sales into a percentage change in income.

los.do: Name the budgeting approach and order the master budget.
los.ek: The master budget starts from the sales budget, then production, materials, labour, overhead, selling and administrative, then the cash budget and pro forma statements. Zero-based budgets justify every item from nothing; rolling budgets add a period as one ends; flexible budgets adjust to actual volume; activity-based budgets build from activities and drivers.

los.do: Prepare production and purchases budgets.
los.ek: Production = budgeted sales + desired ending finished goods − beginning finished goods. Materials to purchase = production needs + desired ending materials − beginning materials.

los.do: Build cash collections and a cash budget.
los.ek: Collections follow the credit pattern (so much in the month of sale, so much the next). Ending cash = beginning cash + receipts − disbursements; a shortfall against the minimum balance is borrowed.

los.do: Forecast with a learning curve and an expected value.
los.ek: On a cumulative-average learning curve, each doubling of cumulative output multiplies the cumulative average time per unit by the learning rate. Expected value is the probability-weighted average of the outcomes.

los.do: Build a flexible budget and separate volume from spending.
los.ek: A flexible budget restates the budget at the actual volume: variable cost per unit × actual units + fixed cost. Flexible-budget variance = actual − flexible budget; sales-volume variance = flexible budget − static budget.

los.do: Compute direct materials price and quantity variances.
los.ek: Price variance = (actual price − standard price) × actual quantity. Quantity variance = (actual quantity − standard quantity allowed for actual output) × standard price. Positive is unfavourable.

los.do: Compute direct labour rate and efficiency variances.
los.ek: Rate variance = (actual rate − standard rate) × actual hours. Efficiency variance = (actual hours − standard hours allowed) × standard rate.

los.do: Compute overhead variances and say who can explain a variance.
los.ek: Variable overhead spending = actual − actual hours × standard rate; efficiency = (actual hours − standard hours) × standard rate. Fixed overhead budget variance = actual − budgeted; volume variance = budgeted − applied, unfavourable when production is below the denominator level.

los.do: Classify responsibility centres.
los.ek: A cost centre manager controls costs; a revenue centre, revenues; a profit centre, both; an investment centre, profit and the assets used to earn it. Managers should be judged on what they can control.

los.do: Compute return on investment and residual income.
los.ek: ROI = operating income ÷ average operating assets = margin × turnover. Residual income = operating income − required rate × operating assets. ROI can lead a manager to reject a project that earns more than the cost of capital but less than the division's current ROI; residual income does not.

los.do: Set a transfer price.
los.ek: The selling division's minimum transfer price is its variable cost per unit plus the contribution margin it gives up on outside sales (zero with idle capacity). The buying division's maximum is the outside market price.

los.do: Read a balanced scorecard and a segment margin.
los.ek: The balanced scorecard has four perspectives: financial, customer, internal business process, learning and growth. Segment margin = contribution margin − traceable fixed costs; common fixed costs are not allocated to segments.

los.do: Tell relevant costs from irrelevant ones.
los.ek: A relevant cost is a future cost that differs between alternatives. Sunk costs are irrelevant. An opportunity cost (the benefit given up) is relevant although it is never recorded.

los.do: Decide a special order and a make-or-buy question.
los.ek: Accept a special order if its incremental revenue exceeds its incremental cost, including any contribution lost on displaced sales. Make rather than buy if the avoidable cost of making is below the purchase price plus any opportunity cost of the capacity.

los.do: Decide to process further, drop a segment, or ration a scarce resource.
los.ek: Process further if incremental revenue exceeds incremental cost; joint costs are sunk. Drop a segment only if the avoidable fixed costs exceed the contribution margin lost. With one constraint, rank products by contribution margin per unit of the scarce resource.

los.do: Price by cost-plus and by target costing.
los.ek: Cost-plus price = cost × (1 + markup). Target cost = the price the market will bear − the required profit: the price comes first and the cost must be engineered to fit.

los.do: Evaluate an investment by payback and net present value.
los.ek: Payback = investment ÷ annual net cash inflow when inflows are even; it ignores the time value of money and everything after payback. NPV = present value of the cash flows at the required rate − the investment; accept when positive. IRR is the rate at which NPV is zero.

los.do: Add free energies of coupled reactions and use ΔG = ΔG°′ + RT ln Q to decide whether a cellular step runs.
los.ek: ΔG values of coupled reactions add; ATP hydrolysis gives about −30.5 kJ/mol under standard conditions; a reaction with ΔG°′ > 0 can still run when Q is small.

los.do: Choose a microscope or stain for a cell-biology question and compute magnification and cell size.
los.ek: Total magnification = objective × eyepiece; light microscopes resolve about 0.2 µm, electron microscopes about 1 nm; cell size ≈ field diameter ÷ cells across it.

los.do: Identify a biomolecule from a chemical test and count the waters released when monomers polymerize.
los.ek: Benedict's: reducing sugars; biuret: peptide bonds; iodine: starch; Sudan/emulsion: lipids; n monomers joined by dehydration release n − 1 waters.

los.do: Classify a biomolecule as carbohydrate, lipid, protein or nucleic acid from its monomer and linking bond.
los.ek: Glycosidic, ester, peptide and phosphodiester bonds; all formed by dehydration, broken by hydrolysis.

los.do: Predict how an inhibitor type changes Km and Vmax of an enzyme.
los.ek: Competitive: Km up, Vmax same; noncompetitive: Vmax down, Km same; uncompetitive: both down.

los.do: Locate each stage of cellular respiration and state its inputs, outputs and ATP yield.
los.ek: Glycolysis (cytosol, 2 ATP net) → pyruvate oxidation + Krebs (matrix) → ETC (inner membrane, O2 final acceptor); ~30–32 ATP per glucose.

los.do: Distinguish the light reactions from the Calvin cycle by location, inputs and products.
los.ek: Thylakoid: H2O split, O2 released, ATP + NADPH made; stroma: rubisco fixes CO2 using ATP and NADPH.

los.do: Predict the direction and energy requirement of a membrane transport process.
los.ek: Passive goes down the gradient; active uses ATP or a coupled gradient; water moves toward higher solute concentration.

los.do: Trace a signal from ligand to response for a GPCR, receptor tyrosine kinase or intracellular receptor.
los.ek: Hydrophilic ligands bind surface receptors and use second messengers (cAMP, Ca2+, IP3/DAG); steroids cross the membrane and act on genes.

los.do: Decide whether a cellular reaction is spontaneous and how coupling or an enzyme changes it.
los.ek: ΔG < 0 is spontaneous; ATP hydrolysis drives endergonic steps by coupling; enzymes lower Ea, never ΔG.

los.do: Order the cell-cycle phases and mitotic stages and name the checkpoint controls.
los.ek: G1 → S → G2 → M (prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase); cyclin–CDK complexes and p53 gate the transitions.

los.do: Compare mitosis and meiosis by ploidy, crossing over and products.
los.ek: Meiosis I separates homologs (2n → n) with crossing over in prophase I; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

los.do: Match an organelle to its function and tell prokaryotic from eukaryotic cells.
los.ek: RER makes secreted/membrane proteins; Golgi modifies and sorts; lysosome digests; peroxisome breaks H2O2 and fatty acids; mitochondria and chloroplasts carry their own DNA.

los.do: Identify cytoskeletal elements and cell junctions by structure and role.
los.ek: Microtubules (tubulin: spindle, cilia), microfilaments (actin: contraction, cleavage), intermediate filaments (keratin: strength); tight, gap and desmosome junctions.

los.do: Choose the experimental technique that answers a cell-biology question and interpret its result.
los.ek: Differential centrifugation separates by size/density; SDS-PAGE by mass; fluorescent tags localize; radiolabel pulse-chase follows a pathway.

los.do: Distinguish viruses, viroids and prions and compute a phage titer from a plaque count.
los.ek: Viroids are naked RNA, prions misfolded protein; titer (PFU/mL) = plaques ÷ (dilution × volume plated).

los.do: Match prokaryotic growth and habitats to Archaea or Bacteria and compute exponential growth from generation time.
los.ek: Extreme halophiles, methanogens and many thermophiles are archaea; N = N₀ · 2^(t/g) during log phase.

los.do: Place a fungus in its phylum and predict the effect of drugs or partnerships that act on fungal biology.
los.ek: Zygomycetes (bread mold), ascomycetes (yeast, sac), basidiomycetes (mushrooms, club); ergosterol in the membrane is the antifungal target; mycorrhizae and lichens are mutualisms.

los.do: Identify a protist by its locomotion, covering or disease and predict its physiology from its habitat.
los.ek: Amoebae: pseudopodia; Paramecium: cilia and a contractile vacuole; Euglena: flagellum and chloroplasts; diatoms: silica; Plasmodium (apicomplexan) causes malaria.

los.do: Relate plant tissues, transport and hormones to function and predict a plant's response to a stimulus.
los.ek: Xylem carries water up by transpiration pull; phloem moves sugar source to sink; auxin drives phototropism, gibberellin stem growth, abscisic acid stomatal closure, ethylene ripening; C4 and CAM limit photorespiration.

los.do: Describe virus structure and distinguish lytic, lysogenic and retroviral life cycles.
los.ek: Capsid around DNA or RNA, no metabolism; lysogenic phage integrates as a prophage; retroviruses use reverse transcriptase.

los.do: Distinguish Archaea from Bacteria and Eukarya by membrane, wall and genetic machinery.
los.ek: Archaea: ether-linked lipids, no peptidoglycan, histones and eukaryote-like RNA polymerase.

los.do: Classify a bacterium by shape, Gram stain and metabolism, and name its modes of gene transfer.
los.ek: Gram+ thick peptidoglycan, Gram− thin wall plus outer LPS membrane; binary fission; transformation, transduction, conjugation.

los.do: Identify the defining features and life cycle of fungi.
los.ek: Chitin walls, absorptive heterotrophs, hyphae/mycelium; haploid-dominant life cycle.

los.do: Place a described protist in its group and explain why Protista is not a natural clade.
los.ek: Eukaryotes that are not plants, animals or fungi (algae, amoebae, ciliates, Plasmodium); paraphyletic.

los.do: Order plant groups by key innovation and identify the dominant generation in each.
los.ek: Mosses (gametophyte-dominant, no vasculature) → ferns (vascular, sporophyte-dominant) → gymnosperms (seeds, pollen) → angiosperms (flowers, fruit, double fertilization).

los.do: Classify an animal by symmetry, germ layers, body cavity and protostome/deuterostome development.
los.ek: Deuterostomes (echinoderms, chordates): blastopore becomes the anus, radial cleavage; protostomes: mouth, spiral cleavage.

los.do: Identify the four chordate features and the traits that separate vertebrate classes.
los.ek: Notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, pharyngeal slits, post-anal tail; amniotic egg separates reptiles, birds and mammals from amphibians.

los.do: Identify skin cells, glands and layers and predict how skin responds to heat, cold and injury.
los.ek: Stratum basale divides; melanocytes make melanin; sebaceous glands oil hair, eccrine glands cool by sweat; vasodilation dumps heat, vasoconstriction keeps it.

los.do: Match bone and cartilage cells, tissue and joints to their roles.
los.ek: Osteocytes sit in lacunae of osteons (Haversian systems); red marrow makes blood cells; hyaline cartilage covers joints, fibrocartilage in discs, elastic in the ear; synovial joints move freely.

los.do: Compare skeletal, cardiac and smooth muscle and predict force from motor-unit recruitment and summation.
los.ek: Skeletal: striated, voluntary, multinucleate; cardiac: striated, intercalated discs, autorhythmic; smooth: unstriated, calmodulin; force rises by recruiting motor units and by summation to tetanus.

los.do: Match antibody classes, antigen presentation and immunization type to the immune response they give.
los.ek: IgM first, IgG most abundant and crosses the placenta, IgA in secretions, IgE allergy; MHC I shows to CD8, MHC II to CD4; vaccines give active immunity, antibodies passed on give passive.

los.do: Match gut hormones and absorption sites to their actions and follow fat digestion and absorption.
los.ek: Gastrin raises acid; secretin brings bicarbonate; CCK releases bile and enzymes; most absorption in the small intestine, water and electrolytes also in the colon; fats leave as chylomicrons into lacteals.

los.do: Compute renal clearance from urine and plasma data and trace the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone response.
los.ek: Clearance = U × V̇ ÷ P; inulin clearance equals GFR; low pressure → renin → angiotensin II → aldosterone and vasoconstriction.

los.do: Trace gametes through the reproductive tracts and match pregnancy hormones to their roles.
los.ek: Sperm: seminiferous tubules → epididymis → vas deferens; fertilization in the oviduct; hCG keeps the corpus luteum; progesterone holds the endometrium; oxytocin drives labor.

los.do: Describe the layers of the skin and their roles in protection and thermoregulation.
los.ek: Avascular epidermis (keratinocytes, melanocytes); dermis holds vessels, glands and receptors; sweat and vasodilation dump heat.

los.do: Predict how bone remodeling and blood Ca2+ respond to PTH, calcitonin and vitamin D.
los.ek: Osteoblasts build, osteoclasts resorb; PTH and calcitriol raise blood Ca2+, calcitonin lowers it.

los.do: Explain each step of the sliding-filament cycle and its dependence on Ca2+ and ATP.
los.ek: Ca2+ binds troponin, tropomyosin uncovers actin sites, myosin power stroke; ATP binding releases the head.

los.do: Trace blood through the heart and vessels and identify which vessels carry oxygenated blood.
los.ek: RA → RV → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary veins → LA → LV → aorta; arteries leave the heart regardless of O2 content.

los.do: Predict the direction a condition shifts the oxygen–hemoglobin dissociation curve.
los.ek: Right shift (lower affinity): ↑CO2, ↑H+, ↑temperature, ↑2,3-BPG; fetal Hb and CO shift left.

los.do: Distinguish innate from adaptive immunity and match B, CD4+ and CD8+ cells to their actions.
los.ek: B cells make antibodies (humoral); CD8+ kill cells presenting on MHC I; CD4+ helpers recognize MHC II on APCs.

los.do: Match a digestive enzyme to its source, substrate and site of action.
los.ek: Salivary amylase (mouth), pepsin (stomach), pancreatic trypsin, lipase and amylase (duodenum); bile emulsifies; absorption is in the small intestine.

los.do: Explain ventilation mechanics and how O2 and CO2 are exchanged and carried.
los.ek: Diaphragm contracts → thoracic volume up, pressure down → air in; exchange by diffusion in alveoli; most CO2 travels as HCO3−.

los.do: Assign filtration, reabsorption and concentration to nephron segments and predict the effect of ADH and aldosterone.
los.ek: Glomerulus filters; PCT reabsorbs most solute; loop of Henle builds the gradient; ADH inserts aquaporins in the collecting duct; aldosterone retains Na+.

los.do: Explain the ion movements behind the resting potential, action potential and synaptic transmission.
los.ek: Na+ in depolarizes, K+ out repolarizes; Na+/K+-ATPase pumps 3 Na+ out, 2 K+ in; myelin enables saltatory conduction; Ca2+ triggers vesicle release.

los.do: Identify the receptor and structure responsible for a sensory function.
los.ek: Rods: dim light; cones: color; cochlear hair cells: hearing; semicircular canals and vestibule: balance.

los.do: Match a hormone to its gland and target action and predict a negative-feedback response.
los.ek: Peptide hormones use surface receptors, steroids act in the nucleus; hypothalamus → anterior pituitary → gland axes are damped by negative feedback.

los.do: Sequence the menstrual cycle's hormone changes and compare spermatogenesis with oogenesis.
los.ek: Estrogen peak → LH surge → ovulation; corpus luteum makes progesterone; one oocyte plus polar bodies vs four sperm per meiosis.

los.do: Compute the risk that a child inherits a human single-gene disorder and match disorders to inheritance modes.
los.ek: Two carriers of an autosomal recessive: 1/4 affected, 2/3 of unaffected children are carriers; carrier mother of an X-linked recessive: 1/2 of sons affected.

los.do: Name the karyotype of common aneuploidies and count chromosomes and chromatids through the cell cycle.
los.ek: Down 47,+21; Turner 45,X; Klinefelter 47,XXY; a 2n cell has 2n chromosomes and 4n chromatids after S phase, n chromosomes with 2n chromatids after meiosis I.

los.do: Order early development and predict the outcome of a change in induction, Hox genes or apoptosis.
los.ek: Zygote → cleavage → morula → blastula (blastocyst) → gastrula; induction signals fate; Hox genes set body-axis identity; apoptosis sculpts digits.

los.do: Estimate how often a sequence occurs by chance in a genome and compare genome features across organisms.
los.ek: A specific n-base site appears about once every 4^n bases; prokaryotic genomes are compact with operons; eukaryotic genomes carry introns, repeats and much noncoding DNA.

los.do: Predict Barr bodies and imprinted expression from a karyotype or parent of origin.
los.ek: Barr bodies = number of X chromosomes − 1; imprinted genes are expressed from one parent's copy only (Prader–Willi paternal loss, Angelman maternal loss of 15q11–13).

los.do: Compute PCR amplification and choose the blot or library that detects DNA, RNA or protein.
los.ek: Each ideal PCR cycle doubles the target: N = N₀ · 2ⁿ; Southern blots detect DNA, Northern RNA, Western protein; a cDNA library holds only expressed genes, without introns.

los.do: Assign each DNA replication enzyme its role and explain leading vs lagging strand synthesis.
los.ek: Helicase unwinds, primase lays RNA primer, DNA pol III extends 5′→3′, pol I replaces primers, ligase seals Okazaki fragments.

los.do: Transcribe and translate a sequence and name the eukaryotic RNA-processing steps.
los.ek: mRNA is antiparallel to the template, read 5′→3′ from AUG; 5′ cap, poly-A tail and splicing happen in the nucleus.

los.do: Predict the protein-level effect of a silent, missense, nonsense or frameshift mutation.
los.ek: Insertions or deletions not in multiples of 3 shift the reading frame; nonsense creates an early stop codon.

los.do: Solve monohybrid, dihybrid and test crosses for genotype and phenotype ratios.
los.ek: Heterozygote cross 3:1; dihybrid 9:3:3:1; test cross with a heterozygote 1:1; multiply probabilities for independent genes.

los.do: Recognize incomplete dominance, codominance, epistasis and linkage from offspring ratios, and convert recombination frequency to map distance.
los.ek: 1% recombinant offspring = 1 map unit; linked genes give excess parental types; 9:3:4 signals recessive epistasis.

los.do: Determine the inheritance pattern of a trait from a pedigree.
los.ek: Autosomal recessive skips generations; X-linked recessive mostly affects males with no father-to-son transmission; dominant appears every generation.

los.do: Explain how nondisjunction causes aneuploidy and predict gametes from a meiosis I vs II error.
los.ek: An error in meiosis I gives all abnormal gametes; in meiosis II, half are normal; trisomy 21, XXY and XO are common results.

los.do: Predict lac and trp operon expression under given nutrient conditions.
los.ek: Lac is inducible: lactose inactivates the repressor, low glucose raises cAMP–CAP; trp is repressible: tryptophan activates the repressor.

los.do: Explain how chromatin modification and DNA methylation regulate eukaryotic genes heritably.
los.ek: Histone acetylation opens chromatin (on); DNA methylation of promoters silences; changes persist without altering sequence.

los.do: Choose and interpret a genetic technology: PCR, restriction digest, gel electrophoresis, cloning, CRISPR or sequencing.
los.ek: PCR cycles denature–anneal–extend, doubling copies (2^n); smaller fragments run farther on a gel; Cas9 cuts where its guide RNA matches.

los.do: Relate genome size to gene number and interpret genomic comparisons between species.
los.ek: Most eukaryotic DNA is noncoding; genome size does not track complexity; shared sequence measures relatedness.

los.do: Trace early development from fertilization through gastrulation and match germ layers to the tissues they form.
los.ek: Ectoderm: nervous system, epidermis; mesoderm: muscle, bone, blood, kidney; endoderm: gut and lung lining; Hox genes set the body axis.

los.do: Apply Hamilton's rule and classify social behaviors and communication signals.
los.ek: An altruistic gene spreads when r · B > C; full siblings r = 1/2, half siblings 1/4, cousins 1/8; pheromones, the honeybee waggle dance and territorial displays are signals.

los.do: Identify the type of selection from a change in a trait distribution.
los.ek: Directional shifts the mean; stabilizing narrows it; disruptive favors both extremes; selection acts on phenotype.

los.do: Calculate allele and genotype frequencies with Hardy–Weinberg and state its assumptions.
los.ek: p + q = 1; p² + 2pq + q² = 1; no selection, mutation, migration or drift, random mating, large population.

los.do: Classify a reproductive barrier and a speciation mode from a scenario.
los.ek: Prezygotic (habitat, temporal, behavioral, mechanical, gametic) vs postzygotic (hybrid inviability, sterility); allopatric needs a geographic barrier.

los.do: Distinguish homologous, analogous and vestigial structures and read relatedness from a phylogenetic tree.
los.ek: Homology reflects common ancestry; analogy reflects convergence; the most recent shared node marks the closest relatives.

los.do: Classify an animal behavior as fixed action pattern, imprinting, habituation, classical or operant conditioning, or altruism.
los.ek: Innate behaviors need no learning; kin selection explains altruism toward relatives sharing genes.

los.do: Predict population growth under exponential and logistic models and contrast r- and K-strategists.
los.ek: dN/dt = rN(K − N)/K; growth is fastest at N = K/2; r-selected: many offspring, little care.

los.do: Classify species interactions by their effect on each partner and order the stages of succession.
los.ek: Mutualism +/+, commensalism +/0, parasitism and predation +/−, competition −/−; primary succession starts on bare substrate.

los.do: Calculate energy transfer across trophic levels and trace carbon and nitrogen through an ecosystem.
los.ek: About 10% of energy passes to each higher level; N2 fixation → nitrification → assimilation → denitrification.

los.do: Calculate percent composition by mass from a formula.
los.ek: Mass % = (n × atomic mass of element) / molar mass × 100.

los.do: Determine an empirical formula from mass data, then the molecular formula from molar mass.
los.ek: Convert to moles, divide by the smallest, clear fractions; molecular = empirical × (M / M_empirical).

los.do: Balance a chemical equation by inspection.
los.ek: Atoms of each element and total charge are conserved; balance pure elements last.

los.do: Convert among mass, moles, particles and volume using molar mass, Avogadro's number and density.
Find the limiting reagent, theoretical yield and percent yield from a balanced equation.
los.ek: Compare moles available ÷ coefficient; the smallest ratio limits; % yield = actual / theoretical × 100.

los.do: Solve for an unknown P, V, n or T with the ideal gas law.
los.ek: PV = nRT with T in kelvin; R = 0.0821 L·atm/(mol·K); 1 mol at STP ≈ 22.4 L.

los.do: Predict a new state with Boyle's, Charles's or the combined gas law.
los.ek: P1V1/T1 = P2V2/T2; hold the constant variables fixed and cancel them.

los.do: Calculate partial pressures from mole fractions using Dalton's law.
los.ek: P_total = ΣP_i; P_i = X_i P_total.

los.do: Apply kinetic molecular theory to compare molecular speeds and effusion rates and predict deviations from ideality.
los.ek: Average KE ∝ T; rate₁/rate₂ = √(M₂/M₁); real gases deviate at high P and low T.

los.do: Rank substances by intermolecular force strength and predict boiling point, viscosity and surface tension.
los.ek: London < dipole–dipole < H-bonding (N, O, F–H) < ion–dipole; London grows with size and surface area.

los.do: Read a phase diagram or heating curve and calculate the heat for each segment.
los.ek: Sloped segments: q = mcΔT; flat segments: q = nΔH_phase; the triple point and critical point bound the liquid.

los.do: Predict how temperature and IMF strength change vapor pressure and normal boiling point.
los.ek: Vapor pressure rises with T and falls with stronger IMFs; boiling occurs when vapor pressure equals external pressure.

los.do: Classify a solid as ionic, molecular, covalent network or metallic and predict its properties.
los.ek: Network solids (diamond, SiO2) have the highest melting points; metals conduct as solids; ionic solids conduct only when molten or dissolved.

los.do: Convert among molarity, molality, mole fraction, mass percent and ppm, and solve dilutions.
los.ek: M = mol/L solution; m = mol/kg solvent; M1V1 = M2V2.

los.do: Calculate boiling-point elevation, freezing-point depression and osmotic pressure.
los.ek: ΔT = iKm; π = iMRT; i is the number of particles per formula unit (NaCl ≈ 2).

los.do: Predict solubility from polarity and how temperature and pressure change it.
los.ek: Like dissolves like; gas solubility falls with T and rises with partial pressure (Henry's law); most solids dissolve better hot.

los.do: Calculate vapor-pressure lowering with Raoult's law.
los.ek: P_solution = X_solvent × P°_solvent.

los.do: Identify Brønsted–Lowry acids, bases and conjugate pairs in a reaction.
los.ek: Acid donates H+, base accepts; a stronger acid has a weaker conjugate base.

los.do: Calculate pH, pOH, [H+] and [OH−] for strong acids and bases without a calculator.
los.ek: pH = −log[H+]; pH + pOH = 14 at 25 °C; for [H+] = a × 10⁻ⁿ, pH is between n − 1 and n.

los.do: Estimate the pH of a weak acid or base from Ka or Kb.
los.ek: [H+] ≈ √(Ka C) when ionization is small; Ka × Kb = Kw.

los.do: Calculate buffer pH with Henderson–Hasselbalch and choose a buffer for a target pH.
los.ek: pH = pKa + log([A−]/[HA]); a buffer works best within pKa ± 1.

los.do: Read a titration curve to find the equivalence point, half-equivalence point and pKa.
los.ek: At half-equivalence pH = pKa; weak acid + strong base equivalence pH > 7; n_acid = n_base at equivalence.

los.do: Write an equilibrium expression and use Q vs K to predict the direction of shift.
los.ek: Products over reactants raised to coefficients; omit pure solids and liquids; Q < K shifts right.

los.do: Predict the effect of a concentration, pressure or temperature change with Le Chatelier's principle.
los.ek: Only temperature changes K; added pressure favors fewer gas moles; heat acts as a product in exothermic reactions.

los.do: Calculate molar solubility from Ksp, including the common-ion effect.
los.ek: For AB2: Ksp = 4s³; a common ion lowers solubility; precipitation occurs when Q > Ksp.

los.do: Solve for equilibrium concentrations with an ICE table and the small-x approximation.
los.ek: Initial – change – equilibrium; drop x when K is tiny relative to the starting concentration.

los.do: Calculate ΔH_rxn from Hess's law, enthalpies of formation or bond energies.
los.ek: ΔH = ΣΔH_f(products) − ΣΔH_f(reactants); with bond energies, broken − formed; reverse a step, flip the sign.

los.do: Predict the sign of ΔS for a process.
los.ek: Entropy rises with more gas moles, solid → liquid → gas, dissolving, and higher T.

los.do: Determine spontaneity and the crossover temperature from ΔH and ΔS.
los.ek: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS; − ΔH, + ΔS always spontaneous; T_cross = ΔH/ΔS.

los.do: Relate ΔG° to K and to E°cell.
los.ek: ΔG° = −RT ln K = −nFE°; K > 1 ⇔ ΔG° < 0 ⇔ E° > 0.

los.do: Calculate heat exchanged in calorimetry and final temperatures of mixtures.
los.ek: q = mcΔT; heat lost by the hot body = heat gained by the cold one; c_water = 4.18 J/(g·°C).

los.do: Apply the first and third laws to a system: sign conventions for q and w, and absolute entropy.
los.ek: ΔU = q + w (work on the system positive); S = 0 for a perfect crystal at 0 K; state functions are path-independent.

los.do: Determine reaction orders and the rate constant from initial-rate data.
los.ek: Doubling [A] doubles rate → 1st order, quadruples → 2nd, no change → 0th; units of k depend on overall order.

los.do: Calculate the remaining amount or time from a first-order half-life.
los.ek: t½ = 0.693/k, independent of concentration; after n half-lives (½)ⁿ remains.

los.do: Read Ea, ΔH and the effect of a catalyst from a reaction energy diagram, and predict how T changes the rate.
los.ek: k = A e^(−Ea/RT); catalysts lower Ea for both directions without changing ΔH or K.

los.do: Derive a rate law from a mechanism's rate-determining step and identify intermediates and catalysts.
los.ek: The slow step sets the rate law; intermediates are made then consumed, catalysts are consumed then regenerated.

los.do: Assign oxidation numbers and identify the oxidizing and reducing agents.
los.ek: F always −1, O usually −2, H +1 with nonmetals; the species oxidized is the reducing agent.

los.do: Balance a redox equation in acidic or basic solution by half-reactions.
los.ek: Balance atoms, O with H2O, H with H+, charge with e−; in base add OH− to both sides to cancel H+.

los.do: Calculate E°cell from reduction potentials and identify anode, cathode and electron flow in galvanic and electrolytic cells.
los.ek: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode; oxidation at the anode; electrons flow anode → cathode; galvanic E° > 0, electrolytic needs input.

los.do: Calculate the mass plated or the current/time needed in electrolysis.
los.ek: n_e = It/F with F = 96 485 C/mol; moles metal = n_e / (electrons per ion).

los.do: Write the electron configuration of an atom or ion, including Cr/Cu exceptions and transition-metal cations.
los.ek: Aufbau, Pauli, Hund; transition metals lose 4s before 3d; half- and fully filled d subshells are favored.

los.do: Assign or validate a set of quantum numbers for an electron.
Draw a Lewis structure and use formal charge to choose the best one.
los.ek: FC = valence − nonbonding e− − ½ bonding e−; the best structure minimizes formal charges and puts negatives on electronegative atoms.

los.do: Predict molecular geometry, bond angle and polarity with VSEPR.
los.ek: Electron domains set the shape (4 → tetrahedral 109.5°, lone pairs compress angles); symmetric shapes cancel bond dipoles.

los.do: Identify hybridization and count σ and π bonds; classify a bond as ionic, polar or nonpolar covalent.
los.ek: Domains 2/3/4 → sp/sp²/sp³; single = 1σ, double = 1σ + 1π, triple = 1σ + 2π; ΔEN > ~1.7 is ionic.

los.do: Count protons, neutrons and electrons in an isotope or ion and compute average atomic mass.
los.ek: Z = protons, A = protons + neutrons; average mass = Σ(fraction × isotope mass).

los.do: Relate photon energy, frequency and wavelength to electron transitions and the experiments behind atomic theory.
los.ek: E = hν = hc/λ; emission when e− falls to a lower level; Thomson (electron), Rutherford (nucleus), Bohr (quantized levels).

los.do: Rank elements by atomic radius, ionization energy, electronegativity and electron affinity.
los.ek: Across a period Z_eff rises: radius falls, IE and EN rise; down a group radius rises, IE falls; cations smaller, anions larger.

los.do: Predict the typical ions, reactivity and compounds of alkali metals, alkaline-earth metals, halogens and noble gases.
los.ek: Group 1 forms +1 and reacts with water to give H2 and hydroxide; halogens form −1, reactivity falls down the group; noble gases are inert.

los.do: Explain characteristic properties of transition elements: multiple oxidation states, colored ions and paramagnetism.
los.ek: Partially filled d orbitals give variable charges, d–d color and unpaired electrons.

los.do: Balance a nuclear equation and identify the decay mode from the change in A and Z.
los.ek: α: A − 4, Z − 2; β−: Z + 1; β+ and electron capture: Z − 1; γ: no change; A and Z both conserved.

los.do: Calculate the remaining fraction or the elapsed time for radioactive decay.
los.ek: N = N₀(½)^(t/t½); decay is first order.

los.do: Calculate binding energy from mass defect and compare nuclear stability.
los.ek: E = Δm c²; 1 u ≈ 931.5 MeV; binding energy per nucleon peaks near Fe-56.

los.do: Choose the glassware or equipment for a measurement and report the result to the right significant figures.
los.ek: Volumetric pipets and flasks are precise; beakers are not; read the meniscus at eye level, one estimated digit.

los.do: Distinguish accuracy from precision, classify an error as random or systematic, and compute percent error.
los.ek: % error = |measured − true| / true × 100; systematic error shifts every reading the same way.

los.do: Identify the correct safety procedure for a lab hazard.
los.ek: Add acid to water; work with volatiles in the fume hood; flush skin or eye exposure for 15 minutes.

los.do: Extract a quantity from a plotted data set, such as a slope, intercept or best-fit value.
los.ek: Linearize first (ln[A] vs t for 1st order; 1/T vs ln k for Ea); the slope carries the physical constant.

los.do: Predict the product of a step from its curved arrows, telling two-electron arrows from fishhooks.
los.ek: Double-headed arrows move electron pairs and fishhooks move single electrons, always from the electron source to the electron sink.

los.do: Draw the curved arrows that convert given reactants into given products.
los.ek: Start arrows at lone pairs or bonds, end at an atom or bond; count formal charges before and after.

los.do: Draw resonance structures and pick the major contributor.
los.ek: Move only π and lone-pair electrons; the best contributor has full octets, fewest charges, and negative charge on the most electronegative atom.

los.do: Predict the steps and selectivity of a free-radical halogenation.
los.ek: Initiation, propagation, termination; Br₂ is highly selective for the 3° hydrogen, Cl₂ much less so; radical stability 3° > 2° > 1°.

los.do: Predict the product of an electrophilic addition, including Markovnikov regiochemistry and carbocation rearrangements.
los.ek: H adds to the carbon with more H; a carbocation shifts H or CH₃ to become more substituted or resonance-stabilized.

los.do: Decide whether SN1, SN2, E1 or E2 operates from substrate, nucleophile/base, solvent and temperature.
los.ek: SN2: 1°, strong nucleophile, polar aprotic, inversion; SN1/E1: 3°, weak nucleophile, polar protic; E2: strong bulky base, anti-periplanar H; heat favors elimination.
los.std: ada-dat:3.1.a, acs-accm-organic:I.B.3, acs-accm-organic:IV.A.2, acs-accm-organic:IV.D.1, acs-accm-organic:IV.E.1, acs-accm-organic:IV.E.2, acs-accm-organic:V.E.2

los.do: Predict the product of a Diels–Alder reaction, including stereochemistry.
los.ek: s-cis diene + dienophile → cyclohexene in one concerted step; dienophile substituents keep their cis/trans relationship; endo is favored.

los.do: Read a reaction coordinate diagram: count steps, locate intermediates and transition states, and find the rate-determining step.
los.ek: Peaks are transition states, valleys are intermediates; the highest barrier is rate-determining; Hammond: a TS resembles the species nearer in energy.

los.do: Predict the substitution or elimination product, including stereochemistry and Zaitsev vs Hofmann regiochemistry.
los.ek: SN2 inverts, SN1 racemizes; small bases give the more substituted alkene, bulky bases (t-BuO⁻) the less substituted one.

los.do: Predict the product of an alkene or alkyne reaction: HX, hydration, hydroboration–oxidation, halogenation, hydrogenation, ozonolysis.
los.ek: Hydroboration is anti-Markovnikov and syn; X₂ adds anti; Lindlar gives cis alkene, Na/NH₃ trans; ozonolysis cleaves C=C to carbonyls.

los.do: Predict the product of an alcohol reaction: oxidation, conversion to a halide or sulfonate, dehydration.
los.ek: PCC stops 1° alcohols at the aldehyde, chromic acid goes to the acid; 3° alcohols resist oxidation; SOCl₂/PBr₃ give halides with inversion.

los.do: Predict the regiochemistry and stereochemistry of ether cleavage and epoxide opening under acid and base.
los.ek: Base or strong nucleophile attacks the less hindered epoxide carbon; acid directs attack to the more substituted carbon; opening is anti.

los.do: Predict the product of an electrophilic aromatic substitution from substituent directing effects.
los.ek: Activators (−OH, −NH₂, −R) and halogens direct ortho/para; deactivators (−NO₂, −C=O, −CN, −SO₃H) direct meta; halogens deactivate.

los.do: Rank carboxylic acid derivatives by reactivity and predict nucleophilic acyl substitution products.
los.ek: Acid chloride > anhydride > ester ≈ acid > amide; a derivative converts only to less reactive ones.

los.do: Predict the product of nucleophilic addition to an aldehyde or ketone: hydride, Grignard, acetal, imine/enamine, Wittig.
los.ek: Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones; Grignard adds carbon then protonates to an alcohol; 1° amines give imines, 2° give enamines.

los.do: Predict the product of an alpha-carbonyl reaction: enolate alkylation, aldol, Claisen, haloform.
los.ek: LDA at low T forms the kinetic (less substituted) enolate; aldol makes a β-hydroxy carbonyl that dehydrates to an enone with heat.

los.do: Plan a two-step or multi-step synthesis by working backward from the target.
los.ek: Disconnect the bond formed last; track carbon count and functional-group changes; reject routes with wrong regio- or stereochemistry.

los.do: Predict which functional group reacts when a molecule carries several.
los.ek: NaBH₄ reduces aldehydes and ketones only; LiAlH₄ also reduces esters, acids and amides; protect an alcohol or carbonyl to spare it.

los.do: Rank compounds from different functional groups by acidity using pKa landmarks.
los.ek: ≈ pKa: HCl −7, RCOOH 5, phenol 10, H₂O 15.7, ROH 16–18, terminal alkyne 25, NH₃ 38, alkane 50.

los.do: Rank acids within a functional group by charge, atom size, electronegativity, resonance, induction, hybridization and sterics.
los.ek: A more stable conjugate base means a stronger acid: larger atom > more electronegative > resonance > induction (falls off with distance) > more s character.

los.do: Predict the products and direction of an acid–base equilibrium.
los.ek: The equilibrium favors the side with the weaker acid (higher pKa); K ≈ 10^(pKa product acid − pKa reactant acid).

los.do: Rank nitrogen and oxygen bases by basicity, including resonance and steric effects on amines.
los.ek: Alkylamines > NH₃ > aniline > amide; lone pairs in resonance or in sp orbitals are less basic.

topics.title: Chemical and Physical Properties of Molecules

los.do: Rank organic compounds by boiling point, melting point and water solubility.
los.ek: H-bonding and molar mass raise bp; branching lowers bp but symmetry raises mp; small alcohols and acids are water-soluble.

los.do: Choose and interpret a separation technique: TLC/column chromatography, acid–base extraction, recrystallization, distillation.
los.ek: On silica, polar compounds have lower Rf; acids move to aqueous NaHCO₃/NaOH as salts, amines to aqueous HCl; distill when bp differ by > 25 °C, otherwise fractional.

los.do: Identify functional groups from characteristic IR absorptions.
Interpret a ¹H NMR spectrum from chemical shift, integration and splitting.
los.ek: Shifts: alkyl 0.9–2, next to C=O 2–2.5, next to O 3.3–4, vinyl 4.5–6.5, aromatic 6.5–8, aldehyde 9–10, acid 10–12; n + 1 rule.

los.do: Count ¹³C NMR signals from molecular symmetry and assign shift regions.
los.ek: One signal per unique carbon environment; C=O 160–220, aromatic/alkene 100–150, C–O 50–90, alkyl 0–50.

los.do: Deduce a structure from a molecular formula and combined IR, ¹H and ¹³C NMR data.
los.ek: Degrees of unsaturation = (2C + 2 + N − H − X)/2; one ring or π bond each; a benzene ring counts 4.

los.do: Identify every functional group in a structure.
los.ek: Know alcohol, ether, aldehyde, ketone, acid, ester, amide, amine, nitrile, acid chloride, anhydride, epoxide, phenol, thiol, imine, enamine.

los.do: Name a compound by IUPAC rules, or draw it from its name.
los.ek: Highest-priority group sets the suffix and lowest locant; longest chain containing it; substituents alphabetical; E/Z and R/S as prefixes.

los.do: Assign R/S configuration to a stereocenter and identify chiral molecules.
los.ek: Rank by atomic number (CIP), lowest priority to the back, trace 1→2→3; if the lowest points forward, reverse the answer.

los.do: Classify a pair of structures as identical, enantiomers, diastereomers, meso or constitutional isomers.
los.ek: Enantiomers invert every stereocenter, diastereomers some; meso has stereocenters and an internal mirror plane; max 2ⁿ stereoisomers.

los.do: Pick the most stable Newman or chair conformation.
los.ek: Anti < gauche < eclipsed in energy; bulky chair substituents go equatorial; a ring flip swaps axial and equatorial.

los.do: Classify a ring as aromatic, antiaromatic or nonaromatic.
los.ek: Cyclic, planar, fully conjugated with 4n + 2 π electrons is aromatic; 4n is antiaromatic; count lone pairs only if they sit in the p system.

los.do: Compare bond lengths, bond angles and hybridization across a structure.
los.ek: More s character means shorter, stronger C–H bonds: sp 180°, sp² 120°, sp³ 109.5°; triple < double < single in length.

los.do: Rank carbocations, radicals, carbanions and alkenes by stability.
los.ek: Carbocations and radicals: allylic/benzylic ≈ 3° > 2° > 1° > methyl (hyperconjugation, resonance); carbanions the reverse; more substituted and trans alkenes are more stable.

los.do: Identify the one aperture a 3-D object can pass through straight on, from any starting face.
los.ek: The object may be rotated before entry but not turned once in; the opening is its exact outer silhouette at the same scale; hidden parts are regular and symmetric indentations repeat.

los.do: Eliminate aperture choices by proportion and by a single distinctive feature before matching the full outline.
los.ek: Many wrong openings have the right shape but wrong size or ratio; check the longest dimension and one asymmetric notch first.

los.do: Select the missing top, front or end view given the other two orthographic views.
los.ek: Top view upper left, front lower left, end lower right; top and front share width, front and end share height; hidden edges are dotted.

los.do: Eliminate view choices by checking solid vs dotted lines and edge alignment with the given views.
los.ek: Every edge in one view must project to a line or point in the others; a feature visible in one view may be hidden (dotted) in another.

los.do: Rank four interior angles from smallest to largest.
los.ek: Compare the openness at equal distance from each vertex; mentally rotate so one arm is horizontal; decide the most extreme angles first.

los.do: Determine the hole pattern on a square sheet after it is unfolded.
los.ek: Unfold in reverse order, reflecting each hole across each fold line; the paper is never turned over; holes per punch = layers at that spot.

los.do: Eliminate unfold choices by counting the expected holes and checking which quadrants must be symmetric.
los.ek: Total holes = punches × layers; a fold line is always a mirror axis of the final pattern.

los.do: Count the cubes in a figure that have a given number of painted faces.
los.ek: Cubes are cemented and equal; every exposed face is painted except the resting bottom; hidden cubes exist only where needed for support; never zero.

los.do: Tally every cube in a figure by painted-face count in one systematic pass, then answer all the questions on that figure from the tally.
los.ek: Go column by column, front to back, and record 1–5 for each cube; the tally total must equal the cube count.

los.do: Identify which 3-D figure a flat pattern forms when folded.
los.ek: Faces adjacent in the pattern stay adjacent; opposite faces of a cube are never adjacent in the net; marked or shaded faces fix orientation.

los.do: Eliminate folded-figure choices by checking one distinctive face pair or a face count.
los.ek: Count faces and edges first; then test which face a marked edge must meet; one impossible adjacency rejects a choice.

los.do: Locate the passage sentence that answers a detail question and match it to the choice that restates it.
los.ek: Detail answers paraphrase the text; choices that copy its wording but change a qualifier, number or relationship are traps.

los.do: Identify the main idea of a passage or paragraph.
los.ek: The main idea covers the whole passage; choices that are true of one paragraph only are too narrow, ones that go beyond it too broad.

los.do: Infer the meaning of a technical term or phrase from its context in the passage.
los.ek: Passages define their terms nearby — by apposition, example or contrast; use the passage's meaning, not outside knowledge.

los.do: Judge whether a statement is supported, contradicted or not addressed by the passage.
los.ek: Except/not and true-statement items require checking every choice against the text; 'not addressed' is not 'false'.

los.do: Draw an inference that follows necessarily from stated facts in the passage.
los.ek: A correct inference needs no outside facts and no extra assumption; reject extreme words (always, never, proves).

los.do: Identify the author's purpose, tone or attitude toward a claim.
los.ek: Scientific passages are mostly neutral-informative; tone choices like hostile or ecstatic are rarely right.

los.do: Trace a cause–effect sequence, comparison or chronology described in the passage.
los.ek: Map the passage's structure (who, what, when, why) as you read so sequence questions take seconds.

los.do: Complete one passage and its questions in about 20 minutes with every item answered.
los.ek: 60 min / 3 passages ≈ 20 min each, ≈ 72 s per item; mark slow items and return; a blank scores the same as a wrong answer.

los.do: Solve linear, quadratic and systems of equations and simplify algebraic expressions.
los.ek: Factor or use x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/2a; eliminate or substitute for systems; check that the answer fits the original.

los.do: Solve a linear or compound inequality and express its solution set.
los.ek: Multiplying or dividing by a negative flips the inequality sign.

los.do: Simplify and evaluate expressions with exponents, roots and scientific notation.
Solve equations and inequalities with absolute value.
los.ek: |x| = a gives x = ±a; |x| < a gives −a < x < a; |x| > a gives x < −a or x > a.

los.do: Set up and solve a ratio or proportion, including direct and inverse variation.
los.ek: a/b = c/d ⇒ ad = bc; direct y = kx, inverse y = k/x; part-to-part vs part-to-whole ratios differ.

los.do: Read and interpret graphs of lines and functions: slope, intercepts, intersections, transformations.
los.ek: Slope = Δy/Δx; y = mx + b; parallel lines share slope, perpendicular slopes multiply to −1.

los.do: Extract and combine values from a table, bar chart or line graph to answer a question.
los.ek: Read the axes, units and scale before any value; percent change = (new − old)/old × 100.

los.do: Decide whether the given statements are sufficient to answer a question, alone or together.
los.ek: Test each statement alone, then together; sufficiency means one determined value, not the value itself; don't compute what you only need to know exists.

los.do: Compare two quantities and decide which is greater, whether they are equal, or whether the relationship can't be determined.
los.ek: Try special cases (0, 1, negatives, fractions); if different cases give different orders, it can't be determined.

los.do: Simplify both sides identically to compare them without computing exact values.
los.ek: Add, subtract or multiply by a positive on both sides; multiplying by an unknown sign is not allowed.

los.do: Calculate the probability of compound events: and/or, independent, dependent and complementary.
los.ek: P(A and B) = P(A)P(B|A); P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B); P(at least one) = 1 − P(none).

los.do: Count arrangements with permutations and combinations.
los.ek: nPr = n!/(n − r)! when order matters; nCr = n!/[r!(n − r)!] when it does not.

los.do: Calculate and compare mean, median, mode, range and standard deviation, including the effect of changing a data point.
los.ek: Mean = sum/n, so a new mean gives the missing value by sum; an outlier moves the mean, not the median; adding a constant leaves SD unchanged.

los.do: Find a weighted average or the combined mean of two groups.
los.ek: Combined mean = (n₁x̄₁ + n₂x̄₂)/(n₁ + n₂); it lies closer to the larger group's mean.

los.do: Solve rate, distance and work problems.
los.ek: d = rt; combined work: 1/t = 1/t₁ + 1/t₂; average speed = total distance / total time, not the mean of speeds.

los.do: Solve percent, discount, markup and interest problems.
los.ek: Successive percent changes multiply (×1.2 then ×0.8 = ×0.96); simple I = Prt; compound A = P(1 + r)^t.

los.do: Solve mixture and concentration problems.
los.ek: Amount of solute is conserved: c₁V₁ + c₂V₂ = c_f(V₁ + V₂).

los.do: Convert units and solve age, consecutive-integer and number-relationship problems by translating words into equations.
los.ek: Chain conversion factors so units cancel; define one variable, write every other quantity in terms of it.

los.do: Convert between Universal and FDI notation, permanent and primary.
los.ek: FDI: quadrant 1–4 (primary 5–8), then position from the midline.

los.do: Recall the primary and permanent eruption sequence.
los.ek: 20 primary teeth by about 3; first molars at 6, second at 12.

los.do: Classify a lesion by G. V. Black's classes.
los.ek: I pits and fissures … VI cusp tips.

los.do: Make a pulpal diagnosis from thermal and electric tests.
los.ek: Lingering pain is irreversible; no response is necrosis.

los.do: Compute clinical attachment level and stage periodontitis by it.
los.ek: CAL from the CEJ; 1–2 mm stage I, 3–4 stage II, 5+ stage III or IV.

los.do: Localize objects with the SLOB rule and recognise angulation errors.
los.ek: Same lingual, opposite buccal; vertical errors elongate or foreshorten.

los.do: Take a chief complaint and history, and run a head-and-neck and intraoral examination in order.
