los.ek: Record the complaint in the patient's words and characterise pain (onset, location, quality, duration, triggers, relief); examine extraorally (asymmetry, nodes, TMJ, glands) before intraorally.

los.do: Predict a test result from the history and order the phases of a treatment plan.
los.ek: Plan in phases: systemic, urgent (acute), disease control, definitive (restorative/prosthetic), maintenance.

los.do: Communicate options and adapt care to the patient's age, needs and values.
los.ek: Explain etiology, alternatives (including no treatment), risks and prognosis; use open questions and reflective listening; tell-show-do for children; plan for xerostomia and dexterity in older adults.

los.do: Relate oral disease to systemic disease and convert HbA1c to an estimated average glucose.
los.ek: Periodontitis and diabetes worsen each other; eAG (mg/dL) = 28.7 × HbA1c − 46.7 (ADAG); A1c ≥ 6.5% is diagnostic for diabetes.

los.do: Give the first drug or action for common office emergencies.
los.ek: Syncope: supine, legs up. Anaphylaxis: IM epinephrine. Angina: nitroglycerin.

los.do: Decide who needs antibiotic prophylaxis against endocarditis and with what.
los.ek: Prosthetic valves, previous IE, some congenital disease, transplant valvulopathy; amoxicillin 2 g.

los.do: Calculate maximum cartridges by weight and by epinephrine limit.
los.ek: mg/mL = % × 10; 1.8 mL cartridges; 1:100,000 = 0.01 mg/mL.

los.do: Explain local anesthetic action, metabolism and the role of vasoconstrictors.
los.ek: Uncharged base crosses the membrane; infection traps the cation; articaine is cleared in plasma.

los.do: Convert NaF concentration to ppm fluoride and compute the probably toxic dose.
los.ek: F is 45% of NaF; 1% = 10,000 ppm; PTD 5 mg F/kg.

los.do: Recognise substance use that changes dental care and total an opioid prescription in morphine milligram equivalents.
los.ek: MME/day = mg per dose × doses per day × conversion factor (codeine 0.15, hydrocodone 1, oxycodone 1.5, CDC 2022); avoid epinephrine within 24 h of cocaine use.

los.do: Use proportion and the supracrestal attachment to plan esthetic and soft-tissue changes.
los.ek: Seen from the front, central : lateral : canine widths follow roughly 1.618 : 1 : 0.618; keep about 3 mm from the restorative margin to bone (about 2 mm of attached tissue plus the sulcus).

los.do: Evaluate treatment outcomes and convert survival over years into an annual failure rate.
los.ek: AFR = 1 − S^(1/years); recall intervals follow risk (often 3–6 months for high caries or periodontal risk).

topics.title: Chemistry of the mouth and host defence

los.do: Relate plaque pH to enamel and root demineralisation, and fluoride to the critical pH.
los.ek: Hydroxyapatite dissolves below about pH 5.5, fluorapatite below about 4.5, root dentin near 6.2–6.7; each sugar exposure drops plaque pH for 20–40 minutes (Stephan curve).

los.do: Use the bicarbonate buffer to compute salivary pH and explain how flow changes it.
los.ek: pH = 6.1 + log([HCO₃⁻]/(0.03·P_CO₂)); stimulated saliva carries more bicarbonate and buffers better.

los.do: Match the host's defences to the stages of gingival and periodontal disease.
los.ek: Neutrophils dominate the early lesion; T cells, then B and plasma cells, the established and advanced lesions; secretory IgA and lysozyme defend saliva; host enzymes (MMPs) and RANKL drive tissue and bone loss.

los.do: Interpret immunisation and exposure tests for dental personnel.
los.ek: Anti-HBs ≥ 10 mIU/mL after the hepatitis B series means protection; a non-responder repeats the series once; post-exposure HIV prophylaxis should start within hours (ideally under 2, at most 72).

los.do: Classify instruments (Spaulding) and state sterilization and monitoring standards.
los.ek: Critical and semicritical items are sterilized; spore tests weekly.

los.do: Compute sensitivity, specificity and predictive values from a 2×2 table.
los.ek: Sensitivity and specificity belong to the test; predictive values depend on prevalence.

los.do: Recognise the limits of general practice and refer, and assess one's own competence.
los.ek: Refer when the case exceeds training or equipment; the referring dentist still owes follow-up; continuing education and outcome audit drive self-assessment.

los.do: Read practice finances and meet OSHA and HIPAA duties.
los.ek: Overhead % = expenses ÷ collections; collection ratio = collected ÷ produced; HIPAA protects health information; OSHA's bloodborne pathogens standard protects staff.

los.do: Plan for emergencies and disasters in the practice.
los.ek: Written plan with roles, evacuation and communication, data backup off site, and drills; dentists may help identify victims through dental records.

los.do: Delegate to allied dental personnel at the right level of supervision.
los.ek: Direct supervision: dentist present and checks; general: dentist authorised but need not be present; the allowed duties are set by each state's practice act.

los.do: Measure a population's caries and choose community programmes.
los.ek: DMFT = decayed + missing + filled teeth; community water fluoridation at 0.7 mg/L (USPHS 2015); school sealant programmes; teledentistry and silver diamine fluoride widen access.

los.do: Apply quality assurance: audit, compare against a standard and fix the process.
los.ek: Plan–Do–Study–Act cycles; weekly biological (spore) testing of sterilisers; a failed spore test means retest, recall loads and repair.

los.do: Compute stress, elastic modulus and Vickers hardness, and compare restoratives with enamel and dentin.
los.ek: MPa = N/mm²; E = σ/ε; HV = 1.8544 F/d².

los.do: Compute flexural strength from a three-point bend test.
los.ek: σ = 3FL/(2bh²); ISO 4049 uses 2 × 2 mm bars on a 20 mm span.

los.do: Compute a probability of failure from Weibull statistics and read the Weibull modulus.
los.ek: P_f = 1 − exp(−(σ/σ₀)^m); a higher m means more reliable, less scattered strength.

los.do: Explain what each composite component does and how filler changes properties.
los.ek: Silane couples filler; camphorquinone absorbs blue light; oxygen inhibits the surface.

los.do: Compute radiant exposure, depth of cure, shrinkage, C-factor and water sorption.
los.ek: J/cm² = mW/cm² × s / 1000; depth = scraped length / 2; shrinkage = 1 − ρu/ρc.

los.do: Compute degree of conversion from FTIR peak ratios.
los.ek: DC = 1 − (A₁₆₃₈/A₁₆₀₈)cured ÷ (A₁₆₃₈/A₁₆₀₈)uncured; the aromatic band is the internal standard.

los.do: Convert filler loading between weight and volume fractions.
Compute water solubility as ISO 4049 defines it and judge sorption and solubility against the limits.
los.ek: Solubility = (m₁ − m₃)/V; limits 40 µg/mm³ sorption and 7.5 µg/mm³ solubility.

los.do: Compute the marginal gap from a thermal-expansion mismatch.
los.ek: ΔL = Δα·L·ΔT; tooth about 11.4 ppm/°C.

los.do: Explain the setting and properties of amalgam, glass ionomer, zinc phosphate and ZOE, and how etching works.
los.ek: High-copper removes γ₂; GI bonds and releases fluoride; eugenol inhibits resin.

los.do: Choose the surface treatment for bonding a ceramic restoration.
los.ek: Glass ceramics: HF + silane. Zirconia: air abrasion + MDP.

los.do: Classify adhesive systems and choose one for a situation.
los.ek: Etch-and-rinse (3- or 2-step), self-etch (2- or 1-step), universal; the hybrid layer; 10-MDP bonds chemically to hydroxyapatite and zirconia.

los.do: Compare zirconia and glass-ceramic classes by strength, translucency and bonding.
los.ek: 3Y-TZP strongest and most opaque; 5Y more translucent, weaker; lithium disilicate is etchable with HF.

los.do: Compute bond strength from a shear or microtensile test.
los.ek: σ = F/A; microtensile beams are about 1 mm².

los.do: Mix gypsum at the right water/powder ratio and choose and handle impression materials.
los.ek: W/P 0.50 plaster, 0.30 stone, 0.24 die stone; pour alginate at once; PVS is the most stable.

los.do: Classify a casting alloy by noble-metal content.
los.ek: High noble ≥ 60% noble with ≥ 40% gold; noble ≥ 25%; silver is not noble.

los.do: Recall root and canal numbers of permanent teeth.
los.ek: Maxillary first molar 3 roots (MB often 2 canals); mandibular first molar 2 roots; maxillary first premolar usually 2.

los.do: Recall cusp and crown features that identify a tooth.
los.ek: Mandibular first molar 5 cusps; maxillary first molar 4 plus Carabelli; mandibular second premolar may have 3.

los.do: Classify occlusion by Angle's molar relationship.
los.ek: Class I: MB cusp of the maxillary first molar in the buccal groove of the mandibular first molar; II: distal mandible; III: mesial mandible.

los.do: Judge an abutment by its crown-to-root ratio.
los.ek: Ideal 1:2; 2:3 is acceptable; 1:1 is the minimum for an abutment.

los.do: Name the nerve that supplies a structure.
los.ek: Muscles of mastication: V3. Facial expression: VII. Taste anterior two-thirds: VII (chorda tympani); posterior third: IX. Tongue movement: XII.

los.do: Know what each muscle of mastication does.
los.ek: Masseter, temporalis, medial pterygoid close; lateral pterygoid opens and protrudes.

los.do: Locate salivary ducts and the landmarks of nerve blocks.
los.ek: Parotid (Stensen) opposite the maxillary second molar; submandibular (Wharton) at the sublingual caruncle.

los.do: Trace the arterial supply and lymph drainage of the mouth.
los.ek: Teeth from branches of the maxillary artery; lower lip and floor drain to submental and submandibular nodes.

topics.title: Tooth development, tissues and developmental anomalies

los.do: Name the cell and germ layer behind each dental tissue.
los.ek: Enamel from ameloblasts (ectoderm); dentin, pulp and cementum from ectomesenchyme (neural crest).

los.do: Recognise developmental anomalies of teeth.
los.ek: Amelogenesis imperfecta: enamel only. Dentinogenesis imperfecta: opalescent teeth, obliterated pulps, linked with osteogenesis imperfecta.

los.do: Explain how clefts form.
los.ek: Cleft lip: failed fusion of the medial nasal and maxillary processes. Cleft palate: failed fusion of the palatal shelves.

los.do: Recall analgesic choices and limits for dental pain.
los.ek: Ibuprofen 400 mg ± acetaminophen 500–1000 mg beats opioids for most dental pain; acetaminophen ≤ 4 g/day (usual adult maximum).

los.do: Choose antibiotics and know their dental side effects.
los.ek: Amoxicillin first line; penicillin allergy: azithromycin or doxycycline (clindamycin no longer recommended for prophylaxis, AHA 2021).

los.do: Recognise drug interactions and complications that change dental care.
los.ek: Epinephrine with nonselective β-blockers: hypertension and reflex bradycardia. Antiresorptives: MRONJ. Bisphosphonates and denosumab before extractions.

los.do: Calculate a weight-based pediatric antibiotic dose.
los.ek: Endocarditis prophylaxis: amoxicillin 50 mg/kg, not above the adult 2 g.

los.do: Find how much drug remains after a number of half-lives.
los.ek: Fraction left = (1/2)^{t/t½}; about 5 half-lives to clear 97%.

topics.title: Oral microbes, infections, immunity and exposure

los.do: Link oral diseases to their organisms.
los.ek: Caries: S. mutans starts, lactobacilli advance. Periodontitis: the red complex (P. gingivalis, T. forsythia, T. denticola).

los.do: Know bloodborne pathogen risk and the response to an exposure.
los.ek: Percutaneous transmission risk, unvaccinated source-positive: HBV up to about 30%, HCV about 1.8%, HIV about 0.3%.

los.do: Classify hypersensitivity reactions met in dentistry.
los.ek: Type I IgE (latex anaphylaxis, penicillin), IV T-cell (contact dermatitis to latex accelerators, nickel, methacrylates).

los.do: Name a soft-tissue lesion from its description.
los.ek: Mucocele: lower lip, after trauma. Ranula: floor of mouth. Fibroma: firm, smooth, on the bite line. Pyogenic granuloma: red, bleeds easily, often in pregnancy.

los.do: Rank lesions by malignant risk and know oral cancer's usual sites.
los.ek: Erythroplakia carries the highest risk; squamous cell carcinoma is most common on the lateral and ventral tongue and floor of mouth.

los.do: Name a jaw lesion from its radiograph and location.
los.ek: Dentigerous cyst around an unerupted crown; periapical cyst at a non-vital apex; ameloblastoma multilocular in the posterior mandible; OKC with Gorlin syndrome.

los.do: Tell the blistering diseases apart.
los.ek: Pemphigus vulgaris: intraepithelial split, Nikolsky positive, desmoglein 3. Mucous membrane pemphigoid: subepithelial split, eye scarring risk.

topics.title: Periodontics, endodontics, prosthodontics, pediatrics, surgery and orthodontics

los.do: Classify partially edentulous arches by Kennedy.
los.ek: I bilateral distal extension; II unilateral distal extension; III bounded posterior; IV a single bounded anterior space crossing the midline.

los.do: Choose pediatric pulp therapy and space maintenance.
los.ek: Vital primary pulp exposure with healthy radicular pulp: pulpotomy. Necrotic primary pulp in a restorable tooth: pulpectomy. Early loss of a primary second molar: distal shoe if the first permanent molar has not erupted.

los.do: Know common oral-surgery thresholds and complications.
los.ek: Alveolar osteitis appears 2–4 days after extraction; usual INR limit for simple extractions about 3.5 (with local measures); ASA classes I–VI.

los.do: Diagnose periapical conditions and choose endodontic treatment.
los.ek: Symptomatic apical periodontitis: tender to percussion. Acute apical abscess: swelling. Condensing osteitis: radiopacity at the apex of an inflamed pulp.

units.title: Systemic disease and medical risk (CC1, CC8, CC16)

los.do: Decide whether to treat from blood pressure.
los.ek: AHA 2017: stage 2 hypertension from 140/90; elective dental care is usually deferred at 180/110 or above.

los.do: Give the drug, dose and route for office emergencies.
los.ek: Anaphylaxis: epinephrine 0.3 mg IM (adult; 0.15 mg child). Angina: nitroglycerin 0.4 mg sublingual every 5 min, up to 3. Hypoglycemia: 15–20 g fast sugar if conscious.

los.do: Read lab values that change dental treatment.
los.ek: INR target 2–3 for most warfarin patients; HbA1c above about 8% means poor control; platelets below about 50,000 need consultation before surgery.

units.title: Ethics, jurisprudence, behaviour and research (FK9, FK10)

los.do: Apply the ADA principles of ethics.
los.ek: Autonomy, non-maleficence, beneficence, justice and veracity.

los.do: Know the rules for consent, records and reporting.
los.ek: Informed consent: diagnosis, proposed treatment, risks, benefits, alternatives including no treatment. Suspected child abuse: report (mandated). Records: never alter; add a dated correction.

los.do: Compute relative risk, odds ratio and number needed to treat.
los.ek: RR = [a/(a+b)]/[c/(c+d)]; OR = ad/bc; NNT = 1/ARR.

los.do: Name the study design and the level of evidence.
los.ek: Systematic reviews of RCTs at the top; then RCTs, cohort, case–control, case series, expert opinion.

los.do: Recommend fluoride supplements by age and water fluoride.
los.ek: ADA 2010 schedule: water < 0.3 ppm: 0.25 mg (6 mo–3 y), 0.5 mg (3–6 y), 1.0 mg (6–16 y); 0.3–0.6 ppm: 0, 0.25, 0.5; above 0.6 ppm: none.

units.title: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control (10–16%)

los.do: Choose contact, droplet or airborne precautions for a disease.
los.ek: Airborne: TB, measles, varicella. Droplet: influenza, pertussis, meningococcus. Contact: C. difficile, MRSA, scabies.

los.do: Put on and take off PPE in the right order.
los.ek: On: gown, mask, goggles, gloves. Off: gloves, goggles, gown, mask.

los.do: Apply ergonomic, home-safety and equipment-safety principles.
los.ek: Wide base of support and lift with the legs; remove throw rugs, add grab bars and lighting; inspect equipment and tag faulty items.

los.do: Apply client identification, fire response and restraint rules.
los.ek: Two identifiers; RACE and PASS; restraints tied to the frame, checked and released at least every 2 hours.

los.do: Respond to emergencies and hazards: disaster triage, hazardous materials, radiation and security events.
los.ek: START triage tags; time, distance and shielding for radiation; sharps and biohazard disposal; follow the facility's security plan.

los.do: Match a diet rule to a condition or a drug.
los.ek: Gluten-free in celiac disease; no tyramine with MAOIs; steady vitamin K with warfarin; steady sodium with lithium.

los.do: Total intake in mL from household measures.
los.ek: 1 oz = 30 mL.

los.do: Teach the use of canes, crutches and walkers, and prevent complications of immobility.
los.ek: Cane on the strong side; move cane with the weak leg; turn at least every 2 h; immobility risks pressure injury, DVT, pneumonia and constipation.

los.do: Position a client for a condition or procedure and say why.
los.ek: ICP: head up 30°, midline. Liver biopsy: right side. Air embolism: left side, head down.

los.do: Provide hygiene, nonpharmacological comfort and sleep promotion.
los.ek: Heat for muscle spasm, cold for acute injury (usual); sleep hygiene: regular schedule, limit caffeine and screens.

los.do: Support elimination: catheters, enemas, ostomies and bladder training.
los.ek: Keep the drainage bag below the bladder; a healthy stoma is pink and moist; remove an indwelling catheter as soon as possible.

los.do: Recognise normal changes of aging and tell them from disease.
los.ek: Expected: presbyopia, presbycusis, slower reaction time, less skin elasticity; acute confusion is not normal aging.

los.do: Name Erikson's stage for an age and use it in care.
los.ek: Trust, autonomy, initiative, industry, identity, intimacy, generativity, integrity.

los.do: Recall the main infant growth and motor milestones.
los.ek: Weight doubles by 5–6 months, triples by 1 year; walks about 12–15 months.

topics.title: Antepartum, intrapartum, postpartum and newborn care

los.do: Score a newborn's APGAR from the five signs.
los.ek: Heart rate, respirations, tone, reflex irritability, color: 0–2 each.

los.do: Write a pregnancy history as GTPAL.
los.ek: Twins are one pregnancy and one birth but two living children.

los.do: Interpret fundal height in pregnancy and after birth.
los.ek: Umbilicus at 20 weeks; after birth firm, midline, down about 1 cm a day.

los.do: Use physical assessment techniques in the right order and read common findings.
los.ek: Inspection, palpation, percussion, auscultation; the abdomen is auscultated before palpation.

los.do: Compute and classify body mass index.
los.ek: kg/m²; 18.5–24.9 normal.

los.do: Recommend screenings and preventive care at the usual ages.
los.ek: Screening schedules follow USPSTF-style guidance (usual): colorectal from 45, cervical from 21 under USPSTF and ACOG (ACS 2020 says 25), mammography by age 40–50 depending on guideline.

los.do: Assess high-risk behaviors and support lifestyle change and self-care.
los.ek: Pack-years = packs/day × years; motivational interviewing; teach-back confirms self-care teaching.

los.do: Choose the therapeutic response and recognise the non-therapeutic ones.
los.ek: Reflect and explore; avoid reassurance, why questions, advice and changing the subject.

los.do: Intervene in a crisis and support stress management and support systems.
los.ek: Crisis care is short-term and directive: ensure safety first, then problem-solve; ask directly about suicide.

los.do: Name a defense mechanism from an example.
los.ek: Displacement, projection, denial, rationalization, regression, sublimation.

los.do: Use behavioral interventions and a therapeutic environment for mental-health conditions.
los.ek: Set clear limits; reduce stimulation for mania; orient to reality, don't argue with delusions; least restrictive intervention.

los.do: Recognise signs of abuse or neglect and report as required.
los.ek: Injuries that don't fit the story, delay in care, patterned bruises; nurses are mandatory reporters of child and elder abuse.

los.do: Recognise withdrawal and intoxication and their usual timelines.
los.ek: Alcohol withdrawal usually begins 6–24 h after the last drink; delirium tremens peaks around 48–72 h; opioid withdrawal is miserable but rarely fatal.

los.do: Support grieving clients and provide end-of-life care.
los.ek: Grief stages are not linear; signs of approaching death include mottling and Cheyne–Stokes breathing; hospice focuses on comfort.

los.do: Adapt care to cultural, religious and family influences.
los.ek: Use a trained interpreter, not family; ask about dietary and religious practices; assess family roles and support.

los.do: Care for clients with sensory or perceptual alterations.
los.ek: Face a hearing-impaired client and speak clearly; orient a visually impaired client to the room using clock positions.

los.do: Calculate tablets or mL for an ordered dose.
los.ek: Desired over have, times the vehicle.

los.do: Calculate weight-based doses, divided daily doses, and check an order against a safe range.
los.ek: Pounds ÷ 2.2; mg/kg/day ÷ doses a day; compare the daily total with the range.

los.do: Draw up a reconstituted medication from its label concentration.
los.ek: Use the mg/mL after mixing, not the diluent volume.

los.do: Recognise IV complications and the first action for each.
los.ek: Infiltration cool and pale; phlebitis warm and red; overload crackles and JVD; air embolism sudden dyspnea.

los.do: Calculate pump rates, gravity drip rates and infusion times.
los.ek: mL/h = volume ÷ hours; gtt/min = mL × drop factor ÷ minutes.

los.do: Calculate titrated infusions in units/h and mcg/kg/min, both ways.
los.ek: Find the concentration first, then dose ÷ concentration.

los.do: Care for central venous access devices and total parenteral nutrition.
los.ek: Confirm tip placement before use; flush per policy; TPN through a central line, glucose monitored, never stopped abruptly; dextrose gives 3.4 kcal/g.

los.do: Apply transfusion safety rules and respond to a reaction.
los.ek: Normal saline only; first 15 minutes; finish within 4 hours; stop it at any reaction.

los.do: Decide ABO and Rh red-cell compatibility.
los.ek: O− is the universal red-cell donor, AB+ the universal recipient.

topics.title: Expected actions, adverse effects and interactions

los.do: Name a drug's class from its suffix.
los.ek: -olol, -pril, -sartan, -statin, -prazole, -dipine…

los.do: Name the antidote for a drug toxicity.
los.ek: Naloxone, flumazenil, protamine, vitamin K, acetylcysteine, digoxin immune fab.

los.do: Apply the timing and mixing rules for insulins.
los.ek: Regular is the IV insulin; glargine has no peak and is never mixed; clear before cloudy.

los.do: Recall therapeutic drug levels and hold parameters.
los.ek: Digoxin 0.5–2.0 ng/mL, hold below 60 apical; lithium 0.6–1.2; INR 2–3.

los.do: Apply the rights of medication administration and route techniques.
los.ek: Right client, drug, dose, route, time, documentation (and more); IM in the ventrogluteal site; insulin subcutaneous.

los.do: Manage pharmacological pain relief safely.
los.ek: Assess pain and sedation; respiratory depression follows sedation; naloxone reverses opioids; PCA is client-controlled only.

los.do: Recall the usual adult ranges for electrolytes, blood counts, renal tests and ABGs.
Flag a value as low, normal or high.
los.ek: Compare with the range; act on potassium first.

los.do: Interpret an arterial blood gas: primary disorder and compensation.
los.ek: Side from pH, cause from whichever value matches it, compensation from the other.

los.do: Link ECG and neuromuscular signs to potassium and calcium imbalances.
los.ek: Peaked T: high K. U waves: low K. Chvostek and Trousseau: low Ca.

los.do: Compute mean arterial pressure.
los.ek: (S + 2D)/3; below about 65 is poor perfusion.

los.do: Score the Glasgow Coma Scale.
los.ek: Eyes 4, verbal 5, motor 6; 8 or less, protect the airway.

los.do: Recognise abnormal vital signs, including orthostatic hypotension.
los.ek: Orthostatic hypotension: systolic drop of 20 mmHg or diastolic drop of 10 mmHg within 3 minutes of standing (usual definition).

topics.title: Diagnostic tests, procedures and their complications

los.do: Prepare clients for diagnostic tests and watch for complications afterwards.
los.ek: Check contrast allergy and renal function; hold metformin around iodinated contrast (usual); after cardiac catheterization keep the leg straight and check distal pulses.

los.do: Prevent and recognise postoperative and procedure complications.
los.ek: Incentive spirometry; early ambulation; dehiscence: cover with sterile saline dressing; watch for hemorrhage, infection, DVT, ileus.

los.do: Calculate pediatric maintenance fluids by the 4-2-1 rule.
los.ek: 4 mL/h for the first 10 kg, 2 for the next 10, 1 for each kg after.

los.do: Estimate burned surface area and the Parkland fluid rate.
los.ek: Rule of nines; 4 mL × kg × %TBSA, half in the first 8 hours.

los.do: Manage a chest drainage system and respond to its problems.
los.ek: Continuous bubbling in the water seal is an air leak; tidaling is expected.

los.do: Choose oxygen devices and targets.
los.ek: Cannula 1–6 L/min; Venturi for a set FiO₂; non-rebreather for the highest; 88–92% in CO₂ retainers.

los.do: Respond to medical emergencies: cardiac arrest, anaphylaxis, choking and hypoglycemia.
los.ek: Adult CPR at 100–120 compressions/min, depth at least 2 in (5 cm), 30:2 without an advanced airway; anaphylaxis: IM epinephrine first.

los.do: Recognise types of shock and read basic hemodynamic indicators.
los.ek: Hypovolemic, cardiogenic, distributive (septic, anaphylactic, neurogenic) and obstructive; shock index = HR/SBP, above about 0.9 is concerning.

los.do: Link pathophysiology to findings and recognise unexpected responses to therapy.
los.ek: DKA: ketoacidosis and Kussmaul breathing; HHS: extreme glucose, no ketosis; an unexpected response needs the provider notified.

los.do: Choose which client to see first from airway, breathing and circulation, acute over chronic, unstable over stable.
los.ek: A silent chest in asthma, a pulseless limb, stridor after neck surgery and a transfusion reaction come before pain at 5/10.

los.do: Assign a task to the least-qualified person who can do it safely.
los.ek: The RN keeps assessment, initial teaching, planning, evaluation and unstable clients.

topics.title: Legal rights, informed consent and ethical practice

los.do: Protect client rights and confidentiality, including in electronic records and social media, and act as an advocate.
los.ek: Share information only with those caring for the client; never post client details; access only records you need; speak up when care is unsafe.

los.do: Apply informed consent, the right to refuse, advance directives and incident reporting.
los.ek: The provider informs, the nurse witnesses; incident reports never go in the chart.

los.do: Coordinate care: hand-off reports, referrals, case management and the right team member for a need.
los.ek: SBAR hand-off; refer to the discipline that meets the need (PT, OT, social work, dietitian); case managers coordinate across settings.

los.do: Apply management and quality-improvement concepts: chain of command, root-cause analysis and PDSA.
los.ek: Report up the chain of command; QI looks at systems, not blame; PDSA tests small changes.

los.do: Use directional terms and the anatomical planes.
los.ek: In anatomical position the body stands facing forward with palms forward. Superior/inferior, anterior/posterior, medial/lateral and proximal/distal are relative terms; sagittal, frontal and transverse planes cut the body into left-right, front-back and top-bottom parts.

los.do: Place organs in body cavities and name their serous membranes.
los.ek: The dorsal cavity holds the brain and spinal cord. The ventral cavity is split by the diaphragm into the thoracic cavity (pleural cavities, mediastinum with the pericardial cavity) and the abdominopelvic cavity. Serous membranes have a parietal layer on the wall and a visceral layer on the organ.

los.do: Name the parts of a feedback loop and tell negative from positive feedback.
los.ek: A receptor senses the variable, a control centre compares it with a set point, and an effector acts. Negative feedback reverses the change (temperature, glucose, blood pressure); positive feedback amplifies it to an end point (labour, clotting, the upstroke of an action potential).

los.do: Match an epithelium to its location and function.
los.ek: Epithelia are named by layers (simple, stratified, pseudostratified) and cell shape (squamous, cuboidal, columnar). Thin simple squamous allows exchange; stratified squamous resists abrasion; columnar cells secrete and absorb; transitional epithelium stretches.

los.do: Tell the connective, muscle and nervous tissues apart.
los.ek: Connective tissue is cells scattered in a matrix of fibres and ground substance (loose, dense, cartilage, bone, blood). Skeletal muscle is striated and voluntary, cardiac is striated with intercalated discs, smooth is unstriated. Nervous tissue is neurons and glia.

los.do: Name the layers of the skin and what each cell type does.
los.ek: The epidermis runs from the stratum basale (dividing cells, melanocytes) up through spinosum, granulosum, lucidum (thick skin only) to the dead corneum. The dermis has a papillary and a reticular layer with vessels, nerves, glands and follicles; the hypodermis is fat and loose tissue beneath.

los.do: Name the cells and structures of bone tissue.
los.ek: Osteoblasts build matrix, osteocytes maintain it from lacunae, osteoclasts resorb it. Compact bone is built of osteons around central canals; spongy bone is trabeculae holding red marrow. Long bones grow in length at the epiphyseal plate.

los.do: Predict how hormones move calcium between bone and blood.
los.ek: Parathyroid hormone raises blood calcium by stimulating osteoclast activity, renal reabsorption and activation of vitamin D. Calcitonin lowers it weakly by inhibiting osteoclasts. Calcitriol raises intestinal absorption.

los.do: Classify bones as axial or appendicular and count the vertebrae.
los.ek: The axial skeleton is the skull, vertebral column, ribs and sternum; the appendicular skeleton is the limbs and their girdles. The column has 7 cervical, 12 thoracic and 5 lumbar vertebrae, then the sacrum and coccyx; there are 12 pairs of ribs, 7 of them true.

los.do: Classify joints and name the movements at synovial joints.
los.ek: Fibrous and cartilaginous joints allow little or no movement; synovial joints have a cavity, capsule, synovial membrane and articular cartilage. Hinge joints flex and extend; ball-and-socket joints move in all planes; pivot joints rotate.

los.do: Describe the sarcomere and what changes when it shortens.
los.ek: A sarcomere runs from Z disc to Z disc. Thin (actin) filaments slide past thick (myosin) filaments: the I band and H zone narrow and the Z discs approach, while the A band keeps its length because no filament shortens.

los.do: Order the steps from a motor neuron's action potential to cross-bridge cycling.
los.ek: Acetylcholine released at the neuromuscular junction opens ligand-gated channels on the motor end plate; the action potential runs down the T tubules and opens the sarcoplasmic reticulum's calcium channels. ATP is needed to detach the myosin head and to pump calcium back.

los.do: Relate motor units, summation and fibre types to force and fatigue.
los.ek: A motor unit is one motor neuron and the fibres it supplies. Force rises by recruiting more units and by stimulating faster (wave summation up to tetanus). Slow oxidative fibres resist fatigue; fast glycolytic fibres are powerful and tire quickly.

los.do: Name the prime mover for a movement and the role of its antagonist.
los.ek: The agonist (prime mover) produces the movement, the antagonist opposes it, synergists assist. A muscle pulls its insertion toward its origin and can only pull.

los.do: Explain the resting potential and compute an equilibrium potential.
los.ek: The resting membrane is most permeable to potassium, so it sits near the potassium equilibrium potential, about −70 mV; the sodium-potassium pump maintains the gradients. At 37 °C the Nernst potential for a monovalent cation is 61.5 mV × log10(outside/inside).

los.do: Follow the phases of an action potential and its conduction.
los.ek: At threshold voltage-gated sodium channels open (depolarisation), then inactivate while potassium channels open (repolarisation, then hyperpolarisation). The absolute refractory period makes conduction one-way. Myelin and large diameter raise speed; myelinated conduction is saltatory.

los.do: Describe a chemical synapse and tell excitatory from inhibitory effects.
los.ek: An action potential opens voltage-gated calcium channels in the terminal; vesicles release transmitter, which binds postsynaptic receptors. Opening cation channels gives an EPSP; opening chloride or potassium channels gives an IPSP. Potentials sum in time and space at the axon hillock.

los.do: Match brain regions to their functions.
los.ek: Frontal lobe: motor cortex and planning; parietal: somatosensory; occipital: vision; temporal: hearing and memory. The cerebellum coordinates movement, the hypothalamus runs homeostasis and the pituitary, the thalamus relays sensation, the medulla holds cardiac and respiratory centres.

los.do: Trace a spinal reflex and the main spinal pathways.
los.ek: A reflex arc runs receptor, sensory neuron (dorsal root), integration centre, motor neuron (ventral root), effector. The stretch reflex is monosynaptic. Dorsal columns carry fine touch and proprioception, the spinothalamic tract pain and temperature, the corticospinal tract voluntary movement.

los.do: Name the cranial nerves by number and main function.
los.ek: Twelve pairs: I olfactory, II optic, III oculomotor, IV trochlear, V trigeminal, VI abducens, VII facial, VIII vestibulocochlear, IX glossopharyngeal, X vagus, XI accessory, XII hypoglossal.

los.do: Contrast the sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions.
los.ek: Sympathetic outflow is thoracolumbar with short preganglionic fibres and norepinephrine at most targets; parasympathetic outflow is craniosacral with long preganglionic fibres and acetylcholine on muscarinic receptors. All preganglionic neurons release acetylcholine onto nicotinic receptors.

los.do: Trace light through the eye and find the power of a lens.
los.ek: Light passes the cornea (most of the refraction), aqueous humour, pupil, lens (adjustable focus), vitreous humour and reaches the retina. Rods serve dim light, cones colour and acuity at the fovea. Lens power in diopters is 1 over the focal length in metres.

los.do: Trace sound through the ear and separate hearing from equilibrium.
los.ek: Sound moves the tympanic membrane, the ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes) and the oval window; hair cells of the spiral organ in the cochlea transduce it, high pitch near the base. The semicircular canals sense rotation, the utricle and saccule linear acceleration and head tilt.

los.do: Classify hormones by solubility and predict where their receptors are.
los.ek: Peptides and catecholamines are water soluble, bind membrane receptors and act through second messengers within seconds to minutes. Steroids and thyroid hormones are lipid soluble, travel on carrier proteins, bind intracellular receptors and change gene transcription.

los.do: Follow a hypothalamic-pituitary axis and predict levels when one gland fails.
los.ek: The hypothalamus releases hormones into the portal system to the anterior pituitary (TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH, GH, prolactin); the posterior pituitary releases ADH and oxytocin made in the hypothalamus. Target hormones feed back negatively, so a failing target gland gives a high tropic hormone.

los.do: Predict the hormonal response to a change in blood glucose.
los.ek: Insulin from beta cells lowers glucose by moving it into muscle and fat and storing it as glycogen and fat. Glucagon from alpha cells raises it by glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis in the liver; epinephrine, cortisol and growth hormone also raise it.

los.do: Describe the composition of blood and find the haematocrit.
los.ek: Blood is about 55% plasma and 45% formed elements. Haematocrit is the fraction of blood volume that is red cells. Erythrocytes carry gases, neutrophils are the commonest leukocyte, platelets are fragments of megakaryocytes.

los.do: Order the steps of haemostasis.
los.ek: Vascular spasm, then a platelet plug on exposed collagen (with von Willebrand factor), then coagulation: the intrinsic and extrinsic pathways meet at factor X, prothrombin becomes thrombin and thrombin turns fibrinogen into fibrin. Plasmin later dissolves the clot.

los.do: Trace blood through the heart and name the valves and sounds.
los.ek: Right atrium, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, lungs, left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, body. The first heart sound is the atrioventricular valves closing, the second the semilunar valves closing.

los.do: Follow the conduction system and read the waves of an ECG.
los.ek: SA node, atria, AV node (delay), AV bundle, bundle branches, Purkinje fibres. The P wave is atrial depolarisation, the QRS complex ventricular depolarisation, the T wave ventricular repolarisation. Heart rate in beats per minute is 60 over the R-R interval in seconds.

los.do: Compute cardiac output, stroke volume and ejection fraction.
los.ek: Stroke volume is end-diastolic minus end-systolic volume; cardiac output is heart rate times stroke volume; ejection fraction is stroke volume over end-diastolic volume. Preload, contractility and afterload set stroke volume.

los.do: Relate flow, pressure and resistance, and the effect of vessel radius.
los.ek: Flow equals the pressure difference over resistance, so mean arterial pressure is about cardiac output times total peripheral resistance. Resistance varies with the inverse fourth power of radius, which is why arterioles control flow.

los.do: Find the net filtration pressure across a capillary wall.
los.ek: Net filtration pressure = (capillary hydrostatic − interstitial hydrostatic) − (plasma colloid osmotic − interstitial colloid osmotic). Positive values filter fluid out, negative values draw it in; the lymphatics return the excess.

los.do: Predict the reflex and hormonal responses to a change in blood pressure.
los.ek: Baroreceptors in the carotid sinus and aortic arch report to the medulla: a fall in pressure raises sympathetic output (heart rate, contractility, vasoconstriction). Over hours the kidney's renin starts the angiotensin-aldosterone system, and ADH retains water.

los.do: Trace lymph back to the blood and name the lymphoid organs.
los.ek: Lymphatic capillaries collect excess interstitial fluid; lymph passes through nodes to the thoracic duct (most of the body) or the right lymphatic duct, which empty into the subclavian veins. Bone marrow and thymus are primary lymphoid organs; nodes, spleen and tonsils are secondary.

los.do: Name the innate defences and the signs of inflammation.
los.ek: Barriers (skin, mucus, acid), phagocytes (neutrophils, macrophages), natural killer cells, complement, interferons, fever and inflammation act without prior exposure. Inflammation shows redness, heat, swelling and pain from vasodilation and increased permeability.

los.do: Assign roles to the cells and antibodies of adaptive immunity.
los.ek: B cells become plasma cells that secrete antibody (humoral immunity). Helper T cells (CD4) read antigen on MHC II and direct the response; cytotoxic T cells (CD8) read MHC I and kill infected cells. IgM comes first, IgG is most abundant and crosses the placenta, IgA is in secretions, IgE drives allergy.

los.do: Tell primary from secondary responses and active from passive immunity.
los.ek: A first exposure gives a slow, small, mostly IgM response and leaves memory cells; a second gives a fast, large, mostly IgG response. Active immunity is made by one's own cells (infection, vaccine) and lasts; passive immunity is borrowed antibody (placenta, milk, antiserum) and fades.

los.do: Explain ventilation with Boyle's law.
los.ek: Contracting the diaphragm and external intercostals enlarges the thorax; alveolar pressure falls below atmospheric and air flows in. Quiet expiration is passive recoil. At constant temperature, pressure times volume is constant.

los.do: Combine lung volumes and find alveolar ventilation.
los.ek: Vital capacity = tidal + inspiratory reserve + expiratory reserve volume; total lung capacity adds the residual volume. Minute ventilation is tidal volume times rate; alveolar ventilation subtracts the anatomical dead space (about 150 mL) from each breath.

los.do: Find partial pressures and predict shifts of the oxygen dissociation curve.
los.ek: A gas's partial pressure is its fraction times the total pressure of dry gas; inspired air is humidified, so subtract water vapour (47 mmHg at 37 °C). Raised carbon dioxide, acidity, temperature and 2,3-BPG shift the haemoglobin curve right, releasing more oxygen to tissue.

los.do: Describe how carbon dioxide is carried and how breathing is controlled.
los.ek: Most carbon dioxide travels as bicarbonate made in red cells by carbonic anhydrase, some on haemoglobin, a little dissolved. Central chemoreceptors in the medulla respond to carbon dioxide through the pH of cerebrospinal fluid and set the normal drive; peripheral chemoreceptors respond to low oxygen.

los.do: Name the layers of the gut wall and the types of motility.
los.ek: From the lumen out: mucosa, submucosa, muscularis externa (inner circular, outer longitudinal), serosa. The submucosal and myenteric plexuses form the enteric nervous system. Peristalsis propels; segmentation mixes.

los.do: Match secretions and enzymes to what they digest.
los.ek: Salivary and pancreatic amylase digest starch; pepsin (from chief cells' pepsinogen, activated by parietal cells' acid) starts protein digestion; pancreatic trypsin, lipase and brush-border enzymes finish; bile salts emulsify fat.

los.do: Describe absorption and the roles of the liver, gallbladder and pancreas.
los.ek: Villi and microvilli give the small intestine its area; sugars and amino acids enter capillaries to the hepatic portal vein, fats enter lacteals as chylomicrons. Secretin calls for pancreatic bicarbonate; cholecystokinin calls for enzymes and gallbladder contraction.

los.do: Count the energy in a meal and say which hormone governs each metabolic state.
los.ek: Carbohydrate and protein give about 4 kcal per gram, fat about 9. In the absorptive state insulin stores glucose as glycogen and fat; in the postabsorptive state glucagon releases glucose from glycogen and by gluconeogenesis, and fat is mobilised.

los.do: Order the parts of the nephron and name its three processes.
los.ek: Glomerulus and capsule, proximal convoluted tubule, nephron loop, distal convoluted tubule, collecting duct. Filtration moves plasma into the capsule, reabsorption returns most of it to blood (about two-thirds in the proximal tubule), secretion adds to the tubule.

los.do: Find the glomerular net filtration pressure and a renal clearance.
los.ek: Net filtration pressure = glomerular hydrostatic − capsular hydrostatic − glomerular colloid osmotic pressure. Clearance of a substance = urine concentration × urine flow ÷ plasma concentration; for inulin or creatinine it estimates GFR.

los.do: Compute filtered load and filtration fraction, and place the actions of ADH and aldosterone.
los.ek: Filtered load = GFR × plasma concentration; filtration fraction = GFR ÷ renal plasma flow, about 20%. ADH inserts aquaporins in the collecting duct to retain water; aldosterone raises sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion in the distal nephron.

los.do: Divide body water into compartments and estimate plasma osmolarity.
los.ek: Total body water is about 60% of body mass; two-thirds is intracellular and one-third extracellular, and about a quarter of the extracellular fluid is plasma. Plasma osmolarity ≈ 2 × sodium + glucose/18 + urea nitrogen/2.8 (mEq/L, mg/dL, mg/dL).

los.do: Compute blood pH from the bicarbonate buffer and the anion gap.
los.ek: pH = 6.1 + log10(bicarbonate ÷ (0.03 × carbon dioxide partial pressure)); the lungs set carbon dioxide and the kidneys set bicarbonate. Anion gap = sodium − chloride − bicarbonate, normally about 8 to 12 mEq/L.

los.do: Follow gametogenesis and the path of sperm.
los.ek: Spermatogenesis in the seminiferous tubules yields four sperm per primary spermatocyte, supported by sustentacular cells; interstitial cells make testosterone under LH. Oogenesis yields one ovum and polar bodies and pauses in prophase I until puberty and in metaphase II until fertilisation.

los.do: Time the events and hormones of the ovarian and uterine cycles.
los.ek: FSH grows follicles, which secrete oestrogen (proliferative phase). An LH surge near day 14 triggers ovulation. The corpus luteum secretes progesterone (secretory phase); without pregnancy it regresses, hormones fall and menstruation begins. hCG from an embryo rescues the corpus luteum.

los.do: Order early development and assign tissues to germ layers.
los.ek: Zygote, cleavage, morula, blastocyst (implants about a week after fertilisation), then gastrulation forms ectoderm (nervous system, epidermis), mesoderm (muscle, bone, blood, heart, kidney) and endoderm (lining of gut and airways, liver, pancreas).

los.do: Name the classes of drug target and the kinds of drug-target interaction.
los.ek: Most drugs act on receptors, enzymes, ion channels or transporters. An agonist binds and activates; an antagonist binds without activating and blocks the agonist. Binding may be reversible or irreversible, at the agonist's own (orthosteric) site or at an allosteric site.

los.do: Read a dose-response curve for potency and efficacy.
los.ek: Response = Emax × C ÷ (C + EC50) for the simplest case. Potency is how little drug is needed (a lower EC50 is more potent); efficacy is the maximum response the drug can produce. A partial agonist has a lower Emax than a full agonist whatever its potency.

los.do: Compute receptor occupancy from affinity.
los.ek: The dissociation constant Kd is the concentration at which half the receptors are occupied; a lower Kd is a higher affinity. Fractional occupancy = [L] ÷ ([L] + Kd).

los.do: Tell competitive from non-competitive antagonism and compute a dose ratio.
los.ek: A competitive antagonist shifts the agonist curve to the right without lowering the maximum, and more agonist overcomes it; the dose ratio is 1 + [B] ÷ KB. A non-competitive or irreversible antagonist lowers the maximum response.

los.do: Quantify selectivity and explain why it is lost at high dose.
los.ek: Selectivity is preferential affinity for one target over another, measured as the ratio of the two Kd or IC50 values. It is relative: at a high enough concentration the second target is occupied too, which is where many adverse effects come from.

los.do: Predict ionisation and absorption from pKa and pH.
los.ek: The un-ionised form crosses membranes. For a weak acid the un-ionised fraction is 1 ÷ (1 + 10^(pH − pKa)); for a weak base it is 1 ÷ (1 + 10^(pKa − pH)). A drug is trapped on the side of a membrane where it is more ionised: weak acids in alkaline fluid, weak bases in acidic fluid.

los.do: Compute bioavailability and explain first-pass metabolism.
los.ek: Bioavailability F is the fraction of a dose reaching the systemic circulation unchanged: F = (AUC oral ÷ AUC IV) × (dose IV ÷ dose oral). An intravenous dose has F = 1. Oral drugs pass through the gut wall and liver first, which can remove much of the dose.

los.do: Compute and interpret the volume of distribution.
los.ek: Vd = amount of drug in the body ÷ plasma concentration. It is an apparent volume: a drug held in plasma by protein binding has a Vd near plasma volume, while a lipophilic drug stored in tissue can have a Vd of hundreds of litres.

los.do: Describe drug metabolism and the effect of enzyme induction and inhibition.
los.ek: Phase I reactions (oxidation, reduction, hydrolysis; mostly cytochrome P450) add or expose a functional group; phase II reactions conjugate (glucuronide, sulfate, acetyl, glutathione) and usually make the drug more water soluble. Inducers raise enzyme levels and lower other drugs' concentrations; inhibitors do the opposite. A prodrug is activated by metabolism.

los.do: Tell first-order from zero-order elimination and compute what remains.
los.ek: In first-order elimination a constant fraction is removed per unit time, so the half-life is constant and the concentration falls exponentially. In zero-order elimination a constant amount is removed per unit time because the enzymes are saturated (ethanol, high-dose phenytoin and aspirin).

los.do: Relate half-life, clearance and volume of distribution.
los.ek: Clearance is the volume of plasma cleared of drug per unit time: CL = dose ÷ AUC for an intravenous dose. Half-life depends on both independent parameters: t½ = 0.693 × Vd ÷ CL.

los.do: Design a loading and a maintenance dose for a target steady-state concentration.
los.ek: At steady state the rate in equals the rate out: maintenance dosing rate = CL × Css ÷ F. A loading dose fills the volume at once: loading dose = Vd × Css ÷ F. Without a loading dose, steady state is reached in about four to five half-lives.

topics.title: When the response is not the one intended

los.do: Compute a therapeutic index and say what a narrow one requires.
los.ek: Therapeutic index = TD50 ÷ ED50 (LD50 ÷ ED50 in animal studies). A drug with a low index (warfarin, digoxin, lithium, phenytoin, aminoglycosides) needs careful dosing and often monitoring of plasma levels or effect.

los.do: Classify adverse drug reactions and explain tolerance.
los.ek: Type A (augmented) reactions are dose-related extensions of the drug's pharmacology and are predictable; type B (bizarre) reactions are unrelated to dose, often immune or genetic, and unpredictable. Tolerance is a reduced response on repeated dosing, from pharmacodynamic change (receptor down-regulation) or pharmacokinetic change (enzyme induction).

los.do: Classify drug interactions.
los.ek: Pharmacokinetic interactions change another drug's concentration (absorption, binding, metabolism, excretion). Pharmacodynamic interactions change its effect at the same concentration: additive (the sum), synergistic (more than the sum) or antagonistic (less).

los.do: Adjust for individual variation in drug handling.
los.ek: Age, body size, organ function, genetics and other drugs change the response to a standard dose. Renal function is estimated by the Cockcroft-Gault equation: creatinine clearance (mL/min) = (140 − age) × weight (kg) ÷ (72 × serum creatinine in mg/dL), multiplied by 0.85 for women.

los.do: Predict the effects of muscarinic agonists and antagonists.
los.ek: Muscarinic activation slows the heart, constricts the pupil and bronchi, increases secretions and gut and bladder motility. Antimuscarinics (atropine and relatives) do the opposite: fast heart, dilated pupils, dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention. Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors raise acetylcholine at both muscarinic and nicotinic synapses.

los.do: Match adrenoceptor subtypes to their effects and agonists.
los.ek: Alpha-1: vasoconstriction, pupil dilation. Alpha-2: reduces central sympathetic outflow. Beta-1: raises heart rate and contractility. Beta-2: bronchodilation and vasodilation in skeletal muscle. Epinephrine acts on all four; phenylephrine is alpha-1 selective, salbutamol beta-2 selective.

los.do: Predict the effects and hazards of adrenoceptor antagonists.
los.ek: Beta blockers lower heart rate, contractility and renin; non-selective ones can cause bronchospasm and mask the warning signs of hypoglycaemia. Alpha-1 blockers relax vessels and the bladder neck and can cause postural hypotension.

los.do: Give the mechanism and signature adverse effect of each antihypertensive class.
los.ek: ACE inhibitors block angiotensin II formation (cough, high potassium, angioedema); angiotensin receptor blockers block its receptor without the cough; dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers dilate arterioles (ankle swelling, gingival overgrowth); thiazides reduce sodium reabsorption; beta blockers reduce cardiac output and renin.

los.do: Place each diuretic class on the nephron and predict its electrolyte effects.
los.ek: Loop diuretics block the Na-K-2Cl carrier in the thick ascending limb (most powerful; lose potassium, calcium). Thiazides block Na-Cl in the distal tubule (lose potassium, retain calcium). Potassium-sparing drugs act in the collecting duct (spironolactone blocks aldosterone; amiloride blocks the sodium channel). Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors act in the proximal tubule; osmotic diuretics throughout.

los.do: Match antithrombotic and lipid-lowering drugs to their mechanisms.
los.ek: Warfarin blocks vitamin K recycling (factors II, VII, IX, X; monitored by INR; reversed by vitamin K). Heparin potentiates antithrombin (reversed by protamine). Direct oral anticoagulants inhibit factor Xa or thrombin. Aspirin irreversibly inhibits platelet cyclooxygenase; clopidogrel blocks the platelet P2Y12 receptor. Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase.

los.do: Classify cardiac drugs for arrhythmia, angina and heart failure.
los.ek: Vaughan Williams classes: I sodium channel blockers, II beta blockers, III potassium channel blockers (amiodarone), IV calcium channel blockers (verapamil, diltiazem). Nitrates relieve angina by venodilation through nitric oxide. Digoxin inhibits Na+/K+-ATPase.

los.do: Explain how local anaesthetics act and compute the amount in a cartridge.
los.ek: Local anaesthetics block voltage-gated sodium channels from inside the axon, in their charged form, after crossing the membrane uncharged; small pain fibres are blocked first. Amides (lidocaine, articaine, bupivacaine) are metabolised in the liver, esters by plasma esterases. A 1% solution contains 10 mg/mL.

los.do: Match central nervous system drug classes to their mechanisms.
los.ek: Benzodiazepines increase the frequency of GABA-A channel opening (reversed by flumazenil). SSRIs block serotonin reuptake. Typical antipsychotics block dopamine D2 receptors (movement disorders). Levodopa replaces dopamine in Parkinson disease. Many antiepileptics block sodium channels (phenytoin, carbamazepine).

los.do: Compare opioids, NSAIDs and paracetamol.
los.ek: Opioids act on mu receptors (analgesia, respiratory depression, constipation, pinpoint pupils; reversed by naloxone). NSAIDs inhibit cyclooxygenase, reducing prostaglandins (gastric irritation, kidney injury, bleeding). Paracetamol is analgesic and antipyretic with little anti-inflammatory action; overdose injures the liver and is treated with acetylcysteine.

los.do: Interpret MAC for inhaled anaesthetics and name the intravenous agents.
los.ek: MAC is the alveolar concentration at which half of patients do not move to a surgical stimulus: a lower MAC means a more potent agent. Solubility in blood sets the speed of onset: a low blood-gas partition coefficient gives fast induction and recovery. Propofol is the usual intravenous induction agent; ketamine blocks NMDA receptors.

los.do: Give the signature adverse effects and dosing pattern of antibacterial classes.
los.ek: Penicillins: allergy. Aminoglycosides: kidney and inner-ear toxicity, concentration-dependent killing. Tetracyclines: tooth discolouration in children, chelated by calcium and antacids. Fluoroquinolones: tendon injury. Macrolides: enzyme inhibition, QT prolongation. Beta-lactams kill in a time-dependent way.

los.do: Match antifungal and antiviral drugs to their targets.
los.ek: Azoles inhibit ergosterol synthesis; polyenes (amphotericin B, nystatin) bind ergosterol and make pores; echinocandins inhibit cell-wall glucan synthesis. Aciclovir is activated by viral thymidine kinase and inhibits viral DNA polymerase; oseltamivir inhibits influenza neuraminidase.

los.do: State the principles of cancer chemotherapy and its common toxicities.
los.ek: Cytotoxic drugs kill a constant fraction of cells per dose and hit dividing cells hardest, so bone marrow, gut lining, hair follicles and oral mucosa suffer. Antimetabolites act in S phase, vinca alkaloids and taxanes in M phase; alkylating agents are not phase-specific. Signature toxicities: doxorubicin heart, cisplatin kidney, bleomycin lung, vincristine nerves.

los.do: Match drugs for diabetes to their mechanisms and hazards.
los.ek: Metformin lowers hepatic glucose output (does not cause hypoglycaemia alone; rare lactic acidosis). Sulfonylureas close beta-cell potassium channels to release insulin (hypoglycaemia). SGLT2 inhibitors block renal glucose reabsorption (genital infection). GLP-1 agonists enhance glucose-dependent insulin release and slow gastric emptying. Insulin replaces the hormone.

los.do: Describe corticosteroid and thyroid drug actions and hazards.
los.ek: Glucocorticoids suppress inflammation and immunity by changing gene transcription; long courses cause adrenal suppression (taper, never stop abruptly), osteoporosis, high glucose, infection risk and oral candidiasis with inhalers. Levothyroxine replaces T4; thionamides (carbimazole, propylthiouracil) block thyroid hormone synthesis.

los.do: Match respiratory and gastrointestinal drugs to their mechanisms.
los.ek: Beta-2 agonists and antimuscarinics dilate the bronchi; inhaled corticosteroids control airway inflammation; leukotriene antagonists block one inflammatory pathway. Proton pump inhibitors irreversibly block the H+/K+-ATPase; H2 antagonists block histamine on the parietal cell; antacids neutralise acid already secreted.

los.do: Trace a token through a decoder-only transformer — embedding, residual stream, attention, MLP, unembedding — and say what each component reads from and writes to the residual stream.
los.ek: Every layer adds to one shared residual stream; attention moves information between positions, MLPs transform each position separately. Causal masking lets position t attend only to positions ≤ t; sampling is from softmax(logits / T).

los.do: Calculate a transformer's parameter count from d_model, n_layers and vocabulary size (drill: compute).
los.ek: Per layer ≈ 12·d_model² (4d² attention + 8d² MLP with d_mlp = 4d); embeddings add V·d (×2 if untied).

los.do: Estimate training compute from parameters and tokens, and convert it to chip-days at a stated utilisation (drill: compute).
los.ek: C ≈ 6ND (2ND forward, 4ND backward); time = C / (N_chips × peak FLOP/s × MFU).

los.do: Find the compute-optimal model size and token count for a budget with the Chinchilla rule (drill: compute).
los.ek: Compute-optimal D ≈ 20N; with C = 6ND, N ≈ √(C/120).

los.do: Extrapolate loss from a fitted power law, and explain why smooth loss gains need not predict when a specific capability appears (drill: compute).
los.ek: L(C) = L∞ + a·C^(−α) is a straight line on log–log axes above the irreducible loss. Task metrics can jump with scale; part of 'emergence' is the choice of a thresholded metric.

los.do: Decompose growth in effective compute into hardware/spend and algorithmic efficiency, and project it a few years forward (drill: compute).
los.ek: IASR 2026: training compute ~5×/yr, algorithmic efficiency 2–6×/yr; the factors multiply.

topics.title: Post-training — RLHF, RLAIF, DPO and reasoning models

los.do: Lay out the RLHF pipeline — SFT, preference data, reward model, RL with a KL penalty — and say what each stage contributes.
los.ek: Objective: maximise E[r_φ(x, y)] − β·KL(π ‖ π_ref); the KL term keeps the policy near the SFT model and limits reward-model exploitation. PPO clips the policy ratio to [1 − ε, 1 + ε] so one update can't move the policy far.

los.do: Calculate preference probabilities from a Bradley–Terry reward model (drill: compute).
los.ek: P(y₁ ≻ y₂) = σ(r₁ − r₂); a reward gap of 1 ≈ 73 %, of 2 ≈ 88 %.

los.do: Contrast RLHF, RLAIF/constitutional feedback and DPO by where the preference signal comes from and whether a separate reward model is trained (drill: classify).
los.ek: DPO solves the same KL-regularised objective in closed form from preference pairs; RLAIF replaces human raters with a model guided by written principles.

los.do: Explain how RL on verifiable rewards and inference-time compute produce reasoning models, and what that shifts for evaluation.
los.ek: IASR 2026: much recent gain comes from post-training and test-time compute, so capability can jump without a bigger pretraining run — and an eval must fix the inference budget it tested at.

los.do: Classify a described failure as specification gaming, reward hacking/tampering, goal misgeneralisation, sycophancy, deceptive alignment or a plain capability failure (drill: classify).
los.ek: Ask in order: was the objective itself wrong (specification gaming)? was the reward signal exploited or tampered with (reward hacking)? is the goal wrong only off-distribution (misgeneralisation)? is the user's view echoed (sycophancy)? is good behaviour strategic (deception)? none — it just couldn't (capability).

los.do: Explain Goodhart's law and predict how a proxy reward diverges from the true objective as optimisation pressure grows.
los.ek: Proxy and target correlate in the bulk of the distribution and decouple in the tails that strong optimisation reaches. Reward-model overoptimisation: gold reward rises, then falls, as KL from the initial policy grows.

los.do: Identify reward hacking in a described coding or agentic transcript — special-casing tests, editing the grader, claiming unverified success — and say what it does to the measurement (drill: classify).
los.ek: A pass won by exploiting the checker scores capability that isn't there; trained on, it reinforces the habit. Read transcripts, not only scores.

los.do: Distinguish goal misgeneralisation from capability misgeneralisation in a described distribution shift (drill: classify).
los.ek: Goal misgeneralisation: capabilities carry over but pursue the wrong goal (the CoinRun agent runs right, not to the coin). Capability misgeneralisation: the agent just becomes incompetent.

los.do: Distinguish outer from inner misalignment in a described failure (drill: classify).
los.ek: Outer: the training objective is wrong. Inner: the objective was fine on the training data but the learned model pursues something else; many goals fit the same training reward.

los.do: Trace sycophancy back to preference training, and design a paired-prompt test that separates it from genuine agreement.
los.ek: Raters reward agreeable answers. Prompts identical except for the user's stated view isolate the effect; measure answer flips.

los.do: Distinguish confabulation, sycophancy and deception by what the model represents as true (drill: classify).
los.ek: Confabulation: no reliable knowledge. Sycophancy: knowledge overridden by a social cue. Deception: represents the truth and instrumentally induces a false belief.

topics.title: Deceptive alignment, scheming and situational awareness

los.do: State the preconditions for scheming — a misaligned goal, situational awareness, and a reason to look aligned during training or testing — and judge which ones a described model shows (drill: classify).
los.ek: Without situational awareness a model can't condition behaviour on being watched; without a goal that outlasts the episode it has no reason to.

los.do: Explain instrumental convergence and why shutdown resistance and resource acquisition follow from many different goals.
los.ek: Staying on, keeping its goal and gaining resources help with almost any objective — which is why FSF frames misalignment risk as interfering with operators' ability to direct, modify or shut down.

los.do: Explain how evaluation awareness and sandbagging undermine safety testing, and name the evidence that would reveal them.
los.ek: IASR 2026: models increasingly recognise test settings. Signs: verbalised test-awareness, gaps between eval-like and deployment-like framings, underperformance that a light fine-tune removes.

los.do: Choose among pretraining-data filtering, SFT, preference training and constitutional training for a stated safety goal, and say what each can't fix.
los.ek: Data filtering removes knowledge; post-training mostly shapes whether knowledge is expressed, so later fine-tuning can undo it. Constitutional AI: principles drive self-critique (SL stage) and AI preference labels (RL stage).

los.do: Explain why refusal training is shallow against fine-tuning on released weights, and what tamper-resistant training attempts.
los.ek: A small harmful fine-tune can strip refusals; safeguards on open weights are easy to remove and the weights can't be recalled (IASR 2026).

los.do: Match debate, recursive reward modelling, iterated amplification and AI-assisted critique to how each lets a weak overseer judge a strong model (drill: classify).
los.ek: Debate: two models argue, a judge decides. RRM: models help humans evaluate the next model. Amplification: decompose into checkable sub-tasks. Critique: a model points out flaws for the human.

los.do: State the empirical condition debate needs, and read a debate or sandwiching result to say whether oversight improved.
los.ek: Debate works if lies are harder to defend than truths; test with weaker judges' accuracy under debate vs a single consultant. Sandwiching: non-experts with assistance on tasks the model can do, scored against experts.

los.do: Calculate performance gap recovered from weak, weak-to-strong and strong-ceiling scores (drill: compute).
los.ek: PGR = (W2S − weak) / (ceiling − weak); 1 = full recovery, 0 = the strong student only imitates the weak labels.

los.do: Explain what weak-to-strong is an analogy for and where the analogy breaks.
los.ek: Humans supervising superhuman models. It breaks because today's strong students weren't trained to mislead, and imitating human errors may be easier than imitating a weak model's.

los.do: Classify a described jailbreak by mechanism — competing objectives, mismatched generalisation, many-shot, prompt injection — without reproducing it (drill: classify).
los.ek: Competing objectives pit helpfulness against harmlessness; mismatched generalisation uses inputs safety training didn't cover (encodings, low-resource languages); prompt injection arrives through data, not the user turn.

los.do: Explain why input/output classifiers plus adversarial training raise attacker cost without eliminating universal jailbreaks, and measure safeguards by cost, not only by success.
los.ek: UK AISI found a universal jailbreak in every system it tested; expert effort to jailbreak bio-misuse content varied ~40× between releases; capability barely predicted safeguard strength (R² ≈ 0.1).

los.do: State the linear representation hypothesis and explain why superposition makes neurons polysemantic.
los.ek: Features are directions in activation space. With sparse features a model stores more features than dimensions, at the cost of interference, so features aren't neuron-aligned.

los.do: Predict whether a toy model stores features in superposition from their sparsity and importance.
los.ek: Dense features: the top-d by importance get dedicated dimensions, the rest are dropped. As sparsity rises, features share dimensions (antipodal pairs, then polytopes).

los.do: Write the SAE objective, explain each term, and name its failure modes (dead latents, feature splitting, absorption).
los.ek: L = ‖x − x̂‖² + λ‖f‖₁ with a dictionary wider than d_model; dictionary size changes which features appear, and absorption makes a latent's label misleading.

los.do: Evaluate an SAE from variance explained, mean L0 and the loss increase when it is spliced into the model (drill: compute).
los.ek: FVE = 1 − ‖x − x̂‖²/‖x − x̄‖²; report CE-loss increase on substitution; sparsity and fidelity trade off along a frontier.

los.do: Explain how a previous-token head and an induction head compose to copy in-context sequences.
los.ek: K-composition: the induction head's keys read the previous-token head's output, so it attends to the token after the earlier occurrence of the current token.

los.do: Design an activation-patching experiment and compute the normalised logit difference recovered (drill: compute).
los.ek: Patch clean activations into the corrupted run; recovered = (LD_patched − LD_corrupt) / (LD_clean − LD_corrupt).

los.do: Classify the evidence behind a described interpretability claim as correlational (probe, attention pattern, max-activating examples) or causal (ablation, patching, steering) (drill: classify).
los.ek: Only an intervention shows the model uses a representation; a probe shows it is decodable.

topics.title: Probing, steering and interpretability for safety cases

los.do: Design a linear probe with a control task and report its selectivity (drill: compute).
los.ek: Selectivity = probe accuracy − control-task accuracy; a high-capacity probe can learn the task itself.

los.do: Explain how a contrastive steering vector is built and what a successful steer does and doesn't show.
los.ek: v = mean(act | A) − mean(act | B); adding αv shifting behaviour shows the direction is causally used, not that it is the model's concept.

los.do: Judge what interpretability can contribute to a safety case today — audits, deception probes, monitors — and where it can't carry the argument.
los.ek: Useful as one layer; not yet enumerative, and robustness against a model optimising against the probe is unproven.

los.do: Classify a described eval as capability or propensity, and as static benchmark, agentic task, red-team exercise or human uplift study (drill: classify).
los.ek: Capability: can it, under best elicitation? Propensity: will it, under realistic conditions? The two need different setups and support different claims.

los.do: Write a threat model that links a capability to a harm pathway, and use it to decide what an eval must measure.
los.ek: Actor, resources, steps, and the bottleneck the model might remove; an eval targets the bottleneck, not the topic.

los.do: Spot the validity flaw in a described eval design — construct mismatch, contamination, saturation, leaky grader, answerable shortcut, unrealistic environment (drill: spot the flaw).
los.ek: Construct validity asks whether the score tracks the threat-model capability. IASR 2026: benchmarks are often outdated, narrow or contaminated, and pre-deployment tests often fail to predict real-world performance.

los.do: Detect and mitigate contamination with canary strings, private held-out sets, perturbed items and release-date splits.
los.ek: Contamination inflates scores through memorisation; a gap between original and rephrased items is the signature.

los.do: Explain why recognition-style (MCQ) knowledge benchmarks misjudge real-world capability, and what open-ended and agentic tasks add.
los.ek: Recognising an answer ≠ producing it or executing it; tacit knowledge and multi-step execution are usually the bottlenecks. Near-ceiling scores also compress differences.

los.do: Compute pass@k from n samples with c correct using the unbiased estimator (drill: compute).
los.ek: pass@k = 1 − C(n − c, k) / C(n, k); not the same as 1 − (1 − c/n)^k when n is small.

los.do: Put a confidence interval on an eval score and decide whether two models really differ (drill: compute).
los.ek: SE = √(p(1 − p)/n), 95 % CI ≈ p ± 1.96 SE; repeated samples of the same item are clustered — cluster SEs by item (AISI repeats each task 10×).

los.do: Compute Cohen's κ for rubric-graded outputs and decide whether grading (human or model) is reliable enough to threshold on (drill: compute).
los.ek: κ = (p_o − p_e) / (1 − p_e); below ~0.6 is weak. Validate model graders against expert labels before trusting them.

los.do: Compute the sample size per arm needed to detect a target difference between two success rates (drill: compute).

List the levers of elicitation — prompting, scaffolds and tools, best-of-n, fine-tuning, helpful-only variants, inference budget — and judge whether a described campaign was adequate for a rule-out claim (drill: spot the flaw).
los.ek: PF v2: test at top-tier settings, with a helpful-only variant and the best scaffolds; any one result is a lower bound, not a ceiling. A rule-out is only as strong as the elicitation behind it.

los.do: Estimate the elicitation gap and widen a threshold margin for future scaffolding gains (drill: compute).
los.ek: Gap = best-elicited − default score; Anthropic's six-month eval interval and PF's lower-bound language both assume later elicitation will find more.

los.do: Design a check for sandbagging: fine-tuning recovery, password-locked controls, consistency across framings.
los.ek: If a small fine-tune restores much higher scores, the original number measured willingness, not capability; PF asks for elicitation that overcomes deliberate underperformance or a conservative upper bound.

los.do: Read a system card's dangerous-capability section and write a one-page briefing for a decision-maker: what was tested, how hard, against what baseline, and what was concluded.
los.ek: Separate evidence (scores, elicitation, baselines, CIs) from judgement (the threshold call); flag redactions and untested pathways.

los.do: Critique a system card or eval report for missing information — elicitation detail, human/expert baselines, uncertainty, threat-model link (drill: spot the flaw).
los.ek: A score with no baseline and no interval can't be compared to a threshold.

los.do: Identify, for a described result, which actor tier (novice, expert, state programme) and which kind of help (knowledge, troubleshooting, end-to-end execution) a framework's threshold is keyed to (drill: map to framework).
los.ek: PF v2 Bio/Chem High: meaningful counterfactual help to novices with known threats; Critical: experts to novel threats, or a full cycle without humans. RSP CBRN thresholds are written as uplift to defined actor tiers (e.g. moderately resourced state programmes).

los.do: Apply PF v2's five tracking criteria to decide whether a proposed risk belongs in a tracked category.
los.ek: Plausible, measurable, severe (thousands dead or hundreds of $bn), net new (not achievable with pre-2021 tools), instantaneous or irremediable.

los.do: Design an uplift RCT at the methodology level: participant population matched to the threat actor, internet-only control arm, model-assisted arm, blinded expert grading on a pre-registered rubric and threshold.
los.ek: Uplift is counterfactual: compare against what the actor could already do without the model, not against zero.

los.do: Compute an uplift effect — difference in proportions, relative risk, and its uncertainty — from arm-level counts (drill: compute).
los.ek: RR = p_treat / p_control; UK AISI reported non-specialists with a frontier model 4.7× more likely to produce an accurate protocol. With small arms the CI on RR is wide; report it.

los.do: Spot the validity flaw in a described uplift study — proxy outcome, weak control, underpowered arms, unblinded graders, participants unlike the threat actor (drill: spot the flaw).
los.ek: Written-protocol accuracy is a proxy for real-world success; IASR 2026 calls real-world uplift highly uncertain.

topics.title: Agentic, autonomy and AI R&D evals

los.do: Project a 50 %-success task-time horizon forward with a doubling time, and find when it crosses a stated horizon (drill: compute).
los.ek: h(t) = h₀ · 2^(t / T_d); IASR 2026 cites a ~7-month doubling, AISI ~8 months for cyber tasks; t = T_d · log₂(h / h₀).

los.do: Lay out an agentic eval in an Inspect-style harness — dataset, solver/scaffold, tools, sandbox, scorer — and name the ways it can be reward-hacked or under-elicited.
los.ek: Dataset → solver → scorer; the sandbox bounds what the agent can touch; stage-wise sub-task scores show where an end-to-end chain breaks (RepliBench: strong early stages, weak later ones).

los.do: Plan a red-team campaign: scope, threat model, red-teamer expertise, success criteria, severity rubric, and handling of hazardous outputs.
los.ek: PF v2 uses expert deep dives to validate automated evals; hazardous transcripts need restricted storage and cleared graders.

los.do: Distinguish model red-teaming, safeguards testing and automated red-teaming, and say what claim each result licenses (drill: classify).
los.ek: Model red-teaming probes capability; safeguards testing measures attacker effort to bypass deployed protections; automated red-teaming scales coverage but misses novel attacks.

los.do: Score red-team outputs with a severity/actionability rubric and report the harmful-response rate by category with a confidence interval (drill: compute).
los.ek: Rate = flagged / attempts with a Wilson or normal CI; weight by severity; report per attack category, not only pooled.

los.do: Decide what in an eval result can be published, what must be redacted, and what goes only to authorities.
los.ek: Publish methods, aggregates and thresholds; withhold operational content. RSP Risk Reports must mark redactions; institutes' disclosure depends on each testing agreement.

los.do: Classify a control protocol — trusted monitoring, untrusted monitoring, defer-to-trusted, trusted editing, resampling — and predict its safety–usefulness trade-off (drill: classify).
los.ek: Control assumes the strong model may be scheming and asks whether the protocol still prevents harm; a red team plays the model. 'Trusted' = weaker but not scheming; human audit budget is the scarce resource.

los.do: Compute the probability a protocol catches a scheming model before it succeeds, from audit fraction, monitor recall and number of attack attempts (drill: compute).
los.ek: If each attempt is caught with probability p, P(caught at least once in k) = 1 − (1 − p)^k; the attacker's best response is few, well-chosen attempts.

los.do: Explain chain-of-thought monitorability and what would destroy it.
los.ek: CoT monitoring works while hard reasoning must pass through readable text; optimisation pressure on the CoT and latent reasoning erode it.

topics.title: Monitoring, kill chains and incident response

los.do: Map a described misuse scenario onto a kill chain and choose the layer where breaking it is cheapest (drill: classify).
los.ek: Defence in depth (IASR 2026): access controls → classifiers → usage monitoring → incident response; each layer only has to stop some attempts.

los.do: Compute residual risk of layered defences assuming independence, and say why correlated failures break the estimate (drill: compute).
los.ek: P(all fail) = Π pᵢ only if failures are independent; a universal jailbreak or shared blind spot correlates the layers.

los.do: Match an attacker class (opportunistic, cybercrime, insider, state operation) to the weight-security level needed and the controls it implies (drill: classify).
los.ek: RAND SL1–SL5 scale from amateur attackers to top-priority state operations; controls include multi-party access, egress limits, hardened hardware and insider-threat programmes.

los.do: Explain why stolen or openly released weights remove every deployment-side safeguard.
los.ek: Whoever holds the weights can fine-tune out refusals and skip monitoring; release is irreversible (IASR 2026).

units.title: Frontier safety frameworks and safety cases

los.do: Compare the RSP, Preparedness Framework and FSF on threshold names, tracked domains, who decides and what happens on crossing (drill: classify).
los.ek: If-then: a capability threshold, early-warning evals, the safeguards it requires, and a no-deploy condition. RSP: capability thresholds, Risk Reports, LTBT review.
